reviewsWithKeywords.title: Virgin Beach with beautiful views!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is an unspoilt beach you can walk meters and meters and it is the same depth. Beautiful views. Take aquashoes for a walk and don't get hurt with the stones in the driveway. It was my turn to see a trumpetfish and a swordfish. Controlled access to a certain number of people a day in two shifts. So get here early so you can access it. There is nothing for sale to not generate trash and they have a dry bathroom. They make recommendations that you take your trash, which I think is perfect. They rent you chairs and folder for $400 pesos, we do not use it because the day was cloudy and we would only be 1 hour. We went through an agency. Which doesn't allow you to stay and enjoy the whole shift...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful !!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful place, beautifully colored beaches.  Very good for carrying children. It has 2 hours from 8 to 12.and from 1 to 5.  And they don't charge to get in.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Peaceful and Playful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Victor and Marianna were a great team. The boat ride was gorgeous. The spot to snorkel was phenomenal. We saw nice creatures and beautiful views. Having fun in the bay with friends was totally worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Outstanding beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Located about 30 minutes from La Paz, nice drive. You need to buy a ticket (can be purchased online in advance). It is a popular beach, however the number of visitors is limited so it won’t be too crowded. The have some umbrellas and there are toilets. Be aware there is no shower and no shop to buy food or drinks. The beach is extremely beautiful with white sand and clear water. The water is ver shallow so less for swimming but great for walks me just stay in the shallow water. I highly recommend also to go up the hill where you have great views.Must do activity in the area!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beaches in Baja California Sur
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A destination full of beautiful landscapes and white sandy beaches with crystal clear water. An abundant fauna and a walk unpredictable if you are first time in La Paz.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: the most beautiful beach of La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We reached the sea by car around 9am. It was hot, the water had the perfect temperature. Shallow and transparent with magnificent views. Probably one of the most beautiful beaches I've seen in my life. I RECOMMEND 100%.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Peace and quiet
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beach in Mexico. I am a lover of sloop beach, its tranquility, peace, crystal clear waters. A paradise to be cared for.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but many jellyfish
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful, but too full of jellyfish (aguamala) and after so much effort X enter we did not enjoy it! Unfortunately outside in August it is unbearably hot and you can not wait to get in the water, but there is the terror of being stung.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise certainly ♥️
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Of the most beautiful beaches I have visited in my life, calm and cold waters. Mood is also quiet because there is limited access as it is a reservation, which makes it a place to relax. You have to bring food and drinks as they do not sell there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: La Paz Trip Worth It
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The driver picked us up at our hotel promptly at 5:05 am.  Nice and comfortable large van.  We quickly picked up the other passengers and off we were to La Paz.  We stopped a little over an hour out of Cabo at a fantastic roadside restaurant where the food was great and affordable.  We then proceeded onto Balandra Beach where we had 2 hours to explore and swim.  From there we went to another beach near town to swim and shower off - kind of a public and popular swimming beach.  From there we went towards the La Paz Malecon where we had lunch at a great little restaurant (inckuded).  From there they took us into the heart of La Paz along the Malecon where you could shop, get ice cream, take pictures, tour and church, etc.  We then loaded up for the drive to Todos Santos to see the church, thr downtown shopping Square, the Hotel Californis and our favorite Tequila Sunrise Bar across from the Hotel California.  We finally headed back to Cabo.  All in all, it was a great day and La Paz is worth seeing.  A quaint coastal town with a European vibe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow the beach and the views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico, it is very relaxing, you can walk and walk. the views if you climb the hill is wonderful. Undoubtedly my favorites

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I’ve been to , the sunset is amazing, calm crystal clear water and clean sandy beach we loved it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It has been considered as one of the best beaches in Mexico, and it is not a lie, my family and I had an extremely good time here, it is very calm, the water only reaches you up to the waist and if you stay still the marine life begins to approach, so much so that we saw 4 puffer fish that were feeding on the sand trail that we moved when walking, !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Professional, breathtaking, and memorable.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Paco, Eddie, Adrian, and captain Jorge were excellent. The coordination is perfect. The food was good, the drinks flowed, and every detail was covered. All we had to do was sit back, enjoy the beautiful scenery, and walk right into the beachfront coral reef experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: El Caribe de la La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spectacular, the water seems like a quiet pool, we went during the morning hours, bought the bracelets a day early and made about 20min of line to enter.Quiet atmosphere, carry an ice cream, umbrella, there is no trash so make sure not to leave either, I recommend to bring some water shoes if you want to go to the fungus that you do not hurt the stones (like my urbanite friends).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach called sloop, I thought it was a spectacle of peace, it takes 3hs to get there by car from Saint Lucas, but it is an effort worth doing. the beach has hours, which I recommend to arrive early. ideal for taking photos and saving memories

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A very beautiful and preserved beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very beautiful, to get there is very fast from peace, the route overland you can do renting a car and in 30 minutes you arrive. As it is a protected area, there are only two check-in times 8 am and 1 pm the maximum number of visitors per shift is 450. We went on weekdays, arrived at 8:00 and took about 10 minutes to get through.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: spectacular this beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: from Cabo San Lucas are 3 hs by car, but it is worth it, it is a spectacular beach, do not miss it, calm and calm water, transparent, without chiringuitos, nor umbrellas. go equipped!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very beautiful and quiet beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach however when we went the sea was "gone" (low tide) and you walk a couple of kilometers in the ""mud"" rather wet dry sand that does like something weird, very little water, and well and then we explained that it would rise with the full moon in those days. You have to take care of those places, although they do awareness work for those who visit to take care, anyway we saw soda stoppers and abandoned shoes......you have to take care of it is our pass to survive on this planet. PD: It struck me that we saw hundreds of a species like nests in the shape of a "churrito" and they explained that it is the ""burrow" of a worm...... I don't know if it was coincidence but my husband gave a tremendous hives. Otherwise beautiful beach, RECOMMENDABLE. A spectacle of nature.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Mexico 🏝️
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The best beach in Mexico is perfect for young children ideal for teaching swimming are several areas of interest but certainly something out of the ordinary

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous. Got there around 7:40 and no problem getting in. Even got a palapa. Didn’t stay long. Be warned that there were a ton of mosquitoes when we went (late Feb).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful! The truth of the most beautiful beaches I have ever visited. Very well preserved. Stunning views of the hills. Crystal clear water, WONDERFUL!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must go at least once
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We left early so we didn’t have to get in line. It wasn’t crowded going early and the scenery is beautiful. We didn’t swim so can’t comment on that but walking around the right rock edges was very interesting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing place to hike and get the best views from the viewpoint. Walk to the sea, without being covered by water. For the photo with the fungus you have to line up a long line but you can get into the water and there but without “touching” the rock.  Very cold water, but after a while you get used to it:)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning location must see.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must see if you are in the area. It is absolutely stunning. There is a restriction on the number of vehicles allowed to enter car park and there are 2 sittings. We arrived in the morning time but it already had the limit so we drove in round the coast and went to other beach for a while which has bars and restaurants on it. Then headed back round to Balandra for the afternoon sitting. There are toilets/changing pods available for a small donation as it is like a protected area. The water is crystal clear, shallow and warm. It is stunning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excursions within an excursion!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The general view of the beach, the extent to which you can walk and the change in the tones of the water as the sun rises more and more are worth enjoying.  The water can be a little cold in the morning and gradually warms up with the sun.  Excursion to the famous Balandra Fungus or walk the other way to another bay with other beaches, plus excursion to the rock are essential to do during the visit, but do one behind another to be able to achieve it within 4 hours available in turn.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A little paradise!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A pristine paradise just nature there are no mass tourists there are no amenities, you can go in stages for a few groups of people not to modify the system.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must do!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Incredible experience!  We arrived in line at abou 8:35 (it opened at 9) and were about 20th in line.  It opened promply (no charge), there are about 20 palapas that were first come first served.  No restrooms, bring beach chairs, we brought our own inflatable paddleboard and were the only ones on the crystal clear water.  We were there on New Year's Day and there appears to be a truck that rents kayaks, paddleboards, and snorkeling equipment however it was closed.  Also, no food sales, so bring a cooler.  Our "shift" lasted til noon and then I think there is another shift at 1pm which is longer but three hours was plenty of time.  Really gorgeous!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: SPECTACULAR VIEW, BUT...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a very beautiful site, the best, the landscapes, the color of the water, the tranquility of the site. To keep in mind, I do not recommend bathing there; because, although it is not everywhere, if it is a place with stones, but mainly because several people we were bitten by something, perhaps a kind of bad water, generating a rash on our bodies, with quite a lot of burning, and discomfort for quite some time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Beach not entirely complication-free.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visiting Balandra Beach involves the following: Visitors are divided into two groups, one group can visit the beach between 09:00 and 12:00, the other group afterwards. It is recommended to be there before changing groups or early in the morning, as the number of visitors is limited and you have to wait in line for admission. An admission fee is not charged.  The permanently installed wooden umbrellas are quickly occupied if you are not fast enough. Chairs and umbrellas can be borrowed at the entrance for a fee from suppliers approaching the waiting cars. In addition, there are hardly any catering facilities (organic reserve). The beach is beautiful, the water clear, but may be full of jellyfish. When we swam out, with the intention of reaching the nearby beach opposite, we were attacked relatively violently; on all parts of our bodies, we first carried stinging, then later on for days on end, intensely itchy blemishes (similar to contact with nettles). We have therefore aborted our plan for safety reasons.So either do not swim, just run a little into the water, or wear an appropriate protective suit. There are also extremely small and many mosquitoes waiting for “victims” at the visitor entrance and checkpoint. A repellent is very appropriate. Had we had all this information before our visit, we would have had more of our stay. You can make the visit to the beach well with a taxi, 20 USD each way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent everything
reviewsWithKeywords.text: All excellent service LocationsLa Paz is amazing place thousand recommended for adult children and couples Attention and cute people

reviewsWithKeywords.title: All very well
reviewsWithKeywords.text: All super good!! Very punctual and safe transfer The vehicles also in very good condition and we took advantage of everything

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful nature view and crystal clear water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful nature view and crystal clear water. Perfect for a BFF getaway just be careful when swimming because there are stingrays and jellyfish but it was a very good vacation for me and my friends that moment.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful places in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful places I have seen in my life, we loved that they control the amount of people who enter, so you feel more comfortable, the views are spectacular and I recommend that you take your water glasses to immerse yourself and be able to see all the marine fauna that is precious. 100% recommended!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A day in Balandra
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sloop is one of my favorite beaches in Mexico, I have visited it many times for many years, this year I returned and found some surprises. It already has hours, morning and semi evening You have to line up if you are driving, only 200 people per shift pass, you have to arrive well early to pass by motor vehicle. If you are not wearing an umbrella, I recommend you be one of the first to grab a few palpitations. Nature don't tell is still sleepy! And then better is the low water with its warm temperature. The view of the cannon from above is a fete, you can't miss it. It's worth climbing to the top.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Can't stay all day, but is so beautiful it's worth it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: -The good: Beach is amazing and rightfully considered one of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico. There are palapas to leave your things and take some shade (believe me, you'll need it). The place is so photo-ready and the water is calm.-The bad: There's limited admittance, and you can only stay for a few hours (they allow to batches of people to come in, so they take you out to allow for the other group) so you have to be there real early in order to have a spot. The water is very shallow, so you'll have to either lay all day, or walk about half a mile to get to an above-waist depth. Overall well-worth the visit. Just bring plenty of sunscreen and hats, caps, whatever works because the sun hits hard. Bring plenty of liquids, as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Jellyfish beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning views. Stinging water. Got hit by dozens of invisible jellyfish. I'm sure it's not like that all year, but proceed with caution in September/October

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but during climate change it’s impossible to swim with soooooo many sting like animals.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Do not plan your trip late September to early October lots of agua mala that is like red string like animals that sting like jelly fish but you can berly see in the water  not visible like jelly fish. Locals say it’s because of the weather change but they won’t tell you what beaches have the most because they still want the tourist money.  If you don’t see everyone inside the water it’s for a reason. Very painful especially for kids.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worst experience ever.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful to beach to see but not worth going there.My family and I just came back and it wasn’t fun at all.I went into the water and they just said to be careful because there were some jellyfish but if get stung just ask the employee there for vinegar.It was infested with jellyfish but you can’t see them. We were the first group to get there and I got stung really bad. I went in half way and run back out and ask the employee there to for vinegar and he said they had already run out of vinegar, he clearly didn’t care and just said it was not a big deal. The restroom were horrible too. I would suggest everyone not to bother to go there.The tour people just want to make business and don’t inform this until you are there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa Balandra
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a wonderful place, we went on a tour and stayed for 2 hours, but what a wonder, crystal clear waters, the only thing you have to keep in mind is the jelly fish, there are many

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Continue to preserve this beautiful heritage
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beach in Mexico. Recommended in the afternoon timetable for the tide to drop... with wind and cold front come the bad waters. The only bad thing is that there are people who come in with music and that breaks the peace of the place and others with dogs that put the local fauna at risk (without considering the waste). But the place is still wonderful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A 3 hour tour
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful water and beaches. The beach was well regulated with the number of people allowed and how long you could stay. No garbage seen on the ground anywhere! Take your own chairs and umbrella if possible, but there are vendors at the entrance that will rent them to you. They also sell food and beverages. The wasps found the food quickly and were annoying, even if you didn’t have food. There are jellyfish. Due to the wasps and finding jellyfish the hard way we left early

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lots of jellyfish + stingrays + no rentals of chairs !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Extremely beautiful beach. Crystal blue waters and the view is absolutely breathtaking. However, when we booked this excursion with destination services at our hotel (riu Baja California 😑)they didn’t warn us of sting rays and jelly fish (that are invisible) . I travelled with my 74 old mother and husband. I was stung several times by jellyfish it wasn’t Pleasant. My mother and I both have immunocompromised illnesses . So knowing this info was key so we could have been more prepared. Maybe worn a wetsuit instead of a bathing suit with swim shoes. We were told there is a place to rent chairs. It wasn’t open. And my god the toilet facilities were absolutely disgusting!! It would be nice to have park rangers or people who work here to explain things and guide ppl. Multiple children screaming cus of stings. And a woman was stung by a stung ray. Wanted to post this to warn others before visiting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible experience! Just go!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had the most amazing experience! This beach is so beautiful and the water is so clear! When the tide is out the water is like a 5 minute walk away from the shoreline and there are sand bars you can walk to and areas in between you can swim in. The water was never over my head and I'm 5'4". There are two time slots you can choose from to go. One is from 8am until noon and the other is from 1pm until 5pm. We went from 1pm until 5pm. There are bees in the brush along the sand so try to avoid those areas. We just happened to get one of the umbrellas that were already there which was extremely helpful as the sun was very bright and hot, and the one we brought from our air b&b was broken. This was an incredible experience! You can see the fish in the water! Bring snacks and drinks for the day and don't forget sunscreen. The sand is incredible and so soft we didn't need water shoes or flip flops. Highly recommend this place! I hope I get the opportunity to go again. It's free to get in too, but you do have to pay to use the bathroom so there's that.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lack of information from the tour
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The amazing views, the only bad thing is that we could not get to the beach, many badaguas and many people hurt. But hence a good experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach experience in La Paz. Come prepared for a hot day. Bring umbrella and drinks with you. There are some umbrellas but not enough abs usually already taken!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beware of jellyfish!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful view and beaches. Food and bar were perfect. lots of little jellyfish, got stung while snorkling and while exploring the beach, it must have been the season. not poisonous, just painful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visit to Balandra
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although we were in Los Cabos we decided to go to Balandra, the beach is beautiful! And very well maintained, the space is very spacious so you could not notice many people

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went by rented car, in general I recommend renting car in La Paz, you do not need to be a van, you have to arrive early, I was car 18 and I could have a palapa, outside you rent chairs and umbrellas the same, bring food and drink, and floats, water gives for that. It is beautiful, in the morning shift the water is cold but at about 10 am it is already warm.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Dream beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited La Paz, very beautiful beaches, we went to Pichilingue, Tecolote, El Tesoro and we tried to enter Playa Balandra, but it was impossible, because there are established schedules and we had to wait 2 hours, so we preferred to take advantage of it on another beach. We will definitely return to visit Balandras and other beaches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BEST BEACH DOWN IN MEXICO
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is paradise, it is without a doubt the best beach in Mexico for everything it represents. Its organization, its cleanliness and its tranquility.It is light years from the Riviera Maya, if you are truly looking for a place to disconnect, to rest and enjoy, this is the place 100/10

reviewsWithKeywords.title: General review
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sloop incredible place, we arrived the second shift entering at 12 on a Friday the quota is limited to 400 people there was space this time but don't trust yourself, incredible place don't stay in front spread out keep walking either to the mushroom or cross to the beaches of face it, be careful there are no shops inside, go prepared with your groceries or food at the entrance they will rent you umbrellas, chairs they will sell you frozen, apples and burritos no more, you may use the umbrella there are not many free palapas or natural shades, I recommend you take some goggles and/or snorkel there are many fish and even though the water does not rise more than 1.2 meters you will be able to see a lot of fauna, be careful at sunset the tide rises and it will simply pass the 1.2 meters, pick up your garbage don't leave anything behind it is a paradise that we must to preserve

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Far drive, short stay, small nibbles and unforgettable experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Since we were here in March 2019, it has become a protected conservation area. There are no fees to park or enter at the time of this review. The only cost is the restroom. We came on a Monday morning. There are two time slots. We came at 8am. We left at 5 am from Cabo and 2.5 hours later we arrived to get in line at 750am. Prior to entering we were greeted by a conservationist and shared:1. Please take care of this land for us, don’t rip anything or take anything from the area. 2. There are no fees to pay. Anything you pay is not related to us (them).3. Keep music down to a reasonable sound level. 4. Please leave it as you left it.5. Please exit beginning at 1145am. 6. Follow the parking attendant instructions when you arrive. (A short distance from the entrance).It was an amazing experience and yes you will get nibbled by small fish. The feeling can be described as a little more than a mosquito bite.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bad bacteria in the water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is absolutely beautiful to look at however there's some kind of bacteria in the water that if it attacks you it feels like multiple needles punching your skin and it is quitepainful. It wasn't fish bites, my rash was on large area of the skin. I got attacked instantaneously on both legs on the entire surface area that was under water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best beach in Mexico
reviewsWithKeywords.text: La Cueva Beach, one of the seven beaches in Balandra Bay. The most beautiful beach in Mexico. It is advisable to arrive by sea, it is very calm and pleasant, without waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's worth the wait. The place is very nice, clean and has little capacity, in fact they control it. Walking to the mushroom stone on the beach is the best. The sea water, the colors, the views EVERYTHING IS WORTH IT. Super recommended.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and wonderful beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches in Mexico, the bad thing is that there is restricted access, we entered the 8 o'clock shift, for this we arrived at 7:00 and there was already a line waiting, but it is totally worth it, it is 4 hours that you They are perfect to get to know the beach well and go up to the viewpoint to take photos. The beach, no matter how many times you go into the sea, never goes beyond your waist, perfect for small children and people who don't know how to swim or are afraid of the sea. There are no vendors so you have to take drinks and food, there are only public bathrooms that are voluntary cooperation. A must-see if visiting La Paz.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ideal for relaxation and children.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful place to coexist with nature, it is a collection of ecosystems in one place. Ideal for younger children as the water height is very low, as well as for good photographs and relaxation. If you are looking for fun it is not your option.It is a reserve so access is controlled, they do not sell food, you must take out your trash, follow the directions and respect the fauna. It is recommended to arrive early because it can fill up, it has limited space and the stay is 4 hours.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No RVs allowed at Balandra Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: To get into Playa Balandra there are two entry slots: 8 am to 12, and 1-5 pm. Cars line up outside the entrance in a dirt road to the right if the entrance road. Today we arrived at 11:30 am and got in line for the 1 pm slot. There were already about 40 cars already lined up. They let a max of 450 people in so we were glad we had come early. After waiting 1.5 hours we got to the front and they would not let us in. Our RV is 24 feet long and they said no RVs. We were super disappointed because we had not read this anywhere. Left and went to Tecolote which is beautiful too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sloop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach! a paradise like few others! You have to arrive earlier because access is controlled... but it's worth the wait, it's beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A show
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is truly one of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico. I loved that the local people take great care to ensure that people do not litter, the beach is clean. You see little fish. I had to go on Holy Thursday and they only let in 450 people in 2 shifts from 8 am to 12 pm and from 1 pm to 5 pm, we had to queue to get in, I liked it because this allows the local people not to lose control of the place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beach I have ever visited. Everything well organized and safe. Services like kayaks are at a great price and the hosts are friendly. Highly recommended for families

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A paradise 20 minutes from La Paz BCS
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A unique view and beach that I had never experienced before, recommended if it is your first time in La Paz BCS. Controlled entries at 8:00 am and 1:00 pm,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches to visit in Baja California Sur, to be precise in the city of La Paz, highly recommended to go with family, friends or partner

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't miss this while in La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful shallow water cove. The pictures don't do it justice. Limited amount of visitors in each time slot from 8-12 and 1-5 so get there early.  This was our first visit and we enjoyed it immensely.  Next time we plan on renting one of the kayaks and going to one of the several secluded beaches across the bay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredibly unique beach spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Otherworldly! So thankful for the tip we were given about this beach. Words and photos can’t really do it justice. So beautiful and though it can get crowded, we went on a Saturday and there were several spots that felt like you were on a secluded, completely private beach. Do the short hike up for the 360 views then enjoy the beach and walking far out into the shallow, crystal clear water. Beautiful experience we will cherish forever!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pristine
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This little piece of paradise is exquisite to look at. However, very touristy with time slots for your visit so be careful to check these out. Water is fresh , really cold in the morning before the sun really heats you up. Other than kayaking not a lot to do so take a good book to relax. Very shallow waters all the way across. First on the beach will grab the free huts otherwise grab/take an umbrella because it does get very hot. Worth the 30 min drive out of town and does have plenty of hiking trails where you can view the entire area from above. It really was picturesque.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach with color
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent the day here with the family. Short taxi ride from La Paz.  Beautiful beach. Super shallow so it's great for kids to swim. Unfortunately there's no services or washrooms in the parking area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clear water and beautiful views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra beach is beautiful and not to be missed! We arrived early and secured a palapa--this or an umbrella is really necessary. The sun is hot! As the tide went out, you could walk across the bay and the water was clear. So beautiful! We also hiked the path to Tecolote beach, which had amazing views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach make sure you come when tide is in...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Would give it five stars if we went when tide was in. Recommend checking that before leaving. Had no problem getting in mid week for the 1pm, showed up at 12:40pm.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice experience. I wasn't very clear about the way to enter, so we arrived at 11:30am and they told us that we had to line up to enter for the 1pm shift, so we did. Finally we arrived and it is a very beautiful beach, the water reaches your knees at most. It is a super instagrammable spot. The only thing I didn't like (which has nothing to do with the organization of the entry) is that you go down the road and when you enter to the right there are people who stop you "as if to ask you for your entry information" and the only thing that They do is want to sell you everything they have. For the tourist or local visitor it is something very uncomfortable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach - a must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth the visit.  You may need to park and walk in so be prepared.  Very busy beach with lots of people around so try to go early.  Gorgeous views, and worth the drive to get there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Part of a swimming with whale sharks tour we did. We stopped at Balandra for lunch. Stunning, stunning beach with fine white sand and clear, clean waters. The part we were on could really only be accessed by boat so it was completely deserted. The beach is protected and they are rightfully careful about how many people can visit each day.  Try and go, it’s so worth it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Balandra
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pretty beach and worth the effort. The area is so shallow that swimming is limited. They do have 2 person kayaks for rent which was a fun way to explore. Take a picnic!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: AMAZING!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth the visit!  As has been stated, plan to arrive early prior to your entry time.  Amazing sandy beach and wading in the water is special. Rented a 2 person kayak for 400 pesos(cash only) and was worth it. Recommend doing the short hike to viewpoint for excellent photo ops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very good experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Superb beach. Limited time on site. We came a little before 12 p.m. and were advised to return around 1 p.m. In fact we were able to get the luggage at 1:30 p.m.Fixed parasols on site but it may be necessary to rent one from the rental companies on site.Water not always turquoise blue, rather green for us, but came a few days after the passage of a hurricane

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach time at Balandra!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go in the morning shift to avoid long lines! The beach is pristine! The agency (state/gov?) that runs the beach does a great job! To keep it clean and enjoyable they allow access in two shifts, 8-12 and 1-close. The long crescent beach allows for spreading out to enjoy the sun. The water is shallow and clear. You can rent Kayaks and/or SUP to paddle around. There is a trail to a view point above the beach which is easy to moderate depending on your age and physical fitness.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches in the world. I recommend it to anyone who wants to discover a new beach and environment. The sun and atmosphere are very cool

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Chill beach in a beautiful location
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Natural protected area that's excellent for relaxation.  We chose the early entry time at 8am. No fee to enter.  We rented an umbrella for 300 pesos from a group selling them at the entry gate (while we waited in line for the gate to open). The 10 or so free palapas fill up fast - so if you aren't in the first few vehicles to enter - bring your own shade.   High tide was at 7am this day - so entering at 8am was ideal. We got in to almost waist deep. By 11am the water in the bay was very shallow.  We walked over around the corner (along the shore or in the water) towards the Mushroom Rock. There was a line to take pictures with it - so we just looked from a distance. It was deep water and nice on the opposite bay from Balandra - so definitely recommend going over there to look.   No one selling anything on the beach was nice. The toilets are available for a donation. Overall a chill spot that's a must-see when visiting La Paz Mexico.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!  Do the view point hike for sure.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is open 8-12 and 1-5.  We got there about 10 and went to the beach and the overlook.  We left at 1130 and there was already a line for the afternoon time.  Bring water sandals.  The rocks are sharp.  You may want sneakers for the overlook. There is a dry toilet.  And they sell water and umbrellas at the front entrance.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun tour for couples
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was very cool and fun, I recommend not bringing things unless you leave them in your car or if it's a tour, only take what is essential.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Please HELP the  stray dogs
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is amazing. But it is located in the middle of nowhere and there are 4 or 5 stray dogs that were abandoned there . The people who take care of the place feed them (as much as they can) but it’s not enough and they do look malnourished so if you can, please take some food and fresh water for them.  This place is just magical, as shown on the pictures. The view from the top is amazing. The beach itself might get a little crowded but if you walk a little further down (take an umbrella with you)  you can probably get a nice stretch of beach to yourself.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach! Must see!   BYO Everything
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is a set of 7 beautiful and pristine beaches.  It is a MUST see in the area, so try to go at least once while staying in La Paz.  We got on the line for the afternoon session (1pm-5pm)  at about 11:35am. It was a Saturdays, so probably one of the busiest days.  We were maybe the 15th car in line at that point.  They let us in around 12:40pm.  You want to get there early if you aren’t bringing your own umbrella, so you can snag one of the free palapas.  This would be a long afternoon without any shade.  Honestly, it’s best to travel with your own umbrella in this region, as most of the beaches either have limited palapas or charge for their use.    We got the fist palapa by the rock formation, and it was such a beautiful spot everyone invaded our space in order to get their Instagram photos, or get by to wade over to the mushroom rock.   I don’t blame them, bc it was a great spot.  Just a little annoying at times (there was a lack of personal space.  So, if you want to be undisturbed, don’t choose that first palapa.  There is no cell service and no facilities there, so bring a cooler with ice, drinks and any food you need.  The water is crystal clear and the sand is white.  The water isn’t very deep, even during high tide.  Check the tide schedule before you go, bc I think its waaaay better at high tide.  I swam across to the beach directly across the water and back (about 1/2 mile each way). There was only an area in the very middle where the water was just over 6ft deep during high tide.  We went once, and that was enough bc there are so many other beaches to see that you don’t have to wait on line to get in to.  Playa Tecolote is very close to there and is an awesome beach for swimming and chilling out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The early morning and the wait to enter is worth it, beach ecology.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You have to arrive early because they only let in 450 people from 8 to 1 and others from 1 to 5, you have to bring whatever you are going to eat, because they don't sell anything, but everything is beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the wait
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can’t come to La Paz and not visit Balandra. If you are going to drive your own car make sure to arrive no later than 7:25 as anyone arriving after that runs the risk of not being let in. If you want to have an Uber drop you off, they charge between $250 and $340 pesos to take you. Make sure to arrange for them to pick you up as well. If you arrive by Uber or taxi, take a photo of the last car in line when you arrive as that will be your spot in line. People without cars stand and wait by the gate. Don’t forget to take the picture because they will make you walk back from the gate if you do not have the picture taken. Also keep in mind that not everyone gets in right at 8 am as they have to tell each group of people the rules before they enter the beach. We arrived by Uber at 7:30 and got in by 8:30There is minimal shade once you get in and no food or drinks. Make sure to come prepared. We bought an umbrella for shade and it has come in handy on all days at the beach as it is super hot pretty much every day in August. Make sure to secure your umbrella as the wind gust can blow them away if not done correctly. The water is very shallow and you can see many fish swimming around you. Make sure to drag your feet while walking to avoid stepping on manta rays and startling them. I only saw one and I was in the water for about 2 hours. Overall, don’t expect a beach with people trying to sell you stuff and get a bunch of money from you. The 3.5-4 hours will fly by if you are well prepared so enjoy your time!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not worthy the long lines to enter
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Unfortunately you have 2 shifts for enter and they only allowed 400 people each turn the beach is clean but no service at all they  have ,expensive rental of chair and umbrella is only business for them ,the bath room don’t have water and aré smelly  by the way you have to pay for use ,only  recommend it for short time staying there  not for spending the entire day there and relaxing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nothing compares to this pristine beach. Try arriving 2-3 hrs before your entry time and bring gear, snacks, and plenty of drink.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but be aware of your surroundings.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A lot of work! We heard amazing things about this beach. We decided to come up from Cabo and stay the night in La Paz so we could experience this beach without getting up at the crack of dawn. We brought an umbrella, a cooler with snacks and drinks. We left the hotel around 7 am and drove 30 minutes on a Monday morning to wait in line. Luckily we got in and were excited! Unfortunately, many people do not know how to secure their umbrellas and the wind gusts tossed two umbrellas at us. One struck my 7 year old in the head after nailing and inverting our umbrella first. Very scary! The woman who this belonged to came over as I was comforting my daughter  who was more scared than hurt thankfully and my husband was holding her umbrella while checking our the damage to ours and said "which one is mine"? Um duh the one that isn't still in the ground? How about are you ok?? I said yours is this loose one that hit us. She took it back down to her set up and proceeded to set it on the sand again without any attempt to secure it along with 2 other umbrellas she had haphazardly secured  by pushing backpacks around the pole. After my husband took ours apart and re-assembled it, he went down there to ask her if she needed help securing the umbrellas and showed her how to use the screw end to twist them into the sand and how to use the umbrella bag as a weight by filling it with sand and anchoring the umbrella to it. We didn't want those things coming our way a second time. All over the beach people were loosing umbrellas so watch out if it is a windy day. We had no idea about the umbrella danger. We were fully prepared for the baja shuffle to avoid being stung by a ray but the umbrella situation was a new one. Also, my older daughter was stung by something in the water. Looking at another post, it could be tiny jellyfish. It was not too painful and left a small red bump. What was a little alarming were the long dark shadows swimming in the shallows. We wondered if there were eel around? We didn't want to look too closely and came in from the water until they left the area. We brought tubes and felt most comfortable floating on those and keeping our feet up and out of the water. Would we go back? Yes... but from a boat tour most likely. It would be nice to have information about what we were in the water with.  It is a beautiful site to see but surprising how much trash was on the beach. We picked up many plastics, napkins, bottle caps and I found two pieces of broken glass as well. Why not charge a bit and have the area cleaned up with this many people oblivious people around?

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth all the Hype, DO NOT buy a pass online to visit.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is no charge to enter, we were scammed by the Cortez Club into buying “parks pass”. The beach is breathtaking. You are able to see the fish and walk along them. The early birds get the “palapas” aka the shaded canopies. We rented a paddle board for $20 bucks an hour. We did see puffer fish in July, be careful where you step. The bathroom situation is odd. Bring coins and expect to use a dry toilet. If you go #2, you sprinkle limestone over it. If you are going from Cabo, go during the week.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a view and welts
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Get there early!  As of July 2023 they only allow 400 people in at 8:00am and then clear the beach to allow the next shift at 1:00pm.  Some people sleep overnight just to ensure a spot to be let in line. Beautiful beaches and water. Definitely wear water shoes so you can walk around the rocks to the other beach which is less crowded.  That is also where you can see the famous rock structure.  Though the lines to take the photo op are long and there is no reprieve from the sun unless you float along the line in the water.  You can literally walk all the way out into the water and still be only chest deep!  Warning!!! There are little microscopic fish that will sting you incessantly!  They were not painful but very annoying.  We all have welts all over us.  Fortunately, they don't hurt or itch like some reviews state.  But maybe we are lucky.  So wear long shirts and pants in the water.  Definitely take time to climb the mountain for stunning views!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Views were amazing and the water is so clear and warm.  Waist deep water throughout the entire area. You are also can rent two person kayak for $25 an hour.  I would suggest purchasing an umbrella for the beach before you get there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is beautiful!! It’s one of those beaches you have to at least visit once. We love to lounge and drink under the sun so this beach was perfect for us the parents lol. There is no waves in this beach my kids said it felt more like a lake they did few like it was a little boring for them but they still managed and had a good time snorkeling w the fishes. There’s 2 time slots from 8-12 and 1-5 they only allow 400 adults at a time they do not count for the small children. We rented a car a drive from Cabo and went in the afternoon and got there at 12:30 and there was already a long line of cars we were probably one of the last cars they let in. I recommend getting there an hour before, take your own food and drinks as there is no vendors inside. Before getting inside the parking lot while in line there’s vendors renting umbrellas and chairs as there is only about 15 palapas inside. If you can I recommend renting an umbrella and chair. If you will be visiting vegetal beaches throughout your trip it may be better to buy an umbrella ($30) for your trip. Would definitely come back again and stay a few days in La Paz before getting to Cabo.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Things to know
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing! Be sure to be there by 12:30. It’s free to enter the park. The parks opens at 1 and closes at 5. They only let a certain amount of cars in.  They have 20 palapas to use for free. First come, first serve.   They do have some for rent outside the beach.  You will not find any food or drinks inside so bring your own. Worth the trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see … wake up early
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is amazing. I was not looking forward to this trip because I heard of the line and the limit number of people they allowed. We drove from Jose Cabo to balandra, we left around 4:30 am and arrive at 8 am. We had to be in line for less than 5 min and we were allowed to get in. It is one of the most amazing places I ever seen. The water was clear and you can see the fish with not equipment. There are two schedules to get in 8 am and 1 pm.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful views with clear water.  The hike is about 10 minutes uphill. Very easy to do, make sure you’re wearing proper shoes as thereIs loose gravel. I’d also suggest taking water shoes as some rocks can be rough/sharp if you want to get a picture with the mushroom rock.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day trip to Balandra + Tecolote
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is the gorgeous series of white sandy beaches with black cobbles. The water was shallow and crystal clear filled with lots of fishes (large orphies, surgeons, parrots etc.). The constant erosion of the coastline lets appear some unusual shapes like the "Hongo". Between Balandra & Tecolote, I walked for about 20min along the main road. I was surrounded on both sides with large rocky mountains filled with cactus. A cliché in TexMex westerns. I felt a sense of emptiness and silence. I can't imagine crossing this place on a longer trail. There were no shades, the spinifex rolling on the side of the road leaves you a dry mouth. I finally reached Tecolote.Tecolote is quite different, the place forms a series of palapas in very bad shapes. The 2km long beach had some black sandy patches and was constantly shattered by upcoming waves. It was winter, you wouldn't except much activity in that season. On the edges of the palapas, this place looks like a dumpster where American retirees and vagabonds would keep popping up. I still enjoy some melting fish tacos from a local palapa, the waiter was kind. I actually fell like in Bill Bryson books venturing in some remote yet inadequate place. The bus returning to La Paz came as a salvation.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the top 10 beaches in Mexico
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful, shallow, warm, and not to be missed.  Great family site with photo-perfect turquoise colors.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Quiet! Peaceful! Worthy of visit!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Peaceful spot good for simple timespending on the sandy beach! Great for camping as you are surrounded by gorgeous mountain landscapes! There is bus picking you up from appr 11:00 till 17:45 up to La Paz! Many tourists arrive here by cars, bicycles! Nice place for kayaking! Excellent sunset views! Good spot for yoga, beach tennis!It seems like you maybe alone there but at the same time all necessary things you may need are nearby!Welcome!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful places on Earth
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches in the world. Must arrive before 8am since only approximate 430 people are allowed at a time. You will love it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Exquisite Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I have ever visited, and I have been to quite a few.The water is sublime in the beach is clean with white sand.It is totally safe and luscious.He will not be disappointed

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach overun with tourists
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach which is being overun by tourists visiting for the day. Reminds me of Maya Bay in Thailand which also was overun by tourists.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good times
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I rented a car to get there and I was just in time , once the lot is full you can’t get to the parking lot ( unless your with a tour)- the tide was out and I presume the blue water would be more picturesque if the tide was in a bit, it was busy but there is a lot of spots - totally worth to check out :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walked for blocks and water only reached my knees!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So pretty and stunning blue water! There are trails to walk to other beaches which include a trip to the famous mushroom shaped rock (insert photo op here).  Suggest hiring a private driver as there are only so many people allowed on beach at a time.  There is one bathroom, kept clean by staff - make sure to tip them!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I ran 8 miles there. For it to be closed. But they let me thankfully after pleading I ran a long ways to get there. Ran into the park. Low tide. Did not look like pictures. Over crowded. There are better spots in baja.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is a beautiful beach located in a protected area. The only way to get there is to take a boat tour with a company that has a license to travel there.  Most often he tour includes some birdwatching along the way,  snorkeling (extra cost), and time and maybe lunch on the beach.  It doesn't take long to walk the entire beach.   It is a nice 4 hour experience."Some say" it is the most beautiful beach in the world.  I'm not so sure about this.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went here to relax and eat lunch after our whale shark tour. It was a beautiful spot... not crowded and very relaxing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Wonderful Walk In The Water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The water was crystal clear and you could literally walk across the bay with the water only coming to your hips! I like that they only allow so many cars in at a time (8-12 and 1-5) We arrived early as they had turned us back the day before because we did not know there were limits and certain hours) The, “Mushroom Rock”, was a little underwhelming in size and you could see it was supported by steel rods. 😳There was a trail to the top of the hill beside the beach which provided great views. Glad we went.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is amazing! There are two entry times 8 am-12 or 1-5 pm. You need to arrive earlier as they have limited capacity if you go by car. You can also get there by boat. Bring water and food as there's nothing available there for purchase.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Even with lousy weather it was wonderful...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Crystalline waters, a feeling of peace and serenity, the ability to walk for a quarter mile into the water without it ever reaching your chest... Balandra Beach is a unique place. Even on a cold day (for that area very unusual) it was still wonderful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful and crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went at low tide , a very cool large bay there were expansive flats with ankle deep to knee deep water. Cool worm poop mounds so probably fish come in a at high tide. Always a crowd local families mostly. Two entry times a day. if you want in at the 1pm time get there 12:30 or earlier. Try going up the road to Tecolokete Beach where you can have lunch , rent chairs and a short walk away is an awesome secluded beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Beach, worth a little hassle.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As of December 2022: Entry times are 8-12 or 1-5. However, you must arrive quite early as we passed by the line of cars around 1230 and it was (roughly) a mile long. There are limitations to how many cars are allowed to enter, and the parking lots are quite small. There didn't appear to be a lot of accessible parking if you have a disability-I think you need to arrive very early to obtain an accessible parking spot.We went right around the holidays (week after X-mas), so I am not sure if other times are better or if this is the norm. I've heard afternoons are most popular & would think weekends are also busier times. Other folks we spoke with said they lined up at least an hour prior to the opening times and were able to park. I am not sure how it works if you are getting dropped off by Uber or bus...We ended up hiking to the beach from an established path between Balandra & Tecelote instead of trying to deal with the car lines & parking. This provided lovely views of Playa Tecololito before dropping down to Playa Shiro. However, I don't think this option would be feasible or preferable for most. If you are accustomed to hiking & weather isn't too hot, just an option. The mushroom rock is a neat geological feature, although we didn't feel the need to stand in line for an obligatory photo. Water was so clear, and my husband did see a sting ray but if you "shuffle" your feet, they will swim away. Fortunately you can see where you are walking rather well. In December the water was not warm, but not so frigid that you couldn't walk/swim. It was a little bit windy on the day we visited, so I didn't fully swim...depending on your height/tide, water is shallow and main beach had a lot of kids playing safely. Although there are areas where it "drops off" and gets deeper further from the main spaces. The beach near the mushroom rock is a little less busy than the "main" beach which is near the parking. There are bathrooms at the main beach parking, although (as always) bring your own tissue just in case. I would just plan to bring everything you need as far as food, water, towels, shade, etc. Make sure you have "reef-safe" sunscreen and a container for trash. The space seems well maintained and is pretty clean, so help keep it that way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty beach arrive early
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a pretty free beach with snorkeling and kayaks to rent. The bathrooms are very clean and off the main parking lot. They allow limited access in turns (8 am-noon & 1-5 pm) only 400 people at a time. Very limited parking at the beach. We arrived at 12:30 for the 1:00 turn and we were one of the last cars to park at the beach lot. When you pull up join the line of cars, do not waste time driving to the gate, they will send you to the back of the line. They have limited palapas for shade. Bring everything you need there is nothing sold at the beach (food, water, towels, sunscreen chairs. ). Check the fise table. We went at low tide and had to walk very far out. pretty hike up the hill and to mushroom rock.There is limited handicap parking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Well managed National Park at Balandra Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very relaxing and scenic. Just be aware that there are two visit times:  8-12 in the morning, or 13-17 in the afternoon. Entrance is controlled, and it is  free, but everyone must leave at the end of the above mentioned visit times. So no one is allowed 12-13 hours, and your car must be off the parking by 12 o'clock, and by 17 o'clock, respectively. This regulation prevents overcrowding. The walk to the mushroom rock is absolutely worth it. There were no food vendors when we visited. Bring your own food/water, or drive for lunch to restaurants at nearby (3km) Tecolote Beach. All very relaxed and enjoyable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit when in La Paz!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I did a lot of research (internet and YouTube) prior to visiting and am glad I did.  Go during high tide or near high tide (there are only 2 sessions to visit per government so timing the day is important). If you plan to walk along the beach to mushroom rock wear water shoes!!  The water was cold and it was a windy day but it was December.  Definitely climb up the hill!  The panoramic view is incredible!  The sand is very soft. There is parking and very clean port-a-potties that are constantly being cleaned.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: GORGEOUS BEACH!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were brought here after Whale Shark and Sea Lion encounter with Mexplore - a company I HIGHLY recommend!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, hike a little. Bring a book.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful area with a shallow beach. The tide was out when we were there so had to wade a long way out to get to waist deep water. Nice to visit once but I won’t drive from Cabo again.There are lots of misinformation about entry. This I confirmed when we visited.2 entries: 8am-12 and 1-5pmPolice clear you out at end of shift. Open 7 days of week but first Sunday of the month is for locals only and yes they enforce.420 people per shift. They count! Only ~300 on the Monday we were there but long line of cars by 12:30. Let us in at 12:50We were not charged any entry fee.No camping here. Go 6 km to Tecolote beach for restaurant/bars/camping.No sign of the oil spill from boat fire that happened last spring.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A relaxing beach, highly recommended
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I think I was there is an off season or something I arrived around noon. Parking was no problem, but I can see if it's busy it would be a major problem. I think they would turn away people. There was no problem getting one of the shaded spots. There are thatched covered small tree sized poles. On the pole are nails to hang things. There are kayaks for rent 350 pesos if I remember correctly, for an hour. I recommend doing this so one may see the whole area easier. There is a gravelly path that goes up a hill. I have a problem knee so I didn't go up the path, but that is a good idea too, if one likes spectacular views. You don't need to go up there to know it will be breathtaking.    The water was pleasnt. I wouldn't say warm more like refreshingly cool. I could've walked from one side of the bay to the other as the water never got deeper than my waist. I'm 5'2". I floated on my back for awhile just enjoying the beautiful blue sky, listening to the birds and children playing. It was very relaxing.    I would like to reiterate this is a protected beach, no garbage allowed. There are no garbage cans so make sure you bring bags to carry away your trash. You are welcome to picnic. There were no food vendors. Bring what you want, but it's calm waters so one won't be surfing, but paddle board, maybe windsurfing. There are outhouses with attendants who will give you toilet paper. One of the stalls is designated for changing or maybe that was just because there weren't a lot of people there that day. I highly recommend this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bring Food, Bring Drinks, Bring a Book (or something to do)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach. We arrived at 12:30 for the second shift of people and we were the second last car to get in! The beach was at quite low tide so we had to walk out quite far to get into any water to swim in. I have to be honest, there’s not much to do here except wade around in the ankle/shin deep water. We thought maybe there would be a food truck or kayak/SUP rentals or something but there was nothing! This is truly a picnic beach so come prepared with water, food, drinks and something to do. We were able to get a free umbrella area to sit under near the end of the beach but we brought our umbrella from home just in case. We didn’t need it but it was good to bring as we got the last “free” umbrella sitting spot.This would be a really nice beach to bring small children as the water is very warm and shallow. We were a bit bored after walking around for an hour so we left after being there for 1 1/2 hrs.There are a pack of dogs (4-5) that patrol the beach and we saw them attack a little dog that someone brought. Good thing it was on a leash and the owner was able to pick it up quickly. I would NOT recommend bringing your dog to this beach because of this.Someone reviewed that this beach is closed until Dec 2022 but it is definitely open!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hidden Gem
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sparkling turquoise blue warm water that anyone can enjoy.  Shallow for much of the expanse, so great place for kids or novice swimmers.  May need to walk a bit further out to get a deeper water swim.  Free palapas for shade, pristine quiet beautiful beach.   To keep the beach quiet, there are now two "shifts" for visitors, 8:00 AM-12:00 noon, and 1:00PM-5:00 PM.  May want to show up 45 minutes or so prior to the afternoon shift to assure a slot.  WELL WORTH the wait.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Almost like a BVI beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a great beach and clear waters, free parking but you have a morning window or afternoon window, they remove everyone at 12 noon. A quick 5 min drive and you are at another beach that has a few beachside eats and bars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beach, part of Whale Shark combo
reviewsWithKeywords.text: White sand, protected cove. Nicer than any beach in Los Cabos (that we’ve experienced), with volcanic rock cliffs and a small sand dune. This beach is a one-hour boat ride from Cabo San Lucas and our captain brought lunch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent shallow beach to spend time with family
reviewsWithKeywords.text: WOW!!!  That was literally the first word out of our mouth when we visited Balandra Beach.  We've been to beautiful beaches before, but not one that was shallow and crystal clear like this.  The water was warm and serene.  We had no issue leaving our children to play by themselves.  The big bonus was the being able to see different schools of fishes swimming around us.P.S.  Arrive early since they're still limiting capacity and there are two shifts when we were there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: World class beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches around and even in Mexico.  Clear, warm water and beautiful sand. Worth the trip. A few changes until August 31  2022 summer there are 2 time slots to visit. 8am to 1pm and 2 pm to 7pm.  Get there early and wait in line in your car If you want a palapa for shade. If not, there is no shade you need an umbrella and bring drinks.  Music is not allowed. After the beach go check out La Paz downtown it's a great town, great vibe an amazing boardwalk where everyone comes out in the evening and hangs out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful magical Baja Bay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful spot. Nice that it is now limited to 200 people per "shift". Very shallow water so not ideal for swimming, but you can swim if you go out a bit further.  Show up early to line up so you make the cut.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is so beautiful and relaxing, seriously you instantly disconnect from the world when you get there in a good way! it is totally relaxing and enjoyable! my 6 years old was able to cross the beach literally walking with my husband, so this is not a beach to swim. I was impressed by all the volunteers and citizen efforts to keep this beach clean and  beautiful! we got there from Los Cabos by car and it was pretty straight forward, we followed the recommendations of getting there early, as they control the number of people that can get in. In iMaps you can follow the directions for Tecolote beach, and then just take the left instead as they are pretty close next to the other. Everything we did to visit this beach was totally worth it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not what I hoped for
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We read the great reviews of this beach and decided to rent a car and drive there from Cabo   I was hoping to swim at this beautiful beach area, but the water is so shallow for so far out, you really cannot swim there, just wade.Also,  the local police target the out-of-towners.  We were pulled over twice for “speeding” which was going 16 kph in a 15 kph zone!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the more attractive beaches i have ever been to, the color of the water is so blue and clear and the only way to have access to this beach is by boat. We took a boat tour with Pita's tours and they provided a meal at the beach with refreshments. If you are in La Paz I would strongly recommend visiting Balandra beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great views, beautiful colors, crystal clear water!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is magical! Great for kids as water is very shallow. We drove from cabo for the day, it's probably not worth it if you intend to just do this beach. We also stopped at La Paz and spent time there which made the whole trip worth the drive and money. (I liked the vibe of La Paz than cabo) :PBest getaway for anyone staying around La Paz or Loretto area.Few things to know before going -Beach has very few spots with shade, get early to grab them.Nothing is sold in the area so bring food and water with you. If you search on Google maps as Playa Balandra it shows a different spot in the downtown area. They allow people only between 8 am to 11am and at 12pm to 3pm.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best beach day of our lives
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches I have ever been to. Water was clearer than the water in Maui ! I suggest going by boat .The sand and water make you feel as if your in another world.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Prettiest beach I have ever been to. Such beautiful colors and shades of blue and so clear we could see the fish. I recommend a boat tour over driving there

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful hikes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I visited Balandra beach 3 times during my stay in La Paz (I never had any trouble getting in). Getting there: I took the bus from the Malecon bus station (this bus stops at all the other beaches on the way as well). I'm very glad there was a bus option as I found ubers and other car ride services scarce in La Paz and still pretty expensive. What sucks about the bus though is that the earliest one leaves at 11am. It costs 60 pesos one way. You can buy a return ticket from the bus station or pay the bus driver directly on the way back. Last bus is around 5h30pm. The first time I went to Balandra, I took the bus to Tecolote beach and hiked to Balandra. The hike is absolutely gorgeous. It's about an hour hike with many picture stops. The hike is moderate, except for one short steep part down a mountain. At the time Balandra closed at 3pm, so by the time I got there I had to leave not long after. The 2nd time I went, I decided to do the same hike again, but this time starting from Balandra, so that I could enjoy time at Balandra beach first. When Balandra beach closed at 3pm, they still let me walk towards Tecolote. I walked on the right side of Balandra beach to the rock formations/mushroom rock, then came across the other side of Balandra beach (much quieter beach) and then came across the steep mountain that I had to climb this time (but since I'm afraid of heights, I preferred climbing it vs going down it). After that, I just followed the path all the way to Tecolote beach. I then caught the last bus from Tecolote at 5h40pm. The 3rd time I went, I got off at Balandra and spent the afternoon there. I hiked up the mountain to the right of Balandra Beach to see the views from the top, which were beautiful. It was getting close to 3pm and I didn't want to leave, so instead I walked to the right side of Balandra beach, by the rock formations and the mushroom rock, and hung out in that area until I caught the bus back from Balandra at around 5h30pm. Balandra beach is beautiful, but in my opinion to see the true beauty of it, you need to see it from a higher viewpoint, hence doing the hikes. Without doing the hikes, it would have felt like a normal beach to me. It is pretty cool how the water is so shallow for such a great distance. The water is clear, but to snorkel you would have to go much further in to get the deeper water. There are free palapas at Balandra beach. The water wasn't too cold for swimming in Feb. It's also a sheltered area from the wind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You have to see it with your own eyes!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I think this is the most beautiful beach I have ever seen. And I have seen many! You THINK you've seen clear water, until you go to Balandra! It is worth the trip, worth the wait, worth it all. Please respect the environment and clean up your trash, wear safe sun screen, and leave no trace!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful to see, but not so much to do.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you want to lounge by a beautiful beach, this is the place. The water is clear and about knee-waist level. As of April 2022, you need to get here by about 11:45 am. At noon, they let in the 1st 300 people. No services.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This is the PEOPLE"S beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For those who may not know, Balandra was in danger of being developed with a hotel on site. It was the citizen's of La Paz that fought and won against development. Currently it is entirely monitor by local volunteers without funding for the government, so when you visit and use the ecological toilet, PLEASE make a donation, the local volunteers are using your donation to provide you with the toilet paper and the eco toilet. I was more than impressed what the citizen of La Paz accomplished by stopping development. I can see why they wanted their beloved Balandra saved, at low tide you can actually walk across to the opposite bays  in VERY swallow waters.No wonder it is loved so much, it is stunning!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Figure out how to get here!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No words for this most beautiful beach......    even the vibe is so relaxing so you can just take in the beauty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Awesome place to visit and spend a day.  I wish there were chairs under the umbrellas they have. It’s hard when you are older or have handicap to sit in the sand. The beauty of this bay/cove is an experience that calms the soul and provides an unforgettable experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: High Expectations, Underwhelming Experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Looking at other reviews, it looks like I am not the only one who found Playa Balandra underwhelming. It's beautiful to look at and a safe place for people needing a very shallow wading area. Lots of people lined up to take a picture with the Hongo Rock - a rock that looks like a mushroom. There are some nice hiking trails up above the beachs that give you great views with the occasional whale sighting. A team of volunteers offer bathroom facilities. New to the experience are entry and use shifts: one from 8-11am and another from 1-4pm. Beach patrols ask you to leave when the morning shift is over. You are expected to leave with all your things in your car and then turn around and get back in line if you want to re-enter. I suppose this makes some sense since it is a popular place. 20-25 palapas line part of the cove. From now on, I think Playa Tecolote or other area beaches will be where we go.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I find the reviews overrated. This is a very isolated beach with NO facilities, no shade.  In fact, I would say its desolate. If you do go, bring everything you need. It's a 15 KLM drive with limited access. Better by boat. Good swimming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I would recommend visiting by boat to avoid the car/people limits.  This place has great sand, shallow water, and lots of sealife!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Natural Beauty!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must see if you are in La paz!  This is a beautiful beach that you can actually walk across to the other side as the water is only about 4’ deep.  Great for families to snorkel and explore. Some of the most beautiful and clear water I’ve ever seen. This is a local treasure and treated as such.There is no food service or restrooms here so pack for a picnic.If not, there’s a great spot to grab a bite just down the road at a GREAT BEACH called TECOLOTE which I highly recommend!!!TECOLOTE does have restroom facilities if it’s a necessity for you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: NOT AS EXPECTED
reviewsWithKeywords.text: All reviews said to get there before 9 a.m. in order to score a palapa. We arrived on a week day @ 8:10. The parking lot was already 3/4 full & there were only 3 out of approx 24 palapas left vacant.Lots of tour busses dropping people off & overall  chaos. We lasted 3/4 of an hr then offered our shade to a man with his kids.All of this before 9 a.m. Totally not  what we were expecting...but now we know.We had explored the area the day prior & found a beautiful, turquoise water, secluded beach up the coast. That was paradise & exactly what were were looking for.Only hope Balandra can survive the masses.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Quiet Tour Stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited balandra as part of a whale shark tour. We learned from another hotel guest poolside that balandra is closed some hours and has limited capacity due to covid regulations- you must go early in the am to get a spot. Despite what you may see others doing you’re not allowed to hike the hills.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Never been to a beach environment like this one- its a must see! Shallow gorgeous waters and beautiful views

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place gets very crowded.  It's beautiful, just not very peaceful.  REcommend doing the hike to see both sides.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We landing on the beach via boat our On-Board-Baja guided Whale Shark Trip. It was stunning! There wasn't many people there and waters were pure turquoise bliss.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in the area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: TripAdvisor has this Beach in two different locations.  We went to the wrong location first, 5 minutes from town.  Then we went to the right location, about a 30 minute drive.  We had to wait in a 30 minute line on a Wednesday afternoon to get into the beach area.  It was worth the wait and it’s the best beach in the area.  Crystal clear water and white sugar sand beach.  Great for small children as water is very shallow very far out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice huge beach, most part are not deep. The access is controlled so if you arrive by car do it earl since the parking lot get full and you will have to wait for a parking spot, however, there is another parking place 1 Km away, so you can park there and walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited this beach on a week day at low tide.  Drove right in and parking spots were available.  Several people were parking at the path were you can hike up over to another beach.  But not necessary.   At low tide you could walk out at least a half mile to this beach which includes the mushroom rock.  It was a fun afternoon!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Plan and ahead and you'll have a transcendent time
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No cell service, very limited parking. Very limited services, a steep and rocky hike to the top of the hill for the best views . . .  and that's what makes this place a glimpse of heaven on earth.
