I found myself thinking that if I had a limited time left on earth, I'd want to come back here to soak up the beauty one more time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful beach, part of Whale Shark combo
reviewsWithKeywords.text: White sand, protected cove. Nicer than any beach in Los Cabos (that we’ve experienced), with volcanic rock cliffs and a small sand dune.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredible beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not to be missed. We went at low tide, which some have complained about; however, it means that you can walk much farther without swimming or wading through deeper water. This is convenient if you are not wearing swim wear. Hint: Wear swim wear. :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to hang out but lots of folks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach about 1/2 hour drive from town.  Drive is amazing through Cactus country.  Beach was much more crowded than we expected.   We did find a free palapa and that made it nice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cleo’s VIP tours, Balandara and La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The highlight of our trip was taking a private boat tour with Cleo’s VIP tours! Two female friends spent $125 each to have a private motor Boat with an experienced Captain and a young Marine Biologist. The best way to see this incredible coast is by boat. They took us around for 5 hours! We snorkeled at a coral reef/island with sea lions and lots of fish! We stopped at pristine beaches with clear warm waters to swim. They provided beer, other beverages and delicious ceviche and burritos at our last stop - a gorgeous secluded beach. They pointed out sting rays and sea turtles. I want to go back! Find Cleo’s tours, give them a deposit and you will not regret it!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool Little Bay, but Too Touristy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went twice, the first time on a Monday no problem parking at noon. The next day it was busier, but still parking was available when people left or at the overflow spot. None of the weird police or parking problems people mentioned before.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach with great view from tower
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice very shallow beach. Best view is from the top on the other side of the water near the radio tower on the top of the hill. This is about 20 min walk each way on supposedly private property (but everyone is walking this trail anyway).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: parking restrictions at beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stars are based on visits from previous years.  I wanted to let folks know that due to covid, they are restricting the number of people allowed to park at Balandra Beach.  We went last week and sat in a line of about 6 cars (on a Tuesday around noon).  They would let one car in for every car that came out.  This is probably good for the beach and makes it a better experience, but planning to go early isa good idea.  We decided not to wait and left.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most beautiful beach!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Balandra is my #1!! Water is cristal clear, the beach is clean and super relaxing. You can walk across to the other side of the beach without a problem. It’s absolutely beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magical
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just incredible ❤️ One of the most beautiful beaches I’ve ever been to. Situated on the Sea of Cortez, north of La Paz this beach is definitely bucket list worthy. The water clarity is intense, the water temperature is perfect and the views are stunning. Limited services here…porta potties in the parking lot, a truck with a few fruit cups and other snack items. The worst part for us was the shakedown from the local police on the way back for a “traffic violation “. We would definitely return again but this time a little more savvy to the local police scams.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We used Baja Falcon tours, which we accessed right on the malecon, on the corner of El Arco hotel. They offered us a great price and it ended up being basically a private tour for my husband , me and my 2 young daughters. They were offering to take us to Espiritu Santo but we just wanted to see Balandra since it was closed from the road. They gave us our own unique tour to calandra, which was beautiful. They were also very careful and were conscious of the environment. The captain and the guide Felipe were very knowledgeable and let us use our time as we liked. They stopped at the famous Hongo rock formation for pictures and provided us with lunch at the beach. They taught my husband how to catch clams right off the bottom of the ocean and we even got to eat them at the beach. The whole experience was amazing, got to see some frogs, snorkel and enjoy the beauty of they beach and even met some sweet straight dogs at the beach. The beaches in Balandra are gorgeous and clean and clear. They keep it almost untouched and there are many fishes and sea life to enjoy if you like to snorkel.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach closed but the hike isn’t
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I wish I had known the beach is closed due to COVID-19 and that there’s no way around it—trust me, I woke up at 445 am to drive there but was met with a health official before dawn who said I couldn’t be there. Instead to get a glimpse, due the hike instead that is about 1/4 mile before the beach parking lot. There’s a fence that says it’s closed but other folks are were walking right around it like I did. The views are stunning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of nicest beaches in all of Mexico
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So beautiful, make sure you visit and get in the water.  The sand is fantastic as well and shallow water for as far as you can see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clear water and its not crowded at all, the only thing its that I heard that there’s a quantity limit per day so we got there at 7:30am just in case, but it’s worth the drive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beware of the police on the highway
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach might be beautiful, but beware of the police on the road to those beaches. They are thugs. They ambush you, invent an infraction and then they tell you, you can pick up your license next week, unless you pay now. That is of course the only option and it is expensive. We paid $200 and were not given any paperwork or any proof that we paid. On the plus side: they were friendly. Recommendation: when you see a police care make sure you follow the rules and pray.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand fleas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: BRING BUG SPRAY!!! Got there at 6 am because of 120 people limit and got attacked by sand fleas. They are everywhere. I am chewed up, looks really bad. You cant hide. And you cant leave if you didnt drive. There is almost no cell phone signal, so arrange the pick up.Its a pretty place, but there is really not much going on. Water is up to your ankles for the most part, you cant swim there. I asked my uber driver to pick me up at 12. And there was more than enough time to take million pictures. It does look much better in the picture.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfection
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took a boat in (700 pesos per person) for a two hour tour. This is the way to go if you ask me. They only allow 200 people in per day, so people line up at 5:30am to get in. Screw that. Our boat left from a nearby beach, then we went to one of the seven beaches in Balandra Bay. We had a 700 foot-long stretch if fine white sand and clear shallow water completely to ourselves (8 people total) for an hour and a half. No, you don't get to spend all day there, but since it got insanely hot in the afternoons, that was fine with us.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely calm waters not very crowded.  Would definitely go back.Some rocks but mostly sand. The day we were there no waves so easy to get into the water

reviewsWithKeywords.title: superb beach !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our boat stopped on Balandra beach for lunch after 2 Scuba dives.This a beautiful  spot to chill or snorkel

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This has to be one of the best beaches in the world. worth the trip.  It's a bit of a drive from La Paz, take your time,enjoy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most memorable and beautiful beach in Baja
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was told by numerous locals that Balandra is a must see when in Cabo. Although it was approx 2.5 drive, it was well worth it! You must arrive by 6am (although) I feel it depends on the season, day, etc. However, I did not want to miss the opportunity, It was probably one of the most surreal and tranquil beaches I have ever visited. I love the protection it has against industrialization. It was picturesque and felt like untouched territory. We were able to see the infamous mushroom tree and walk across the beach to the other side. A few tips before traveling, make sure your car is full with gas (mine was not & the nearest gas station was 30 min away). Bring food & drinks, there are no vendors except a small truck that I think sales small things like soda and snacks. There is a porta potty bathroom that you pay a peso or so to use. I would definitely bring the chairs that are low so you can lay in the middle of the water. It is a beautiful experience and there are palapas for shade.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must visit.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a gorgeous beach! Consider coming on a boat tour (we did). The main beach has a limit of the number of visitors allowed each day. But if you come by boat tour, you’ll get to visit the other side of the bay, and the entrance limit won’t apply to your party.  And most tours include lunch, which is a bonus!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Soft white sand, turquoise waters..clean..authentic Mexican/Spanish/Latin music playing, free palapas, snack truck (reasonably priced). What's not to love!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking in every way!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We arrived to Balandra Beach at 12pm on a Sunday and were told the beach was at capacity. So we got in line and wait. They said it could be 20 minutes to 2 hours depending upon how many cars came out and at what pace.  We decided to go down the road to another beach which worked out ok. We went back to Balandra beach about 3:30pm and went right in. I think if you don’t go extremely early then you will need to wait til late afternoon. It’s really worth the drive from Cabo and is a spectacular place to see. The water here is so clear and with small pools you can walk and walk for what seems like miles and just enjoy the beautiful views. The beach has been protected by limiting the amount of crowds and I can appreciate that since it was very clean. Parking is free and in a paved lot. Definitely the highlight to my trip to Cabo!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A little paradise..
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I enjoyed Balandra beach so much, not far from La Paz but also the white sand, emerald/turquoise water, tranquility, marine life and way locals preserve it.. a place to anjoy..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lives up to it’s hype
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We kept hearing that Balandra Beach was one of the most beautiful in the world, but couldn’t get into it by road...we finally got there by boat, and now we agree - see it yourself if you can!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful- bring some money to bribe your way in
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Got there at 8 in the morning and were told that they had already met capacity of 70 for the day. I begged as we had driven up from Cabo and really wanted to spend the day here, no budging at all. After about 5 min of all my sob stories I offered $20 for our 2 cars of families. That was easy! Gate suddenly opened and the rule of 70 didn’t apply.  The beach is beautiful. Bring sunscreen and water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is a beautiful bay that is composed of several beaches. It’s a 15 minute drive from La Paz and more than 2 hours from Cabo San Lucas. The beaches are amazing and with very little people. To go to the main one you need to arrive very early in the morning (no later than 6) to be allowed to enter and drive to it (as of December 2020, they were only allowing 120 people per day). In case you don’t make it, you can still drive to Pichilingue and take a boat from there. Depending on what you want to do, they can charge you from 30-35 per person to 60-70 (in case you want to snorkel) for an hour or 2. I recommend you bring snacks and drinks,  as the boat is allowed to drop you off at all beaches except the main one, which is the only one where food and drinks are sold. I spent time at The Hongo beach and thought it was simply amazing. The pictures I took don’t make it any justice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clear blue water!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most beautiful beach I have seen in West Mexico just like the Caribbean. Sand was white and clean and too. I hope I can go again someday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach of the world!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach!!! Out of the 57 countries I have had the chance to visit, this is for sure it is the best and most beautiful beach I have been to. The colors of the water, the different bays, the cleanliness, the protection of the beach to avoid crowds and damage of the nature is amazing.Please be careful to arrive really early in the morning (around 5am) because they only allow 120 persons per day. If you do not plan to arrive that early, the only way to enter is with a private boat tour from La Paz.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family new year
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Twice visited this beach with On Board  with Baja company. Great place, wonderful swims. Thank you to Victor, captain, Rosario and  Paolo, tour guides for historical and geographical information, biological update, great lunches :), and readiness to help with paddle boarding.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relax and Recharge day!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We arrived a day early to La Paz for our tours with Whale Sharks and Sea Lions, so we decided to venture out to some of the local beaches to sightsee and enjoy the warm weather.  Fortunately for us we awoke early in the morning and got to the beach  around 8:00 AM.  Little did we know at the time that they were counting cars and was not allowing many more after we got there.  The beach is so nice and the water is crystal clear all across the bay.  You can easily walk to the Mushroom Rock from the beach and we even walked across the bay to the other side ( it's a lot farther than it looks BTY).  Sand is soft and easy on your feet, but we highly recommend aqua shoes or sandals if you want to  get pics around the Mushroom Rock because the rocks in the water are painful if you happen to step on one or you want to get close for a photo.  Could easily spend quite a bit of  a whole day there, but we moved on to other beaches after about 3-4 hours there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Baja Hidden Treasure!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have in Cabo many times but had never been in La Paz so we decided to visit it this time (it's the capital city of Baja Sur), the city was very calm and dwellers super friendly, it was a good and relaxing experience,The main atraction is the city is this beach called "balandra" where you can visit a landscape like no other you had seen before and even get a picture with a strange rock-formation with the shape of a mushroom, they calle it "el hongo rock" seing this rock formation is the equivalent of el arco in Cabo San Lucas (but in its own way), Balandra is an excellent location and a "can't miss" atraction!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach visit by boat
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous turquoise water and white sand. All Natura terrain behind—not one invasive plant. Hornet fish and blowfish right up by the shore. Paradise.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking but...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I arrived by boat where there are no limitations on MAX persons occupancy. Indeed place is beautiful but perhaps not my favorite, water level is so low and calm that it gets boring after some time. There are "funnier" beaches neraby.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: There's a reason it's so famous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is very beautiful. The baby blue and emerald-colored water, the peaceful ambiance, the white sand. This is a very relaxed, cool place. This is a must-see when visiting La Paz

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We woke up today early and decided to take our chances to get in.At 8:00 AM sharp we were at OXO buying our snacks and drinks.We arrive at 8:34AM at balandra after a complicated way considering the construction at the road.We were lucky, they told us that only five more persons will be allowed considering the 220 MAX persons occupancy allowed.The occupancy is only once counted, meaning that even 10 persons get out they will not allow any one else inside. Is only 220 total a day. Our beach neighbor told us that they arrived at 5:00AM to be allowed to enter at 8:00So my recomendación: Arribe at most 8:00AM. We were very lucky, but a lot of persons were left out.It sounds too early buy you won’t regret.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning and unspoiled
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pictures don't do this beach justice - social distancing and limited availability to access the beach is still in force, so go early! Take snacks and water as there are no facilities/restaurant or food service there. Take your chairs and umbrellas too, althogh there are a few available to the public,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Restricting to a very small amount of people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I imagine it was beautiful, but they won’t like more than a small number of people. The entrance is blocked by police. And I came there at 11 AM, but there are the beaches around

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't come to Baja California
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Don't come to Baja or La Paz during the pandemic. Is a ghost town and the customer services are the worst. All. I mean all the beaches are closed. Near and far. I understand the social distances criteria. However, how I'm going to transmit the virus at an empty beach is beyond me. Save your money and go somewhere else.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: THE MOST WONDERFUL BEACH IN MEXICO
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Easy to get from La Paz to Balandra Beach, half an hour by car, taxi or bus.beach where you can walk for up to 800 meters with the water at your waist and 100% transparent full of colorful and shaped fish. Between 2 hills and a cliff is this wonderful beach where the famous mushroom-shaped rock naturally eroded by the wind is found.a beach worth visiting because it is the only one in the world like that, do not waste time and when you go to La Paz or Los Cabos go visit it is a 2 hour drive to Los Cabos, passing through Todos Santos town that you have to know too .Area protected by La Marina de Mexico with parking and eating areas. You can take any type of drinks, food and umbrellas for you to spend an excellent day. You can also camp as it is guarded and 100% safe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A bus from the local bus terminal will bring you here in 45 minutes.  It feels like you're in another world with the gorgeous scenery.  Bring food and drinks.  There are only a few small carts with snacks and water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: it is weird this atraction is not the number 1 in La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this atraction should be the number 1 atraction in la paz, nothing can beat it, it is such a calm and beautiful beach with an otherworldly sense of tranquility, if you are from another country you will definitely love this experience

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning bay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go early in the morning to avoid crowds. We were the only ones there at 8 am in a weekday. If you are fit, walk up to hill above the bay to take in the vista. The view is breathtaking. I wish we’d had time to rent a kayak.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Outstanding Playa!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I cannot think of a beach lagoon with water that looks so sparkling and clear. Our day trip out and back by bus was the highlight of our five days in La Paz. Go during the week to avoid crowds and snag yourself a free palapa. Absolute heaven!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Morning Kayak
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach with a few amenities. We rented a kayak and spent a couple hours paddling around. Nice place to spend some time. Go early because the parking lot fills up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous place, surprised at hectic scene
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It wasn't so much the crowds, but the food concession and beach peddlers that disappointed me.  I went there expecting a pristine UNESCO protected beach, with no food or bathroom facilities.  We arrived complete with a cooler, towels and our own bathroom supplies. It was wall to wall people, with a much-appreciated entrepreneur renting out umbrella tables and chairs for 400 pesos as there is no shade, and 2 porta potties manned by a couple who dispensed 4 sheets of tissue for a donation, but they wiped down and sprayed after each use which was nice.  In all, the beach was an absolutely stunning experience and I am very glad I got to see it first-hand.  The rock formations there and on the highway were really cool too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra and tecelotes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach outside of la Paz. Head north up highway 11 and you’ll see the signs for balandra. It’s really easy to find. Follow signs towards pichilinque then to balandra. After balandra I’d you’re hungry cruise about 3-5 miles towards tecelote for food, drinks, another amazing beach with camp sites. They have about 10 beach restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fun to enjoy the water and sun! Such a great beach for kids-- so shallow for so long. Just ok for snorkeling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Used to be the most amazing natural beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is nothing in comparison  to Balandra’s natural beauty, blue calm waters and the shallow nature of this body of water. However, over advertising it has made it crowded with visitors, bus loads full. The peaceful nature has been destroyed, but the beauty remains.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the Most Beautiful Beaches in Mexico but has Almost No Services
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have been all over Mexico and this is the most beautiful white sandy beach we have seen.  It is missing services and facilities which is a real problem.  Definitely worth a visit but Tecolote Beach less than a mile away is also very nice and has lots of facilities and plenty of restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra Beach is so breathtaking--you won't be disappointed! It does get crowded on weekends (we were there on Constitution Day, so like a weekend), but it emptied after 4 pm. Kayaks are available to rent, so that is very convenient.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A great beach but I went on a bad weather day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a cool beach , and I arrived via boat from La Paz. It’s cool to be able to walk in very shallow water for many miles with no waves BUT I will advise that my particular visit did not look as pretty as the pictures. There’s lots of pelicans. We did paddle boarding. I was cold and the ride there was bumpy. Wish I had not gone in February.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a gorgeous beach you can easily spend the day at. There are fresh fruit stands, a refreshment stand and a some people selling bread/empanadas. It’s worth a walk up on the hill for a really nice view! The water is quite shallow so you can walk around easily

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous and must see beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was my first time visiting this place and this nice and peaceful beach. The water is so clear, you can walk into the beach and water will just go above your ankles, and then by your knees. Nice place to go!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Beach - so beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to Balandra Beach at the suggestion of the owners of our hotel. We were in Todos Santos, so the route was to La Paz, then past it. Worth it!Parking was a minor issue, but we were there on a week day and I imagine it would be a lot worse on the weekend.But such a beautiful beach. Low tide meant you could walk half way across the bay! Be sure to walk all the way around the rock formations.There is a place you can hike up a short way above the beach for a spectacular view of the whole area. There are food carts at the beach. But before taking the left fork at the Balandra sign shortly before the beach, you can take the right fork which will lead you to restaurants, etc.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: amazing place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: playa Balandre is one of the most famous and amazing place on the earth, we were there early in the morning to enjoy the beach and the enviroment

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful fine, white sand beach. Hidden away a little and not overly busy. When the tide is down you can go out pretty far from the beach on some sand bars.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were lucky enough to get to see this beautiful beach. Not only by car, but also boat for a private lunch,on a whale sharks excursion .Where are Captain nearly caught a Mai Mai with his hands. Walk to right on Balandra Beach. Famous Mushroom Rock is on the other side of rock outcrop. Or you can walk over the hill. Gets a little crowed, and tide goes down. With no shade. Bring umbrella and pesos for fresh fruit drinks, Jewelry, Blankets and the bathroom. Road work on the way. About 20 min. from La Paz

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful place to stop and take in the beautiful views! Climb up the cliff to see all around you or enjoy the beautiful shallow beach! We even saw people paddle boarding in the mangroves :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most beautiful beach in.the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is just a must visit if you travel to La Paz, I personally went with the local guide Karen, she took us to an unbelievable hike and saw amazing landscapes, took us snorkeling wichh was a lot of fun, took us kayaking trough the manglar, set a camping and fed us with a delicious ceviche, a full day tour!  Her local phone: 612-1402857

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped at this beach after doing some swimming with whale sharks, and it is beautiful, nice white sand, quiet cove, perfect spot for a picnic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking Bay!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful aqua marine water.  Safe, shallow, calm beach.  Great for famililes.  Bring your own food and drinks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful shallow water beach, emerald green water. The road isn’t the best but worth the trip. We drove from Cabo to La Paz 2 1/2 hr drive

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Impressive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful place,. Two couples travelling together. The men hiked to the top and took pictures of the amazing views. Ordered lunch on the beach from Ceasar. Loved the 2hole experience

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Warning its beautiful but full of stingrays!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The only reason I am giving this a low rating is so you may be warned that there are stingrays actually several smaller ones that blend in with the sand and they have the tiniest warning signs at the entrance of the beach so that they don’t scare tourists off but don’t get me wrong most beautiful beach Ive seen but even doing the shuffle in the sand you can still get stung by stingrays as I was and it was a terrible experience that has taken me almost a year to recover fully from the area of injury infact with the incident happen many tourists were unaware of the stingrays also please watch your kids its not worth the risk several locals informed us that happens more frequently then youd think even to the locals so if you go use a kayak and don’t risk walking because sting rays don’t always see you you shuffle because they hide under the sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach if it's within a close distance
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove 2 hours each way to get to Balandra Beach and although it was a beautiful beach, I don't think I'd take my whole day to do this trip again.  But if you are close, definitely visit.  Make sure that when you park, you realize that around the corner of the rocks, is a whole other section of beach which isn't visible until you continue walking.  The water was very shallow where we were but walked out to a sandbar and deeper water.  We snorkeled in open water and didn't see much.  Had we gone over closer to rocks (which didn't seem safe) there may have been more to see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a very interesting beach!  The water was very shallow, even at high tide, so you could walk around the point to get to the next point with the mushroom rock.  However, we chose to hike over the ridge - not difficult, and on to the next ridge.  We were rewarded with beautiful views, lots of flowers and cacti, and even a roadrunner (bird).  Back on the beach, there was an impromtu band playing (pretty poorly, but a LOT of fun) and vendors selling enormous donuts, empanadas, fresh fruit, and beverages.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach Near La Paz, Baja Sur, Mexico
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Take your own food and drink and enjoy this lovely beach about about 5  miles from La Paz.   It seems further.   Sadly  you need a vehicle to get there.    There are a few vendors and interesting group of beachgoers.    Nice sand, pretty water pretty clean considering that it's near the ferry terminal and port.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach Crowded, Location Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When you go to Playa Balandra, be ready (at least on weekends) for a crush of people and challenging parking. The beach is crowded. Tha said, the beaches are also splendidly beautiful and are of soft sand. There are some steep, but not-too-difficult hikes up the headland that offer gorgeous views, if you want to be away from beach people and noise. Plus- with my natural history interest, I found walking around the edge of the mangroves delightful and peaceful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Daytrips to Balandra and Tecolote
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a beautiful place and thankfully fully protected from the development sharks to keep it a national treasure for Mexicans and travellers alike.Absolutely beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: best beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beautiful !  worth the visit, best not on weekends as it can get a bit crowded stunning water color , easy to get to

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach I have ever seen
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is definitely out of the way, but it felt like discovering a lovely hidden secret. It felt like an authentic, non touristy Mexico experience. White sand, dramatic bluffs, desert landscapes, the clear shallow blue water of the bay on the Sea of Cortez, families enjoying the day, street food vendors, and an absence of annoying drunk spring break types. I would definitely go back, again and again and again!.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra Beach is a must visit for all.  Clear shallow water suitable for all.  Clean sandy beach a great place to spend a few hours or the entire day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: VIP tours
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went to Balendra on a whale shark/ sea lion combo tour with La Paz VIP tours. The beach itself is a wonder, where desert meets sea. Its right around the corner from San Rafaelino, a sea lion colony of about 70 animals that VIP uses as an alternative in January when the seas around Espiritu Santo get a bit gnarly. Crystal clear water and you can wade out pretty far and still be only waist deep on a six foot tall person like myself. If you have an AKASO, Go Pro, or other actiob camera bring it with you as you might be walking close to some very beautiful and interesting fish. Nice to see a beach littered with shells (among other things; I also found a triggerfish) instead of plastic. Not to be missed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome beach to relax
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing views.   Go early to find park g and a spot on the beach as it gets busy as the morning goes on.  You can wade in the shallow waters for ever!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the loveliest beaches I’ve seen!  Clean sand and Shallow clear, warm water for half a mile out. Fab vistas. You can rent umbrellas or a palapa and picnic all day. Calm waters- great kayaking or even swimming if you get to deeper water. Fruit/juice/ snack shacks and portable toilets. Parking lot gets full early but there’s a bus from town.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited this beach twice whilst in La Paz. Such a lovely place to sit around for a few hours - take your own food/ drink as there’s not really much choice there. We hired a kayak and paddled over to one of the beaches on the other side of the bay. Lovely to have our own private beach for a while!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crystal Clear Water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of our favorite beaches in the La Paz area. The addition of washrooms at the beach is a huge improvement.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One if the most beautiful beaches I've been to in Mexico. Lots of locals go to Balandra so there are families, couples and friends. Make sure and walk around to the right of the beach. There is more beach and not as crowded. You can walk in the water because its shallow for a long way. There were a few vendors there the day we went but don't count on it. Bring food and drink with you. The parking lot is small so get there early or park along the road. You won't be disappointed. Don't have a car. You can ride the Playa Bus from La Paz.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see and family friendly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One giant sandbar that allows you to walk to beaches where you will be the only one. Warm water that is perfect for wading and sitting and relaxing. You can venture out to where you can snorkel. Little to no waves so this beach is perfect for small children or elderly. No restaurants, but a food truck that served fresh fruit was there. The beach was not overrun with sellers peddling their wares, but I did see a few. No restrooms— just beautiful white sand and protection from the stronger winds. Thatched Permanente umbrellas available for shade. Picturesque and so worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Getting crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was very sad to see that this magical place is starting to get crowded. The colors of the sea are unique and amazing. You can walk for many meters at the same hight.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Blue water, white sand, and You!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were here mid October 2018.If you're looking for a non-overcrowded beach with blue water and white sand, then this is the place for you.We took the 40-minute city bus to, and and from Balandra.No restaurant.  No café.  There is a tienda(camper kiosk) that sells munchies and beverages.Bring a parasol and cooler for beverages & lunches/munchies.From this beach you can actually walk (via trail or shoreline) to the infamous Mushroom Rock.Enjoy your visit to Playa Balandra!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: the whitest sand and bluest sea the best place to while away a few hoursnothing there so you need to take everything

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best if you visit by boat there are breathtaking places you can’t get by car!! We had a sailboat and the experience is just amazing you can swim with rays if you get near the shore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach! At the time of writing (January 2020) you can take the bus from the tourist bus station at the Malecon for about 150 pesos return. The bus leaves the Malecon every hour on the hour and departs the beach every hour on the :20. Beautiful spot and well worth a day. There are some small vendors selling fruit, water, etc.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a beautiful beach to play on and have a lunch on.  Sand was absolutely amazing. At low tide you can walk across the bay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: the best beach ever!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this is the most incredible beach I´ve ever seen in my life, at this place you can´t miss the mushroom, dont go on weekends it is crowded, you can go on the rest of the week and early in the morning, you will have the beach just for you, the best season is at the begining of november the water and the weather is warm :)there are no restaurants it is a virgin beach.at this place I had My ring!!!!! finally :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took a day trip from La Paz and came across Ballandra Beach. The gentle hike to the view spot was gorgeous. The beach is so pretty- although it was busy with a cruise ship group. Wear water shoes though!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun beach to explore
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even after reading about how beautiful it was, it was better than I expected. We took a 20 min Uber ride from La Paz that cost less than 200 MXN and arrived just before noon. It was a Saturday and it was fairly busy but still plenty of space to relax. There was hardly any cell phone service at the beach and no Ubers available nearby even when we did get a signal. There were taxis in the parking lot, but we managed to catch the  Playabus (which goes to/from the tourist bus terminal on the malecón) on the way home. It does come all the way into the parking lot for both drop off and pick up. 50 MXN one way. Don't forget to bring sneakers to climb up the hill and get a wonderful view. The prettier, less crowded side is over the hill or you can walk around the big rock cliff to the right end of the main beach. There were a couple vendors selling empanadas, chips, and coconuts and fruit. There were a couple port-a-potty style bathrooms in the back corner of the parking lot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Be warned
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is picturesque and idealistic. Clear waters and cool breezes. However the sand hides a lot of sand fleas. Don’t lay your towels on the sand better to use the beach umbrella and seats you can rent. If you do get bites, please get some anti itch cream. Better to get it treated before it becomes an issue later. When you get home put all you clothes in dryer and run on high for 30 minutes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great sunsets
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We are and wandered the shallows with our babe in arms.  Warm water and very safe.  Worth the short, pleasant drive out of town.  Check the tide chart before you go.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but if you’ve been to Caribbean -pass
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I couldn’t wait to go to this place because of all the rave reviews.  It was beautiful, but certainly not jaw dropping like some beaches in the Caribbean. I guess if we didn’t have to drive 2 hours from Cabo to get there it would be worth the trip.  I wouldn’t bother unless you plan to spend the full day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice out of the wind but cold wa
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a nice place not windy like Tecolote . Water cold, you can buy a coconut , there are kayaking there is a

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful beach not to be missed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The travel was long from Cabo San Lucas but all worth it.  Be careful with cows crossing as we almost got into an accident.  They have signs and believe those signs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Once Upon a Time Gem. Now more like a flea market
reviewsWithKeywords.text: the unfortunate downside of being beautiful and promoted = huge hordes of people.  Balandra is hardly enjoyable these days. And soon they will be building condos nearby.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful little piece of heaven!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a quiet and secluded beach. We felt relaxed and peaceful here.  This was part of a tour we took and we only stayed for about an hour and ate lunch.  But the water is calm and clear.  We thoroughly enjoyed this little piece of heaven.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great expanse of shallow estuary with abundant bird and fish life if you paddle far.Great sunsets then Mosquitoes!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: 14/12We three British middle aged guys were touring in BC in the first half of December. We had heard about this famous beach  and along with a Spanish friend took an Uber from our Apartment (200) all the way, taking about half an hour (some road renovations slowed us down for a bit but expect a fast road in the future (for better or worse).Arriving at about 2:30 we found quite a busy beach with stalls selling drinks and food next to the big car park. Lots of boats were anchored offshore too. There was plenty of space though and it was easy to find cool shade under the cliffs. After sorting our own drinks we took to walking across the estuary which proved very shallow at the time we were there.My Spanish friend found a puffer fish that 'blew up' when he approached it. I saw a 10 inch wide black and white skate zip past. The birds were the more interesting and visible wildlife though. Obviously there were the pelicans and herons but paddling right across to the other side of the bay I saw a couple of oystercatchers. The beaches there were completely empty next to the (set back) mangrove.On returning to my friends I went round the rocky coast looking for the sacred mushroom rock, expecting it to be a large part of the landscape. I found nothing. I must not have gone round far enough.A word of caution as the rocks are quite rough and even paddling you can scrape yourself if you tread on a rock. I am still suffering four days later with a cut little toe. Take care. The water is clear enough to navigate the rocks.The beach was remarkably clean compared to some I have visited in BC. The water was clear and free from polystyrene balls or plastic. It seems the locals and tourists do respect the area. Large bins are available in the car park, although no discernible recycling in place.Oh wandering round the rock cliffs to the right side I noticed people were still walking down the track over the hill to the adjacent bay and some had set up loud music systems which was a little annoying as it disturbed the peace and romance. The music stopped later after sunset although it was still sounding as the people left the beach.Towards dusk my Spanish friend wanted to quickly pop over to Tecolite beach the other side of the peninsula. As the sun set we found ourselves surrounded by thousands of mosquitoes! Blood was pouring out of bites and we quickly ran back as the passing bus driver laughed! It did not stop my collecting a couple of handfuls of litter strewn by the road though which I put in the big white bins in the car park before returning to my friends. It seems that the littering is a problem still where it is not enforced.On returning the sun had already set and the bay was dotted with ghostly figures in the golden and orange colours of the sky. It was all very romantic.Eventually we just had to go and rather than summoning an Uber from town half an hour away we jumped on the waiting bus, paid 50 each, at 18:15 and off it went, to Tecolote beach, the lights being turned off completely on the way so it was pitch black inside, picked up a couple of people and returned back to Balandra (lights going off again obviously to stop attracting Mosquitoes)! It then left at 18:30 promptly to get back to the Chinese Hotel Pekin by 19:30.On arriving back and looking up Dengue Fever it actually does occur in BC but in talking with locals it does not! We shall find out in a week when I am back in London!I also looked up the TA page today to see that the mushroom is not actually very big at all! I did not miss much.All in all this was a magical place and worth the excursion. We had gone relatively off peak and the car park was quite full. If it is peak time I expect it will be so busy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Shallow bay with sandbanks, feeding pelicans and other seabirds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Shallow waters make this pretty bay safe and family friendly. Its a very large bay with multiple sandbanks so you can wade out for 100m at waist height, whilst watching feeding pelicans and other seabirds and gazing at fish and crabs in clear water.  The famous mushroom rock (hongo) needs a 15 minute wade out at high tide.  The sun sets over the bay is beautiful but be prepared to run afterwards due to heavy mosquito attack.... the nature reserve has a mangrove swamp. Buses run all day till dusk for 50 pesos each way, or Uber it for 200- 250 each way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Shallow bay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Balandra is a small bay 2 minutes from Playa el Tecolote.The beach is quite busy with tourists. Beautiful turquoise waters.It is very shallow so you can walk around in water up to you knees. Not many swimming opportunities though.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach.  Nice fine sand and very shallow water that goes forever.  Very  popular however and can be busy. Definitely worth the trip though.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning clear water, beautiful color, and some protection from the N wind
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The locals nearly all got off at this beach which was more protected than the beach Tecotote? At the end of the road.  There were bathrooms an dmore options to eat at Tecotote, but the locals much prefer the longer crescent shaped Balandra.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Totally in love
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most stunning beach I have ever been- the shallow Cristal clear water and soft white sand - go early because parking is limited we had to park on the road, no bars or restaurants so bring your own food and drink- still worth it. We have put our towels under the rock but you can pay for umbrellas if you want - my pictures were not edited so what you see is what you get !!! There is a disabled access but I have no idea where does it leads to - lack of Matt on the sand, toilets are portable type and lacking disabled ones

reviewsWithKeywords.title: As beautiful a beach as I've ever seen
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great day trip from LaPaz. There is plenty to do here. Kayak rentals and food trucks make this a great place to spend the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not too far from La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This interesting beach would be great for anyone who is a non-swimmer!We even saw a woman walking her dog in here :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really awesome spot. Took an Uber up there for a few hours. The bay is really pretty, and we brought our snorkel masks and saw lots of fish on the far end of the bay. Warm waters

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastically beautiful lagoon just minutes from downtown La Paz.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The largest sandy lagoon I have ever seen, this beach remains in my memory as a paradisical spot.  It's important to go at high tide - even then the water is very shallow and you can walk almost across the bay!  You can bring a picnic but there are some refreshments available on site, and some ambulant vendors on the beach.  The straw huts are free - amazing! - and the parasols are paying. Enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Our wedding anniversary trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra, amazing beach, speechless must visit if you are in Los Cabos San Lucas must take the photo with the mushroom rock it is just beautiful. clean clear ocean waters. from San Jose del Cabo it takes approximately 2.5 hours by driving your own car. bring your drinks and food. MUST bring water shoes since the entire beach is full of rocks. leave your  personal belongings in the bus, car or bring a waterproof pouch for you phone, money, keys. you must climb the rocky mountain and enjoy the spectacular view, it is out of this world.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome Beach, but needs reliable restroom facilities
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra Beach in La Paz is an awesome beach and nobody should miss a stop here when they are visiting the Los Cabos area.  Even the drive to the beach is very scenic and enjoyable.  Parking space is limited at the beach, so go early.  Once at the beach, one should not miss the short hike up the hill to get a full view of the crescent shaped beach.  Actually, three such beaches are visible from the hill, though they are separated from each other.  Also, one can get a view of the iconic Mushroom Rock from the top of the hill, or one can get closer to the rock by hiking down to the second beach.  The water is pretty shallow and the waves are pretty calm making this is a perfect beach for families.  There several palapas, but again better to come early.  Kayaks are available for renting.  There were vendors selling some snacks, fruits and coconuts in the parking lot.  Restrooms are unreliable, if they are open at all.  This is the only drawback.  This awesome beach needs reliable restroom facilities.Balandra Beach is must-visit destination in the Los Cabos area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, worth the visit.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped here for a short visit as part of an excursion. The beach is nice and the water is very shallow and warm. A must see if you are in the area, it was a nice treat when we couldnt swim in the waters at our resort. It was quite busy with lots of people but big enough to have your own space. Parking lot was busy. There was food trucks, but did not eat anything. Would definately return for a full day, the roads seem well marked to find this area also if you are driving.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The worlds biggest swimming pool!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a really unique and cool Beach area. Balandra actually is several beaches in a Bay. The water is shallow enough to walk from one side of the bay to the other. So finding a quiet place to lay out isn't hard. There are Hills to climb to get a full view of both sides of the Bay and also serves as an amazing place to sit and watch the Sun come down. All the parking is free and public, so don't let the guys at the opening try to con you into paying for parking. I would submit pictures but apparently all my pictures are too big file sizes. Sorry!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very busy, get there early
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Arrived on a Thursday at about 1145 and the beach was already extremely busy and the parking lot full requiring you to park along the side of the road. Free palapas if you arrive early, otherwise, 400 pesos for a table, 4 chairs and Palapa. Only one food truck available, so best to bring your own cooler and snacks. There is also porta potties located at the end of the parking lot. Very calm water that allows you to walk out for some time and only be waist in. Nice beach to spend 1/2 day there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: We took the boat and the dog.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you come to LP, this is a must see. Either Balandra or Tecalote. You won't be disappointed, and the food is amazing!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, but...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very unique because it is shallow, the sand is very soft. We were there on a windy day, so the water was not the best. The "mushroom" rock has been repair and you can see metal rods in the base of the rock and some concrete patching it is not worth seeing. Also, there is nothing around this area so bring a cooler. There are some vendors in the parking lot selling fresh coconut and other stuff. The parking lot is very small so you may have to park on the side of the road.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breath taking beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The place it's just absolutely beautiful wonder of nature. I recommend to bring your own food and drinks if you think to stay for the complete day although bring a bag to get all the garbage with you! The only thing I would like to say to people is that respect for the beach it's very important I saw some graffiti on the rock and a lot of people leaving garbage after they left. This is unacceptable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice family beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach. Very calm water. Several palapas. Great way to spend a day or few hours. Can take a bus from La Paz or drive and park there. Gets crowded but still was comfortable. Nice sunsets here as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The good and bad (there’s no ugly)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a popular beach especially with locals. Go early or late if you really want a palapa, otherwise bring your own shade, because there are no trees or buildings for shade. The waves are nonexistent as the water is completely still and you can walk out 1/2 mile and still touch the bottom. There is a vendor selling cold drinks out of his truck in the parking lot if you forgot yours. It’s about a half hour drive from LaPaz to get to the beach but the road is good. Also watch for stingrays. We were told by a friend in Cabo that on average whe he was there, at least 1 person gets stung. I brought my goggles as swam around for 30 minutes and sure enough, I found one. He was only about 6” across but I touched his back with a shell and he swam a couple feet away and re-hid himself! I didn’t see any other fish than that. Anyway it’s a nice spot, there’s my thoughts, Enjoy!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This is an unbelievable beach and water experience as you witness the tide charges the bay completely changes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Arrive early to get use of one of the free Palapa’s and then enjoy the beautiful water and bay are.  When the tide goes out you can walk completely across the bay in water just above your ankles at most, or walk towards the sea and see lots of fish around you without needing snorkeling gear.  Careful though if there is no breeze as the tiny black bugs carry a mean vicious bite that lasts for 3 to 4 days.  Make sure to spray.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the long drive from Los Cabos
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So glad we booked a day trip to La Paz from Los Cabos that included a two-hour stop at Balandra Beach. Beautiful, secluded beach with smooth sand and clear water. In fact, the water was so clear we could see fish swimming by the rocks without having to use snorkeling gear. Free palapas for those who get there early, or rent an umbrella if needed. Memorable excursion and the highlight of our trip to Baja California Sur.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach, white sand and warm turquoise water, lovely little concessions offering goodies. A must see

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is a hidden gem. The water is warm and clear. They have tabels and chairs avaiable for rent. There is food trucks avaiable - no beer sold here, bring your own

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: La Paz VIP Tours brought us here after our whale shark tour, and it was GORGEOUS! Totally secluded and so stunning.  Crystal clear water.  Hidden gem.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, Lots of bugs
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very pretty. It's Protected, no surf, so great for kids. It's shallow, so you can Wade out for a LONG time. We were there only tourists here on a week day. We've read it gets really busy on the weekends. Out of a week in Mexico this was the only place I got bit by bugs.There are porta potties and one little truck to buy some snacks at. Other than that, there are no amenities. Bring your own everything.Just down the road is another beautiful beach (I think prettier) with lots of trucks, bars, etc. But it's not as protected, so there are waves that roll in (small ones while we were there). We were told to watch out for sting rays while at both beaches. We found one at Balandra, buried in the sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Playa Bus
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is a turistica bus station on the malecon where you can buy round trip tickets to balandra. Taxis will charge tourists double and uber signal doesn’t pick up that far from the city. The playa bus will take you to the parking lot (at least it did for me) but will pick you up, up the road where dudes are selling fruit and coconut water. No one told me that so I waited for the bus 3 times before I realized they weren’t coming back to the parking lot. I got bit by a red ant or some bug in the sand. I left my clothes sitting on the sand and whatever it was bit me in the back when I put my shirt back on. We sat under the shady cliff rocks so not sure if the red ants are still by the palapas or not. By 3 pm there were 2 Palapas available but by noon when I got there they were all taken. It’s $13 for the hour to rent a kayak or sup board. We got one and paddled to the mushroom rock. Be sure to hike to the top to get a good panorama. The rock trail is behind the parking lot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see, make the effort, great place for kids
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely clear water, safe place, shallow for kids for kids to play.Bring your towels, umbrella and cooler.  They do have portable toilettes and a few vendors with fruit or snacks for sale.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty Beach slightly off the beaten path
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is very clean, in spite of the crowds.  You need to "tip" in order to get an umbrella and table, which is highly recommended.  Shallow and easy to swim in so great for families--the waves are almost non existent, and you can swim or walk in pristine waters.  There are two remote beaches right across the way that you can swim to if you are reasonable fit.Once you get done here, drive further north about a mile and you will see four or five "bar huts" right on another beach.  You can enjoy cold beer and have a decent lunch here before you head back to town.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Make the effort, and visit this place!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were staying in CSL, but had a car, so we drove the newer highway up to La Paz, and then around it to Balandra Beach (Google maps is worthless when you try to find it, they try to point you into the center of the city for some reason.  Search for "Playa Balandra" to get the correct map).We went there on a Monday, and it was surprisingly busy, but not terrible.  They have a good parking lot, and there are Port-A-Johns on the back end of the lot (but either bring your own TP, or pay the ladies at the table next to them.  Also, they seem to lock them up around 6, so if you gotta go, you better go before dinner!)The good snorkeling was around the "mushroom" and the rocky areas in that vicinity.  Lots of fish there.  Bring a camera!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hidden gem! Take your own towels, cooler, snacks.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved loved this beach!  Reminds us of Isla Mujeres crystal clear water.  Super shallow all around so very safe for kids.  We stayed in Cabo, but so worth the drive.  We only stayed about 3 hours, I wish we would have been better prepared to stay longer.  This beach was voted best beach in Mexico by my favorite YouTuber (Alan x el Mundo).  So I was delighted when we ran across one of the food vendors from his video.  Will upload pic—you gotta try her ratoncitos!  Bring lots of small change pesos for the food vendors.  My son got stung by a bee— maybe pack some bug repellent and Benadryl.  We also drive after into the town of La Paz— it was so charming!  But the beach here was heaven on Earth!  Go!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a beautiful beach. It’s all very shallow, so at some points you can almost walk the entirety of the cover and get to the other adjacent beaches. There was even an ice cream cart that was making rounds in the water. I took an Uber there and back from the Malecon, just bear in mind you may have to keep an eye out, because Ubers are only available if the driver is less than 15mins away at another beach or at Balandra dropping someone off. There is also a Playa Bus that does the rounds around the beaches and comes approximately every 30mins. You can rent an Umbrella for the day, and there are some built in Umbrellas for free, but come in early, or else you will be without one. It is not recommended to be under the sun without an Umbrella — it is VERY hot. There are vendors that offer food service. Bring cash with you and please tip them!! They are offering a service in weather unfit to work in, for your pleasure, so don’t be cheap. Pesos to USD or Euros are more than substantial. Would definitely recommend. Great for kids. For sure bring plenty of water and sunscreen.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove the 2+ hours from Cabo San Lucas to visit the Balandra beach and had a great time.  It is like a huge swimming pool.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth going
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So convenient to grab a bus to this pretty unique place.  I went early so was lucky enough to snag a little palapa.  It got very crowded later, even on a weekday.  If you go solo remember to take a waterproof pouch for your valuables since you can spend a long time walking across the bay.  Water shoes are nice to take also.  I will go back when in La Paz.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you love the beach and clear turquoise water, this is the place to go. A popular spot for locals to take their families on days off. It feels like a hidden gem of peaceful tranquility. You can walk for hours in chest deep water. If you desire an umbrella, be early for the permanent palapas or rent one. There are washrooms, donation for paper required, so take your own if you don’t want to pay. Look for food vendors on the beach wearing black aprons. They will take your order, call it in and have it delivered directly to you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Calming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach.  Water is very calm with nice color.  You could walk out very far and still only chest high.  It was not terribly busy but I think cause of the time of the year.  There are vendors there but they were not a bother like resort beach areas.  You can see alot of marine life up around the rock areas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Warm water even in th dead of winter
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This playa has more than just cozy water the landscape is beautiful and you can walk through the water to almost every corner of the bay.  A pod of orcas visited just last May.  Sometimes there is a snack van but play it safe and BYO

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The place is really amazing. If you are a person who is into panoramic  views this is a most in your list. It is perfect for all kind of people, kids friendly and since the water level is to low it's  great also for people who doesn't  know how  to swim. The prosBeach is very chill place.Low level water and warm.There's  2 more beaches infront if you need some more privacy or a less crowded beach and one on the side which has  the iconic mushroom looking rock in La Paz.  You can get there by kayak, boat, swimming or paddle board. There's  also a walking trail if you want to go hiking around and see the beaches from top where you can get cool views day and night.You can rent a shadow with table and seats. You can also rent kayak and paddle board. Theres also free shadows if you get there in time. The Cons: No toilets nearby.Gets too crowded so best times is to go pretty early and stay there until all people starts to arrive. Sometimes water tide is too low. Parking can be hard. Not many bins around. It is a nice place to be for a few hours and then maybe spend some  time in other beaches around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach 🏝
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. Lots of locals. Rent a car and drive yourself. There is a snack van and plenty of parking. The drive is easy and uneventful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pros: Amazing beach. Calm, turquoise water. Water level is up to your waistline for over a mile. Sugar fine sand. Con: Limited parking so be there early in the morning. Prepare to pay 10 MXN pesos to use the restroom. No restaurant close by so don't look for one. Bring your own food and drinks as you can't rely the quality of the food that's being sold in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No words, surrounded by mountains, calm!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My recommendation, go early, in the middle of the week and you’ll enjoy it more! Remember to take some food and drinks with you, there is a small parking lot, have some tennis shoes and or water shoes either to climb the small rock and reach the iconic ”Mushroom” or to go walking in the water to also reach this landmark.Have a good camera, enjoy the sunset if you stay long enough...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice peaceful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a great time. We loved the fact that our kids could play in the beach like if it were a giant (long) pool most was less than 3 feet deep. Snacks available to buy and if you forgot supplies, sunscreen, inflatables, sandals, swimwear, snacks etc there was a mobile truck that would sell supplies. I saw a waiter offering services couldn't figure out were they had the restaurant.  There is shades and chairs but many people took their own and their ice chest with food. Kayaking for rent was fun, bummed that they ask for an ID and my husband forgot to get it back and now had to get a new driver's licence.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Totally Unique
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A truly unique beach with splendid views of the surrounding bare hillsides serves as a majestic backdrop of waters of sapphire.must be on your bucket list. for more beautiful travel destinations follow me on Instagram:@baughbrian

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was amazingly beautiful, pictures can't do it justice. The water was clear and refreshing, the beach was incredibly clean. As an American I find it horrible how little respect we give to each other and natural beauty. The day we visited, the bulk of the beachgoer's were locals. Everyone picked up their waste, taking it home with them. I saw no garbage cans, especially overflowing ones like I see here at parks and Galveston. Everything was stunningly clean. Visitors were polite, considerate to others and we'll behaved. Dogs are allowed and owners apparently quickly clean up behind them.Kayaks are available for rental. Some thatched umbrellas are available to those arriving early. Many brought their own beach umbrellas as it became crowded. I advised planning to arrive between 10:30 and 11 to ensure parking at the free paved lot. We left around 2 and cars were parked along the road at least a 1/4 mile from the beach. As we loaded our car newcomers stood by to claim the parking spot by walking into it as we backed out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very crystal clear water but it was very crowded.  We went last Thursday mid day.  No place to park if we had a car.  We took an Uber there with no issue but coming back was hard. We had to find a taxi and squish several people into the cab. Overall it was a good experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach close to La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best beach close to La Paz!  That’s what most anyone will tell you, and it’s true. There is a lot to do here, but don’t expect a ton of stores and restaurants, because you won’t find them here. The area is well protected, but there are walking sales people, and food and drinks can be purchased at one of the trailers. Kayak rentals are also available. Essentially, this beach is a super clear shallow bay That is about a mile and a half long by a mile across. It almost never goes over your waist line. The water is warm, the sand is white, and it is absolutely beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Try the "ratones de queso"!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a beautiful beach! Try the local treats like the ratones de queso (like a mini cheese cake) at the beach. Warning, do not get very deep on the water because you may get 'bited' by tiny parts of the agua malas, stay on the shore... such a nice place

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra is crowded!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Haven’t been here for almost 10 years when we used to have the beach to ourselves. It was crowded, but still very beautiful and clean!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to watch the sunset on a Monday evening. It’s was still very busy. Beautiful views and blue waters. Just a shame some visitors left litter and played loud music

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most amazing and beautiful beaches in Mexico
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walk across a lagoon beach in the aqua waters for 30 minutes to reach the other side. It a bit a a drive yet... well worth the trip to an amazing secret location. Locals know of this special place and now we do to. Pictures don’t do it justice. Pack a lunch, and water proof bags for the phone so you can walk in waist deep water for hours.Make sure you get your pictures in front of the mushroom shaped rock.The sunset is incredible if you choose to stay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Turquoise waters, swimmable beach, clear and clean.I’ve got no negative remarks. Absolutely beautiful!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Glistening Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra's natural features made this beach one of my favorite stops while in La Paz. The water was crystal clear. I didn't need snorkeling gear to see various small sea creatures swim past my legs. The water's temperature and depth were perfect, Lastly, it was clean and not crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: go early in the day so you can use one of the palapas for shade.  Beautiful, crystalline waters!!  inflatable kayaks are usually available to rent from the beach.  Take your own water and food.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: nice beach but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a great beach to visit but there were other beaches that were also as beautiful but were less crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to this beach with some friends that live in Cabo. Amazing place the water is beautiful and you can walk very far out in the water. Many families enjoy the day there. One Great place I have ever visited. Worth the trip from Cabo, good highway to drive to get there, will definitely return.Hongo De Balandra is a great place for pictures and you walk through the water to see it. Amazing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Still a Wonderful, Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I first visited Balandra Beach about 20 years ago and it certainly has changed, but then what hasn’t in that time. The water is amazing and most of the changes were for the better. Get there early and get a palapa or a shady spot near the rock overhangs. Wish we could have spent the day like we did 20 years ago. Don’t miss this place!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach - please keep it clean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is an amazing place to visit. If you go, try to pickup at least 5 pieces of trash. The sea, the animals and our planet will be thankful that some visitors mitigate the harm made by other who came before.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: saw the mexican movie called camino a marte its just like the movie
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this place is beautiful almost as if you were in a different planet more specifically mars, if you saw the mexican movie camino a marte you will rapidly recogniza this beautiful place

reviewsWithKeywords.title: so beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: another beautiful beach from baja but this is  a very special one, there no waves just you and the desert

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Water you can walk in safely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is amazing to see a beach where you can walk for about a mile in most directions without needing to swim.  The water is beautiful and picturesque.  If you hike the surrounding cliff, you'll get a beautiful overlook of the waters leading to the ocean.  The waters look like a malachite stone in color.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Mexico
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach for kids,  beautiful sightseeing. No bathrooms or services, still you can rent some tables and chairs..  there are some palapas to be used by free, but those get busy early.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Place! Most Go.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful and unique please, must arrive early on weekend if you want a 'palapa' (sunshade). The restrooms are not fancy, just basic. This place is well maintained.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique crystal clear water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We arrived in the morning and were able to park in the lot.  It gets quite busy later and you have to park on the narrow road in.  Great opportunities to hike around the hills with beautiful views of the bay.  Also, you can walk around the whole bay along the beach.  The water is quite shallow so you can walk out as far as you'd like.  There are restrooms and a stand to buy some food, but no other facilities

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing and Beautiful!!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s now one of the best beaches I’ve ever been to! U have to see it! We stayed in Cabo and booked a city tour to La Paz which included a two hour stop at Balandra beach! Definitely one of the best choices we made. It’s a 2hr drive to and from but tour guide fills it with great stops at towns and markets, with lunch included! Of course Balandra our highlight!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was seriously one of the most beautiful beaches I've had the pleasure to visit. It doesn't look like much from the distance but it's really quite lovely. The water is Crystal clear with a beautiful blue hue. The water is not too deep making it great for those who want to enjoy the water but can't swim. You can actually see where you're walking because the water is so clear. The beach had nice soft sand and some nice rocky areas that are quite scenic. The parking area fills up quick so you may want to go early or take a bus if possible. There are bathrooms but they are like outhouses so prepare for that.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach for kids. Shallow water to almost no water at low tide. This beach use to be one if the best in the world. It had now been overrun with visitors and tour busses. Parking can be a real challenge.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: As Advertised.  GO! plus the beaches along the way are amazing.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go here as well and you might as well stop at the beaches along the way.  SO amazing.  We went on a sunday and it was busy.  I bet a week day you could have it to yourself.  The next beach over has bars and jet ski rentals etc.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A hidden jewel ..!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the top 10 most beautiful beaches in the world. Clean, safe, quiet and some reefs to do some snorkelling..!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing place, the color of the water is unique
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is really nice, plus the view from the surrounding hills is really worth the short climb (<5mn). The beach is small and the number of free umbrellas is limited, so you should get there early (before 9am).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra beach really is beautiful, u like anything I had ever seen. The color of the water against the rock formations and mountains are so beautiful. The only downside would have to be the stingrays. There are a lot her please be careful! My son got stung by one and we had to leave In a hurry to get him to a doctor. Those stings are no fun, and extremely painful. Seeing all those children in there made me so worried sick. Drag your feet make noise that should help to get them out of your way, we learned that too late.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Beach is one of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra Beach is one of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico.It is very shallow so it is very safe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most unusual, amazing and picturesque beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: About 20mins NE of La Paz, Baja Sur you will find a piece of heaven.  This white sand beach in an incredibly shallow triple bay has warm water, gentle currents and enables you to wade 100's of yard out and along the bay.  The very gentle swells cause little undulations in the water depth resulting in alternating hues of blue.  Take a walk up the stony path to the top of the hill next to the beach for amazing views of the triple bay , the Sea of Cortez, and the mountains beyond.  Make sure you look behind you for a view of the lagoon in green march among the desert. Quite a contrast.  No facilities but usually a food truck on site.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise for little ones
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a beautiful beach!!! Little ones will love the shallow waters and the soft white sand. Unfortunately there are no services at this beach, so no toilets. However there is a small van selling food and other essentials. Parking is free, but limited.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Incredible view, sand and water! Go early and try to stay to the far left. And climb the mountain to see on the the best views you can find!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, very shallow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed sitting beneath permanent mushroom umbrellas (get there early if you want one), walking the beach and wading in the water.  Not many fish for snorkeling, but a good place to practice for young kids.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the most beautiful beach in La Paz and Mexico, here is a place so quiet, with white sand beaches and turquoise transparent waters, it is surrounded by the exotic desert providing this an expectacular view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Incredible
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Is a quiet place, beautiful clear water and amazing views, if you are planning to go book with Baja Desconocida, wonderful service and profesionalism.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice sandy beach, gradual water depth from shore, nice swimming.  Beautiful scenery and the color of the water is that turquoise you just won't ever forget.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice place to chill
