reviewsWithKeywords.text: Peaceful and relaxing. Take a short hike up to get a better view. It is breathtaking plus a UNESCO site. There is some sun shade provided or you can purchase. We went to another side of the beach and just hung out for a bit. Note: stingrays in the area so make sure you shuffle your feet in the sand and you will be fine.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great hike, snorkeling and beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Enjoyed the 3 mile hike around the beaches with incredible views, and the miles of white sand beaches, good snorkeling around the reefs. We stayed away from the main beach other than at the start and end of each day here. Shallow waters for miles.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: WOW!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful, unique and unspoiled beaches I have ever visited. So happy it has been untouched by many of the mega resorts that have ruined many other beaches in Mexico. It is worth a trip to La Paz just to see this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not to be missed. Check the tide table and go when it's falling so you can wade out to the mouth of the bay. Worth the drive up there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: WOW! Don't tell anyone about this place!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were told by several that the drive from Cabo to Playa Balandra was 1 1/2 hours.  We found even without much traffic it was 2 1/2 hours one way.  We rented a car and stopped at Todos Santos to see Hotel California and at La Paz to see the local festival setting up and to get some delicious sandwiches from a cute little coffee shop to take to the beach.  This is definitely a whole day trip.  Was is the highlight of our trip? Absolutely, without a doubt!  The water is more clear than at any beach I've ever been to.  The day we were there you could walk all the way across to the other side and the water would barely be over waist high.  There were quite a few cars there, but not crowded at all.  It almost seemed like we had the whole place to ourselves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach with liw water level to walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a especial beach where you can walk in low water crisraline turqouise waters.When you arrive tgere is a beach beside the parking lot but you keep walking around by the mountain and you can find a lot of spots to stop and use the montain side to give you shade. Taje water shoes to walk on rhat greats waters up to your waist more or less and sone food and drinks to nake a pucnic ir buy some fruits over ther and rent a chairs and un umbrella for your day. ENJOY IT

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Shallow beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You can't really swim here, or snorkel.  Thigh high water.  But beautiful, and peaceful before the tour buses show up (9am).  Good place to get sun, or kyack.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: a nice family or couple day destination
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has low tide at bout 4:30 in the winter. Its great walk nice and shallow during low tide you can walk right up to the rock. wonderful destination; vendors always on beach renting sun shades, artisian crafts and coconuts. Get a coco preparado...yummmy.This place is picturesque, Its where I have seen people fly drones, pretend they are models posing for photos, and the cutest toddlers having a great time (on the very large sand spit at low tide). we usually spend the day taking snacks etc.At high tide you need to swim to the valadra. the beach is a big "c" shape. as soon as the sun is ready to set get your but outta there the mosquitos ravishly attack! They are not out before sunset so you can enjoy your day.Everyone is better at respecting the beaches so please respect the environment and take your stuff with you. only downfall is busy so parking lot is large, just take your time...after all your already there!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is maybe one of the most beautiful beaches I've ever been to. It was windy and a bit chilly in La Paz so we assumed we wouldn't want to spend long at the beach but we got there and it was gorgeous. Hot, sunny, no wind - the perfect beach day!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Rated the best beach in Mexico
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach lived up to the hype. Definitely a beautiful beach especially when traveling with little ones. This beach is truly breathtaking and is a must when traveling to La Paz. Calm water, knee high depth, and warm.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow, just wow!  Must see.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing place.  We went at low tide and were able to walk across the bay to the beaches on the other side.  Water was clear turquoise, warm and shallow.  Sand was creamy white.We spent 5 hours there.  Had a spot in the shade next to the cliffs and walked around those whole bay.There are toilets in the parking lot area.Bring your own food and water.You can catch a bus here from the bus terminal on the Malecon in La Paz (Eco Baja Tours).  Costs $100 Pesos and takes 40 minutes.  One bus goes back and forth all day, with the last one being at sunset.An Uber from the centre of La Paz to here quoted $200 Pesos, so $400 Pesos return.  Drive takes 20 minutes.Also saw cyclists along the road.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand and more sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was a beautiful beach, you can walk for a long ways before it’s deep. There are some public palapa’s to use. Beware the lady just sitting under the public palapa, she will charge you to use one of her umbrellas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun in yhe sun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent an afternoon. Very enjoyable with food available in the parking lot and walk to see mushroom rock.  Very unique.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth a morning or afternoon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. If you're adventurous, wear hiking shoes and climb over hill to private beach (looking at beach from ocean , youre headed left.) If not, throw down towel & enjoy beach, sand and ocean views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Incredible beach to bring young kids very safe no waves.  Definitely bring your own snacks and water and clean up after yourself. The water is very shallow and a beautiful light aqua there are two parts to the beach which you can explore walking on the water.  We went in February and it was warm enough for swimming and lounging. Please bring Biodegradable sun screen.  Protect these beautiful natural areas, be a traveler not a tourist.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went here with the hubby on a Monday afternoon. There were trinkets, snacks, and drinks for sale (non-alcoholic). We walked across the small bay to our own private beach were the hubs snorkeled around some rocks with excellent results. I walked around in the shallows and saw several types of fish. If you want food drive the extra kilometer to Tecolote Beach and have delish lunch right on the beach under an umbrella.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is an amazing beach away from tour areas of La Paz.  We took an Uber to the beach and arranged a pickup time later in the day.  We hiked, walked the lagoon, and relaxed in the sun.  It was perfect.  The water was too cold to swim (visited in February) but perfect to cool off if you got too warm in the sun.  Just walking in the lagoon you can see fish, starfish, shells, and beautiful birds.  This should be a 'must do' if you are in the area.  There is a parking lot, restrooms and food trucks so even though it is remote, there are amenities.  There are also palapas but I recommend bringing your own umbrella so you can be more selective where you want to relax on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A small piece of Paradise on Earth
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are in la Paz and you did not visit this beach you did not go to la Paz!!!Balandra is a clean, isolated from the city (only 25 min or less), gorgeous beach that has clear waters and a beautiful natural sea made mushroom shaped rock that has been there for 100 years or more (a picture spot definitely).The water depth is so nice that you can walk for miles and miles and water will still be at your hip or knee level (depending on your height).Take a cooler down there with your beers and gatorades, one umbrella, and you should be set to enjoy an excellent day at a gorgeous beach!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hard to park but beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went on a Sunday which seems to be a big day for Mexican families. Very hard to park so be careful and don't go all the way up if you see a bunch of cars. The road is very narrow. But the beach was beautiful, the water was nice, and it was better than expected. I should also say that the bathrooms were very reasonable and clean

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A nice place to spend the day if you have a car.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is beach is very clean and there are palapas at no charge.  Vendors are very polite and there are not many of them.  Great place for kids as the whole bay is no more than mid thigh deep.  Mostly ankle deep.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved Balandra. We took an Uber there from our hotel in La Paz and spent the day there. There is a shuttle you can take but we wanted to get there early in the morning (before the shuttle started running for the day). There are basic toilets. There was a couple keeping them clean between each use so make sure you bring money to tip them. The snorkelling was great as was the hiking. The water was pretty chilly when we were there so you may want to pack a rash guard shirt to help keep you warm.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Want to be there now!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited on our lunch stop on our whale shark excursion.  Pulled in, anchored the boat and enjoyed lunch, sitting on the sand.Simply Breath-taking, shallow, no one but the 8 of us there . . .the water and sand were like coves in the Caribbean.You can drive about 1/2 an hour north of the CostaBaja resort area, park in and walk, as well. It's a beach frequented by locals, so it can get crowded on holidays and weekends, we were told.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in La Paz!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went out to Balandra Beach after swimming with the whale sharks and sea lions, the beach is majestic! Super soft white sandy beaches and plenty of fish to see while snorkeling. It is perfect for paddleboarding too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Even though we visited on the weekend, there was plenty of room on the beach. The sea was out so as there is only a gentle gradient paddling was the order of the day. Apart from someone flying a drone and a couple of others swilling beer and listening to AC/DC it was free of most annoyances.Sand is soft and the beach is free from litter.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beaches!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Head to Balandra bay for a breathtaking day on the sea of Cortez! It’s a family friendly beach with the most beautiful clear waters and sandy shores! Away from the hustle and bustle of the resorts, you’ll find serenity while you take in some sun! If you’re looking for a bit more activity....Kayaking, whale and sea tours are available too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk for miles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice sand and clear water. The waves are very small. The water depth is perfect for children or people that walk to walk into the water and not worry about a drop off. The beach area is very big ....no food or thing like that when we visted but there was someone renting paddle boats . I also undersatnd you can take a bus to the beach for 70 pesco return but i did not use it ...so check it out ..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pristine beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We arrived at Balandra beach by kayak and were able to enjoy an almost private beach away from parking area. Fine white sand, clear turquoise water to gaze at while eating lunch. It is possible to walk across bay at low tide.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Photo op!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely beautiful setting. Walk across the bay for privacy on the other side! When the tide is out, you can get “walk on water” pics!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breath Taking Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches on the planet. Almost no amenities, but worth it. Just to stare and wonder at the beauty of Baja. The last time we were there, some vendors were there and we had to pay for a shaded spot. But this is a must see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Nice but Crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went on a weekend and the place was packed. There are palapas to rent but most people brought their own shade. Crowds aren't our thing so we wandered in the shallow waters (the tide was out) for a half hour before leaving. Very picturesque and I'd be happy to spend more time here when there are fewer people.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach near La Paz.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is magical. When the tide is out you can walk a long way out  to the mushroom rocks. The water is a spectacular shade of aqua. It’s a must see sea!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was perfect! We were able to walk a little ways from the the parking lot and it felt like we had the place to our selves. The water is shallow a long ways out so it was great for strolling in water up to your hips and louging around in the ocean

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This is one of the most beautiful beachs in the baja!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you have the chance, this place is a must! Balandra beach is amazing! From cabo san lucas it is about a 2 hour drive, you can even spend the night at a hotel in town. The water is very calm and cristal clear! Perfect for kids to swim or learn on there own.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Girls trip to La Paz- beach day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We came here on a Sunday and although there were quite a few people it wasn’t overcrowded and we were able to find a peaceful spot. We got some fresh coconuts before heading to our spot. You’re able to walk out through the water across the majority of the bay as it’s only 2-3 feet deep which makes for some great photo opportunities. The weather was great only downside was the abundance of flies that liked to harass us. Would definitely go back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach but at low tide it is gone!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra beach is a really nice beach. you arrive early to get a Palapa but beware that at low tide the beach disappears.  That can be good if you want to walk around the rocks to see the sites on the other side but if you want to swim! We were told there is no food there, so we brought a lunch and a few beers however there was a small restaurant.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Rented a car for the day and drove up to Balandra, commute was roughly a half hour. Parked right in the very front of the parking lot closest to the beach. Grabbed a spot under one of the palapas. Wandered over the rocks and around to the other beach and walked to the mushroom rock which was a bit of work during high tide, recommended water shoes if possible but we made it with no trouble. Went back over to our spot under the palapa and sun bathed for an hour or so. Around 11am or so it started to finally get busy. I decided to rent a kayak and we ended up buying 2 cups of fresh fruit from one of the vendors and kayaked over to the other beach directly to the south. It was great, we had our own private beach enjoyed our fruit and sunbathed some more. Ended up walking up and down both ends of our beach looking for shells and marine life. Found some beautiful fish, crabs, pelicans and even a anemone. Ended up staying a total of five hours or so. If you wanna avoid the crowds highly recommend driving up early and seeing everything you’d like to. Besides the kayaks they do have umbrellas and chairs available for rent and even paddle boards. We were there early enough that we experienced both high and low tide. During the low tide there were dozens of sand bars and I even walked out about 150 yards or so and water was barely up to my shins. Water is some of the clearest I’ve ever seen. Absolutely a must visit if you’re ever in La Paz. Will definitely be coming back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful natural pool
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a unique beach. Awesome colors, nice sand. Be careful with the jellyfish and rocks but only in specific areas. Perfect for children and families.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Part of a tour
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went to beautiful Balandra Beach with MeXplore Tours.  Great time.  Started the tour with the whale sharks and had lunch on the beach.  A place to go see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hidden paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is just amazing. We arrived in the morning after a quick visit to El Tecolote, it was about 9:30 so finding a place to park wasn’t an issue. We started to walk along the beach and just jumped into the water and we were amazed with the amount of sea life around the rocks! We walked around the rocks for quite a long time just amazed and grateful with the small things Mother Earth provides us. You can lay in the beach, you can walk on the bay from one beach to the other and see sea life or you can even hike the mountains and take some great photos of this amazing place. There’s kayaks and SUP boards to rent and some people selling refreshments and some snacks. Definitely a place not to be missed if you are in La Paz.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: shallow, clear water, soft sand. great place for kids to play and swim. we had a picnic and the kids found lots of fish skeletons and cool things!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow.... 360 degree beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach ranks one of the top ten that I've ever been to.  There is something unique about being surrounded in this large 'cove', 'bay', or whatever we should call it.  The tide comes in/out and it can be like being in a swimming pool.  White sand, totally clear, turquoise water, wow.  My kids were in heaven because it was shallow, safe and they were always looking for interesting critters or shells on the white sand - easy to spot something that stood out.  Family even saw an octopus - but I missed it.  Cannot recommend this spot highly enough.  No facilities so beware and treat it respectfully.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beauitiful but Popular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An amazing natural land and seascape. I'd recommend coming ready to hike a little and perhaps wade a bit and you can get away from the crowds and maybe have a couple hundred yards of pristine beach to yourself. Hike up to get the birds eye view from the top of the central hill above the parking lots. Bathrooms were not open when I was there so that can be an disgusting issue in the desert where the landscape is so delicate and toilet paper doesn't decay anywhere as fast as in other wetter places. Pack it out people!! A kayak guide told me that years ago when he was a kid in La Paz there used to be many sea turtles in Balandra Bay but now they hardly ever appear there because of all the people. Leave them alone if you see them and maybe one day they'll come back in abundance. Look at the tide charts and time your visit to include a high tide. Our visit was almost all low and outgoing tide so we didn't get the full aqua blue water effect but still beautiful and very wade-able.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Get there Early
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a very unique place.  The last 10 minutes of drive is very beautiful.  We got there early and grabbed shade under a palapa.  It did not take long for the crowds to come.  It was a week before Christmas so we expected it to be busy.Very sad to see people using the sand/beach near the rocks as a toilet.  I was totally grossed out by this and will not go back.  There are now toilettes in the parking lot, but I'm afraid some people still decide to take a crap wherever they want.  So if you want to stay away from seeing this maybe go in the water, and back to your beach towel.  Do not hike around the corner to the other beach, you might see a surprise.There are also a couple of less busy beaches on the way out there that may be worth a visit.  Obviously not as nice, but there is food and drink there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not worth a trip from Cabo
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were in search of diversity and authentic, less commercialized beaches and that’s exactly what we got, and didn’t like it.It’s crowded, garbage everywhere on the beach, but the water itself is fun for walking, shallow and unspoiled.Not worth a 2+ hour trip from Cabo, sorry.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: awesome but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pichlingee Beach much better and has two oceanside bars......!!! Families welcome ! great drinks and service. Awesome sunset!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: love it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: top 10 beaches in the world!!! u must come n visit !!!! u can rent umbrellas n chairs there if u wish , bring your own water !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Peaceful wade in clear waters!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra beach (really it is three coves of gorgeous white sand beaches) is a wonderful way to spend the afternoon. It is about a 30 minute drive outside of La Paz with good roads. The beaches have no amenities (such as washrooms). There is one vendor with kayak rentals and a t-shirt vendor. Many Mexican families come to spend the day and bring their picnics, chairs and blankets. The water is very shallow and one can easily walk into each of the coves. Pretty fish to see. I recommend wearing water shoes in case you come across a ray in the sand. Come prepared with your water, snacks, sunscreen and towels to spend a glorious day. No entrance fee.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beachVery good point of viewIdeal for child because not dangerous at allNot easy to park car because many people

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Its probably the best spot in Baja
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Honestly, beach is simply awesome. Water is warm, quiet and so pure. The cool visit could be in week days (early in the morning) because is very popular. Parking for free. Eco-friendly bathroom. No showers but is fine. Palapas (eco-umbrellas) are for free: first come, first serve. Also you can ask for some lunch in restaurantes near there. Is a perfect spot to spend a day and even a Night of camping (for free). So, paradise exist. Is here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love it. The best vista is the south part of the beach with a view of the mountains and the beach. Get a coco for 60 pesos, enjoy the white sand. Climb to the top of the hill for the best view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach even with holiday crowds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Family oriented beach with minimal services available. Take the bus from the malecon for a few dollars or rent a car. Parking was limited on the Christmas holiday we visited. Had a great experience with the bus. There were vendors offering service from a restaurant 1 km away but may only happen on busy days. Clear beautiful water with a family oriented vibe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Please arrive early so you can enjoy the beach without the crowd. Take goggles and a snorkel because fish are beautiful in there, and prepare to spend hours of il dolce far niente. Amazing place with cristaline water, no waves, nd you can walk a mile with the cold water up to your waist line. Few beaches this beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful beach surrounded by rock and cactus. Our hotel ran a shuttle to the beach which was about 30 min away. There are shaded palapas however they were all taken when we got there. Henry was renting umbrellas, table and chairs if you want. A couple of stalls selling cold drinks and juices. No food. Few people selling tourist items to purchase. There were a couple of portable washrooms.  The tide changes dramatically and reveals many sandbars. You can walk and walk and walk and walk and still be maybe your knees.  Lots of people had small dogs that were loving it. We stayed for a couple of hours and then walked over to the tolocote beach about 30-40 min walk away with restaurants on the beach.  A great place to spend the day. Be sure to bring sunscreen in case you can’t get an umbrella

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a great beach, especially if you have little kids (which we don't). Its really shallow and has "3 lagoons". You can actually walk across to the other side to several other beaches as well, its nice and shallow. But if you want to go for a swim you can definitely wade out into deeper waters too. We did some stand up paddle boarding too. There are kayaks and paddle boards for rent there. We went there 3 times/days. Overall a great beach and very photogenic one too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most incredible beach I’ve ever visited
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful shallow beach where you can wade for hundreds of yards in any direction! Clear, clean water that feels great. If you’re in La Paz, you HAVE to come here.I do have some suggestions on how to make sure you get the best experience. Think of this beach as more of a park than a tourist attraction—there aren’t many amenities. So, you should:•Bring a cooler with plenty of beverages. If you bring alcohol, you might also pack some drinks high in electrolytes like gatorade to stay hydrated.•Use a bathroom before.•Pack your basic beach needs: sunscreen, sunglasses, towels, etc.•Buy some cheap lawn/beach chairs to sit in. If you rented a car to tour the area, these can come in handy at other beaches as well! You can give them away before you go back home.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunningly beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must see when visiting la Paz. The water is crystal clear and warm.  You can wade comfortably for several hundred yards.  Recommend hiking the trails above.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Bay!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous turquoise bay facing the Sea of Cortes.  The water is shallow with sandy bottom so you can literally walk across to the other side.  I walked across bare foot but there are some stinging sting rays under sand,  so would use Aqua Socks next time. Take the Aguila bus from La Paz for $100pp/round trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely all day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was picture perfect and super warm. Even with a few people there it did not seem crowded. A great way to spend two or three hours.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: its a magnificent white beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Dont stay on the first beach, there are three! Summon up a little effort and walk/swim around to the third bay and you might have your very own paradise!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow ! So pretty here just go see it! Everywhere you look here it’s gorgeous! We loved it so much we went back the next day!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous- just wish there were more services
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful here, but you need to be prepared for no bathroom and no bar or restaurant.  The water is calm as a bathtub. Lots of interesting birds to see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, mediocre snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is the busiest beach we visited while in Baja Sur. The main beach was a little crowded, so we waded around the rock point to the second beach and had a great time sunning and swimming. The only good snorkeling we found was on the rocks near the mushroom rock. There's lots of sandy and shallow water, which is fun to pay in though, and our kids enjoyed that. And frankly, since this is such a draw for people, it meant other beaches (with better snorkeling) were relatively empty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Favorite beache
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This places is so beautiful, it’s my favorite beach of baja! I love spending all day at this beach and the color of the water is beautiful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tour stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our tour group spent an hour here. The water is amazing...super calm and you can walk to the other side since the water was so shallow.  There are people here selling snacks and renting out equipment and chairs and umbrellas. Would have rated this beach a 5 except the outhouse style bathrooms were locked up with padlocks ☹️.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were lucky enough to make it out here several times during out visit to La Paz and is always worth the trip!  It is a beautiful spot!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful waters
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Extremely beautifully clear water . Great place to spend the day.. We packed a cooler and spent the entire day

reviewsWithKeywords.title: AMAZING
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We rented a car and drove to balandra , very easy and fast from La Paz. No need to tell you how, just follow signs . Amazing scenery , you’ll see mangroves .... cactus forest and amazing beaches on the way there.  There is a truck that sells a bit of everything , so if you are one of those who doesn’t like to carry anything around , you’ll be able to buy at least something to drink and a floating device (lol). They have restrooms on site. Before you get to the parking you’ll see a trail going up to the top of the hill that seats right Above balandra.  You’ll get amazing views of the entire bay ( recommended ). Go earlier in the day , ties change during the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love this beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was here at low tide and was able to walk out to the mushroom rock but take water shoes or sandals incase the water is higher. What an amazing sight!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful shallow bays with white sand beaches - a must see if in the area!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The public beach has parking and porta potties, incredible views, warm shallow waters, white sand and was very clean when we were there on a Saturday. Plenty of space to spread out too. Other beaches in the area can be reached only by boat and are also spectacular. Take a photo with Mushroom Rock!.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clearest water I've ever seen.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is pretty amazing totally chill, guys selling hats and food kids playing nobody acting stupid the clearest calmest water I've ever seen white sand, slight drive to get to but no big deal. I'd give it  5 stars but at the end of the day it still just a beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach that paints itself!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must while visiting La Paz. The bays are full of colors and life. The parking lot leads to one of the bays that most of the people go to. I would recommend going over the small hill and go to the other bay. Bring snorkel gear, umbrella and environmentally safe sunscreen. They have a small snack shop and a guy with coconuts for sale. You can rent a umbrella on the beach for 200 pesos for the day. This bay has a lot of people were you can rent kayaks or walk 500 plus feet in waste high water depending on the tide. If you want a view from above to see both bays, you can go up a small hill that will lead you to a path that leads you to the point. You can see this path from the parking lot. Enjoy!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach for kids, a few vendors with umbrellas, etc. Make sure your trip does not coincide with a ferry departure - took us more than 1hr from La Paz due to ferry traffic. Our toddler loved the water, but I have never seen so many wasps in one place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Looks like small lake
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Driving from las Cabos to la Paz is scenic and interesting drive on mostly well-paved divided Hwy. The malecon walk and drive thru the centro area are the main attractions of the town. The Balandra Beach is not worth spending time to drive. Contrary to our expectation that the beach would be right on the ocean, rather it s enclosed on three sides with little mountains and an inlet for sea water from the fourth side. Nothing extraordinary of its being with shallow water and smooth off-white sands. A couple of food trucks are there to sell snacks, cold drinks and fresh coconuts slit open for sweet water. For a day trip to la Paz it is not worth going to Balandra, rather enjoy the town and plenty of restaurants on the Malecon.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I have ever seen. A true gem with clear and calm waters and beautiful hikes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lots of people and lot of moise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful but full of algae. There is a lot of people and a lot of noise and music. The parking is just next to the beach which is very ugly. You can climb the mountains and walk all the beach across.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ranked as one of the top beaches in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The water is crystal clear and you can walk around the cove as the water is chest high at the deepest point. There are 2 coves to explore. Kayak & SUP boards available to rent. I would bring a float, sunscreen, a small cooler, and sun umbrella. Uber is available and very reasonable may cost you only $8-$10 one way from La paz. Do not miss this beach! It is a very memorable lifetime experience of breathtaking beauty & fun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice way to spend the day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are visiting, you can rent an umbrella, chair and get food and drink at the beach. Of course, you can always bring your own. Not much for snorkeling, but it is a relaxing spot to soak up some sand. There is a public bathroom there as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect spot for lunch on the sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As part of our tour with VIP tours, Captain Eddy and guide Katrin prepared a great lunch on the beach.  We'l come back on our own as it is an easy drive from La Paz.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: We arrived late so it was not as busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We decided to head to Balandra after visiting La Ventana and the area (actually we did a big loop from El Triunfo, up to La Ventana and then to Balandra Beach which was a nice way to spend a day). There were still a lot of people at the beach and in the water which looked as if it was quite shallow for quite a ways out. We arrived for the sunset so that was about 630pm. What I didn't get to see because I arrived so late, was the beautiful blue of the water. It looks incredible. Lots of parking at this time and the sunset was pretty. I think I'd come back again during the day to experience it more.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a wonderful beach about 20 mins drive from La Paz. We got there around 10 am and found it to be quite and easy to park. Contrary to other reviews the is a refreshment truck selling drinks and snacks, and also toilet facilities ( just think of a massive litter box for people, and you’ll get the idea. Go in, do your business, and cover it with the sand provided!!!!😬😬😬). During the coarse of the morning, the proverbial beach vendors arrive in droves to sell their wares, rather annoying, unless you’re in dia need of a flotation devise or beach attire.  SUP and kayaks can be rented for about $18 an hour. We found this particularly useful as it was high tide , and access to the mushroom would have been impossible without it.The beach itself is fairly clean, although it’s obvious that there are some people that camp there , and maybe don’t pick up after themselves as much as they could.Another issue is that there were many dogs there with their owners........ they are not able to use the human litter box, rather they just go in the sand. Not so nice if your digging in it, and come across a big dog turd!!On the whole, this is a must if you’re in the area.  Check for tidal updates........

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Quite and beautiful!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As we were driving....we came across this beautiful beach! When we arrived, there was only 2 other couples there. Later in the day it got busier. We came in the mid morning and then stopped to have lunch down the road to another great find!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best beach in La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We (2 adults and an 11 year old) spent an afternoon at this beach. This one is in my opinion the best 'family' beach. Warm clean waters, shallow beach, and white soft sand.  What more can you ask for!And if that isn't enough at low tide you can walk along the shoreline to the famous El Hongo 'mushroom' rock, or hike to it (over a hill).Bring food & beverages and a parasol as it can get really hot early to late afternoon.Take the bus there, it's only a 25-30 minute ride and relatively inexpensive.Cheers :o)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely preferred this beach hands down over Tecolote beach! Palapas are free to the public. Get there early and stay all day! Bring lunch, water, snacks in a cooler because no restaurants around. Beach is super clean, water is pristine and you can walk out prettty far and still be touching the ground and the water is refreshing. You can also rent kayaks and paddle boards there if you want.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must while in La paz or cabo.A 2:30 hour drive from cabo this is truly one of the most beautiful beaches on earth.Peaceful and clean.Highly recommend to BOB since there is no restaurants or stores.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I really liked Balandra Beach its really nice and the water is very warm. Please help keep this area clean when going. Note: this location does not have restrooms or changing area, since its a protected area by the government.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing bay! The water is crystal clear, cactuses all around the hills. If you rent a car you should take a visit even if your hotel is in San Jose Del Cabo like ours.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise!!! Exists
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must when visiting La Paz or Los Cabos.Nice, beautiful, clean.A real jewel.Take care of our planet and be conscious.Keep it clean.Nice people and attention.A must...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach at La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was our favorite beach. Very nice and peaceful. The level of the water would barely go over your knees. Depending on the day, there could be almost no waves which makes it perfect for kids or people who are afraid of waves. Important to know: there are a few free Palapas, that are nice and can offer you the shade you need to survive the sun. However you need to arrive early if you want to get one of these!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The perfect beach at the perfect location. We went during the week and it was not packed. I can see on the weekends the place being full but we were lucky to get one of the palapas and enjoyed a lovely day in this piece of paradise. A must when visiting La Paz

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good beach near La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although it’s a little bit overrated, as you need to walk more than 100 meters to get the water pass your knees, is a nice and safe beach to go with little ones.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Peaceful relaxation!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This quiet beach is absolutely gorgeous!  Shallow turquoise water await to refresh and soothe you.  The contrast against the white sand and arid backdrop is stunning!  Not much in terms of activity... which is part of the charm!  You CAN rent some kayaks and there is one snack-bar (no tables) at the entrance but Balandra is best enjoyed with your own cooler.  No need to taxi if staying in La Paz:  bus terminal has regular buses for 100 pesos per person (return - 45 min drive along the coast). We went on the 1:30pm bus to miss the hottest part of the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overhyped
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We made the trip from Cabo to Balandra with much anticipation. Positives? Great coconut stand and soft sand. If you have kids it allows for wading without too much worry. Negatives? We found the beach a little smelly with dark weeds on parts of the sandy shoreline which was not attractive at all! Compared to beaches in the Virgin and Cayman Islands and Jamaica, Balandra leaves a lot to be desired.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful blue water !!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful place with a nice blue water,  but when we went,  the tour man told us it was the first time in his life that the place was crazy crowded, so we didn’t enjoy the please . It was impossible to get to the “ mushroom spot” because it was too many people , but when we went to the the Espíritu  Santo island , we passed by on the boat and I took some pictures .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: stroll in the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra was spectacular, its the first I strolled in the beach..water was so clean & clear and you can walk from the shore and across walking..although the the end acroos is a deep cavity that you can’t see the bottom so be careful...water was warm & perfect for non swimmers...so family oriented..there are no abnoxious vendors to harrass you..they are regulated and they stay where there suppose to... you can rent umbrella beach for 180 mexican pesos

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach and area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Easy to find, good parking area, very clean, shallow water, great to take children and pet. No restaurants in the area, BYO food and drinks or go to Tecolote next to it for lunch

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach ever !!!’
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I’ve been to most of the best beaches all over the world and Balandra Beach is right there in the top.It is the most beautiful place,many different coves that all face different directions.Each one more amazing than the last.Kayaks are available for rent and you can paddle around the whole area which is huge or you can walk through the thigh deep water to some.The water is crystal clear with white sand beaches. I never wanted to leave ever,but you know how that goes.I was in La Paz for the whole month of July and spent much time at Balandra. If you love beaches like I do then this is a can’t miss!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Beach and Clean Water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is amazing!You can swim in clean waters, I recommend you to use snorkel equipment.If you arrive on morning you have the beach only for you. You can also do Kyak and aquatic sports in this beach.Greetings from Portugal

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach with warm tranquil waters!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra Beach is a beautiful retreat about 2 hours from Los Cabos.  It is worth a day trip!  The water is crystal clear and very warm.  It is a lagoon so there are no waves or rip currents.There are some local vendors with fresh fruit, beverages, shaved ice and souvenirs.  You can rent chairs, sun umbrellas and kayaks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular and safe swimming beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great place for kids, very shallow waters. A must see attraction if you can't surf, but want to relax in the water. You can wade hundreds of meters out to sea, and a few vendors had delicious mangos on a stick.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great but avoid the Sunday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: White sands, turquoise water, good palapa and also a place to rent umbrellas and buy something Everything you need to enjoy a great beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Top 5 beach in Mex
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not to miss when visiting La Paz. 30 minutes by car. Sandy White beaches, great for snorkeling. Suggestion take an umbrella and chairs and cooler with food and drinks. Don't miss this place

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful (and crowded)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is gorgeous, but if you happen to be there during the weekend be ready to share the beauty with many many other people. We got there a little before noon and the beach was already pretty packed, but more people kept arriving steadily all afternoon. If you're not carrying to many things can always go for a swim or climb to cross the rock barrier that separates the crowded beach from it's private secluded twin (but the walk or swim can be a little tricky). We ended up paying for a parasol and a couple of chairs and finding a nice little spot on the right side of the beach next to the rocks).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great for kids bur crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Certainly not what it used to be, does not live up to the hype anymore. Still a very nice beach in the early hours before it becomes super crowded. Perfect spot for kids, safe shallow crystal clear waters. No restroom or other services. Get there early and grab a free family shade or get in late and rent a tiny umbrella shade for 300-400mxn pesos. Bring your drinks and food and lots of sun protection.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Vacayion
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My cousins and I came to Playa Balandra from Cabo San Lucas. Unfortunately, we came on a Sunday and it was packed, no area to put our stuff, visitors with loud DJ speakers. We decided to go to Playa Tecolote.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: nice small beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: we went here as part of the boat tour with the cortez club so they dropped us here while the divers went out.  it's a pretty little spot with crystal clear water and a nice beach.they have a mushroom rock to look at and you can snorkel there as well.it was empty in the morning but when we came back in the afternoon it had filled up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Meh
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not as cool as it used to be. Bit dirty nowadays. Super crowded. I rather visit other beaches. Small parking lot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowed in July
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I read all the wonderful reviews and was so hyped to take my teen son there. Got there on a Tuesday about 1PM and was so disappointed. Car lot was full and people were parked along both sides of a one lane unpaved road leading up to entrance so our van guide couldn't drive in. I was determined to at lease take my son to see it, so we left the rest of the family in the van to walk down there. My dad couldn't make the walk. We got to the beach and it was so crowded. Families had staked out every possible area to lay a towel. There were a handful of vendors with mangos, drinks etc. My son and I walked into the water, noticed a couple of small fish, the mushroom rock and left. Our driver took us to Tecolote Beach. A much better beach. I'll do my review for this one too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved this beach, it was very busy when we went. Bring lots of water and snacks, and an umbrella for shade.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach and Vibe
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have spent several days at Balandra so far this trip, and it is our favorite hangout in La Paz. Heartily recommended.We have been riding the public bus from the terminal on the Malecon (just across from the two story waterfront pavillion) near the whale museum. Ecobaja counter sells tickets...100 pesos roundtrip.The trip follows the coast through desert north of town and takes about 40 minutes, depending on locals getting on and off at various stops. First bus (the one you want to catch to avoid the crowds) is at 10 AM. Returns roughly every two hours, with last one early evening.The early bus drops you at the public parking area by the beach, but because the road fills up, it picks you up several hundred meters up the road. Make sure you clarify with driver where pickup is!There are two beach areas. The main beach where 90% of the people go has vendors and blue portable rental umbrellas (200 pesos per day-ish). About 99% of visitors we have run into are locals or from other parts of Mexico.  That may just be the season...not sure.The best beach, though, is "around the corner" to the right when facing water, and requires either walking in shallow water around a point to see the cove, or a climb up and over the rocks to reachit. This beach is gorgeous and calm, and has only a fraction of the visitor load of the main beach area. This is also the area with the "mushroom rock". We have only gone to the more secluded beach, and avoided the booming crowd that seems to gather each day at the main beach.Note: There are no bathrooms at either beach. Also, please, please, PLEASE pack out your trash.  We take an extra bag to carry out any trash we find...which hasn't been much, but is heartbreaking to see.Despite temperatures of over 100 F each day we have been there, the water has been siper clear, cool and refreshing, and there have been very few (if any) biting insects. Wear reef walkers and/or shuffle your feet in water to avoid stingrays. Lots of small fish, some larger ones cruising through, all sand bottom and very shallow lagoon. The whole bay / cove has truly incredible colors of different aquamarine shades with the water right up to sand dunes with a desert backdrop and red / brown cliffs.Really, Balandra is one of our very favorite beaches ever, right up with any we have visited in the Agean islands in Greece,  Crete, Thailand, Bali, other parts of Mexico and the Caribbean. It is a special, lovely spot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Beach Spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came here on the city bus from la Paz. Earliest bus is at 10am 100 pesos rt then it runs every 2 hours coming back.  Beautiful and quiet when you get there early. There are palapas on the beach for shade. If they are all taken people don’t mind sharing. You spend most of your time in the water anyways. Bring a snorkel and mask and you can see some fish by the rocks.  Don’t forget your sunscreen and waterproof bag for your camera.  Water shoes are needed if you want to go on the rocks to take pics of the mushroom rock.  Enjoy the unspoiled area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It is a fascinating place - very shallow water for the whole bay, sand bottom
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is an extraordinary place unprecedented in my experience.  The whole huge bay it set in the midst of desert hills about a half-hour drive from La Paz. There are no bathrooms or restaurants at the beach, just a few food trucks. Its a locals family beach. The whole bay is less than chest deep, no kidding, and you can walk hundreds of yards off the beach and still be mostly dry. It's beautiful, but it is a hang out, no waves, place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Warning about theft from this beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stopped at this beach for a quick swim. Left a camera and some cash in the trunk of the rental car. Returned a short time later and the car was still locked and seemingly undisturbed. Discovered cash missing when i got my wallet - no credit cards were taken. They went through my wife's purse and very carefully took some small amounts of cash, went through all our bags and took a couple of other small items (Kindle) then looked uip and took off. Granted we're an easy mark and made the mistake of leaving stuff in the car but it was a just a quick dipso didn't fuss with the usual security. This is clearly a very organized theft so just use this as a reminder.Otherwise, an okay beach but nice water - like a giant ocean swimming pool.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking! A must visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Highlight of our trip to la Paz. Water has great visibility and super shallow. We could see the little fish swim around and could walk half way across the beach with the water until our waist. Most beautiful sunset of our lives!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This is a great preserve
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This location is well worth a stop. It is a part of the natural preserve. It is very pretty and a clean area. On the day we visited, it was a bit cloudy and we got a break from the heat of the sun. This area has no staff members to help with questions and answers.  There were several boats anchored in the area.  Most of them had smaller boats to get to the beaches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Remote beach worth the drive!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with pure white sand and shallow water. There are no facilities so pack a cooler, sunscreen, beach umbrella and snacks for a fun day. Bring your favorite floats to soak up the sun or snorkel. Approximately 3 hour drive each way from Cabo San Lucas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This one is clean and looks like a pool. My favorite from the area. Make sure you were swimming shoes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Visitor
reviewsWithKeywords.text: All a good experience. The favorite locals beach they say. We were given chairs to sit on the beach. Good place for children.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our friends and we like to leave our "stuff" on the beach and walk out a little into the water and plant our umbrellas and chairs. It's fun sitting in the water. If you go out further, you need to shuffle your feet so the little rays know you're coming their way so they have time to get out of the way. Not difficult and its a great view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach period.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I can honestly say this is the nicest beach I have ever been to, the sand is so nice and soft, the water is so clear It feels like a big pool, awesome place to visit!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great place to relax, but a bit crowded sometimes. You can easily walk across the bay if the crowds get too much. Not much snorkeling. Great views from the hill overlooking the bay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow! I thought it was so beautiful here. Shallow, warm water that is perfectly still. I could have swam around all day. It was part of a tour so only had an hour. If you like swimming and the beach it is a must go while in La Paz.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is  an amazing beach young children and adults love this beach. About 2 miles of walking inside the warm water which never reach above our shoulders. Crystal clear water. Just beautiful. We adore this place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is absolutely gorgeous. Traveling with small children we have to be mindful of the waves and the water was absolutely perfect for our toddler here. It was something out of a postcard! We tried going the first time but didn’t arrive until 11 and the palapa were all taken so next time we arrived at 10 am and snagged one. Only thing to note: SAND FLEAS! Bring bug spray. I was eaten alive!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: AMAZING!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We thoroughly enjoyed this beach, only a short trip from La Paz.  Kayaked in the mangroves and walked through the crystal clear, warm waters.  You don’t need a mask and snorkle to see an array of sea life.  Next time we’d take a cooler with cerveza and maybe a few snacks since the beach hasn’t been commercialized at all.  Totally unique beach experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day excursion
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We rented a car from Cabo to head this way, it was well worth the drive. The beaches are white, warm waters and crystal clear you can walk for miles in waste high water. Bring you own food and drinks as the cart is very expensive since it’s unpopulated. You can rent paddles boards or kayaks. This is the sea of Cortez side which is very different than the pacific. The drive was safe and fairly easy directions wise. A must adventure and you can stop at other places along the way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Aqua Agua: Wade in Clear Shallow Water Among the Schools
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beautiful beach was full of surprises. Maybe because I didn't do my homework, went on a whim and had no idea what to expect. Many wouldn't drive 2 hours out of Cabo San Lucas (the tourist area) and come to a beach they only heard from a local "was beautiful and you can wade out as far as you can imagine and see fish and stingrays!" Well, that was enough for me to visit this amazing aqua reserve and I was pleasantly surprised. Perhaps I was a bit nervous on the ride up as we rented a car to get there and braved the foreign roads on our own. Certain things to note that you don't see in the US are military vehicles with large guns and men in military garb commonly driving by on the roads. They are common in the area, however, and most likely looking out for the safety of tourists.We drove through a few "deserted" desert areas, some random desert homes, and eventually ended up in La Paz. (It is pretty much a straight shot on the freeway so you will not get lost.) La Paz was built up and rather quaint. It was the traditional beach town, complete with statues, a harbor, restaurants, markets, and most helpful was an information booth, which provided free brochures. (Balandra is about 45 minutes outside of La Paz.) We took the brochure and were off.This Sea of Cortez treasure was like nothing I had ever experienced. I have been in some amazing locations and a few beaches stick out such as a tiny beach on the Caribbean Island of Carriacou which also had some shallow beaches, but they were not tucked away and protected such as this. They also were not shallow nearly as far out as Balandra Beach.It was an extreme delight to not even need snorkeling gear. The water was so clear you can see schools of assorted fish left and right (obviously be careful not to get too close to the stingray.)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you visit La Paz, Balandra beach is a must.  Its a very safe beach, and you can walk inside the sea more that 100 yards. The scenario is amazing combining the dessert and the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful place!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go as early as possible! One time we went by car around sunrise and it was so magical. There was no one there, climbed up the little mountain for a perfect view and enjoyed it so much. If you go early you are sure you have a beach umbrella to project yourself against the sun. Another time we took the bus from Malecon (100 peson return), it was way more crowded on the beach but still wonderful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hidden Gem!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is one of my favorite beaches to visit in La Paz BCS. It is located about 25min drive from La Paz. The beach offers turquoise blue clear waters that are amazing to walk and swim into.  You can walk hundreds of feet into the ocean and will not sink in, 3-4ft deep. It's a Giant Natural swimming pool, perfect for Kids! I was a little skeptical to get in the water due to we were warned by locals to watch for stingrays, I recommend shuffle your feet in the sand.  But really no Stingrays to be seen. There are vendors that rent kayaks and paddle boards. We had an amazing day enjoying the beach, waters, and taking all the vitamin D from the sun. My recommendation is to stop by an Oxxo and buy a cooler and drinks to go, you may also take snacks. Lots of sunscreen needed or get there early to get a Palapa, about 15 of them available for public use at no charge. Parking is also available at no charge. If by the time you leave and feel hungry, just drive about 7minutes to El Tecolote Beach and they have variety of beach front restaurants. Balandra is a must visit!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came here and it was amazing, crystal clear waters and light blue colors. there was just some garbage around which was disappointing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The most gorgeous beach ever!!! You can walk and walk and the cristal clear water doesn't go higher than you're waist. It has beautiful white sandy beaches and it's an adventure to get to the famous rock!! Worth the climb through the rocks!!!One of my favorite places to go!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches in Mexico
reviewsWithKeywords.text: 2nd time in this beach and it is just very amazing. Last time there was no people, but this time, although it was crowded, we enjoyed very much.Worth going there even if you are in Cabo.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is an absolutely amazing place. It is so peaceful and serene. It is the absolutely perfect place to spend a day. It's great for small children to play and enjoy the water safely. My 16 month old was able to wade in the water without fear of waves or rip tides. It was a little less than knee deep when we went, but I hear it can get as deep as waist high. It is a bit of a drive and in the middle of nowhere, but that just adds to its appeal. It is the perfect place for kayaking, canoeing, or paddleboarding. The day we were there it was 104 degrees outside, but there was a nice breeze and it only felt to be in the 80s (I was incredibly surprised when I saw the actual temperture). It has parking and a decent amount of palapas for shade, but there are no other amenties; no food or bathrooms. There was a truck vendor selling miscellaneous items, but you should take any food or water you want to consume. We went midweek and there were a decent amount of people there. I would expect it to be very busy on the weekend as it is such a great place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice, quiet and scenic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is one of the beaches I never saw before due to the good quality of water and the scenic landscaping.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely beautiful location just 30 minutes from La Paz. In May the water is still a little chilly, but warm enough to snorkel or play... floating in the rafts was too cold.  If you take snorkeling equipment, walk around the point towards the right, walk across that new beach to the next point. This is where the mushroom rock is. Get in the water there then keep heading that direction down the coast. You’ll see a good variety of fish, including puffers if you are paying attention. Also some anemones, soft corals, urchins, etc.  it was impressing for shore based snorkeling

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking Balandra Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: During our 7-day trip to Cabo, we opted to be courageous and drive to see the famous Balandra Beach in La Paz, Mexico. The approximately 2-5 to 3 hour drive was fun. Parking was a breeze and it wasn't packed since most folks were either in school or at work. The water was at least knee height throughout the entire day just as we were told it would be. Area is very safe and there are no issues in the parking lot or in the actual bathing area. We would definitely come back with friends and family as well as a bit better prepared with gear. Balandra Beach was very clean as well. Great place for couples as well as family and friends.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of my favourite Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is by far one of my favourite beach in Mexico! It can be crowded but you can always find a spot to be on your own. It's just like paradise!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Heaven on Earth
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My friend and I spent a couple days in Baja California Sur México and got a chance to take a road trip from Cabo San Lucas to La Paz BCS is around 2hrs away, we had been told about Balandra Beach, saw a couple of pictures online and decided to go, OMG!! What a beautiful place, so if you're in BCS México tristemente me it's worth the trip!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Time at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Everyone should take the time to visit this beach.Beautiful stunning color and very shallow to walk in.Nice short drive from Hyatt Place where we stayed 20 minutes.There are no washrooms at this beach which was the only negative. Plenty of parking and there was a good amount of visitors which made the beach feel more safe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were able to rent SUP and cruise around the whole area. It was beautiful beach with clear blue water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, nice scenery but not for swimming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra Beach is a lovely beach about 30min out of La Paz.The sand is nice and there are shelters around the beach but get there early if you want one.The water is warm and reasonablely clear but you can walk out a couple of hundred metres and still only be knee deep, so not for swimming.Around the point is Mushroom Rock which is a nice 10min walk either along the sand and across the rocks at the point or in the water a lower tide.There's a vendor there that sells mangoes but not much else so bring drinks and any food you want for your stay.To get there Ecobajatours, at the Malecon terminal, have regular buses that cost 100 Pesos for the return trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have never seen a beach like this. The water is crystal clear and you can walk out so far and the water wont go past your waist. Get there early if you want an umbrella/palapas. There are about 20 of them and they get taken fast. Other than that there is no shade. We encountered some rude people who would not share there palapa even though there were just 2 of them and were in the water the whole time. But besides that bring a ton of sunscreen and have fun. There is no restrooms so your on your own. They do have a little vendor and they come around and you can order ceviche or fresh fruit which is really nice. Definitely worth the visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Breath taking beach, get there early to get a shade umbrella, we arrived around 10:30 on a tuesday.  Remember bug spray as the sand flies bite a lot in the shade.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing and secluded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent two days here just relaxing. A few quiet, quaint, accessible beach used by tourists and locals alike.  It's not much for swimming or waves - excellent for wading, SUP/sea kayak and just enjoying the beautiful, peaceful setting. No services.. you can go to the next beach (about a 5 minute drive) if you need food and restrooms.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not to miss but arrive early
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is not to miss if you are in La Paz. It’s not far and really great. But it gets crowded quite quickly, which can change the experience. Arrive early. And don’t forget to climb on the top of the small mountain next to the beach you will be rewarded by a breath taking view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There are several bays and you can walk in the sea from one beach to the other. Shallow and transparent water. Lots of fishes. No services on the beach, but still it is wonderful. Must see place! You can rent a car, go by taxi or by bus from Malecon. Buses just pass every 1.5 hour.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beauty beyond belief
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra beach was my favorite beach we visited! We drove 2.5 hours from Los Cabos to go there thanks to the locals we spoke with at our resort. They all recommended Balandra for its beauty and the shallow, beautiful waters. Balandra has beautiful white sand (in complete contrast to Los Cabos’ pebbly sand beaches). The sand was like sugar. Very fine and soft. The water was placid and very shallow for several hundred feet. We could let the kids roam and explore without fear of waves or drop offs in the water. We rented a paddle board for $16/hour and tried that out. Was the PERFECT place to learn / self- teach paddle boarding! The water, due to the depth, was warm and inviting unlike the other areas of the Sea of Cortez which were still quite cold!! As other posts have mentioned, there is little shade at Balandra. There are now approximately 10-12 palapas to escape the sun under. There are also overhangs from the cliffs where we found shade along with the very friendly locals. There are now a few vendors who sell food out of the back of their truck. A man was asking the locals if they wanted ceviche (he seemed like a delivery guy) but he didn’t ask us. If my Spanish were better, we would have enjoyed ceviche on the beach.... We did however, enjoy empanadas on the beach from Doce Cuarenta, a hip coffee and sandwich shop in La Paz.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Calm, serene and beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was lovely. The water was crystal clear and still as can be. We went to the section that you can only reach by boat, and it was very secluded which made for an incredibly peaceful experience. I recommend checking it out!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Bay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Crowded when we visited over Easter weekend.  This is a beautiful beach!!  I wish it hadn’t been so busy when we visited but this is a place to hang out for the day.  Water is clear with lots of marine life.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a very beautiful beach just outside of La Paz. Totally worth the drive. Pack your own snacks...no services.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Picture Perfect!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent several hours here with 6 adults and 6 children (ages 8-5 months). We brought our inflatable paddle boards and spent the day on our own private spot. Fun in the sun, snorkeling, and loving life.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach on the continent
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love Balandra Beach.  My brothers and I frequent La Paz and always spend a day or two swimming around Balandra.  If you can handle the trek, keep walking to the last beach in the bay.  The water is clearer, and the fish are more plentiful.  For a real good swim, go from Balandra to Tecolote.  The swim between the two has even better snorkeling and larger fish.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see, clearest water ever!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go early in the day as it can get quite busy. Take a beach umbrella with you, there are some shade palapas but you might not get one.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hideaway beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really cool semi-hidden beach.  The water is pretty shallow, especially when the tide is out, so you can walk pretty far out in the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bad timing on our part
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Samana Santa is a huge celebration here in the Baja sur.  Everyone goes to the beach with family.  Not just this beach, all beaches were packed.  We got all the way there from San Jose del Cabo (2hr+ drive) and couldn’t even get to the beach it was so busy.  Definitely bad timing for us.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful treasure
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is beautiful. We were luck enough to visit when it wasn’t too crowded . The second time we went there was not parking so we left and stopped by a beach closer to La Paz but no were near as nice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too Hot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Balandra Beach in the middle of the day. It is just as pictured - shallow water, nice beach, beautiful. BUT be forwarned: there are no toilets, no wind, no waves, no shells for beachcombers, & if you aren't lucky enough to snag a spot under an umbrella, it is just too hot. So we relocated to Telecote Beach: food, toilets, wind, waves & plenty of shells. Balandra would be fun for families with toddlers, but not for us.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's all true
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Previous posters have summed it up quite well... Playa Balandra is a beautiful place.  The various hues of blue water against a backdrop of desert mountains is stunning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach ideal for families. You can walk forever and before the water level reaches your waist. Calm water, beautiful  beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is gorgeous. The water is so clear and shallow. We went in few feet and the water won’t go above our waste. Just make sure you bring your own food/drinks/snacks since they don’t sell anything there. Great place to relax and enjoy the view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Get there early!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a gorgeous beach. I am sure by previous posts it has already been said. We got there by 9:30 and was one of three cars. We left at 1:00 and it was packed. Several vendors for a Thurs. We rented SUP for an hour. 250 pesos an hour. Go. Enjoy. Relax!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pristine and lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably the nicest beach in La Paz! Go early as the crowds are minimal and the basin is filled with water. At low tide the basin practically empties out and you're left with wet sand. Located a 30 minute drive from the La Paz Malecon it can be challenging to get to but taxi cabs take will you out there for approximately 300 Pesos ($15) which isn't bad considering the distance. However, there are public buses (at Obregon and Cinco de Mayo) that run approximately every hour for less than 100 Pesos. There are no public services at the beach such as changing rooms or restrooms so put your suit on ahead of time and bring your own TP if you think you'll need it. Bring lots of sunscreen and a hat if you have one!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Swimmable, beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I travel to Cabo at least once a year, and Balandra iso ne of our favorite spots. We rent a car and drive up from our hotel. It is a swimmable beach, which if you've been to the Cab area you know that is rare.  The water is beautiful, warm and calm.  IT gets busy, so get there early if you want to claim some shade. There are always a few vendors there for snacks, drinks and necessities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Beach is beautiful, the major problem that I found is the lack of available parking lot and that there’s no restrooms available; so you should guess your options available when you gotta go... hope the authorities solve this issue because this is a great place to visit in La Paz.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just beautifuk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach.  Get there early for shade.  Walk to the mushroom walk and enjoy a serene beach.  Shallow, but sparkling blue.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Watch out for the bus timetable - they do their own thing. We had to hitch back. No cafe/bar - take everything you need - it’s a must see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just unique
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s really like two crescent shaped bays connected to each other. You have to walk or wade to the right side to get to the iconic, mushroom shaped rock formation. At high tide we could walk across the bay at about waist depth, at very low tide it was about to knee depth.  Out past the iconic rock where it gets deeper you can actually swim. If you wade or swim around the outcropping of rocks beyond the iconic rock there is another, even nicer beach. We took the local bus from La Paz, which was very easy and took about 40 minutes but was a scenic ride for 100 pesos round trip. The bus also goes to Técoloté about 5 minutes away (the bus stops at Balandra coming and going).Note that there is a parking lot next to the beach (behind the row of palapa) and garbage cans, but no other facilities, i.e., no restrooms and no vendors.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Completely worth the drive
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was completely blown away.  Our trip to Cabo is complete with our day excursion at LaPaz.  Balandra Beach is simply amazing.  We can't wait to come back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Really amazing beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is such a pretty spot.  You can easily get away from the "crowds",  we went on a Sunday, the busiest day of the week and it was still very peaceful.  Safe, gorgeous, unspoiled, clean.  You can take a short hike up a hill to get an amazing view.  You can wade (it is very shallow) across the bay to a private beach. There is decent free parking (no restroom though)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A peaceful place to spend time walking between the different beaches across from each other and next to each other. There’s a total of 7 white sand beaches. No one bothers you. You need to take your own picnic

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It was worth the travel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We red the reviews from Trip Advisor and decided to drive out there.  It was worth the drive.  It was not your regular beach.  One side was black rocky mountains and other side was super fine sand.  Water was really shallow and light blue.  You have to walk for a while to actually get to deeper area to be able to swim.  There was free parking very close to the beach.  Many palapas for people to use.  We went even further and found a secluded are to sit.  Mountain looked like it was an inactive volcano.  There were caves at the bottom where people were sitting  there to hide from the sun.  We were there till 4 pm.  We returned thinking water may be returning soon.  We didn't want to get trapped in the area we were in.  THERE ARE NO BATHROOMS.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach only 15 to 20 min drive from la Paz baja, also very shallow waters.only minor problem there aren't public bathrooms but you can drive 5 mim arond the corner to coyote beach and there is a seafood restaurant bar.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach but no beach bar or restaurant facilities
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A lovely beach but Tecolote is the better beach a few minutes away. Good for kayaking and snorkelling but it was cool in February when we visited. Water was warm but ambient temp was off-putting.  Just one man’s opinion.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach you’ve never heard of
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you surf, there are no waves. Beautiful white sand shallow cove. Mangroves at the top of the cove. Natural tunnels in the rock structure. Palapas open to the public.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique. Awesome.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Rustic and no facilities. But so fantastic. Sheltered from wind. Shallow crystal clear water. Shells for kids. Snorkel for adults. Palapa for shade. A view I will not soon forget!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra Beach is beautiful and remote, but it was very crowded on a Saturday afternoon. There is a fairly big expanse of sand along very shallow water, so it would be great for families with small children. There are several palapa-style umbrellas, but I imagine they are claimed fairly early in the day. There are many sandbars, so it is fun to walk way out in the water and only be up to your ankles. You may want to wear water shoes so you can explore the rock formations and tide pools at low tide. No bathrooms or other facilities.
