There were a couple of pick-up trucks in the parking area selling fresh fruit, but no other food or beverages. It is in a very quiet cove, so you are facing rocks not the open sea. Worth a visit, but I didn't think it was quite worth the hype.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Natural pool exciting view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Do no miss it ! It is the only beach to check out in the area. 25 min north from La Paz doen town, you can park your car on a small public parking and access the beach, take your shoes off here you are in. Just connect mother nature and enjoy the feeling, and the panoramic view

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Shallow tidal lagoon
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Awesome place to visit. Went at low tide, when you can walk for at least 300-400 feet and the water is just waist deep. Great place to take kids and specially those who love to see crabs and fish. The sunset from the hilltop is breathtaking. Besides some nice shades there are no other facilities here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!,,
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You need a car or take a tour, but this place is gorgeous. There are no services - bring your own water and snacks. Good place to let the kids go in the water because it is so shallow

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must, jus be careful to take all your beach gear and food/water if you are planning to stay the day. It is a virgin beach area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing stretch of beach with enormous area of shallow water to enjoy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good, clean beach that stretches for ever surrounding a huge lagoon-like area of shallow sea.  Excellent for relaxing or paddle-boarding

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A large perfect beach in a protected cove. About 20 palapas lined up on the beach (no charge). Very shallow water but we were able to use a kayak. OK snorkeling around the rocks on the other side of the cove. A bit cool in February but still swimable. It's about a 25 minute drive from downtown La  Paz. There's also a city bus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice virgin beach. It's like a giant pool, not deep at all.Calm water.I think it could have some ecofriendly infrastructure, it´s the only thing missing to have an excellente place

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very pretty little bay, fairly clean too! Easy place to wade in the water. Had some fun helping a little fish build his house!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most amazing beach I've ever visited
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I am not a beach person. I feel the need to preface this review with that statement, because I did not want to leave Balandra Beach the day we visited. It is truly one of the most beautiful places I have ever been.The enormous bay is only waist deep for hundreds of meters, and the pristine waters and sand just enhance every aspect of the place. I would return in a heartbeat.The beach isn't overrun with vendors like many other popular beaches in Mexico, and the distance from La Paz seems to keep crowds down. We were there on a Saturday in February, and while finding shade was tough, the place was not so crowded that it was overwhelming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, not crowded and much cleaner than the private resort beach! Easy short drive from town

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool Place, Better on a Sunny Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: La Paz is a very industrial port city but some of the beaches are interesting because the water is clear, very shallow and walkable.  It was fun to take a hike in this area that has sand dunes and some great places for pictures.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beatiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a great time there, this beach has a lot of people on weekends, it is beautiful ant there is the famous stone fungus, a symbol of la Paz

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Belongings Stolen
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful area however we went out for one hour and our camera and phone were stolen. It was super busy and we hid them in our car... I know i know... I'm in Mexico... don't leave stuff in the car but I can't exactly take everything with me out... Saddest part is all the memories /photos gone. Lesson learned. So beautiful and a must see but go looking poor and leave NOTHING behind. That way you will enjoy and not have the bad experience we had.Adios

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Day Trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: While driving the Baja we stopped in to check out this beach. It was nice and sheltered as this was a windy day. Great for a little kayak adventure.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I love this place! Incredible views and great place to spend a great day! Bring your own umbrella also water and things to eat because there no place to buy things!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beach trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: best beach in bajashallow warm un busywould def recommend to visitabout 45 mins by buslots of other great beachs near by

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely beautiful!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was absolutely beautiful and different from any beach I’ve ever seen. We stopped by to have some lunch after our day or snorkeling with whale sharks and sea lions. Watch out for things that may have washed ashore, my boyfriend stepped on a dead porcupine fish and the spikes punctured his foot. We were lucky enough to spot a shark very close to the beach. We had just climbed back into the boat and started to take off when I saw something, the captain even got his phone out to record because he said sharks never come into the beach there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Easy access to an amazing beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have visited this beach a few times and love it for its tranquil blue waters and white sand. Great for relaxing, bird watching, snorkeling and swimming. Its just a short drive from La Paz.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing day at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very beautiful public beach where you can enjoy the water and views (climbing up the rocks).Kayaking is also nice - although the water in winter is still quite cold.Unfortunately day tours pass by the beach so it has become quite touristic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach for walking if too cold to swim. There were a few areas that provided shade, so nice spot for a picnic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and easy fun
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Bring a picnic and shade. No bathrooms. It was nice to not have any vendors hovering around. We did not encounter stingrays. We got to experience a relaxing and more secluded time near the rock formation in the first half of our day. When we returned to the beach closer to parking, we enjoyed the party crowd with live music even! It felt like two different places but in good way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Largest Swimming Pool in the Wrold
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We recently revisted Balandra Bay after a twenty year absence.  Its beauty continues to take your breath away.  Its depth is only mid-calf, extending for probably a half-mile plus from shore.  We were informed it is now a protected area, and we noticed how visitors were careful to pick up their garbage.  There is a parking area with adequate spaces during mid-week, but you might have to park on side of road during a weekend.  There are no facilities, bathrooms or restaurants.  It is peaceful, tranquil, a gem.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Must see!  Climb the hill for the view.  Shallow, safe, no amenities. Easy drive from La Paz.  Good parking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I truly believe after going up and down the Baja, that by far this is the most amazing beach in all of Mexico. The sand is icing sugar white and soft, the water is clear clean warm and completely beyond words amazing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the visit!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful and very clean beach! Worth the visit!! to walk on the sea its great, water is without waves.. very peaceful and beautiful place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A bay like no other!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent 2 days here, SUPing and swimming and wading. Breathtaking scenery and clear, beautiful water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove from Cabo to La Paz for the day; it was a beautiful drive. The crystal clear waters of the bay were amazing. It was not as secluded as we thought but the beach is huge and everyone is spread out so it was fine. We had a palapa (free) which was great. Fun for swimming, exploring, and relaxing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, go early!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were cancelled for our diving trip and decide to head to Balandra Bach to know the place. Once we get there, the beautiful of the place catch us and desire to stay the day there. Was really fortunate for us just to arrive early, we could choose a nice Palapa to have shadow from the sun and spend all morning there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Incredibly beautiful and peaceful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Incredibly beautiful and peaceful, even during a norte! The ports were closed, but it was beautiful in this protected cove.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sunset with Mushroom Rock in pictures
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was not difficult to get to, about 25 minutes from the tourist area of La Paz.  Once parked, you walk about 15 minutes to the rock.  Beach was quite clean and I am glad people respect the environment and did not throw much trash around, unlike some places in Asia or elsewhere.  Go late in the afternoon, like 4 pm or after to catch sunset and there will be less tourists clamoring over the rock then.  You can take pictures without others around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It is paradise!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You must visit this beach , water is super clear and crystal , nature so amazing that you can walk across the bay from one side to another, the sea only reaches knee height.  When the tide starts to reside in the afternoon, the bay is even shallower and small sand islands start to appear.  It’s beautiful!  Locals said that there are mosquitoes or kind of bees after 4pm, so be careful , I believe perfect timing to visit this beach from 11-4pm.  Has some palapas, no food around , you will see some caves and rocks around , beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Low tide experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a cool tide pool, sea life walk around beach expereince- tons of sealife all around- daughter did get a small Jellyfish sting wading in water- not without dangers but worth the great memories

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bello pero peligroso
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Una playa muy bonita con aguas muy claras. Pero tengas cuidado con las medusas. Yo fui y me pico una. No hay servicios de sanitario y/o un lugar para comer. Hay mejores playas sin duda. Beautiful beach with crystal clear waters. But be careful with the jellyfish!! I went a few days ago, and I was stung by one. There are no bathrooms and a place to eat. I think there are better beaches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but watch out for bees
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove to Balandra on one of the days staying there in La Paz. It was beautiful and the fact that you can walk out so far on low tide is fun. You can also rent kayaks and take it around. The only part that I didn't like was that from the moment you drive in, you start seeing bees flying around. I'm nervous around so many so that was a major distraction. To my luck, I got STUNG by one however it was my fault for laying back on my towel, and not looking first. That's how many bees there were! I still have the bruise today a week later. Would I go back? Maybe but I'd be distracted....

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were there on an overcast day but it was still absolutely beautiful. Lots of tide pool critters to see and the beach was totally wadable during low tide.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the taxi ride!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra was probably the highlight of our trip. Absolutely gorgeous beach, pretty secluded, if youre willing to venture along the coastline you can easily find private areas where very few people are out there. Highly recommend, only complaint is we didnt bring beer!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Shallow beach so you can walk out a long way. The water is no deeper than waist deep.It was easy to find and get too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach at high tide.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: at high tide, it is one of the most beautiful beaches we have ever been to. But at low tide, its not as good.  Also, depending on the time of year, it can get packed with lots of locals.   Be sure to climb up to the top of the overlook very carefully.  Lots of loose rocks, but its well worth it. The views are amazing and the sunset is one of a kind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Rocky Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place was truly amazing. The water was crystal clear with white sugar sand. The backdrop looks like a chunk of the Grand Canyon with wild cacti growing on the mounds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Drove there on a cloudy day.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful spot! The four stars are only because of the weather, which was out of our control. Highly recommended as cloudy days are extremely rare.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing...just amazing.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just no words describe the beauty of this place. The Palapas have just been redone. Beach is very kid friendly. There are however no public restrooms and the trash cans seem to fill up quick.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise no more, it's been discovered
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went on a Saturday. Parking lot full, palapas taken (last time I visited there were no palapas..)Still a pretty spot, but not what it was ten years ago.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach 🏖👍🏻☀️
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches we visited when in Cabo. Was worth the drive of 2 hrs with screaming/hungry kids in the car.You can walk all the way across and the water would reach a little over your waist. Water is a little chilly but once you get in and with the scorching nice sun you later feel the water get a little warm. Also water was a bit salty unlike any other beach .Don’t recommend taking any sodas since there’s quite a few bees 🐝 . Also make sure to use the restroom before you get there (maybe an OXXO) since no restrooms or showers at all, especially if your traveling like us with 9 kids. There’s a couple of umbrella’s but have to get there early to get your own, since later in the afternoon more people come. There’s also a guy renting Kayaks for an hour for 2 or 3 people in a single kayak , 2 people was $250 pesos for an hour which is not bad. Highly recommend you wearing water shoes since there’s quite a few unusual things in water eg. some type of slugs and some small fishes.Overall would definitely visit again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: ok, everyone wants to find that special beach with white sand and crystal clear water.  Well this is it.  the netire bay is no more than 5 ft deep at any point and lots of fish to snorkle with as well.take food and drink as No restaurants or bars there. but 5 min away at Tecolote Beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hidden gem near La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is excellent for those who can't swim well since the crystal clear water is pretty shallow. And the best part, at least for those who'd rather travel by foot than with a rental car, is that there IS a bus that goes here from La Paz's Bus Terminal (Aguilar). From November to December, the bus for that route runs every 2 or so hours, and the last bus back to La Paz is at 5:45PM. For a round-trip ride, the cost is 100 pesos (5 USD), and the travel time is about an hour each way. I highly suggest taking an earlier bus to get the full glimpse of the beach in all its colorful splendor. Unfortunately for me, I only had enough time to take the 3:30PM bus, and I didn't get there until around 4ish. The beach was still beautiful but it didn't have the alluring blue color that I was hoping to see. It's quite a sight to behold with the shallow beach stretching in every direction being wrapped in a mountainous embrace by hills that are adorned with green, spiny cacti. When planning a trip to La Paz, make sure you allot enough time for this beach as well as the Tecolote beach, which is a bit farther away. I only got to see Balandra but it's still worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great White Sand Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a clean beach with free plapas if you get there early. You can walk around the rocks to the Flower Rock when the tide is low.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is beautiful, but the day we went there were WAY too many people.  The water is calm, clear and shallow.  Perfect for famililes with small children and conveniently close to town.  Fortunately we found other beaches nearby that weren't as congested.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cabo whale shark tour
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Incredible sunset visit to balandra water very warm. One of the most spectacular beaches in Mexico great for snorkeling and enjoying the beach and views

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach and bay!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a short 30 minute drive from La Paz, definitely the nicest beach in the area.  The road is not marked very well but if you hit the ferry port you are on the right track.  Nice clean shallow water, great for kids.  There are many palapas on the beach but are taken by 10:30 so get there a bit early if you want shade.  We shared ours with an older Mexican couple who had come out later in the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Water is stunning !!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Decide to drive here from San Jose del Cabo.. maybe 3 hours (one way).  Would of loved to have stayed near by for a night instead of driving back right away, lots of places I would of loved to stop at ..but we were leaving for home the next morning:(I read where people mention something about a food truck.. but not while we were there. Come prepared with extra bottled water, food, blanket to sit on and a floating device (this would if been the bomb for me). No restrooms.A handful of palapas lined the beach.  We hunkered down by the rocks to get a break from the sun.I did see a vendor renting out kayaks and such.  If we would have gotten here earlier in the day, would have defiantly done that. Great inlet, could of went over to the other side to visit.. but you really could of walked to the other side, water was waist deep if that ....so beautiful and relaxing.Couple dogs were out running in the water ..looked like they were enjoying this as much as we were.Lot of great rock formation.  As of right now,  this place it pretty much untouched..but give it time and their will be building all over this area :( which will be just another tourist trap.Would defiantly take this drive again..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An absolute must "go to" when in La Paz!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Take everything you need, because they don't sell a thing here, but pack the cooler, some shade and spend the day swimming in this natural pool!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Perfect turquoise warm waters and white, fine sand. This is one of the most picturesque beaches we've seen and incredibly quiet. If you're in La Paz, Balandra is a must visit!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most beautiful beach ever!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach a 30-minute busied from the Malecon in La Paz. There are very few services, so bring everything you need!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must see in La Paz but you don't have to spend all day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is definitely a must see.  We spent about 3 hours here and it was very enjoyable.  The water is from waist to chest high for what seems like miles.  The water was a great temperature and we never did get chilled nor did we need a wetsuit.  There weren't a lot of fish in the first 500 feet of beach but, once you get to the rocks you will want your snorkel gear because the snorkeling was great.  From where you park your vehicle as you look out over the Palapas the rocks are off to the right.  As you go around those rocks you will see another beach which you can't see from the parking lot.  At the end of that beach is the balancing rock that everybody photographs.  Once you get to the balancing rock, this is the place for some good snorkeling and fish viewing.  We did not end up with a Palapa and I probably wouldn't again unless I had young ones.  Kakaks were available and I think it was $250 pesos per hour.  If you are in a hurry I would grab a kayak.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach! Water is blue and clear. Great for snorkeling and walking along the rocks. Bring food-drinks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth the drive, very clean beach.  Great for taking in the view of the Beautiful Sea of Cortez.  It can be very busy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of my favorite beaches, great for families with young kids, friends and couples, the colors of this place makes you believe in paradise!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most amazing beach area.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No stingrays and we walked for hours barefoot in the water. Highly recommend the kayak. No bathrooms, no beverages or food for sale. There are like 12 palapas

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Desert vs Ocean = Contrast
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Based on reviews, I had high expectations on this beach. When we visited Balandra it was low tide and 90ish F weather and had just visited Coyote beach. The contrast was magnificent as you sea the dry desert, but yet you have a beautiful crystal clear ocean and when you look further you can see a deeper blue ocean with sea boat passing by. People were taking advantage of the low tide and were walking to the other side of the mountains or kayaking. We admired the views, took some photos and ran to our car with ac. They don't have any vendors on the beach so you must bring your own beverages, but they had free palapas. I would recommend Coyote beach as the waters were calmed and you can swim and there were vendors. By all means, visit Balandra and admire the contrasts.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful locals beach and cove
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were so excited to have found this spot! It was relatively uncrowded, had plenty of parking, and public palapas available for use (some in the water and others on the beach). All palapas were being used when we arrived so luckily we brought our own beach umbrellas, which were great for the crazy hot sun, but it was so windy they kept getting blown away (not sure how often it's windy since we only came once). The water itself was surprisingly cool since most of the bay is no more than waist deep. Snorkeling wasn't great although you could see several school of fish swimming around. There are no facilities or food/drinks for purchase anywhere on this beach. There also were no vendors anywhere on the beach, which was a great relief from Cabo! I recommend getting there early (before 2 pm) to get a public palapa!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most beautiful beach in Mexico
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach, protected from the waves which makes it very easy to swim. As it is quite big and far from the city, not a lot of people go there. One of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful bay
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Don’t miss this stunningly beautiful beach. No sign of any jellyfish when we went - just amazing. Not very crowded either.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very beautiful public beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is my first time in Mexico. It is very beautiful beach. You have to visit the mushroom, icon of la paz. Good thing to realize that this is a public beach. My friend told me that peoples of la paz refused hotel investment in order to make this beach publicly accessible and to protect environment. It's like people's wins over capital. No fee to enjoys this beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Snorkling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is October my family and I spent the day here.  The water is higher than when we visit in the winter months.  Went snorkling around the rocks near the upside down rock (on the right side of the beach) and it was great.  I continued snorkling quite far and came to another white-sandy beach.    It is true, there are agua malas (microscopic jelly fish) and they do sting.  I applied a thick coat of vasoline jelly as a barrier between my skin and the agua malas and it worked.  I didn't get stung once but other people did.  Suggestion is to pack a cooler with water and food.  It gets very hot out there so bring shade with you i.e. cabana or tarp with poles.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beware the “Agua Mala”!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra Bay is very pretty, but please be aware that in the warmer months (like now, October) swimmers can get badly stung by tiny invisible creatures. The locals call it “agua mala” — “bad water”. I call it “a bunch of tiny microscopic bendejos”! I went there for a snorkel at about 9:30am on a lovely clear October morning. The place was deserted, the water was warm and clear, and I set out with my snorkel gear and thankfully a long-sleeved swim shirt. That shirt saved me from having a horrible itchy rash over my whole body... I hit an area where these little buggers congregate, and got badly stung. It feels like stinging nettles being rubbed all over your skin. I have been stung by jellyfish before in Mexico, but there was nothing to see in the water. The rash didn’t,t appear until that night, and an awful, bumpy, itchy rash it is. Thank goodness I had that swim shirt on... most jellyfish &o their nasties can’t sting through even a thin layer of fabric. Even nylons offer protection -next trip I am bringing several pair.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent Christmas Eve on this beach in 2016 and it was lovely.  We were able to walk all the way across the bay to the other side.  The beach was clean and uncrowded.  There is a small snack stand there where you can buy limited things, but it's good to bring your own

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Quite disappointing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We came to this beach with very high expectations because everybody told us that it was amazing. Arriving there and walking around for a while, we could not understand at all the hype about this beach. Shallow and brackish water, not really clean beach. Definitely no place to swim or even pass the day in our opinion. Even Playa el Tecolote 2 minutes drive from there was nicer for a swim. Both of them still nothing in comparison to the beaches around Todos Santos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: best beach in La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this is a must on your trip... far but totally worth it!!beautiful beach, beautiful views, free, nature, calm & short water, ideal for kayak!don't miss it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: one of my favorite spots
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I never want this place to be crowded so I should keep everyone away but really it's amazing!  Not easy to get to. We rented a car and drove from San Jose Del Cabo.  Long drive but went by fast and we would do it again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: No sign of impact from hurricane Lidia
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We explored all the famed Cabo swimmable beaches after hurricane Lidia and will not feel comfortable sending our kids into the water except this one. Beautiful and don't forget your snorkeling gear - no vendor here for equipment rental

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Sunset !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a really nice and quaint beach with a stunning outlook for a sunset. I climbed the hill to get a better look and was totally worth the hike.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hermoso paisaje
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Una de las playas más bonitas que he visistado en Mexico. One of the most beautiful beaches in mexico, You might wanna go after raining season so the water level goes up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra beach has a huge expanse of sandy beach with lots of shallow water to play in. The snorkelling out around the rocks was quite good too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Touring La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Calm water,  clean and everyone was friendly.. also not too deep for those that don't swim.  We didn't realize to bring swimming outfits. Also you can see fish swimming

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The natural paradise endless pool
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach of your dreams. A natural pool with no end.You should come and walk to the stone, little far but worth it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing beach, great for small kids.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Picturesque beach on the northern outskirts of La Paz offer calm shallow water which is great for little kids.Recommend getting there early to get a Palapa.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went kayaking in Bay with Cortez Club and was well worth our time.  Really a beautiful area with a number of beach, crystal clear water and easy to kayak across all of it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach but not worth the drive.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Don't get me wrong, it is a beautiful beach but it was super packed. There was no parking and it was a Tuesday afternoon.It was just okay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach. Shallow and warm forever. Rent a kayak and head to the right along the shore. Turquoise and gorgeous wayers
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Private beach with about a dozen shade shelters. A few vendors - food and trinkets - and you can rent kayaks (which I recommend). Very accessible via bus from the malecon in La Paz. I would be there now if I could be.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Interesting Place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a beautiful and interesting place. Not sure if it's worth a drive from cabo san lucas. We rented a car and drove to the beach from Cabo via todos santos and a stop at Hotel California and it took about 2.5 hours. The beach parking lot was small and filled to the brim but we managed to find a place to park. The bay was beautiful however, the water was warm and had an unpleasant smell near the beach and there was lots of sea scum floating in the water which was pretty pretty gross. You could walk out into the bay forever and the water was only waist deep, pretty cool as far as that goes. And if you had a kayak it would be all the more interesting as it is such a big area to explore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hands down the best beach in BCS
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pull out the checklist:1. Crystal clear water-check2. Swimmable-check3. Plenty of aquatic life--check4.  Desolate-check5. Minimal tourists--check 6. White sand-check7. Pure nature- checkThis list can go on and on, but you get the picture.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful calm waters perfect for children, 1st time paddle boarding & view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Make the trek to Balandra Beach to enjoy the calm shallow waters of this amazing beach.  You can swim, snorkel and just kick back.  There are a few vendors that rent stand up paddle boards and kayaks.  If you get there early, grab a palapa for the shade.  There are chairs and tables set up on the beach that you can use.  Personnel on the beach do sell snacks, water and 1 vendor appeared to be selling fish.  The best vendor is the ice cream cart that is in the water..:)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magical Beach in Baja
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved this beach, a lovely expansive shallow lagoon with clear water surrounded by gently rolling, desert hills. Nice beach with palapas, parking and restrooms. A great place to spend the day, very relaxing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Shallow waters all around, you can walk to the other side and have your own private beach. However recommend you bring some of your own shade if you come on a busy day

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is one of the most beautiful beaches in the world!! A hidden gem, but make sure you take your gear there when you go visit! Take a towel and an umbrella if not you would have to rent one, it is insanely hot but the water is amazing!!! Water reaches about 5ft high, its like a giant swimming pool!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful places on earth
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a paradise!Its better to get there by boat. We went with Cora Tours they really know the place, so they tell you exactly where the best scuba diving spots are.it is great for kids because its very shallow.Dont miss it if you ever go to La Paz

reviewsWithKeywords.title: so we decided to visit the mushroom shape rock
reviewsWithKeywords.text: after being some days in cabo we decided to visit the famous mushroom shape rock in balandra breach, it was a very very quite beach there were no waves so we could easly walk a lot of meters in this beach, it is very relaxing and admiring the mushroom rock was worth the visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most Beatiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the most beautiful beach you will ever see. The water is crystal clear, the beach is gorgeous and a must see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of The Most Beautiful Beaches in Baja California Sur
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The first time I laid eyes on Balandra Beach, I was stunned. Having traveled the Baja Peninsula extensively, I thought that I had seen the most beautiful of what the beaches had to offer. This place is magnificent.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went there twice in our short 3 days getaway in la paz....... Gorgeous.. The water is nice..... The activity is affordable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: BEAUTIFUL AND CALM
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is very calm. I recommend it for smaller kids. Most beautiful beach I have visited in La Paz

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are in La Paz make sure you check out Balandra. One of the most beautiful beaches in the world. Completely isolated and protected beach means nothing but absolute serenity.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Warm and clear water with wonderful views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I went there after going to Isla Espiritu Santo with On board Baja travel agency, they took us to a part of the beach that is not accessible by car or walking, so it was a more private part of the Beach. This is a very big place and the depth of the water varies a lot depending on where you are, what doesnt really change is that it is amazingly beautiful wherever you look at. It has a little for all tastes, there is a part  of the beach (where the famous stone is) which is crowded and if you are more into privacy, you can walk a little bit more of do SUP until you get to a more quiet place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bring everything!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a nice, calm and pretty beach at La Paz! We brought our full face snorkel mask and we expend the entire day in water. Bring a wetsuit coz the water is a little chill. Food and drinks are a must coz there is just a small kiosk and nothing else.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: paradise beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a jewel of nature, I had never seen such a beautiful bay and could walk safely and admire the surroundings ... worth spending some time there and just make the trip to meet her

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautful Beach!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra beach is absolutely the most beautiful beach in Baja Mexico!  The water is stunning and the color changes depending on the angle of the suns rays. Incredibly breath taking. Its not deep and you can walk out forever.  Definitely a must see if you visit La Paz!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's a Drive, But Worth It!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful!  If you want a relaxing, photo op beach....this is it.  It was an all day trip for us.  We drove from San José Del Cabo and it took about 2 to 3 hours to get there.  (We stopped on the way and had lunch.) There are two ways to get there from San José Del Cabo. On the way there, we went the Hwy 1 route.  It's mostly a two lane highway that goes through the mountains.  It was nice, but the steep turns/curves to get through the mountains became relentless.  If (when) you get stuck behind a slow truck or car, it's really hard to get around it because there are very few long enough stretches to see if a car is coming from the other direction (and I'm not a timid driver).  On the way back, we decided not to re-live Hwy 1, so we took the route that is mainly Hwy 19 with a partial toll in Cabo (about 35-50 pesos).  It was less hectic and we even managed to get to our dinner reservations on time--which we thought wasn't gonna happen.  We used our iphone 7 to take a panoramic pic of the view and it was beautiful to send to friends and family at home or on social media.  (Ok, my 15 yr old daughter did it, but I used it. ;) )  The really nice thing about the water there is the fact that it's about waist high deep.  You can walk out very far (maybe even to the opposite beach, I'm not sure) throughout the cove.  My daughter and her friend went paddle boarding and said it was super easy to rent the boards and loved it.  There are snacks and drinks you can buy as well as umbrellas, tables, and chairs to rent.  (We rented an umbrella, one table, and four chairs for 250 pesos.)  I think we got the last umbrella, so be aware that it isn't an endless supply.  (You will definitely need some sort of umbrella if the weather is nice, don't think you won't.)  The beach had a lot of people on it, but not too many at all (at least the day we went on a Thursday).  We had plenty of room around us.It's considered one of the best beaches in the world. So, if you are near or even if it's a bit of a drive to get there....go experience this beach.  You won't regret it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the beaches in Cabo for children. I have a 7 year old that was able to swim almost through the whole place in the ocean. He also did some kayaking there and visited the mushroom rock. Water was clear!!! Great place for children.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very busy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We arrived around 10 am. Already, the parking lot was getting full. We found a corner for the car (Toyota Prius) but could not pull forward entirely because the spot had a huge rock. The parking was free.Already all the public umbrellas were taken. A vender offered to rent some chairs, table and umbrella. This came up to 250 pesos. People keep on arriving. It was a Monday, and I just cannot imagine this place on a weekend. I searched for some food. Not a lot of options there. Someone had a stand and sold candy and lots of unhealthy food, and some cold sodas. Someone else had mango. It would have been a great idea to be better prepared with some sandwiches. Dogs were permitted on the beach, but not in the water. When we were ready to go, we could not proceed. Someone with a huge Toyota Hilux had packed right behind the Prius. I saw someone else wanting to leave, but there was also a car parked right behind him. This is when I witnessed the Mexican collaboration system. A group of men lifted the badly parked car and moved it just enough to allow the other guy to leave. Eventually we found the Hilux owner and he left with his big truck. Lots of other eager drivers wanted the spot and I had to stand in the way to prevent them from taking the spot until the Prius was out. That parking lot was a madhouse. The beach itself was the best one. The water was very shallow and clear.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra Beach is unlike any other spot I have seen, and I've been to many of the best beaches in the world. Totally unexpected as the Pacific side of Mexico is not usually as clear and blue as the Cancun side. This place is an exception. It's like mother nature coughed up tons of pure white sand and filled the whole bay. Then flooded it with clean clear water that never goes past waste or chest level. You can wade all over the bay, look at fish, cool rock formations, hills of sand piled high and deep on the shores, and just float around in warm clear blue water. Warm water and warm beaches make this place a one of mother natures masterpiece's. Go there!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing day at beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took a cab out to the beach, walked along the waters edge to the beach around the point and had the beach to ourselves all day. We hiked up the hill and over the top to the little rental building where the cab dropped us off  I do not recommend that hike,  to many rattle snakes. Stay by the beach. Take lots to drink.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went there after swimming with sea lions, and it was really lovely. It's nice and calm and so pretty. Chrystal clear water

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the Best Beaches I have ever seen in my life! A must visit place! La Paz! 30 minutes from Downtown and Malecon La Paz! Please arrived at least 8:30am to save your palapa but must bring your own food and drinks! Loved it!! Will come back!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just AMAZING!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the place to take your young kids if they are into snorkeling or just playing at the beach.  It's not that crowded when I came here and nearly walked across to the other side of the bay.  Bring your picnic snacks and make sure you potty ahead of time.  Else fine a bush because there is not bathroom.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect spot to relax
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is beautiful. The water is very shallow and calm so it is perfect to visit with children or people who can't swim. We took por paddleboards and explored other nearby beaches. Definitely one of our favorite spots in La Paz.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: World Class Beach so far unspoiled by Commercialization *Heads Up no Washrooms* Dog Friendly :)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning Beach, warm clean water. We went 4 times during our 10 day stay we loved it so much! We were staying at the Hyatt Place La Paz and therefore were only a quick 15 minute drive from this glorious beach. Small parking lot, that did overflow on the weekend. We were there at the end of May beginning of June and the water was perfect. Apparently it gets quite cold in the winter months. You can rent paddle boards etc there. there are free palace's that fill up first and then you can rent umbrellas and chairs for approximately $5-$10 depending how busy the beach is.... worth it! There was a food truck and souvenir sales there as well. No washrooms so plan ahead before leaving town or prepare to go in the desert!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beatiful and unrefined...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra Beach is a beautiful location. We took the time to follow the beach and walked to Mushroom Rock. This place is magical. I suggest that you follow the shore toward Mushroom Rock to more secluded beaches. Be aware to NOT climb the sand dunes, there are snakes on them. The Baja is a magical place and this beach is part of that magic.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just amazing and a great place to visit!! You definitely need to kayak and go see the famous rock of Balandra!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the Drive....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove all the way from Cabo San Lucas which took about two hours. Getting through Cabo with the road construction and navigating through the unknown streets of La Paz took some time. Allow yourself extra time if this is your first trip.We stopped for lunch along the Malecon in La Paz which afforded us a much needed break. The drive up to Balandra (Spanish for sloop) took about 30 minutes.The waters are crystal clear and you can virtually walk across the bay. The depth is mostly 3 ft and at the deepest maybe 5 feet. There are kayaks, chairs and umbrellas for rent. Local venders have water, and other cold drinks. There are no restrooms.If you have kids of any age, this is the pace to take them. No currents and the consistent clear shallow water will put anyone at ease.We were there during the week in early June and the parking lot was full. I am not sure what it's like on weekends as this beach is popular with the locals.As we have a place in Cabo we will plan on spending the night in La Paz to allow us more time for all the other activities there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: WHAT A BEACH...!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the most photographed and popular beaches in La Paz, and for the Baja as well. About a 30 minute drive out the bay from the city, you wouldn't know it was there until you made the final curve. White-sand beaches, and desert-like cliffs add to the experience. A must-see for anyone visiting the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ranked one of the best beaches in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: At low tide you can walk all the way across the bay. The water is warm and the sand is fine. Also the location of El Hongo (the mushroom rock).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach till you drop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: walk forever is crystal clear warm water, see fish and wildlife, soft sand, amazing colours and landscape, best beach ever.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach close to La Paz - worth the drive!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We headed out to Balandra mid morning and the place was already busy!  Rented chairs, table and umbrella on the beach and enjoyed the fabulous view.  Also rented a SUP and took turns paddling in the cove.  The water is so warm and shallow you'd think you were in a bath!  Busy, but everyone was so friendly and social it made for a very fun day.  No bathrooms is the only real downside. Highly recommend.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach in the middle of the desert, perfect for kayaks. There are no bathrooms there, so you can go to the town next to Balandra, no more than 4 minutos away, the name of this beach is Tecolote.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fanstatic Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the best beaches I have experienced in Mexico.  The water is calm and clear. The water level is low enough to walk across to the other side of the beach.  This seems to be a favorite spot for the local - so it gets crowded with families and large groups.  However, still a great place to spend the day or few hours.  There is only one vendor that has a few snack items for sale; umbrellas and chairs for rental - so, it is best to bring your own stuff.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Giant swimming pool!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The water is so calm and blue! It was also a pretty nice temperature when we were there as well. It's also very shallow. You have to walk out really far to even get waist deep! I recommend bringing plenty of snacks, drinks, etc in a cooler so you can stay for several hours. There are people selling food, drinks, water, hats etc. in the event that you forget something, but the selection may be limited. This is a great place to go for fun in the sun!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Top beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I have ever been. Feels like being in Greece. Unfortunately some people visiting are loud, noisy, irrespectful and lack in education and sensitivity to admire this paradise.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Extremely crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Water level waaay too low and very crowded no umbrella rentals available. People selling mangos tried to rip me off bought 2 mangos and gave them a $20 USD and try to give me back 60 pesos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A day of sun and sea
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with colors that reflect a true acquarium. A bus service from downtown La Paz make it easy to reach from town without the need of a car, snacks and drinks can be bought on place and kajak rental is available as well. It's advisable to arrive in the early morning to have the chance to enjoy a free umbrella.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wedding Anniversary
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous place hidden in La Pax, you definitely have to visit this paradise...You will not regreat it, tour Lobito with Edgar is who to book with.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfection
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow, clean warm and perfect.  We visited for a  few hours in our Panga with Baja Expeditions and could have spent a day "earthing" in this pristine spot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: one of the most stunning place i have visited
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is imposible to be in Baja California Sur and not pay a visit to this place! So easy to get to. Spend the day, it is never overly busy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Marvelous spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: just a lovely, peaceful beach, about 30 minutes from the Malecon ... WELL worth the trip.  Only downside, no food available for sale... so take a picnic

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went mid week in late April. It was pretty quiet and a beautiful beach with a shallow, warm, clean, bright blue bag that is ideal for paddle boarding or families. Well worth the drive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Everyone loves this beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a beautiful white sand beach, absolutely packed with families camping out for the day.  Not my cup of tea, the beach in front of our hotel was just as calm and much quieter.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Place For Family
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The bay is amazing.  It is mostly shallow and you can walk out into the middle of the bay.  Just make sure you shuffle your feet to avoid being stung by any sting rays.  Also, make sure you walk up to the mirador from the road leading to the parking lot for some amazing views and photo opportunities.  There are hardly any fish in the bay and so not much to see underwater.  They rent kayaks as well which we did as a family.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a beautiful beach.  Make sure to rent one of the umbrellas...it gets really hot and the sun is very intense.  We were there on a Saturday and the crowds started showing up in the later afternoon.  We took the Eco Baja Tours bus from the Malecon.  It was a good price, but the buses are a little unpredictable...sometimes they pick you up and drop you off at different spots so it is easy to miss the bus.  There is limited food and water here, so pack something.  There are manta rays here, so be careful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach.....too crowded for me. Beautiful water but all of the tourists go here too packed for my likings

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Don't miss this beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely beautiful!!!! Gorgeous soft sandy beach and clear water. Take a cooler. Although no food/drink place at this beach definitely the most beautiful of this stretch of beaches

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although the water was really Cold, its scenary its very beautiful. In the Beach you can find snacks, drinks (sodas and water) and you May rent umbrellas and chairs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crystal water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you're planning to go to balandra, be there early.There is not a lot parking slots, and the umbrella renting is limited.Beautiful beach with crystal water and you can have a nice walk to go on the other side of the watch an emblematic rock like a mushroom.If you have aqua shoes bring them, a lot of rocks on the way and some at the bottom of the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Super beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clean and relax beach natural space with great view . You can see and stay for a long  time enjoying the water you can walk to the balandra stone to take pictures and enjoy the natural  blue water

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pristine beach better accessed by boat
reviewsWithKeywords.text: even though we were here at the highest possible time (Easter), it still felt quite private and extremely enjoyable. Great quality sand and very clear water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Get there early or late to avoid the crowds but spectacular beach.  Make sure and bring most of what you need as there isn't much to buy there which is part of the beauty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Quiet and lovely. Recommend going early in the morning. We have rented a car to get there and it was good decision.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not to be missed!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is one the most beautiful beaches I've ever been to. You can walk forever out in the water! Make a point of going up there when you are in LaPaz!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Heaven on earth
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Paradise -perfect beach to relax at or kayak or paddle bots! Not much food , so eat lunch in La Paz before !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra Beach Beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Approximately 2 and 15 min away from Cabo by car was a wonderful find in La Paz. Highly recommended if you are staying in Cabo for some time. Beach is not crowded at all during the week Water is warm tranquil so inviting to jump in. Bring your cooler with drinks as there really is nothing there as far as resorts. Young kids love it. You can Rent a kayak or stand up board along with chairs and umbrellas at that beach. No beer sales only snacks sold there. Safe drive

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful if you come into it by water; just OK otherwise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is a quick drive (less than 30 minutes) from La Paz.  Now that it has become more popular, like anything, it's lost some of its awesomeness.   Aside from the long sandbar and a view of the icon of La Paz, a mushroom stone carved away by water (think of it like Lovers Arch in Cabo), another beach up the way is just as beautiful (Tecolote)   But you probably would not feel this way if you hadn't seen it previously.   The truly breathtaking way to see it is to come into the cove by boat.  From that perspective there are several beautiful and secluded sand bars to lounge on.  Perfect for paddle boarding because the water is so calm.  There's also a mangrove area which is OK to paddle through, but it is a bit stiffeling with no air moving around much.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We love coming to this beach when we visit La Paz. It is so beautiful. We rented a kayak to paddle around the coves, but it really was too windy for this. Be aware of the wind before you rent. It's easy to wade around the shallow water even if it's cool like it is in January. Pick a sunny day during this month. There are a few permanent thatch umbrellas that you can use or bring your own. Fun place to take kids. There is a little vendor truck where you can rent paddle boards and kayaks. They also have snacks, drinks and sunscreen. There was a souvenir vendor the day we went also. We travelled here January 2016.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A favorite daysail from La Paz - Picnic, swim, and be back before sundown
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra is about a two hour sail from La Paz.  In the daytime, we anchor off the famous "Mushroom Rock".  We swim and snorkel in crystal clear water about two fathoms deep.  As always, the colorful reef fish favor the rocky areas.  This is a superb area to learn standup paddle boarding in the calm inner coves.  Novice kayakers have much to explore along this coast.  Larger sailboats and motor yachts anchor far out near the entrance to the bay.  Other visitors have warned about the stingrays that lie in the shallow waters, so shuffle your feet when you walk and they will move out of your way.  They are not aggressive, only defensive.  Summer is not the best season to visit as the bobos and other flying insects may pester you.  We haven't been bothered by jellyfish, but they may be a periodic issue.  It's always a good idea to ask the locals and observe carefully before entering the water anywhere.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crystalline
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful, quiet beach. No motor boats allowed. Several palapas to sit under. Shallow , clear water with many sand bars. Must walk out a bit to swim. Perfect for little ones!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is truly a most wonderful place.  The beach is wide, white and usually not overly crowded but we were there on a week day so not sure about weekends. Bring your own umbrella or there are some rentals.  Not much shade.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is about a 30 minute car ride from La Paz. The road is being worked on so there could be some delays. Also, there is a port near there so there are lots of big trucks speeding on the two lane road. One you pass the port, then the road is less crazy. There is a parking lot, small place to buy some drink and rent gear. The water is calm and the tide takes the water out quite a ways. You can walk out far with the water still at the knees. Be aware that there are small stingrays resting in the sand under the water. It is safer to scoot your feet while in the water instead of picking them up. Apparently, people get stung quite frequently and it is very unpleasant. There are some umbrellas on the beach. You can easily swim or walk around the rocks and there is a really nice deserted beach on the other side of this one. I felt the water a bit too cold to swim but that is my personal taste. I like warm water. Probably better to rent a car so you can come and go as you please.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a beautiful landscape, great place to relax!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra beach is not mentioned in most of the travel guides we've used to plan our trip. Talking to a local person, he suggested it to us, and what a great surprise!!This beach offers calm water, with different colors due to sand benches and a beautiful rock formation that completes the visual. It is easy to go up on the mountains that surround the beach and take incredible pictures... and the sunset is simply terrific!!We took the day to relax there, in the main beach part you can find shadow and some infrastructure, but in the next one, where you can find the hongo, you must be prepared for the sun, nothing there.We had a car, so we went to another beach, with waves, Tecolote, to have lunch, and I got the best pulpo ceviche of the trip!! Unfortunately I won't remember the name of the restaurant, but it has a sign with pictures of the food... so fresh, awesome.We came back to Balandra to see the sunset, a bonus to close the day!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Balandra one of the top ten beaches in Mexico according to the US Today
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and one of the top 10 beaches in Mexico rated by the US Today as I found this article by google it and I can say that for sure it is like to have a private paradise!! Balandra is a public beach with nothing in it but the beautiful sea of Cortes and the incredible almost white sand that everybody can enjoy for free. So if you go to La Paz visit Balandra is a must!!! It is amaizing the beautiful landscape you can apreciatte whe you are there!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: For a day at the beach...perfect!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Balandra beach is a popular local/family beach. The water is shallow and warm for a LONG distance so kids can play in a large area. If you want more quiet and you're mobile, just walk to the next beach around the corner but bring an umbrella if you want shade. If you want even more peace and quiet, just walk around the next corner and it's even better...very few people and a rock overhang that give shade until around 4 pm. Note: no bathroom facilities at all so you need to go au natural. There are some vendors at the first beach but bring what you want just to be safe. The walk to the second beach is fairly easy, but to the third is over coarse volcanic rock and you need to be nibble-footed and in shape to make it there. The first beach you cand drive straight there or take a local bus. Either way, go earlier as most people start showing up at around 11 and the shade huts at the first beach get taken up quickly.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful, peaceful beach. Few amenities. You can walk a long ways in the warm, very shallow water. If you love beaches you should not miss the one.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best beach I've ever been to.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place was increditable. Soft white sands, clear water. Great for kids. Get there early to get a good spot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Heaven in beach form!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had heard of Balandra the same time I heard of La Paz....had very high expectations for the beach and it did NOT disappoint. Plus, it was far less touristy than I would've thought! Easy to get to either by $5 bus round trip or your own car. Beautiful, breathtaking, calm, relaxing- water is crisp and cool. Would pack your own drinks and food! Definitely a place you think you'll hang out for a few hours but end up wanting to be there from dawn to dusk

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: White sand, azure blue water surrounded by rocky mountains creates a beach experience that will be memorable.  My husband and I arrived at the beach beach after swimming with whale sharks and seals.  Lunch on the beach..a lovely day.  You can reach the beach by car.  If you are in La Paz take a ride to this beautiful beach and enjoy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mother Nature's giant turquoise wading pool!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is amazing. The water is so clear and shallow throughout the whole bay. Reco buy a cheap floaty on Amazon. Also b/c they have no services I reco bringing an ice chest with some beers and snacks. We hired a van to take us there and paid approx $7/hr for him to wait for us.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Protected and isolated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is a few miles out of La Paz, and is in a protected bay so the water is very calm. There is a decent sized beach and a concession stand for snacks. If you drive a few hundred meters from the beach, you can pull over to the side of the road, climb a very steep hill, and see toward La Paz and out to the Sea of Cortez - a beautiful view.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most Beautiful Beach in the World
reviewsWithKeywords.text: All I can say is just plan a full day at this beach. If you can, get there at high tide and watch it go out and back in again. Walk all over, take pictures all over,take in the blues, browns, greens and crystals. If you are lucky, grab a palapa. Bus ride from town if $5 round trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A giant pool!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We did Balandra on day two of our trip and definitely want to go back. The beach was large with plenty of room to find your own personal oasis. Water was clear and very cool. There's a little stand where you can rent tiki hunts, kayaks, SUP, and buy small snacks The scenery just leaves you in awe. One of the best beaches I've ever been to

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, great for windy day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: After fighting the winds at El Tecolote, I headed to Balandra and had a completely different experience.  Sheltered, shallow, non-commercial...several little beaches tucked in amongst the cliffs.  Wonderful, peaceful place to relax, at least on a weekday in March...can't speak to busier weekends or holidays.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's like a 3D postcard of paradise.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We got here early (10:30AM) so that we could score on of the free palapas - and then lounged and bathed for hours. The water is so clear and you can walk (for quite a ways) and have the water not even hit your waist. Water was cool but refreshing in March but we loved this place so much that we came back twice! Rented a double kayak for an hour from a local guy (had to give our ID which I wasn't thrilled about but we got it back afterwards). Even offered to share our palapa with a local family that showed up later when all the palapas were gone - safe, fun and enjoyable. Had no problem leaving my stuff under the palapa while my husband and I swam. I saw some people came as part of a tour - so if you don't have a rental car, you can do that. Plenty of parking and the usual people selling local wares. No one was pushy - a simple "no gracias" had them moving on.  The one guy you shouldn't say "no gracias" to is the burrito guy. He came by the first time and I didn't take him up on his offer of a burrito - but there isn't any food out there so on the second visit I decided to give it a try.  $30 pesos for 2 - not your traditional American style burritos but smaller almost like a "roll up". Get the meat one - the bean one doesn't stay warm and isn't good. He delivers to your palapa but on the way out, I stopped by his car where his family was working to grab another ... and he had hot sauces! A definite treat!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but no bathroom
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was absolutely breathtaking!!! Unfortunately we had to cut the day short, as there was no public washroom that we could find. 😬Remember to shuffle your feet to stir up any sting rays so you don't step on them.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach for everyone
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The bay is very shallow so the water is safe for young children.  There are water toys for rent.  A good pic site but check on the tide before you go.  Make certain you navigate the shore to the mushroom rock.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bandera Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful. Easy to get to from La Paz. Shallow, clear, popular beach with stunning rock backdrop. Some hawkers at beach. A few concessions. Good place for swimming, kayaking, sunning?

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous but the Whale Sharks Had Just Blown My Mind
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We did this as a blend of two tours (I was the only one booked to go to Balandra so they merged this and the Whale Shark Tour) - and I went with the Museum of the Whale (you get a free tour of the museum too).It is one of the most beautiful beaches in the world, but after the tour we were cold and being put on the beach felt more like a punishment, I just wanted to wrap up and get in a hot shower.  But it is stunning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Born to be wild
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Probably the wildest though accessible beach of BajaThere is a parking lot and a small food and beverages shop just beside. The water is really shallow so great for young kids and elder peopleI don't concur with the "best beach of BCS or even Mexico" but it's definitely the best of this area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unbelivably beautiful beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent a wonderful day here with our kids (7 and 10). The beach is stunningly beautiful and the water is so shallow that you can just walk out for hundreds of metres. Would be a great place for those with young children. I can't do justice to it with words so go and see for yourselves!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Heaven!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What can we say??  I have been all over the world and this was by far been the most gorgeous beaches we are ever at. So beautiful and amazing crystal-clear water blue blue. Don't miss it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful spot, can be a bit crowded.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go during the week if you can, it gets a bit crowded on the weekend.  Lovely spot for wading, and if you climb around the corner (through a spot that unfortunately is often used as a bathroom) then you're on another beach, and on the way to the rebuilt balancing rock (La Honga I believe).  Past that you can keep going, wading and walking, and get to another beautiful beach which you're likely to have to yourself.  Go when the sun is out and the water is beautiful blue (it loses a bit of color as the sun goes down).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the highlights of our trip.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches we've ever visited. The water is so clear and pristine. So glad we had the opportunity to vist this most spectacular setting. A word to the wise...check the tide charts before you go. The second time we went the entire bay was almost empty of water! We still had a good time but not as enjoyable as we had to walk so far to get to the water. Did manage to get to the Mushroom that trip though and it was worth the walk. I would definately recommend this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful scenery!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You have to hit this beach just for the stunning photo opportunities!  Make sure you go right around the corner to the right, walk the beach on the other side until you get to the Hongo.  But beware little stinging jellyfish in the water, and we are pretty convinced we saw a shark on the far side of the Hongo.  Another couple said it was a dolphin and some kids told us it was a Marlin... we will never know for sure, but best to be prudent.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My favorite beach near La Paz - beautiful water and scenery!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent several hours at this beach - the beach is really beautiful and it is fun to hike up the rocky parts for beautiful views of the beach. The water was very clear and shallow for a long stretch - we enjoyed walking in to the beach in the clear waters. Highly recommend this beach if you are in La Paz. Also, it is very easy to get to from La Paz - you can take the Aguila bus from the Malecon bus station and it runs quite often during the day. They have a schedule at the bus stop and it was only 70 pesos for the bus ride from Malecon to Balandra beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clear, warm waters. Great view!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a short drive out of La Paz but well worth it. When we arrived it was a bit busy but the beach and the water was very, very clear. The hills surrounding the area were very dry and brown which provided an excellent contrast to the aqua colored water. There are a few beaches around this bay, two that are easily accessible from the parking lot, two that had people on them but I don't know how they got there. There are chair and kayak rentals on the beach. Unless you really have the urge to kayak, I'd recommend skipping it. You can almost walk the entire bay area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A hidden gem
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Balandra Beach while vacationing in Cabo San Lucas.  The 4 hour round trip was well worth it. The Beach was beautiful and clean.  We made some great memories there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach ever!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful, remote, awe- inspiring. Water is crystal clear. Great for snorkeling. Shallow water for kids.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: When tide is out, there is a lot less beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best part of Balandra is the short hike up the rocky hills for beautiful views of the sand and water expanse.  The bay area that Balandra is in is very shallow, so the tide level (in or out) make a huge difference in the look of the beach area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: the most beautyful beach in La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: turcoise water, long beach, nice to walk or swim,repaired from the wind, the sand is so thin!! You have to go there, and take wonderful pictures!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sand is soft, the bay is shallow and walkable, and palapas line the beach. Claim your spot and enjoy warm sun and cool breezes in Baja while your friends shiver up north!  When the tide is coming in wading birds fish along the rocks...white ibis, egrets, herons...all having dinner while people walk around them. A great place to spend the day and see the mushroom rock - one of the La Paz landmarks. Just remember it's a natural area. Pack your food and drinks in and your trash out. There is no restaurant or bathroom at this beach but nearby beaches have both - El Tesoro, Pichilingue and Tecolote. Just buy a drink or food at the restaurant and you can use their facilities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A place to catch your breath
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Don't let the popularity of the place fool you, it's relatively unpopulated. Keep walking around the "mushroom" and find a spot to perch during low tide and you will likely be the only person in sight-the rocks keep most people on the sand. Take along a snorkel and mask to catch sight of flute fish and minnows. I waited several hours until the tide came up and swam back to the beach. What a serene experience!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The most beautiful beach in mex
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were there only for a couple of hours unfortunately we didn't had more time, but the time we spend there was awesome, the views, the beaches are so clean and well preserved, they are so virgin no one is there selling you a thing, you can find peace and very amazing sight seen the views are just out of this planet, I would recommend to be there around noon (12:00pm) the color of the sea changes with the sea level

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool beach, beautiful views, lots of people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were here on a weekend so lots of people but as we arrived around 3, we still were able to get a spot under a palapa. I think it would be cool to get their early and rent a kayak to go across to one of the isolated beaches across the way. It's very shallow so you can walk quite a distance so perfect for kids. Want more peace and quiet, go further down or across to a quiet beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A short 15 minute drive from La Paz. Get there early to grab a public umbrella. Rent a kayak. There is a path on the road leading up to a hill from you have a fantastic view of the beaches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Calm lovely beach !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches I ever saw. Perfect to go with family and even younger kids. You can walk far into the sea water is clear and beautiful . There are no restaurants or so hence real calm . During the day less Mexicans or tourists in the evening a bit more when it is cooler. It is about 30 minutes drive from la Paz . But a must go .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beutiful beach north of town
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Took a 30 minute cab ride out here.  Spent a couple hours out here walking around in the shallow water.  Took lots of photos of birds and the mushroom rock.  Several of us got stung a few times in the legs while in the water.  Did not see anything in the water but felt like mosquito bite and luckily it did not leave a mark or welt.  Not much shade or shelter from the sun so take sunscreen and wear water shoes.  There are no services here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tiny cove open on wonderful beaches when tide is low
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Close to Tecolote beaches, very different but as attractive, tenants of shops offer canoe and other nice activities in a safe context

reviewsWithKeywords.title: paradise!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: one of the most beautiful beaches i've ever laid eyes one. scored a 4/5 because i found it to be a tad too windy. if you plan on spending the day, bring a lunch. there is nothing out there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Among Best Beaches We Have Visited
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We are not great surf beach people.  But we do admire a great beach, and this is one.  Although I have pictures, there are already enough here.  We stopped for lunch.  No facilities that we could find here, so be on notice.  There was a truck selling drinks.  And free thatch umbrellas, although in late January it was so beautiful not needed.  The inlet that the beach is on is all of 3-4 feet deep so you can walk across.  Great kayaking and they are for rent.  You need to be aware of a few jellyfish and some rays asleep in the middle of the channel, but hey, this is Mexico.  A great and beautiful place to stop.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: clear water and amazing views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: i was there with Friends, the water was very clear and great temperatura. we could see lots of fish, great for scuba diving

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beautiful water and white sand, secluded beach.  if I could give more stars, I would!  walk along waters edge and see crabs scurrying along the rocks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the most beautiful beach ever. It's a little out of the way. You have to drive outside of LaPaz past the port but it so worth. There are summer palapas, chairs and kayaks available to rent. There are also a few local vendors to see. The real draw to the beach is after you walk or past the rock face to the right. Breath taking. We live in Cabo and make the two hour drive at least once a month to relax in the peacefulness.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous scenery.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The stark contrast of color within the scenery here alone is worth a visit. Time your arrival at high tide for best scene and swimming. Weekends are busy with local day trippers. There are numerous palapa shade structures available free of charge. We opted for a umbrella and two lounges-$22 US- from the kayak rental/snack truck guys. The water is crystal clear and quite shallow for a great distance.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tranquilty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing tranquility and warm waters. Nice to be able to wade out as far as you can to find that you are waist high in water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a very nice beach. It is shallow so would be good for kids & good for kayaking. We walk from one side of the bay to the other & water only got our waist. Worth the drive out from La Paz only about 20 min - 30 min.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sandy blue water beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I absolutely loved this beach. You can wade out quite a long way and walk into the water. There are grass huts for shade or you can rent chairs but you just need to throw a blanket down under one and enjoy the sun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A nice slice Baja Mexico
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stayed in La Paz for a week and it was a blast!! it is a samll fishing town with enough activites to keep you busy for a week, slow pace good food and firendly folks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful beaches I've been to.
