Sitting on this beautiful white beach looking at the scenery and eating  fresh cervechi was so calm and peaceful. The sand is powdery and doesn't even stick to you. Definitely a unique experience. Since we were the only ones there, this is not at all what happens when you go to a CA beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A tropical paradise of blue water and white sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An incredibly beautiful place and on the day we went there was hardly anyone else there, great for a swim and to see the mushroom rock

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Shallow, private, beautiful waters and beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took a road trip from San Jose del Cabo to La Paz and came to Balandra Beach and were very glad we did, the beach is a very cool experience with water only about up to your knees as far out as one could walk, perhaps a 1/4 mile or more. The shallow water would make a perfect setting for families with young children and we even saw a dog on a paddleboard! They have palapas for you to sit under if you want shade, but there are no other facilities except a vendor selling snacks and trinkets.  If you wanted, you could walk across the inlet through the water with your things and set up in one of the many completely private beach areas, which we will definitely do next time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach, secluded, untouched, a must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has 3 parts, 1 part you can drive to, and the other two you need to take a boat to get there. Go to the boat only portions, as there are fewer people, and it really feels like you are on a secluded beach, with beautiful shades of blue waters, and fine white sand. Bring a nice lunch and relax in the Sea of Cortez.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: don't forget your camera, is spectacular! flat water and white sand! Bring also food and drinks, as there is nowhere to buy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walk Forever when the Tide goes out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went two times to Balandra beach. The second time the tide was going out, stayed for the afternoon. By the time we left around 4 o'clock The Bay was nearly empty of water. So if you hadn't seen it prior and arrived late in the afternoon you might be disappointed.As you couldn't really kayak and it looked desolated. But all the other reviewers are correct it really is beautiful! The different birds are really something to watch and photograph. There are Palapas to hook your belongings onto the poles. The day we went it was also windy, so probably a good choice to be protected from the wind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, Must See
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to Balandra beach this last Saturday for about 4 hours in the afternoon. There were some tourists and many locals at the beach but it was not overcrowded. The beach is clear and the water was moderately warm. The water is about knee high for several hundred yards out and there are several smaller beaches in the bay you can walk to through the water. We took a taxi for 550 pesos (about $33 with the current exchange of 18 pesos=$1) from the Costa Baja resort. Taxi drivers can drop you and return at a specified time. There was one vendor open on Saturday who was renting umbrellas and chairs for 200-300 pesos. There are some fixed umbrellas on the beach, so if you are there during the week you can likely snag one of those. There are no bathrooms and only some drinks and light packaged snacks for purchase. I am unsure how often the stand is open on weekdays when the beach is likely far less busy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A "must go" in La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is just beautiful, quiet and has a magnificent view! If you plan to be there for a long time is best to bring some food and drinks because there is not much around.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastice public beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just the most beautiful beach near La Paz!!  Easy to find and super safe for children.  Lovely rock formations too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You can wade for a mile
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It seems that way, anyway.  The water is warm and cerulean, the sand is white, the rocks are volcanic, the children are laughing, it's like a dream.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My favorite 5 star beach in the world.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So many people come to La Paz and don't get out to this excellent swimming, snorkeling beach in rural setting. Only 20 minutes out of town and well worth the drive. Child safe as you can walk out aprox half a kilometer in pristine clear turquoise water. No wind as its sheltered in a quiet cove. No services but ample parking. Often a food trailer has snacks drinks and souvenirs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Rent Kayak to truly enjoy the Balandra Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Most beautiful beach I have ever seen. Went  twice just to enjoy the beauty. Rent a kayak and cruise the bay. You see lots of fish while kayaking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice beach not too far from La Paz.  Waded around in shallow water and checked out the mushroom rock.  Didn't really find a good place to snorkel.  A little bit of trash from some ignorant beach goers, but unfortunately that happens.  Much cleaner than Tecolote which we visited afterword.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must See Beach in Baja
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The is possibly the best beach for kids I've ever been too. It is a lagoon/bay that fills in to waist height at high-tide and has no waves. At low tide, the lagoon nearly empties and you can walk out and explore the inter-tidal marine life for hundreds of meters. I've probably been 10 times in 5 years, and it hasn't changed a bit. It is great for SUPing, kayaking, relaxing on the shore or wading out for as far as you want. It is a spiritually significant beach to the indigenous people of Baja and is protected from further development, so should stay pristine indefinitely. There is one small kiosk in the parking lot where you can get snacks, rent a kayak or a SUP, but they don't serve beer - everyone brings their own.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, get there early its popular!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing bay, sooo. shallow. We wore our reef shoes and shuffled our feet as told, we didn't see any sing rays. Walked all the way round to the famous rock and snorkelled in water only 4 foot deep, very clear and chilly. No toilets here. We sat on the beach near some locals cooking up lunch for the entire family. Car park is small. So we headed over to Tecolote for lunch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If anything a bit too crowded because easily accessible. Lovely at end of day or early in the morning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good as the pictures
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent a half day there and it was a beautiful as the pictures we had seen in the magazine.  It was sunny all day so that helped the color of the water which was turquoise and clear.  We were warned about stingrays but walked all the way across to the deserted beaches, back and then across to the mushroom rock and never saw one.  There were four of us so don't be deterred by that.  Yes, there were wasps here and there but nobody ever got stung.  If you are in the area, it is a must see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We sailed into this gorgeous bay and anchored in crystal clear water. The rock formations around the bay are very cool and there are 4 or 5 seperate white sand beaches to laze around on. This beach is a popular picnic beach just a short drive or panga trip from La Paz so its popular with the locals. The craggy mountains to the south are Coyote hills I believe. It is a special place.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wow. Just Wow.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is surreal. Miles and miles of knee-deep, crystal clear water and white soft sand. Lots of fish and birds - off-the-beach snorkeling near the rocks is amazing. A perfect place to take a day off, find a sheltered cove, read a book, take a dip, hike a hill and do whatever you like. One of the most beautiful places I have ever been to. Magical.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It is the best beach for kids
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Water there is so shallow and calm,  you can walk long way in and still in shallow water. It's parking lot is so crowded and most people are locals. No restaurant. Only good beach. Bo one told us this beach and found it by ourself. Highly recommend it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Possibly nicest beach in La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful shallow bay with very safe swimming for children.  Unfortunately if you want to swim in deep water you will have to go very far out.  However the beach is very clean (not always the case in Mexico) with little garbage.  On the weekends and holidays it can get very crowded with locals. There is a SUB rental kiosk but no food or drink for sale.  You can see that means it is not really used by tourists, possibly because you need a car to get there

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, lots of people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was beautiful! The water is very shallow for much of it, but we had a very lovely time. Great views, lots of birds!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paraiso
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach you dream about at your desk on Monday morning! An amazing little "hidden" gem with white sand beach, palapas for shade and a wide, shallow, warm-watered bay for splashing around in. Minimal  services (NO restrooms) include a truck selling cold sodas and packaged snacks and a kayak and umbrella rental. Though small, the bay is deep and rocky so even if there are many people here, they are spread out along the beach allowing for privacy even on busy days.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Our favorite beach near La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We think Balandra is the prettiest beach near La Paz.  Plenty of room to spread out.  Good wading and snorkeling in the shallow bay (but shuffle your feet if you're wading to avoid the stingrays).  There is a snack bar that has drinks and rents umbrellas, chaises and kayaks.  Kids love it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: very touristy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There were a lot of vendors looking for you to spend your money. It was interesting to see the marina present as they had a first aid station set up. Not as nice as tecolote

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Restful and scenic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing. Beautiful turquoise waters crashing steadily on soft white Sandy shores. Incredible conglomerate walls of volcanic rock. Private beach with a few locals and some tourists. There are peddlers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you love to exploring inside to cortez of sea, this is a great place for snorkeling. We went with friends at this beach in La Paz and is like little lost paradise in La Baja that you must to exploring !! I recommend this place if you visit la paz one day

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too beautiful for words
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Perfect turquoise beach. White sand, wading pool depth, and pretty as a picture. Be sure to shuffle walk when baby manta rays are present!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful place. The water is very warm and shallow. Would be a great place to take kids to swim. We rented snorkeling equipment, and found beautiful tropical fish here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: QUIET TRANQUIL WATERS
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Playa Balandra is 24 kms. from La Paz where you will find the calm tranquil waters perfect for families and travellers to escape from everything.  The lagoon comprises 7 private beaches of which 5 are only accessible by kayak, paddle board (for rent at the main beach) and swimming.  At low tide, guests can almost walk across to the other beaches.On windy days, the beaches are well protected. Although Balandra is absolutely beautiful, there are no food or drink services, but Palya El Tecolote is only 1 km. from Balandra where you will find bars, restaurants and palapas to enjoy.Palapa Azul, a bar restaurant, serves the best Margarita in all of Baja, along with a full menu of delectable seafood dishes.I live on the mountain overlooking these beaches and has been my home for 7 years.Don't forget to see the "mushroom rock" which Balandra is famous for!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach on a bay, not a ocean beach with waves. Bring food and drinks. Very relaxing. Kayaking and paddle surfing available for a small fee.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We took the advise of other reviewers and ventured out to this place - not too easy to find if you don't have a GPS since the road signs were non-existent.  Fortunately the local police on the road directed us.  The area is still not developed yet.  All we saw were few cars and a vendor truck and that's how we guessed we arrived.  It took us 3 hours drive from Los Cabos.  It was a very windy day as we could feel the sand pelting on our face.  However, the water was still calm.  The water is shallow and you can walk in for quite a distance before the water reaches your waist.  We could see that this would be a great family beach with future resorts build around it.  If we didn't have to drive for such a long time to get back to Cabos and if we had beach chairs and umbrella, we would have stayed longer!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful and quiet
reviewsWithKeywords.text: perfect for couples looking for nice secluded beach (on weekdays) and for families with children as there are no waves and it is shallow for a long distance. I visited on a cloudy and windy day and still worth seeing it. Visit with your car or hire a cab for a day (80$) and visit all the beaches in la paz but you can spend most of your time here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beautifully hidden gem near La Paz!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Quite the hidden gem. Loved it. If you can get a shuttle or taxi or take a rental car here, do it.  It's a quiet and beautiful beach with clear blue water. Not a lot of wind since it's in a protected bay.  Not a ton of people. Some Locals and Tourist. Like any beach, bring your towels, coolers, sun umbrella and your own food. I saw one group pitch a tent. There is a small truck that rents out paddle boards, kayaks, some tables, umbrellas, and very limited snack like chips and soda. There are some permanent Palapa style umbrellas but that's on a  first come basis. Again, not a ton of people here so the chances of getting one early in the day is good.You can hike up the rock mountain or walk around the beach to see the mushroom rock. Great views from the top of the rock mountain but make sure to wear the proper shoes. Lots of loose rocks and as you make your way to the Mushroom rock, you will encounter sand and water depending on the tide.There is parking lot. I saw a porta potty.This is a great little adventure nearby. The kids will love it. You will love it too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: AMAZING!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a must while in LaPaz. I was in heaven for the day. Turquoise water and white sandy beach. Hardly onyone on the beach. Bring a cooler and food with you. Really nothing there at all. A hut to rent paddle boards and a vendor at the beginning of the beach. Take a walk around the rocks to the right. You will end up inside a beautiful bay. It is shallow crystal clear bay.It was windy everywhere else on the coast. This beach is protected. We will be going back for sure!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Speechless
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pictures are not good enough to show how nice is this place. Calm ocean, blue transparent water and clean sand

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches in La Paz
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach, very clean and the water is amazing. A must when visiting La Paz. Take a cooler, a shade and some food with you, there is very little services so be prepare. There are some rental umbrellas and a soda truck near by but that's about it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach for windy day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: In la Paz if the wind is high, this is one of the few protected beaches. The sand is nice beach clean and water warm but very shallow.  The surrounding cliffs make a picturesque view from the water. There was a food truck with some paddle boards.  Visited by locals and tourists.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: calm spectacular beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: fairly large beach, shaped like 2/3 of a circle with lots of little coves going around.  the mushroom rock is pretty cool to check out but being able to walk couple hundred feet from shore tells you how calm and shallow a lot of the water is here.  naturally its nice and warm as a result.  southern end has some ok snorkeling but this is more of beach to just relax and melt away.

reviews.title: Virgin Beach with beautiful views!
reviews.text: It is an unspoilt beach you can walk meters and meters and it is the same depth. Beautiful views. Take aquashoes for a walk and don't get hurt with the stones in the driveway. It was my turn to see a trumpetfish and a swordfish. Controlled access to a certain number of people a day in two shifts. So get here early so you can access it. There is nothing for sale to not generate trash and they have a dry bathroom. They make recommendations that you take your trash, which I think is perfect. They rent you chairs and folder for $400 pesos, we do not use it because the day was cloudy and we would only be 1 hour. We went through an agency. Which doesn't allow you to stay and enjoy the whole shift...

reviews.title: Beautiful !!!
reviews.text: A beautiful place, beautifully colored beaches.  Very good for carrying children. It has 2 hours from 8 to 12.and from 1 to 5.  And they don't charge to get in.

reviews.title: Peaceful and Playful
reviews.text: Victor and Marianna were a great team. The boat ride was gorgeous. The spot to snorkel was phenomenal. We saw nice creatures and beautiful views. Having fun in the bay with friends was totally worth it.

reviews.title: Outstanding beach
reviews.text: Located about 30 minutes from La Paz, nice drive. You need to buy a ticket (can be purchased online in advance). It is a popular beach, however the number of visitors is limited so it won’t be too crowded. The have some umbrellas and there are toilets. Be aware there is no shower and no shop to buy food or drinks. The beach is extremely beautiful with white sand and clear water. The water is ver shallow so less for swimming but great for walks me just stay in the shallow water. I highly recommend also to go up the hill where you have great views.Must do activity in the area!!!

reviews.title: Beautiful beaches in Baja California Sur
reviews.text: A destination full of beautiful landscapes and white sandy beaches with crystal clear water. An abundant fauna and a walk unpredictable if you are first time in La Paz.

reviews.title: the most beautiful beach of La Paz
reviews.text: We reached the sea by car around 9am. It was hot, the water had the perfect temperature. Shallow and transparent with magnificent views. Probably one of the most beautiful beaches I've seen in my life. I RECOMMEND 100%.

reviews.title: Peace and quiet
reviews.text: The most beautiful beach in Mexico. I am a lover of sloop beach, its tranquility, peace, crystal clear waters. A paradise to be cared for.

reviews.title: Beautiful but many jellyfish
reviews.text: Beautiful, but too full of jellyfish (aguamala) and after so much effort X enter we did not enjoy it! Unfortunately outside in August it is unbearably hot and you can not wait to get in the water, but there is the terror of being stung.

reviews.title: Balandra and hidden beaches
reviews.text: Great experience, Fernando, pack, Jorge, Santiago and Jo were great, very helpful and made sure everybody had the best time!

reviews.title: Paradise certainly ♥️
reviews.text: Of the most beautiful beaches I have visited in my life, calm and cold waters. Mood is also quiet because there is limited access as it is a reservation, which makes it a place to relax. You have to bring food and drinks as they do not sell there.

reviews.title: La Paz Trip Worth It
reviews.text: The driver picked us up at our hotel promptly at 5:05 am.  Nice and comfortable large van.  We quickly picked up the other passengers and off we were to La Paz.  We stopped a little over an hour out of Cabo at a fantastic roadside restaurant where the food was great and affordable.  We then proceeded onto Balandra Beach where we had 2 hours to explore and swim.  From there we went to another beach near town to swim and shower off - kind of a public and popular swimming beach.  From there we went towards the La Paz Malecon where we had lunch at a great little restaurant (inckuded).  From there they took us into the heart of La Paz along the Malecon where you could shop, get ice cream, take pictures, tour and church, etc.  We then loaded up for the drive to Todos Santos to see the church, thr downtown shopping Square, the Hotel Californis and our favorite Tequila Sunrise Bar across from the Hotel California.  We finally headed back to Cabo.  All in all, it was a great day and La Paz is worth seeing.  A quaint coastal town with a European vibe.
Lovely if you visit go up the mountain to have the best view Take plenty of water to rinse off at the exit Eat little and drink little water before going

reviews.title: Wow the beach and the views
reviews.text: Of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico, it is very relaxing, you can walk and walk. the views if you climb the hill is wonderful. Undoubtedly my favorites

reviews.title: Amazing beach
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I’ve been to , the sunset is amazing, calm crystal clear water and clean sandy beach we loved it.

reviews.title: Beautiful place
reviews.text: It has been considered as one of the best beaches in Mexico, and it is not a lie, my family and I had an extremely good time here, it is very calm, the water only reaches you up to the waist and if you stay still the marine life begins to approach, so much so that we saw 4 puffer fish that were feeding on the sand trail that we moved when walking, !

reviews.title: Professional, breathtaking, and memorable.
reviews.text: Paco, Eddie, Adrian, and captain Jorge were excellent. The coordination is perfect. The food was good, the drinks flowed, and every detail was covered. All we had to do was sit back, enjoy the beautiful scenery, and walk right into the beachfront coral reef experience.

reviews.title: El Caribe de la La Paz
reviews.text: Spectacular, the water seems like a quiet pool, we went during the morning hours, bought the bracelets a day early and made about 20min of line to enter.Quiet atmosphere, carry an ice cream, umbrella, there is no trash so make sure not to leave either, I recommend to bring some water shoes if you want to go to the fungus that you do not hurt the stones (like my urbanite friends).

reviews.title: beautiful beach
reviews.text: This beach called sloop, I thought it was a spectacle of peace, it takes 3hs to get there by car from Saint Lucas, but it is an effort worth doing. the beach has hours, which I recommend to arrive early. ideal for taking photos and saving memories

reviews.title: A very beautiful and preserved beach
reviews.text: The beach is very beautiful, to get there is very fast from peace, the route overland you can do renting a car and in 30 minutes you arrive. As it is a protected area, there are only two check-in times 8 am and 1 pm the maximum number of visitors per shift is 450. We went on weekdays, arrived at 8:00 and took about 10 minutes to get through.

reviews.title: spectacular this beach
reviews.text: from Cabo San Lucas are 3 hs by car, but it is worth it, it is a spectacular beach, do not miss it, calm and calm water, transparent, without chiringuitos, nor umbrellas. go equipped!!

reviews.title: Very beautiful and quiet beach
reviews.text: Beautiful beach however when we went the sea was "gone" (low tide) and you walk a couple of kilometers in the ""mud"" rather wet dry sand that does like something weird, very little water, and well and then we explained that it would rise with the full moon in those days. You have to take care of those places, although they do awareness work for those who visit to take care, anyway we saw soda stoppers and abandoned shoes......you have to take care of it is our pass to survive on this planet. PD: It struck me that we saw hundreds of a species like nests in the shape of a "churrito" and they explained that it is the ""burrow" of a worm...... I don't know if it was coincidence but my husband gave a tremendous hives. Otherwise beautiful beach, RECOMMENDABLE. A spectacle of nature.

reviews.title: Best beach in Mexico 🏝️
reviews.text: The best beach in Mexico is perfect for young children ideal for teaching swimming are several areas of interest but certainly something out of the ordinary

reviews.title: Balandra
reviews.text: Gorgeous. Got there around 7:40 and no problem getting in. Even got a palapa. Didn’t stay long. Be warned that there were a ton of mosquitoes when we went (late Feb).

reviews.title: Awesome.
reviews.text: Beautiful! The truth of the most beautiful beaches I have ever visited. Very well preserved. Stunning views of the hills. Crystal clear water, WONDERFUL!

reviews.title: Must go at least once
reviews.text: We left early so we didn’t have to get in line. It wasn’t crowded going early and the scenery is beautiful. We didn’t swim so can’t comment on that but walking around the right rock edges was very interesting.

reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.text: Amazing place to hike and get the best views from the viewpoint. Walk to the sea, without being covered by water. For the photo with the fungus you have to line up a long line but you can get into the water and there but without “touching” the rock.  Very cold water, but after a while you get used to it:)

reviews.title: Stunning location must see.
reviews.text: This is a must see if you are in the area. It is absolutely stunning. There is a restriction on the number of vehicles allowed to enter car park and there are 2 sittings. We arrived in the morning time but it already had the limit so we drove in round the coast and went to other beach for a while which has bars and restaurants on it. Then headed back round to Balandra for the afternoon sitting. There are toilets/changing pods available for a small donation as it is like a protected area. The water is crystal clear, shallow and warm. It is stunning.

reviews.title: Excursions within an excursion!
reviews.text: The general view of the beach, the extent to which you can walk and the change in the tones of the water as the sun rises more and more are worth enjoying.  The water can be a little cold in the morning and gradually warms up with the sun.  Excursion to the famous Balandra Fungus or walk the other way to another bay with other beaches, plus excursion to the rock are essential to do during the visit, but do one behind another to be able to achieve it within 4 hours available in turn.

reviews.title: A little paradise!!
reviews.text: A pristine paradise just nature there are no mass tourists there are no amenities, you can go in stages for a few groups of people not to modify the system.

reviews.title: Must do!!
reviews.text: Incredible experience!  We arrived in line at abou 8:35 (it opened at 9) and were about 20th in line.  It opened promply (no charge), there are about 20 palapas that were first come first served.  No restrooms, bring beach chairs, we brought our own inflatable paddleboard and were the only ones on the crystal clear water.  We were there on New Year's Day and there appears to be a truck that rents kayaks, paddleboards, and snorkeling equipment however it was closed.  Also, no food sales, so bring a cooler.  Our "shift" lasted til noon and then I think there is another shift at 1pm which is longer but three hours was plenty of time.  Really gorgeous!

reviews.title: SPECTACULAR VIEW, BUT...
reviews.text: It is a very beautiful site, the best, the landscapes, the color of the water, the tranquility of the site. To keep in mind, I do not recommend bathing there; because, although it is not everywhere, if it is a place with stones, but mainly because several people we were bitten by something, perhaps a kind of bad water, generating a rash on our bodies, with quite a lot of burning, and discomfort for quite some time.

reviews.title: Balandra Beach not entirely complication-free.
reviews.text: Visiting Balandra Beach involves the following: Visitors are divided into two groups, one group can visit the beach between 09:00 and 12:00, the other group afterwards. It is recommended to be there before changing groups or early in the morning, as the number of visitors is limited and you have to wait in line for admission. An admission fee is not charged.  The permanently installed wooden umbrellas are quickly occupied if you are not fast enough. Chairs and umbrellas can be borrowed at the entrance for a fee from suppliers approaching the waiting cars. In addition, there are hardly any catering facilities (organic reserve). The beach is beautiful, the water clear, but may be full of jellyfish. When we swam out, with the intention of reaching the nearby beach opposite, we were attacked relatively violently; on all parts of our bodies, we first carried stinging, then later on for days on end, intensely itchy blemishes (similar to contact with nettles). We have therefore aborted our plan for safety reasons.So either do not swim, just run a little into the water, or wear an appropriate protective suit. There are also extremely small and many mosquitoes waiting for “victims” at the visitor entrance and checkpoint. A repellent is very appropriate. Had we had all this information before our visit, we would have had more of our stay. You can make the visit to the beach well with a taxi, 20 USD each way.

reviews.title: Excellent everything
reviews.text: All excellent service LocationsLa Paz is amazing place thousand recommended for adult children and couples Attention and cute people

reviews.title: All very well
reviews.text: All super good!! Very punctual and safe transfer The vehicles also in very good condition and we took advantage of everything

reviews.title: Beautiful nature view and crystal clear water
reviews.text: Beautiful nature view and crystal clear water. Perfect for a BFF getaway just be careful when swimming because there are stingrays and jellyfish but it was a very good vacation for me and my friends that moment.

reviews.title: One of the most beautiful places in the world
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful places I have seen in my life, we loved that they control the amount of people who enter, so you feel more comfortable, the views are spectacular and I recommend that you take your water glasses to immerse yourself and be able to see all the marine fauna that is precious. 100% recommended!

reviews.title: A day in Balandra
reviews.text: The sloop is one of my favorite beaches in Mexico, I have visited it many times for many years, this year I returned and found some surprises. It already has hours, morning and semi evening You have to line up if you are driving, only 200 people per shift pass, you have to arrive well early to pass by motor vehicle. If you are not wearing an umbrella, I recommend you be one of the first to grab a few palpitations. Nature don't tell is still sleepy! And then better is the low water with its warm temperature. The view of the cannon from above is a fete, you can't miss it. It's worth climbing to the top.

reviews.title: Can't stay all day, but is so beautiful it's worth it
reviews.text: -The good: Beach is amazing and rightfully considered one of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico. There are palapas to leave your things and take some shade (believe me, you'll need it). The place is so photo-ready and the water is calm.-The bad: There's limited admittance, and you can only stay for a few hours (they allow to batches of people to come in, so they take you out to allow for the other group) so you have to be there real early in order to have a spot. The water is very shallow, so you'll have to either lay all day, or walk about half a mile to get to an above-waist depth. Overall well-worth the visit. Just bring plenty of sunscreen and hats, caps, whatever works because the sun hits hard. Bring plenty of liquids, as well.

reviews.title: Jellyfish beach
reviews.text: Stunning views. Stinging water. Got hit by dozens of invisible jellyfish. I'm sure it's not like that all year, but proceed with caution in September/October

reviews.title: Beautiful beach but during climate change it’s impossible to swim with soooooo many sting like animals.
reviews.text: Do not plan your trip late September to early October lots of agua mala that is like red string like animals that sting like jelly fish but you can berly see in the water  not visible like jelly fish. Locals say it’s because of the weather change but they won’t tell you what beaches have the most because they still want the tourist money.  If you don’t see everyone inside the water it’s for a reason. Very painful especially for kids.

reviews.title: Worst experience ever.
reviews.text: Beautiful to beach to see but not worth going there.My family and I just came back and it wasn’t fun at all.I went into the water and they just said to be careful because there were some jellyfish but if get stung just ask the employee there for vinegar.It was infested with jellyfish but you can’t see them. We were the first group to get there and I got stung really bad. I went in half way and run back out and ask the employee there to for vinegar and he said they had already run out of vinegar, he clearly didn’t care and just said it was not a big deal. The restroom were horrible too. I would suggest everyone not to bother to go there.The tour people just want to make business and don’t inform this until you are there.

reviews.title: Playa Balandra
reviews.text: What a wonderful place, we went on a tour and stayed for 2 hours, but what a wonder, crystal clear waters, the only thing you have to keep in mind is the jelly fish, there are many

reviews.title: Wonderful!
reviews.text: A wonderful beach that leaves you breathless by its beauty. Be careful because it can be visited only with a limited number with two shifts at 9 and 13. Not to be missed

reviews.title: Continue to preserve this beautiful heritage
reviews.text: The most beautiful beach in Mexico. Recommended in the afternoon timetable for the tide to drop... with wind and cold front come the bad waters. The only bad thing is that there are people who come in with music and that breaks the peace of the place and others with dogs that put the local fauna at risk (without considering the waste). But the place is still wonderful.

reviews.title: A 3 hour tour
reviews.text: Beautiful water and beaches. The beach was well regulated with the number of people allowed and how long you could stay. No garbage seen on the ground anywhere! Take your own chairs and umbrella if possible, but there are vendors at the entrance that will rent them to you. They also sell food and beverages. The wasps found the food quickly and were annoying, even if you didn’t have food. There are jellyfish. Due to the wasps and finding jellyfish the hard way we left early

reviews.title: Lovely beach, but I never forgot about the place!
reviews.text: Clearly, the best beach is Balandra Beach, BCS, Mexico. I went there on my last beach vacation in 2012. Someday I will go there again!

reviews.title: Lots of jellyfish + stingrays + no rentals of chairs !
reviews.text: Extremely beautiful beach. Crystal blue waters and the view is absolutely breathtaking. However, when we booked this excursion with destination services at our hotel (riu Baja California 😑)they didn’t warn us of sting rays and jelly fish (that are invisible) . I travelled with my 74 old mother and husband. I was stung several times by jellyfish it wasn’t Pleasant. My mother and I both have immunocompromised illnesses . So knowing this info was key so we could have been more prepared. Maybe worn a wetsuit instead of a bathing suit with swim shoes. We were told there is a place to rent chairs. It wasn’t open. And my god the toilet facilities were absolutely disgusting!! It would be nice to have park rangers or people who work here to explain things and guide ppl. Multiple children screaming cus of stings. And a woman was stung by a stung ray. Wanted to post this to warn others before visiting.

reviews.title: Incredible experience! Just go!
reviews.text: We had the most amazing experience! This beach is so beautiful and the water is so clear! When the tide is out the water is like a 5 minute walk away from the shoreline and there are sand bars you can walk to and areas in between you can swim in. The water was never over my head and I'm 5'4". There are two time slots you can choose from to go. One is from 8am until noon and the other is from 1pm until 5pm. We went from 1pm until 5pm. There are bees in the brush along the sand so try to avoid those areas. We just happened to get one of the umbrellas that were already there which was extremely helpful as the sun was very bright and hot, and the one we brought from our air b&b was broken. This was an incredible experience! You can see the fish in the water! Bring snacks and drinks for the day and don't forget sunscreen. The sand is incredible and so soft we didn't need water shoes or flip flops. Highly recommend this place! I hope I get the opportunity to go again. It's free to get in too, but you do have to pay to use the bathroom so there's that.

reviews.title: Lack of information from the tour
reviews.text: The amazing views, the only bad thing is that we could not get to the beach, many badaguas and many people hurt. But hence a good experience.

reviews.title: Nice beach!
reviews.text: Great beach experience in La Paz. Come prepared for a hot day. Bring umbrella and drinks with you. There are some umbrellas but not enough abs usually already taken!

reviews.title: beware of jellyfish!
reviews.text: Beautiful view and beaches. Food and bar were perfect. lots of little jellyfish, got stung while snorkling and while exploring the beach, it must have been the season. not poisonous, just painful!

reviews.title: Visit to Balandra
reviews.text: Although we were in Los Cabos we decided to go to Balandra, the beach is beautiful! And very well maintained, the space is very spacious so you could not notice many people

reviews.title: Worth it
reviews.text: We went by rented car, in general I recommend renting car in La Paz, you do not need to be a van, you have to arrive early, I was car 18 and I could have a palapa, outside you rent chairs and umbrellas the same, bring food and drink, and floats, water gives for that. It is beautiful, in the morning shift the water is cold but at about 10 am it is already warm.

reviews.title: Dream beaches
reviews.text: We visited La Paz, very beautiful beaches, we went to Pichilingue, Tecolote, El Tesoro and we tried to enter Playa Balandra, but it was impossible, because there are established schedules and we had to wait 2 hours, so we preferred to take advantage of it on another beach. We will definitely return to visit Balandras and other beaches.

reviews.title: BEST BEACH DOWN IN MEXICO
reviews.text: This place is paradise, it is without a doubt the best beach in Mexico for everything it represents. Its organization, its cleanliness and its tranquility.It is light years from the Riviera Maya, if you are truly looking for a place to disconnect, to rest and enjoy, this is the place 100/10

reviews.title: General review
reviews.text: Sloop incredible place, we arrived the second shift entering at 12 on a Friday the quota is limited to 400 people there was space this time but don't trust yourself, incredible place don't stay in front spread out keep walking either to the mushroom or cross to the beaches of face it, be careful there are no shops inside, go prepared with your groceries or food at the entrance they will rent you umbrellas, chairs they will sell you frozen, apples and burritos no more, you may use the umbrella there are not many free palapas or natural shades, I recommend you take some goggles and/or snorkel there are many fish and even though the water does not rise more than 1.2 meters you will be able to see a lot of fauna, be careful at sunset the tide rises and it will simply pass the 1.2 meters, pick up your garbage don't leave anything behind it is a paradise that we must to preserve

reviews.title: Far drive, short stay, small nibbles and unforgettable experience
reviews.text: Since we were here in March 2019, it has become a protected conservation area. There are no fees to park or enter at the time of this review. The only cost is the restroom. We came on a Monday morning. There are two time slots. We came at 8am. We left at 5 am from Cabo and 2.5 hours later we arrived to get in line at 750am. Prior to entering we were greeted by a conservationist and shared:1. Please take care of this land for us, don’t rip anything or take anything from the area. 2. There are no fees to pay. Anything you pay is not related to us (them).3. Keep music down to a reasonable sound level. 4. Please leave it as you left it.5. Please exit beginning at 1145am. 6. Follow the parking attendant instructions when you arrive. (A short distance from the entrance).It was an amazing experience and yes you will get nibbled by small fish. The feeling can be described as a little more than a mosquito bite.

reviews.title: Bad bacteria in the water
reviews.text: The beach is absolutely beautiful to look at however there's some kind of bacteria in the water that if it attacks you it feels like multiple needles punching your skin and it is quitepainful. It wasn't fish bites, my rash was on large area of the skin. I got attacked instantaneously on both legs on the entire surface area that was under water.

reviews.title: Pacific in the Pacific Sloop
reviews.text: One of the best beaches I have visited and I think it is excellent that they have schedules and access control for your protection.

reviews.title: The best beach in Mexico
reviews.text: La Cueva Beach, one of the seven beaches in Balandra Bay. The most beautiful beach in Mexico. It is advisable to arrive by sea, it is very calm and pleasant, without waves.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: It's worth the wait. The place is very nice, clean and has little capacity, in fact they control it. Walking to the mushroom stone on the beach is the best. The sea water, the colors, the views EVERYTHING IS WORTH IT. Super recommended.

reviews.title: Beautiful and wonderful beach.
reviews.text: One of the best beaches in Mexico, the bad thing is that there is restricted access, we entered the 8 o'clock shift, for this we arrived at 7:00 and there was already a line waiting, but it is totally worth it, it is 4 hours that you They are perfect to get to know the beach well and go up to the viewpoint to take photos. The beach, no matter how many times you go into the sea, never goes beyond your waist, perfect for small children and people who don't know how to swim or are afraid of the sea. There are no vendors so you have to take drinks and food, there are only public bathrooms that are voluntary cooperation. A must-see if visiting La Paz.

reviews.title: Ideal for relaxation and children.
reviews.text: A beautiful place to coexist with nature, it is a collection of ecosystems in one place. Ideal for younger children as the water height is very low, as well as for good photographs and relaxation. If you are looking for fun it is not your option.It is a reserve so access is controlled, they do not sell food, you must take out your trash, follow the directions and respect the fauna. It is recommended to arrive early because it can fill up, it has limited space and the stay is 4 hours.

reviews.title: No RVs allowed at Balandra Beach!
reviews.text: To get into Playa Balandra there are two entry slots: 8 am to 12, and 1-5 pm. Cars line up outside the entrance in a dirt road to the right if the entrance road. Today we arrived at 11:30 am and got in line for the 1 pm slot. There were already about 40 cars already lined up. They let a max of 450 people in so we were glad we had come early. After waiting 1.5 hours we got to the front and they would not let us in. Our RV is 24 feet long and they said no RVs. We were super disappointed because we had not read this anywhere. Left and went to Tecolote which is beautiful too.

reviews.title: Sloop
reviews.text: Beautiful beach! a paradise like few others! You have to arrive earlier because access is controlled... but it's worth the wait, it's beautiful!

reviews.title: A show
reviews.text: It is truly one of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico. I loved that the local people take great care to ensure that people do not litter, the beach is clean. You see little fish. I had to go on Holy Thursday and they only let in 450 people in 2 shifts from 8 am to 12 pm and from 1 pm to 5 pm, we had to queue to get in, I liked it because this allows the local people not to lose control of the place.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: The most beautiful beach I have ever visited. Everything well organized and safe. Services like kayaks are at a great price and the hosts are friendly. Highly recommended for families

reviews.title: A paradise 20 minutes from La Paz BCS
reviews.text: A unique view and beach that I had never experienced before, recommended if it is your first time in La Paz BCS. Controlled entries at 8:00 am and 1:00 pm,

reviews.title: Incredible beaches
reviews.text: One of the best beaches to visit in Baja California Sur, to be precise in the city of La Paz, highly recommended to go with family, friends or partner

reviews.title: Don't miss this while in La Paz
reviews.text: Beautiful shallow water cove. The pictures don't do it justice. Limited amount of visitors in each time slot from 8-12 and 1-5 so get there early.  This was our first visit and we enjoyed it immensely.  Next time we plan on renting one of the kayaks and going to one of the several secluded beaches across the bay.

reviews.title: Incredibly unique beach spot
reviews.text: Otherworldly! So thankful for the tip we were given about this beach. Words and photos can’t really do it justice. So beautiful and though it can get crowded, we went on a Saturday and there were several spots that felt like you were on a secluded, completely private beach. Do the short hike up for the 360 views then enjoy the beach and walking far out into the shallow, crystal clear water. Beautiful experience we will cherish forever!

reviews.title: Pristine
reviews.text: This little piece of paradise is exquisite to look at. However, very touristy with time slots for your visit so be careful to check these out. Water is fresh , really cold in the morning before the sun really heats you up. Other than kayaking not a lot to do so take a good book to relax. Very shallow waters all the way across. First on the beach will grab the free huts otherwise grab/take an umbrella because it does get very hot. Worth the 30 min drive out of town and does have plenty of hiking trails where you can view the entire area from above. It really was picturesque.

reviews.title: Stunning beach with color
reviews.text: Spent the day here with the family. Short taxi ride from La Paz.  Beautiful beach. Super shallow so it's great for kids to swim. Unfortunately there's no services or washrooms in the parking area.

reviews.title: Clear water and beautiful views
reviews.text: Balandra beach is beautiful and not to be missed! We arrived early and secured a palapa--this or an umbrella is really necessary. The sun is hot! As the tide went out, you could walk across the bay and the water was clear. So beautiful! We also hiked the path to Tecolote beach, which had amazing views.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach make sure you come when tide is in...
reviews.text: Would give it five stars if we went when tide was in. Recommend checking that before leaving. Had no problem getting in mid week for the 1pm, showed up at 12:40pm.

reviews.title: Beautiful place
reviews.text: Very nice experience. I wasn't very clear about the way to enter, so we arrived at 11:30am and they told us that we had to line up to enter for the 1pm shift, so we did. Finally we arrived and it is a very beautiful beach, the water reaches your knees at most. It is a super instagrammable spot. The only thing I didn't like (which has nothing to do with the organization of the entry) is that you go down the road and when you enter to the right there are people who stop you "as if to ask you for your entry information" and the only thing that They do is want to sell you everything they have. For the tourist or local visitor it is something very uncomfortable.

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach - a must see
reviews.text: Worth the visit.  You may need to park and walk in so be prepared.  Very busy beach with lots of people around so try to go early.  Gorgeous views, and worth the drive to get there.

reviews.title: Stunning beach
reviews.text: Part of a swimming with whale sharks tour we did. We stopped at Balandra for lunch. Stunning, stunning beach with fine white sand and clear, clean waters. The part we were on could really only be accessed by boat so it was completely deserted. The beach is protected and they are rightfully careful about how many people can visit each day.  Try and go, it’s so worth it!

reviews.title: Beautiful Balandra
reviews.text: Pretty beach and worth the effort. The area is so shallow that swimming is limited. They do have 2 person kayaks for rent which was a fun way to explore. Take a picnic!

reviews.title: AMAZING!
reviews.text: Worth the visit!  As has been stated, plan to arrive early prior to your entry time.  Amazing sandy beach and wading in the water is special. Rented a 2 person kayak for 400 pesos(cash only) and was worth it. Recommend doing the short hike to viewpoint for excellent photo ops.

reviews.title: Very good experience
reviews.text: Superb beach. Limited time on site. We came a little before 12 p.m. and were advised to return around 1 p.m. In fact we were able to get the luggage at 1:30 p.m.Fixed parasols on site but it may be necessary to rent one from the rental companies on site.Water not always turquoise blue, rather green for us, but came a few days after the passage of a hurricane

reviews.title: Beach time at Balandra!
reviews.text: Go in the morning shift to avoid long lines! The beach is pristine! The agency (state/gov?) that runs the beach does a great job! To keep it clean and enjoyable they allow access in two shifts, 8-12 and 1-close. The long crescent beach allows for spreading out to enjoy the sun. The water is shallow and clear. You can rent Kayaks and/or SUP to paddle around. There is a trail to a view point above the beach which is easy to moderate depending on your age and physical fitness.

reviews.title: Disappointment at Playa Balandra
reviews.text: 12/26/23 we paid for the local bus to Playa Balandra and upon arriving at the gate around 1pm, were told that  the beach was at capacity and no more persons allowed for the rest of the day. Nowhere, in anything  I had read in TripAdvisor comments and other “local, about” Playa Balandra comments, nor from asking locals for info, was it mentioned that one could arrive there and be turned away.Beware.

reviews.title: The best beach
reviews.text: One of the best beaches in the world. I recommend it to anyone who wants to discover a new beach and environment. The sun and atmosphere are very cool

reviews.title: My visit to Balandra
reviews.text: Incredible place. Spectacular views, we enjoyed it a lot, I loved it!!! Highly recommended for everyone.

reviews.title: Chill beach in a beautiful location
reviews.text: Natural protected area that's excellent for relaxation.  We chose the early entry time at 8am. No fee to enter.  We rented an umbrella for 300 pesos from a group selling them at the entry gate (while we waited in line for the gate to open). The 10 or so free palapas fill up fast - so if you aren't in the first few vehicles to enter - bring your own shade.   High tide was at 7am this day - so entering at 8am was ideal. We got in to almost waist deep. By 11am the water in the bay was very shallow.  We walked over around the corner (along the shore or in the water) towards the Mushroom Rock. There was a line to take pictures with it - so we just looked from a distance. It was deep water and nice on the opposite bay from Balandra - so definitely recommend going over there to look.   No one selling anything on the beach was nice. The toilets are available for a donation. Overall a chill spot that's a must-see when visiting La Paz Mexico.

reviews.title: Beautiful!  Do the view point hike for sure.
reviews.text: This beach is open 8-12 and 1-5.  We got there about 10 and went to the beach and the overlook.  We left at 1130 and there was already a line for the afternoon time.  Bring water sandals.  The rocks are sharp.  You may want sneakers for the overlook. There is a dry toilet.  And they sell water and umbrellas at the front entrance.

reviews.title: A dream place
reviews.text: The place is incredible, we arrived at 8:10, we passed quickly, we climbed the pig to appreciate the wonderfulness of this place.

reviews.title: LANDSCAPE
reviews.text: It is a very interesting option to visit in the La Paz area, there are two visiting shifts at 8 in the morning and at 1 p.m.It has a capacity of 400 people per visit.It is undoubtedly very interesting to go up to the viewpoint, which allows you to have a complete view of the area.To go to the Hongo area, you either go by water or rent a rowboatBoth options are valid since it has no depthThe place does not have any bar so you have to bring water or drinks, as well as umbrellasIf you have very well-kept bathroomsIt is definitely worth a few hours of your time.

reviews.title: Fun tour for couples
reviews.text: It was very cool and fun, I recommend not bringing things unless you leave them in your car or if it's a tour, only take what is essential.

reviews.title: A must if you visit Los Cabos
reviews.text: We went by car from Cabo San Lucas, if you don't know it I recommend activating the GPS, in the same way we bought everything we needed to take to the beach, it is almost the last one and there is nothing around it but desert and more sea.They did not charge us any access, they only told us that they do control people's access, we entered in the second hour, they allowed us access at 12:30 pm and we could stay until five, there are dry bathrooms and they only ask you for a tip, there is Umbrella rental, forced to go to the sloop mushroom which is about 100 meters from the entrance. We went up to the viewpoints and it was an incredible view.

reviews.title: Please HELP the  stray dogs
reviews.text: Balandra is amazing. But it is located in the middle of nowhere and there are 4 or 5 stray dogs that were abandoned there . The people who take care of the place feed them (as much as they can) but it’s not enough and they do look malnourished so if you can, please take some food and fresh water for them.  This place is just magical, as shown on the pictures. The view from the top is amazing. The beach itself might get a little crowded but if you walk a little further down (take an umbrella with you)  you can probably get a nice stretch of beach to yourself.

reviews.title: Fantastic beach! Must see!   BYO Everything
reviews.text: Balandra is a set of 7 beautiful and pristine beaches.  It is a MUST see in the area, so try to go at least once while staying in La Paz.  We got on the line for the afternoon session (1pm-5pm)  at about 11:35am. It was a Saturdays, so probably one of the busiest days.  We were maybe the 15th car in line at that point.  They let us in around 12:40pm.  You want to get there early if you aren’t bringing your own umbrella, so you can snag one of the free palapas.  This would be a long afternoon without any shade.  Honestly, it’s best to travel with your own umbrella in this region, as most of the beaches either have limited palapas or charge for their use.    We got the fist palapa by the rock formation, and it was such a beautiful spot everyone invaded our space in order to get their Instagram photos, or get by to wade over to the mushroom rock.   I don’t blame them, bc it was a great spot.  Just a little annoying at times (there was a lack of personal space.  So, if you want to be undisturbed, don’t choose that first palapa.  There is no cell service and no facilities there, so bring a cooler with ice, drinks and any food you need.  The water is crystal clear and the sand is white.  The water isn’t very deep, even during high tide.  Check the tide schedule before you go, bc I think its waaaay better at high tide.  I swam across to the beach directly across the water and back (about 1/2 mile each way). There was only an area in the very middle where the water was just over 6ft deep during high tide.  We went once, and that was enough bc there are so many other beaches to see that you don’t have to wait on line to get in to.  Playa Tecolote is very close to there and is an awesome beach for swimming and chilling out.

reviews.title: The early morning and the wait to enter is worth it, beach ecology.
reviews.text: You have to arrive early because they only let in 450 people from 8 to 1 and others from 1 to 5, you have to bring whatever you are going to eat, because they don't sell anything, but everything is beautiful.

reviews.title: Worth the wait
reviews.text: You can’t come to La Paz and not visit Balandra. If you are going to drive your own car make sure to arrive no later than 7:25 as anyone arriving after that runs the risk of not being let in. If you want to have an Uber drop you off, they charge between $250 and $340 pesos to take you. Make sure to arrange for them to pick you up as well. If you arrive by Uber or taxi, take a photo of the last car in line when you arrive as that will be your spot in line. People without cars stand and wait by the gate. Don’t forget to take the picture because they will make you walk back from the gate if you do not have the picture taken. Also keep in mind that not everyone gets in right at 8 am as they have to tell each group of people the rules before they enter the beach. We arrived by Uber at 7:30 and got in by 8:30There is minimal shade once you get in and no food or drinks. Make sure to come prepared. We bought an umbrella for shade and it has come in handy on all days at the beach as it is super hot pretty much every day in August. Make sure to secure your umbrella as the wind gust can blow them away if not done correctly. The water is very shallow and you can see many fish swimming around you. Make sure to drag your feet while walking to avoid stepping on manta rays and startling them. I only saw one and I was in the water for about 2 hours. Overall, don’t expect a beach with people trying to sell you stuff and get a bunch of money from you. The 3.5-4 hours will fly by if you are well prepared so enjoy your time!

reviews.title: Not worthy the long lines to enter
reviews.text: Unfortunately you have 2 shifts for enter and they only allowed 400 people each turn the beach is clean but no service at all they  have ,expensive rental of chair and umbrella is only business for them ,the bath room don’t have water and aré smelly  by the way you have to pay for use ,only  recommend it for short time staying there  not for spending the entire day there and relaxing

reviews.title: Balandra Beach
reviews.text: Nothing compares to this pristine beach. Try arriving 2-3 hrs before your entry time and bring gear, snacks, and plenty of drink.

reviews.title: Beautiful but be aware of your surroundings.
reviews.text: A lot of work! We heard amazing things about this beach. We decided to come up from Cabo and stay the night in La Paz so we could experience this beach without getting up at the crack of dawn. We brought an umbrella, a cooler with snacks and drinks. We left the hotel around 7 am and drove 30 minutes on a Monday morning to wait in line. Luckily we got in and were excited! Unfortunately, many people do not know how to secure their umbrellas and the wind gusts tossed two umbrellas at us. One struck my 7 year old in the head after nailing and inverting our umbrella first. Very scary! The woman who this belonged to came over as I was comforting my daughter  who was more scared than hurt thankfully and my husband was holding her umbrella while checking our the damage to ours and said "which one is mine"? Um duh the one that isn't still in the ground? How about are you ok?? I said yours is this loose one that hit us. She took it back down to her set up and proceeded to set it on the sand again without any attempt to secure it along with 2 other umbrellas she had haphazardly secured  by pushing backpacks around the pole. After my husband took ours apart and re-assembled it, he went down there to ask her if she needed help securing the umbrellas and showed her how to use the screw end to twist them into the sand and how to use the umbrella bag as a weight by filling it with sand and anchoring the umbrella to it. We didn't want those things coming our way a second time. All over the beach people were loosing umbrellas so watch out if it is a windy day. We had no idea about the umbrella danger. We were fully prepared for the baja shuffle to avoid being stung by a ray but the umbrella situation was a new one. Also, my older daughter was stung by something in the water. Looking at another post, it could be tiny jellyfish. It was not too painful and left a small red bump. What was a little alarming were the long dark shadows swimming in the shallows. We wondered if there were eel around? We didn't want to look too closely and came in from the water until they left the area. We brought tubes and felt most comfortable floating on those and keeping our feet up and out of the water. Would we go back? Yes... but from a boat tour most likely. It would be nice to have information about what we were in the water with.  It is a beautiful site to see but surprising how much trash was on the beach. We picked up many plastics, napkins, bottle caps and I found two pieces of broken glass as well. Why not charge a bit and have the area cleaned up with this many people oblivious people around?

reviews.title: Worth all the Hype, DO NOT buy a pass online to visit.
reviews.text: There is no charge to enter, we were scammed by the Cortez Club into buying “parks pass”. The beach is breathtaking. You are able to see the fish and walk along them. The early birds get the “palapas” aka the shaded canopies. We rented a paddle board for $20 bucks an hour. We did see puffer fish in July, be careful where you step. The bathroom situation is odd. Bring coins and expect to use a dry toilet. If you go #2, you sprinkle limestone over it. If you are going from Cabo, go during the week.

reviews.title: What a view and welts
reviews.text: Get there early!  As of July 2023 they only allow 400 people in at 8:00am and then clear the beach to allow the next shift at 1:00pm.  Some people sleep overnight just to ensure a spot to be let in line. Beautiful beaches and water. Definitely wear water shoes so you can walk around the rocks to the other beach which is less crowded.  That is also where you can see the famous rock structure.  Though the lines to take the photo op are long and there is no reprieve from the sun unless you float along the line in the water.  You can literally walk all the way out into the water and still be only chest deep!  Warning!!! There are little microscopic fish that will sting you incessantly!  They were not painful but very annoying.  We all have welts all over us.  Fortunately, they don't hurt or itch like some reviews state.  But maybe we are lucky.  So wear long shirts and pants in the water.  Definitely take time to climb the mountain for stunning views!!

reviews.title: Beach
reviews.text: Views were amazing and the water is so clear and warm.  Waist deep water throughout the entire area. You are also can rent two person kayak for $25 an hour.  I would suggest purchasing an umbrella for the beach before you get there.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: Balandra is beautiful!! It’s one of those beaches you have to at least visit once. We love to lounge and drink under the sun so this beach was perfect for us the parents lol. There is no waves in this beach my kids said it felt more like a lake they did few like it was a little boring for them but they still managed and had a good time snorkeling w the fishes. There’s 2 time slots from 8-12 and 1-5 they only allow 400 adults at a time they do not count for the small children. We rented a car a drive from Cabo and went in the afternoon and got there at 12:30 and there was already a long line of cars we were probably one of the last cars they let in. I recommend getting there an hour before, take your own food and drinks as there is no vendors inside. Before getting inside the parking lot while in line there’s vendors renting umbrellas and chairs as there is only about 15 palapas inside. If you can I recommend renting an umbrella and chair. If you will be visiting vegetal beaches throughout your trip it may be better to buy an umbrella ($30) for your trip. Would definitely come back again and stay a few days in La Paz before getting to Cabo.

reviews.title: Things to know
reviews.text: Amazing! Be sure to be there by 12:30. It’s free to enter the park. The parks opens at 1 and closes at 5. They only let a certain amount of cars in.  They have 20 palapas to use for free. First come, first serve.   They do have some for rent outside the beach.  You will not find any food or drinks inside so bring your own. Worth the trip.

reviews.title: Must see … wake up early
reviews.text: The beach is amazing. I was not looking forward to this trip because I heard of the line and the limit number of people they allowed. We drove from Jose Cabo to balandra, we left around 4:30 am and arrive at 8 am. We had to be in line for less than 5 min and we were allowed to get in. It is one of the most amazing places I ever seen. The water was clear and you can see the fish with not equipment. There are two schedules to get in 8 am and 1 pm.

reviews.title: Breathtaking
reviews.text: Beautiful views with clear water.  The hike is about 10 minutes uphill. Very easy to do, make sure you’re wearing proper shoes as thereIs loose gravel. I’d also suggest taking water shoes as some rocks can be rough/sharp if you want to get a picture with the mushroom rock.

reviews.title: Day trip to Balandra + Tecolote
reviews.text: Balandra is the gorgeous series of white sandy beaches with black cobbles. The water was shallow and crystal clear filled with lots of fishes (large orphies, surgeons, parrots etc.). The constant erosion of the coastline lets appear some unusual shapes like the "Hongo". Between Balandra & Tecolote, I walked for about 20min along the main road. I was surrounded on both sides with large rocky mountains filled with cactus. A cliché in TexMex westerns. I felt a sense of emptiness and silence. I can't imagine crossing this place on a longer trail. There were no shades, the spinifex rolling on the side of the road leaves you a dry mouth. I finally reached Tecolote.Tecolote is quite different, the place forms a series of palapas in very bad shapes. The 2km long beach had some black sandy patches and was constantly shattered by upcoming waves. It was winter, you wouldn't except much activity in that season. On the edges of the palapas, this place looks like a dumpster where American retirees and vagabonds would keep popping up. I still enjoy some melting fish tacos from a local palapa, the waiter was kind. I actually fell like in Bill Bryson books venturing in some remote yet inadequate place. The bus returning to La Paz came as a salvation.

reviews.title: One of the top 10 beaches in Mexico
reviews.text: Beautiful, shallow, warm, and not to be missed.  Great family site with photo-perfect turquoise colors.

reviews.title: Quiet! Peaceful! Worthy of visit!!!
reviews.text: Peaceful spot good for simple timespending on the sandy beach! Great for camping as you are surrounded by gorgeous mountain landscapes! There is bus picking you up from appr 11:00 till 17:45 up to La Paz! Many tourists arrive here by cars, bicycles! Nice place for kayaking! Excellent sunset views! Good spot for yoga, beach tennis!It seems like you maybe alone there but at the same time all necessary things you may need are nearby!Welcome!!!

reviews.title: One of the most beautiful places on Earth
reviews.text: One of the best beaches in the world. Must arrive before 8am since only approximate 430 people are allowed at a time. You will love it

reviews.title: Exquisite Beach
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I have ever visited, and I have been to quite a few.The water is sublime in the beach is clean with white sand.It is totally safe and luscious.He will not be disappointed

reviews.title: Beautiful beach overun with tourists
reviews.text: Beautiful beach which is being overun by tourists visiting for the day. Reminds me of Maya Bay in Thailand which also was overun by tourists.

reviews.title: Good times
reviews.text: I rented a car to get there and I was just in time , once the lot is full you can’t get to the parking lot ( unless your with a tour)- the tide was out and I presume the blue water would be more picturesque if the tide was in a bit, it was busy but there is a lot of spots - totally worth to check out :)

reviews.title: Walked for blocks and water only reached my knees!
reviews.text: So pretty and stunning blue water! There are trails to walk to other beaches which include a trip to the famous mushroom shaped rock (insert photo op here).  Suggest hiring a private driver as there are only so many people allowed on beach at a time.  There is one bathroom, kept clean by staff - make sure to tip them!

reviews.title: Crowded
reviews.text: I ran 8 miles there. For it to be closed. But they let me thankfully after pleading I ran a long ways to get there. Ran into the park. Low tide. Did not look like pictures. Over crowded. There are better spots in baja.

reviews.title: Nice spot for a beach day
reviews.text: This is a huge tidal basin the enjoy very low depth when flooding.  The park is closed when the basin is full and open when it’s out.

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: Balandra is a beautiful beach located in a protected area. The only way to get there is to take a boat tour with a company that has a license to travel there.  Most often he tour includes some birdwatching along the way,  snorkeling (extra cost), and time and maybe lunch on the beach.  It doesn't take long to walk the entire beach.   It is a nice 4 hour experience."Some say" it is the most beautiful beach in the world.  I'm not so sure about this.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: We went here to relax and eat lunch after our whale shark tour. It was a beautiful spot... not crowded and very relaxing.

reviews.title: A Wonderful Walk In The Water
reviews.text: The water was crystal clear and you could literally walk across the bay with the water only coming to your hips! I like that they only allow so many cars in at a time (8-12 and 1-5) We arrived early as they had turned us back the day before because we did not know there were limits and certain hours) The, “Mushroom Rock”, was a little underwhelming in size and you could see it was supported by steel rods. 😳There was a trail to the top of the hill beside the beach which provided great views. Glad we went.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: This beach is amazing! There are two entry times 8 am-12 or 1-5 pm. You need to arrive earlier as they have limited capacity if you go by car. You can also get there by boat. Bring water and food as there's nothing available there for purchase.

reviews.title: Even with lousy weather it was wonderful...
reviews.text: Crystalline waters, a feeling of peace and serenity, the ability to walk for a quarter mile into the water without it ever reaching your chest... Balandra Beach is a unique place. Even on a cold day (for that area very unusual) it was still wonderful.

reviews.title: beautiful and crowded
reviews.text: We went at low tide , a very cool large bay there were expansive flats with ankle deep to knee deep water. Cool worm poop mounds so probably fish come in a at high tide. Always a crowd local families mostly. Two entry times a day. if you want in at the 1pm time get there 12:30 or earlier. Try going up the road to Tecolokete Beach where you can have lunch , rent chairs and a short walk away is an awesome secluded beach.

reviews.title: Gorgeous Beach, worth a little hassle.
reviews.text: As of December 2022: Entry times are 8-12 or 1-5. However, you must arrive quite early as we passed by the line of cars around 1230 and it was (roughly) a mile long. There are limitations to how many cars are allowed to enter, and the parking lots are quite small. There didn't appear to be a lot of accessible parking if you have a disability-I think you need to arrive very early to obtain an accessible parking spot.We went right around the holidays (week after X-mas), so I am not sure if other times are better or if this is the norm. I've heard afternoons are most popular & would think weekends are also busier times. Other folks we spoke with said they lined up at least an hour prior to the opening times and were able to park. I am not sure how it works if you are getting dropped off by Uber or bus...We ended up hiking to the beach from an established path between Balandra & Tecelote instead of trying to deal with the car lines & parking. This provided lovely views of Playa Tecololito before dropping down to Playa Shiro. However, I don't think this option would be feasible or preferable for most. If you are accustomed to hiking & weather isn't too hot, just an option. The mushroom rock is a neat geological feature, although we didn't feel the need to stand in line for an obligatory photo. Water was so clear, and my husband did see a sting ray but if you "shuffle" your feet, they will swim away. Fortunately you can see where you are walking rather well. In December the water was not warm, but not so frigid that you couldn't walk/swim. It was a little bit windy on the day we visited, so I didn't fully swim...depending on your height/tide, water is shallow and main beach had a lot of kids playing safely. Although there are areas where it "drops off" and gets deeper further from the main spaces. The beach near the mushroom rock is a little less busy than the "main" beach which is near the parking. There are bathrooms at the main beach parking, although (as always) bring your own tissue just in case. I would just plan to bring everything you need as far as food, water, towels, shade, etc. Make sure you have "reef-safe" sunscreen and a container for trash. The space seems well maintained and is pretty clean, so help keep it that way.

reviews.title: Pretty beach arrive early
reviews.text: This is a pretty free beach with snorkeling and kayaks to rent. The bathrooms are very clean and off the main parking lot. They allow limited access in turns (8 am-noon & 1-5 pm) only 400 people at a time. Very limited parking at the beach. We arrived at 12:30 for the 1:00 turn and we were one of the last cars to park at the beach lot. When you pull up join the line of cars, do not waste time driving to the gate, they will send you to the back of the line. They have limited palapas for shade. Bring everything you need there is nothing sold at the beach (food, water, towels, sunscreen chairs. ). Check the fise table. We went at low tide and had to walk very far out. pretty hike up the hill and to mushroom rock.There is limited handicap parking.

reviews.title: Well managed National Park at Balandra Beach
reviews.text: Very relaxing and scenic. Just be aware that there are two visit times:  8-12 in the morning, or 13-17 in the afternoon. Entrance is controlled, and it is  free, but everyone must leave at the end of the above mentioned visit times. So no one is allowed 12-13 hours, and your car must be off the parking by 12 o'clock, and by 17 o'clock, respectively. This regulation prevents overcrowding. The walk to the mushroom rock is absolutely worth it. There were no food vendors when we visited. Bring your own food/water, or drive for lunch to restaurants at nearby (3km) Tecolote Beach. All very relaxed and enjoyable.

reviews.title: Must visit when in La Paz!
reviews.text: I did a lot of research (internet and YouTube) prior to visiting and am glad I did.  Go during high tide or near high tide (there are only 2 sessions to visit per government so timing the day is important). If you plan to walk along the beach to mushroom rock wear water shoes!!  The water was cold and it was a windy day but it was December.  Definitely climb up the hill!  The panoramic view is incredible!  The sand is very soft. There is parking and very clean port-a-potties that are constantly being cleaned.

reviews.title: GORGEOUS BEACH!
reviews.text: We were brought here after Whale Shark and Sea Lion encounter with Mexplore - a company I HIGHLY recommend!

reviews.title: Nice beach, hike a little. Bring a book.
reviews.text: This is a beautiful area with a shallow beach. The tide was out when we were there so had to wade a long way out to get to waist deep water. Nice to visit once but I won’t drive from Cabo again.There are lots of misinformation about entry. This I confirmed when we visited.2 entries: 8am-12 and 1-5pmPolice clear you out at end of shift. Open 7 days of week but first Sunday of the month is for locals only and yes they enforce.420 people per shift. They count! Only ~300 on the Monday we were there but long line of cars by 12:30. Let us in at 12:50We were not charged any entry fee.No camping here. Go 6 km to Tecolote beach for restaurant/bars/camping.No sign of the oil spill from boat fire that happened last spring.

reviews.title: A relaxing beach, highly recommended
reviews.text: I think I was there is an off season or something I arrived around noon. Parking was no problem, but I can see if it's busy it would be a major problem. I think they would turn away people. There was no problem getting one of the shaded spots. There are thatched covered small tree sized poles. On the pole are nails to hang things. There are kayaks for rent 350 pesos if I remember correctly, for an hour. I recommend doing this so one may see the whole area easier. There is a gravelly path that goes up a hill. I have a problem knee so I didn't go up the path, but that is a good idea too, if one likes spectacular views. You don't need to go up there to know it will be breathtaking.    The water was pleasnt. I wouldn't say warm more like refreshingly cool. I could've walked from one side of the bay to the other as the water never got deeper than my waist. I'm 5'2".
