I floated on my back for awhile just enjoying the beautiful blue sky, listening to the birds and children playing. It was very relaxing.    I would like to reiterate this is a protected beach, no garbage allowed. There are no garbage cans so make sure you bring bags to carry away your trash. You are welcome to picnic. There were no food vendors. Bring what you want, but it's calm waters so one won't be surfing, but paddle board, maybe windsurfing. There are outhouses with attendants who will give you toilet paper. One of the stalls is designated for changing or maybe that was just because there weren't a lot of people there that day. I highly recommend this beach.

reviews.title: Bring Food, Bring Drinks, Bring a Book (or something to do)
reviews.text: This is a beautiful beach. We arrived at 12:30 for the second shift of people and we were the second last car to get in! The beach was at quite low tide so we had to walk out quite far to get into any water to swim in. I have to be honest, there’s not much to do here except wade around in the ankle/shin deep water. We thought maybe there would be a food truck or kayak/SUP rentals or something but there was nothing! This is truly a picnic beach so come prepared with water, food, drinks and something to do. We were able to get a free umbrella area to sit under near the end of the beach but we brought our umbrella from home just in case. We didn’t need it but it was good to bring as we got the last “free” umbrella sitting spot.This would be a really nice beach to bring small children as the water is very warm and shallow. We were a bit bored after walking around for an hour so we left after being there for 1 1/2 hrs.There are a pack of dogs (4-5) that patrol the beach and we saw them attack a little dog that someone brought. Good thing it was on a leash and the owner was able to pick it up quickly. I would NOT recommend bringing your dog to this beach because of this.Someone reviewed that this beach is closed until Dec 2022 but it is definitely open!

reviews.title: Hidden Gem
reviews.text: Sparkling turquoise blue warm water that anyone can enjoy.  Shallow for much of the expanse, so great place for kids or novice swimmers.  May need to walk a bit further out to get a deeper water swim.  Free palapas for shade, pristine quiet beautiful beach.   To keep the beach quiet, there are now two "shifts" for visitors, 8:00 AM-12:00 noon, and 1:00PM-5:00 PM.  May want to show up 45 minutes or so prior to the afternoon shift to assure a slot.  WELL WORTH the wait.

reviews.title: Almost like a BVI beach
reviews.text: This is a great beach and clear waters, free parking but you have a morning window or afternoon window, they remove everyone at 12 noon. A quick 5 min drive and you are at another beach that has a few beachside eats and bars.

reviews.title: BEACH CLOSED til Dec 2022
reviews.text: BEACH CLOSED.  We've been to this wonderful beach before, but on this trip we've been told three times now that it is CLOSED until December 2022 due to an oil spill and need for cleaning.  We thought we would hike to one of the other beaches to the north, and the water and beaches seemed fine.  Didn't see signs saying trails were closed.  But while there a marine patrol boat came up and told us we had to leave.  They told another boatload of local picnicers and a sailboat in the bay to also clear out.  They were polite about it at least.  Authorities told us the beaches would remain closed until December.  Let's hope it doesn't take that long.  Tecolote beach further north was open and fine.

reviews.title: Wonderful beach, part of Whale Shark combo
reviews.text: White sand, protected cove. Nicer than any beach in Los Cabos (that we’ve experienced), with volcanic rock cliffs and a small sand dune. This beach is a one-hour boat ride from Cabo San Lucas and our captain brought lunch.

reviews.title: Excellent shallow beach to spend time with family
reviews.text: WOW!!!  That was literally the first word out of our mouth when we visited Balandra Beach.  We've been to beautiful beaches before, but not one that was shallow and crystal clear like this.  The water was warm and serene.  We had no issue leaving our children to play by themselves.  The big bonus was the being able to see different schools of fishes swimming around us.P.S.  Arrive early since they're still limiting capacity and there are two shifts when we were there.

reviews.title: World class beach
reviews.text: One of the best beaches around and even in Mexico.  Clear, warm water and beautiful sand. Worth the trip. A few changes until August 31  2022 summer there are 2 time slots to visit. 8am to 1pm and 2 pm to 7pm.  Get there early and wait in line in your car If you want a palapa for shade. If not, there is no shade you need an umbrella and bring drinks.  Music is not allowed. After the beach go check out La Paz downtown it's a great town, great vibe an amazing boardwalk where everyone comes out in the evening and hangs out.

reviews.title: Beautiful magical Baja Bay
reviews.text: Beautiful spot. Nice that it is now limited to 200 people per "shift". Very shallow water so not ideal for swimming, but you can swim if you go out a bit further.  Show up early to line up so you make the cut.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: The beach is so beautiful and relaxing, seriously you instantly disconnect from the world when you get there in a good way! it is totally relaxing and enjoyable! my 6 years old was able to cross the beach literally walking with my husband, so this is not a beach to swim. I was impressed by all the volunteers and citizen efforts to keep this beach clean and  beautiful! we got there from Los Cabos by car and it was pretty straight forward, we followed the recommendations of getting there early, as they control the number of people that can get in. In iMaps you can follow the directions for Tecolote beach, and then just take the left instead as they are pretty close next to the other. Everything we did to visit this beach was totally worth it!

reviews.title: Not what I hoped for
reviews.text: We read the great reviews of this beach and decided to rent a car and drive there from Cabo   I was hoping to swim at this beautiful beach area, but the water is so shallow for so far out, you really cannot swim there, just wade.Also,  the local police target the out-of-towners.  We were pulled over twice for “speeding” which was going 16 kph in a 15 kph zone!

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach
reviews.text: One of the more attractive beaches i have ever been to, the color of the water is so blue and clear and the only way to have access to this beach is by boat. We took a boat tour with Pita's tours and they provided a meal at the beach with refreshments. If you are in La Paz I would strongly recommend visiting Balandra beach.

reviews.title: Great views, beautiful colors, crystal clear water!
reviews.text: This place is magical! Great for kids as water is very shallow. We drove from cabo for the day, it's probably not worth it if you intend to just do this beach. We also stopped at La Paz and spent time there which made the whole trip worth the drive and money. (I liked the vibe of La Paz than cabo) :PBest getaway for anyone staying around La Paz or Loretto area.Few things to know before going -Beach has very few spots with shade, get early to grab them.Nothing is sold in the area so bring food and water with you. If you search on Google maps as Playa Balandra it shows a different spot in the downtown area. They allow people only between 8 am to 11am and at 12pm to 3pm.

reviews.title: The best beach day of our lives
reviews.text: One of the best beaches I have ever been to. Water was clearer than the water in Maui ! I suggest going by boat .The sand and water make you feel as if your in another world.

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: Prettiest beach I have ever been to. Such beautiful colors and shades of blue and so clear we could see the fish. I recommend a boat tour over driving there

reviews.title: Beautiful hikes
reviews.text: I visited Balandra beach 3 times during my stay in La Paz (I never had any trouble getting in). Getting there: I took the bus from the Malecon bus station (this bus stops at all the other beaches on the way as well). I'm very glad there was a bus option as I found ubers and other car ride services scarce in La Paz and still pretty expensive. What sucks about the bus though is that the earliest one leaves at 11am. It costs 60 pesos one way. You can buy a return ticket from the bus station or pay the bus driver directly on the way back. Last bus is around 5h30pm. The first time I went to Balandra, I took the bus to Tecolote beach and hiked to Balandra. The hike is absolutely gorgeous. It's about an hour hike with many picture stops. The hike is moderate, except for one short steep part down a mountain. At the time Balandra closed at 3pm, so by the time I got there I had to leave not long after. The 2nd time I went, I decided to do the same hike again, but this time starting from Balandra, so that I could enjoy time at Balandra beach first. When Balandra beach closed at 3pm, they still let me walk towards Tecolote. I walked on the right side of Balandra beach to the rock formations/mushroom rock, then came across the other side of Balandra beach (much quieter beach) and then came across the steep mountain that I had to climb this time (but since I'm afraid of heights, I preferred climbing it vs going down it). After that, I just followed the path all the way to Tecolote beach. I then caught the last bus from Tecolote at 5h40pm. The 3rd time I went, I got off at Balandra and spent the afternoon there. I hiked up the mountain to the right of Balandra Beach to see the views from the top, which were beautiful. It was getting close to 3pm and I didn't want to leave, so instead I walked to the right side of Balandra beach, by the rock formations and the mushroom rock, and hung out in that area until I caught the bus back from Balandra at around 5h30pm. Balandra beach is beautiful, but in my opinion to see the true beauty of it, you need to see it from a higher viewpoint, hence doing the hikes. Without doing the hikes, it would have felt like a normal beach to me. It is pretty cool how the water is so shallow for such a great distance. The water is clear, but to snorkel you would have to go much further in to get the deeper water. There are free palapas at Balandra beach. The water wasn't too cold for swimming in Feb. It's also a sheltered area from the wind.

reviews.title: You have to see it with your own eyes!
reviews.text: I think this is the most beautiful beach I have ever seen. And I have seen many! You THINK you've seen clear water, until you go to Balandra! It is worth the trip, worth the wait, worth it all. Please respect the environment and clean up your trash, wear safe sun screen, and leave no trace!

reviews.title: Beautiful to see, but not so much to do.
reviews.text: If you want to lounge by a beautiful beach, this is the place. The water is clear and about knee-waist level. As of April 2022, you need to get here by about 11:45 am. At noon, they let in the 1st 300 people. No services.

reviews.title: This is the PEOPLE"S beach
reviews.text: For those who may not know, Balandra was in danger of being developed with a hotel on site. It was the citizen's of La Paz that fought and won against development. Currently it is entirely monitor by local volunteers without funding for the government, so when you visit and use the ecological toilet, PLEASE make a donation, the local volunteers are using your donation to provide you with the toilet paper and the eco toilet. I was more than impressed what the citizen of La Paz accomplished by stopping development. I can see why they wanted their beloved Balandra saved, at low tide you can actually walk across to the opposite bays  in VERY swallow waters.No wonder it is loved so much, it is stunning!

reviews.title: Figure out how to get here!
reviews.text: No words for this most beautiful beach......    even the vibe is so relaxing so you can just take in the beauty.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: Awesome place to visit and spend a day.  I wish there were chairs under the umbrellas they have. It’s hard when you are older or have handicap to sit in the sand. The beauty of this bay/cove is an experience that calms the soul and provides an unforgettable experience.

reviews.title: High Expectations, Underwhelming Experience
reviews.text: Looking at other reviews, it looks like I am not the only one who found Playa Balandra underwhelming. It's beautiful to look at and a safe place for people needing a very shallow wading area. Lots of people lined up to take a picture with the Hongo Rock - a rock that looks like a mushroom. There are some nice hiking trails up above the beachs that give you great views with the occasional whale sighting. A team of volunteers offer bathroom facilities. New to the experience are entry and use shifts: one from 8-11am and another from 1-4pm. Beach patrols ask you to leave when the morning shift is over. You are expected to leave with all your things in your car and then turn around and get back in line if you want to re-enter. I suppose this makes some sense since it is a popular place. 20-25 palapas line part of the cove. From now on, I think Playa Tecolote or other area beaches will be where we go.

reviews.title: Overrated
reviews.text: I find the reviews overrated. This is a very isolated beach with NO facilities, no shade.  In fact, I would say its desolate. If you do go, bring everything you need. It's a 15 KLM drive with limited access. Better by boat. Good swimming.

reviews.title: Excellent crew and we saw a whale
reviews.text: We made a four-hour boat trip with Baja Protours on March 2 and had a great time.  The boat left at 9 a.m., and we were back at the dock by 1 p.m.  Luis and Alejandro were the crew and are an excellent team as they are informative and personable.  Snorkelled with sea lions, saw a whale up close and then a few hours on Balandra beach.  Great ceviche lunch.  I highly recommend this trip, and they only take six passengers.  There were only four of us, so it was good to have the extra space.

reviews.title: Amazing beach!!
reviews.text: I would recommend visiting by boat to avoid the car/people limits.  This place has great sand, shallow water, and lots of sealife!!

reviews.title: Beautiful Natural Beauty!!!
reviews.text: A must see if you are in La paz!  This is a beautiful beach that you can actually walk across to the other side as the water is only about 4’ deep.  Great for families to snorkel and explore. Some of the most beautiful and clear water I’ve ever seen. This is a local treasure and treated as such.There is no food service or restrooms here so pack for a picnic.If not, there’s a great spot to grab a bite just down the road at a GREAT BEACH called TECOLOTE which I highly recommend!!!TECOLOTE does have restroom facilities if it’s a necessity for you.

reviews.title: NOT AS EXPECTED
reviews.text: All reviews said to get there before 9 a.m. in order to score a palapa. We arrived on a week day @ 8:10. The parking lot was already 3/4 full & there were only 3 out of approx 24 palapas left vacant.Lots of tour busses dropping people off & overall  chaos. We lasted 3/4 of an hr then offered our shade to a man with his kids.All of this before 9 a.m. Totally not  what we were expecting...but now we know.We had explored the area the day prior & found a beautiful, turquoise water, secluded beach up the coast. That was paradise & exactly what were were looking for.Only hope Balandra can survive the masses.

reviews.title: Nice Quiet Tour Stop
reviews.text: We visited balandra as part of a whale shark tour. We learned from another hotel guest poolside that balandra is closed some hours and has limited capacity due to covid regulations- you must go early in the am to get a spot. Despite what you may see others doing you’re not allowed to hike the hills.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: Never been to a beach environment like this one- its a must see! Shallow gorgeous waters and beautiful views

reviews.title: Crowded
reviews.text: This place gets very crowded.  It's beautiful, just not very peaceful.  REcommend doing the hike to see both sides.

reviews.title: Amazing beach!
reviews.text: We landing on the beach via boat our On-Board-Baja guided Whale Shark Trip. It was stunning! There wasn't many people there and waters were pure turquoise bliss.

reviews.title: Best beach in the area
reviews.text: TripAdvisor has this Beach in two different locations.  We went to the wrong location first, 5 minutes from town.  Then we went to the right location, about a 30 minute drive.  We had to wait in a 30 minute line on a Wednesday afternoon to get into the beach area.  It was worth the wait and it’s the best beach in the area.  Crystal clear water and white sugar sand beach.  Great for small children as water is very shallow very far out.

reviews.title: Must see
reviews.text: Nice huge beach, most part are not deep. The access is controlled so if you arrive by car do it earl since the parking lot get full and you will have to wait for a parking spot, however, there is another parking place 1 Km away, so you can park there and walk.

reviews.title: Great beach!
reviews.text: We visited this beach on a week day at low tide.  Drove right in and parking spots were available.  Several people were parking at the path were you can hike up over to another beach.  But not necessary.   At low tide you could walk out at least a half mile to this beach which includes the mushroom rock.  It was a fun afternoon!

reviews.title: Plan and ahead and you'll have a transcendent time
reviews.text: No cell service, very limited parking. Very limited services, a steep and rocky hike to the top of the hill for the best views . . .  and that's what makes this place a glimpse of heaven on earth.  I found myself thinking that if I had a limited time left on earth, I'd want to come back here to soak up the beauty one more time.

reviews.title: Wonderful beach, part of Whale Shark combo
reviews.text: White sand, protected cove. Nicer than any beach in Los Cabos (that we’ve experienced), with volcanic rock cliffs and a small sand dune.

reviews.title: Incredible beach
reviews.text: Not to be missed. We went at low tide, which some have complained about; however, it means that you can walk much farther without swimming or wading through deeper water. This is convenient if you are not wearing swim wear. Hint: Wear swim wear. :)

reviews.title: Great place to hang out but lots of folks
reviews.text: Beautiful beach about 1/2 hour drive from town.  Drive is amazing through Cactus country.  Beach was much more crowded than we expected.   We did find a free palapa and that made it nice.

reviews.title: Cleo’s VIP tours, Balandara and La Paz
reviews.text: The highlight of our trip was taking a private boat tour with Cleo’s VIP tours! Two female friends spent $125 each to have a private motor Boat with an experienced Captain and a young Marine Biologist. The best way to see this incredible coast is by boat. They took us around for 5 hours! We snorkeled at a coral reef/island with sea lions and lots of fish! We stopped at pristine beaches with clear warm waters to swim. They provided beer, other beverages and delicious ceviche and burritos at our last stop - a gorgeous secluded beach. They pointed out sting rays and sea turtles. I want to go back! Find Cleo’s tours, give them a deposit and you will not regret it!!!

reviews.title: Cool Little Bay, but Too Touristy
reviews.text: I went twice, the first time on a Monday no problem parking at noon. The next day it was busier, but still parking was available when people left or at the overflow spot. None of the weird police or parking problems people mentioned before.

reviews.title: Nice beach with great view from tower
reviews.text: Nice very shallow beach. Best view is from the top on the other side of the water near the radio tower on the top of the hill. This is about 20 min walk each way on supposedly private property (but everyone is walking this trail anyway).

reviews.title: parking restrictions at beach
reviews.text: Stars are based on visits from previous years.  I wanted to let folks know that due to covid, they are restricting the number of people allowed to park at Balandra Beach.  We went last week and sat in a line of about 6 cars (on a Tuesday around noon).  They would let one car in for every car that came out.  This is probably good for the beach and makes it a better experience, but planning to go early isa good idea.  We decided not to wait and left.

reviews.title: Most beautiful beach!!!
reviews.text: Playa Balandra is my #1!! Water is cristal clear, the beach is clean and super relaxing. You can walk across to the other side of the beach without a problem. It’s absolutely beautiful!

reviews.title: Magical
reviews.text: Just incredible ❤️ One of the most beautiful beaches I’ve ever been to. Situated on the Sea of Cortez, north of La Paz this beach is definitely bucket list worthy. The water clarity is intense, the water temperature is perfect and the views are stunning. Limited services here…porta potties in the parking lot, a truck with a few fruit cups and other snack items. The worst part for us was the shakedown from the local police on the way back for a “traffic violation “. We would definitely return again but this time a little more savvy to the local police scams.

reviews.title: Police guarded/impossible to access
reviews.text: My girlfriend and I booked an Airbnb for an entire week and tried getting onto Balandra everyday at 5:00am. The police guard it and only let their friends in or those willing to pay a premium. There is much better/warmer/accessible beaches around La Paz.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: We used Baja Falcon tours, which we accessed right on the malecon, on the corner of El Arco hotel. They offered us a great price and it ended up being basically a private tour for my husband , me and my 2 young daughters. They were offering to take us to Espiritu Santo but we just wanted to see Balandra since it was closed from the road. They gave us our own unique tour to calandra, which was beautiful. They were also very careful and were conscious of the environment. The captain and the guide Felipe were very knowledgeable and let us use our time as we liked. They stopped at the famous Hongo rock formation for pictures and provided us with lunch at the beach. They taught my husband how to catch clams right off the bottom of the ocean and we even got to eat them at the beach. The whole experience was amazing, got to see some frogs, snorkel and enjoy the beauty of they beach and even met some sweet straight dogs at the beach. The beaches in Balandra are gorgeous and clean and clear. They keep it almost untouched and there are many fishes and sea life to enjoy if you like to snorkel.

reviews.title: Beach closed but the hike isn’t
reviews.text: I wish I had known the beach is closed due to COVID-19 and that there’s no way around it—trust me, I woke up at 445 am to drive there but was met with a health official before dawn who said I couldn’t be there. Instead to get a glimpse, due the hike instead that is about 1/4 mile before the beach parking lot. There’s a fence that says it’s closed but other folks are were walking right around it like I did. The views are stunning.

reviews.title: One of nicest beaches in all of Mexico
reviews.text: So beautiful, make sure you visit and get in the water.  The sand is fantastic as well and shallow water for as far as you can see.

reviews.title: Very nice
reviews.text: Clear water and its not crowded at all, the only thing its that I heard that there’s a quantity limit per day so we got there at 7:30am just in case, but it’s worth the drive.

reviews.title: Beware of the police on the highway
reviews.text: The beach might be beautiful, but beware of the police on the road to those beaches. They are thugs. They ambush you, invent an infraction and then they tell you, you can pick up your license next week, unless you pay now. That is of course the only option and it is expensive. We paid $200 and were not given any paperwork or any proof that we paid. On the plus side: they were friendly. Recommendation: when you see a police care make sure you follow the rules and pray.

reviews.title: Sand fleas
reviews.text: BRING BUG SPRAY!!! Got there at 6 am because of 120 people limit and got attacked by sand fleas. They are everywhere. I am chewed up, looks really bad. You cant hide. And you cant leave if you didnt drive. There is almost no cell phone signal, so arrange the pick up.Its a pretty place, but there is really not much going on. Water is up to your ankles for the most part, you cant swim there. I asked my uber driver to pick me up at 12. And there was more than enough time to take million pictures. It does look much better in the picture.

reviews.title: Perfection
reviews.text: We took a boat in (700 pesos per person) for a two hour tour. This is the way to go if you ask me. They only allow 200 people in per day, so people line up at 5:30am to get in. Screw that. Our boat left from a nearby beach, then we went to one of the seven beaches in Balandra Bay. We had a 700 foot-long stretch if fine white sand and clear shallow water completely to ourselves (8 people total) for an hour and a half. No, you don't get to spend all day there, but since it got insanely hot in the afternoons, that was fine with us.

reviews.title: Highly negative
reviews.text: Following an afternoon at a nearby beach (Balandra was limited to 220 people because of Covid guidelines) we were robbed by La Paz police on our way home just outside the city.  They pulled my wife and I over in our rental car on a remote stretch of the highway, falsely claimed we were speeding, 140 km an hour.  The primary cop/thief had removed his bullet proof vest, to which his badge and name plate was attached and left it in the car with his partner before approaching our vehicle, while demanding I "unseat" from the car and provide my driver's license.  He then told me I needed to pay him MX 12,000 (about $600) cash or go to the station and kept repeating, in Spanish, something about "maniona".  I told him we had to be on a plane maniona to go home and that we were running low on cash.  I countered at $100; then he a $300; I at $200; he insisted $250.  Only then, after yelling at my wife who started taking photos on her Iphone while sitting in the car and threatening to take us both to the station, did he return my license and release us.  Attached is this armed thug's photograph.

reviews.title: Balandra Beach
reviews.text: Lovely calm waters not very crowded.  Would definitely go back.Some rocks but mostly sand. The day we were there no waves so easy to get into the water

reviews.title: Only sunset
reviews.text: Sunset views are the best. Before and after sunset, some bad characters might wish to sell you or try to rip you off. Those bad people are the off putter about this beach.

reviews.title: superb beach !
reviews.text: Our boat stopped on Balandra beach for lunch after 2 Scuba dives.This a beautiful  spot to chill or snorkel

reviews.title: beautiful
reviews.text: This has to be one of the best beaches in the world. worth the trip.  It's a bit of a drive from La Paz, take your time,enjoy

reviews.title: The most memorable and beautiful beach in Baja
reviews.text: I was told by numerous locals that Balandra is a must see when in Cabo. Although it was approx 2.5 drive, it was well worth it! You must arrive by 6am (although) I feel it depends on the season, day, etc. However, I did not want to miss the opportunity, It was probably one of the most surreal and tranquil beaches I have ever visited. I love the protection it has against industrialization. It was picturesque and felt like untouched territory. We were able to see the infamous mushroom tree and walk across the beach to the other side. A few tips before traveling, make sure your car is full with gas (mine was not & the nearest gas station was 30 min away). Bring food & drinks, there are no vendors except a small truck that I think sales small things like soda and snacks. There is a porta potty bathroom that you pay a peso or so to use. I would definitely bring the chairs that are low so you can lay in the middle of the water. It is a beautiful experience and there are palapas for shade.

reviews.title: A must visit.
reviews.text: What a gorgeous beach! Consider coming on a boat tour (we did). The main beach has a limit of the number of visitors allowed each day. But if you come by boat tour, you’ll get to visit the other side of the bay, and the entrance limit won’t apply to your party.  And most tours include lunch, which is a bonus!

reviews.title: Bad experience.
reviews.text: Bad experience. 40 minutes away from La Paz, it was closed. They open at 5am, and allow only 120 visitors per day. At least the road to Balandra is nice. There is a lack of information available online about the restrictions, so I hope this post can help you and save you the trip there.

reviews.title: Perfect!!
reviews.text: Soft white sand, turquoise waters..clean..authentic Mexican/Spanish/Latin music playing, free palapas, snack truck (reasonably priced). What's not to love!

reviews.title: Breathtaking in every way!
reviews.text: We arrived to Balandra Beach at 12pm on a Sunday and were told the beach was at capacity. So we got in line and wait. They said it could be 20 minutes to 2 hours depending upon how many cars came out and at what pace.  We decided to go down the road to another beach which worked out ok. We went back to Balandra beach about 3:30pm and went right in. I think if you don’t go extremely early then you will need to wait til late afternoon. It’s really worth the drive from Cabo and is a spectacular place to see. The water here is so clear and with small pools you can walk and walk for what seems like miles and just enjoy the beautiful views. The beach has been protected by limiting the amount of crowds and I can appreciate that since it was very clean. Parking is free and in a paved lot. Definitely the highlight to my trip to Cabo!

reviews.title: A little paradise..
reviews.text: I enjoyed Balandra beach so much, not far from La Paz but also the white sand, emerald/turquoise water, tranquility, marine life and way locals preserve it.. a place to anjoy..

reviews.title: Lives up to it’s hype
reviews.text: We kept hearing that Balandra Beach was one of the most beautiful in the world, but couldn’t get into it by road...we finally got there by boat, and now we agree - see it yourself if you can!

reviews.title: Beautiful- bring some money to bribe your way in
reviews.text: Got there at 8 in the morning and were told that they had already met capacity of 70 for the day. I begged as we had driven up from Cabo and really wanted to spend the day here, no budging at all. After about 5 min of all my sob stories I offered $20 for our 2 cars of families. That was easy! Gate suddenly opened and the rule of 70 didn’t apply.  The beach is beautiful. Bring sunscreen and water.

reviews.title: Breathtaking
reviews.text: Balandra is a beautiful bay that is composed of several beaches. It’s a 15 minute drive from La Paz and more than 2 hours from Cabo San Lucas. The beaches are amazing and with very little people. To go to the main one you need to arrive very early in the morning (no later than 6) to be allowed to enter and drive to it (as of December 2020, they were only allowing 120 people per day). In case you don’t make it, you can still drive to Pichilingue and take a boat from there. Depending on what you want to do, they can charge you from 30-35 per person to 60-70 (in case you want to snorkel) for an hour or 2. I recommend you bring snacks and drinks,  as the boat is allowed to drop you off at all beaches except the main one, which is the only one where food and drinks are sold. I spent time at The Hongo beach and thought it was simply amazing. The pictures I took don’t make it any justice.

reviews.title: Clear blue water!
reviews.text: The most beautiful beach I have seen in West Mexico just like the Caribbean. Sand was white and clean and too. I hope I can go again someday.

reviews.title: Best beach of the world!!!
reviews.text: Amazing beach!!! Out of the 57 countries I have had the chance to visit, this is for sure it is the best and most beautiful beach I have been to. The colors of the water, the different bays, the cleanliness, the protection of the beach to avoid crowds and damage of the nature is amazing.Please be careful to arrive really early in the morning (around 5am) because they only allow 120 persons per day. If you do not plan to arrive that early, the only way to enter is with a private boat tour from La Paz.

reviews.title: Family new year
reviews.text: Twice visited this beach with On Board  with Baja company. Great place, wonderful swims. Thank you to Victor, captain, Rosario and  Paolo, tour guides for historical and geographical information, biological update, great lunches :), and readiness to help with paddle boarding.

reviews.title: Relax and Recharge day!!
reviews.text: We arrived a day early to La Paz for our tours with Whale Sharks and Sea Lions, so we decided to venture out to some of the local beaches to sightsee and enjoy the warm weather.  Fortunately for us we awoke early in the morning and got to the beach  around 8:00 AM.  Little did we know at the time that they were counting cars and was not allowing many more after we got there.  The beach is so nice and the water is crystal clear all across the bay.  You can easily walk to the Mushroom Rock from the beach and we even walked across the bay to the other side ( it's a lot farther than it looks BTY).  Sand is soft and easy on your feet, but we highly recommend aqua shoes or sandals if you want to  get pics around the Mushroom Rock because the rocks in the water are painful if you happen to step on one or you want to get close for a photo.  Could easily spend quite a bit of  a whole day there, but we moved on to other beaches after about 3-4 hours there.

reviews.title: A Baja Hidden Treasure!
reviews.text: We have in Cabo many times but had never been in La Paz so we decided to visit it this time (it's the capital city of Baja Sur), the city was very calm and dwellers super friendly, it was a good and relaxing experience,The main atraction is the city is this beach called "balandra" where you can visit a landscape like no other you had seen before and even get a picture with a strange rock-formation with the shape of a mushroom, they calle it "el hongo rock" seing this rock formation is the equivalent of el arco in Cabo San Lucas (but in its own way), Balandra is an excellent location and a "can't miss" atraction!!

reviews.title: Beach visit by boat
reviews.text: Gorgeous turquoise water and white sand. All Natura terrain behind—not one invasive plant. Hornet fish and blowfish right up by the shore. Paradise.

reviews.title: Breathtaking but...
reviews.text: I arrived by boat where there are no limitations on MAX persons occupancy. Indeed place is beautiful but perhaps not my favorite, water level is so low and calm that it gets boring after some time. There are "funnier" beaches neraby.

reviews.title: There's a reason it's so famous
reviews.text: This beach is very beautiful. The baby blue and emerald-colored water, the peaceful ambiance, the white sand. This is a very relaxed, cool place. This is a must-see when visiting La Paz

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: We woke up today early and decided to take our chances to get in.At 8:00 AM sharp we were at OXO buying our snacks and drinks.We arrive at 8:34AM at balandra after a complicated way considering the construction at the road.We were lucky, they told us that only five more persons will be allowed considering the 220 MAX persons occupancy allowed.The occupancy is only once counted, meaning that even 10 persons get out they will not allow any one else inside. Is only 220 total a day. Our beach neighbor told us that they arrived at 5:00AM to be allowed to enter at 8:00So my recomendación: Arribe at most 8:00AM. We were very lucky, but a lot of persons were left out.It sounds too early buy you won’t regret.

reviews.title: Stunning and unspoiled
reviews.text: Pictures don't do this beach justice - social distancing and limited availability to access the beach is still in force, so go early! Take snacks and water as there are no facilities/restaurant or food service there. Take your chairs and umbrellas too, althogh there are a few available to the public,

reviews.title: Restricting to a very small amount of people
reviews.text: I imagine it was beautiful, but they won’t like more than a small number of people. The entrance is blocked by police. And I came there at 11 AM, but there are the beaches around

reviews.title: Balandra Beach during Pandemic
reviews.text: We went to Balandra Beach on Sep 14. At the entrance there is a line of cars in front of a road block. They allow a car enter once amother car leaves the area. Once you enter you can't drive to the Balandra Beach, you can only go to Playa Escondido. The beach there is ok. The local tour agency told us that the Balandra isn't closed but they only allow 120 people to drive in and it fills our pretty quickly in the morning. You can also take a water taxi from Escondido to Balandra Beach and it costa you 2000 pesos for 4 people (price tag at a restaurant at farest left side of Escondido. Hopefully this is helpful to whomever decides to go there.

reviews.title: Don't come to Baja California
reviews.text: Don't come to Baja or La Paz during the pandemic. Is a ghost town and the customer services are the worst. All. I mean all the beaches are closed. Near and far. I understand the social distances criteria. However, how I'm going to transmit the virus at an empty beach is beyond me. Save your money and go somewhere else.

reviews.title: an out of this world scenery!
reviews.text: exquisite location, if mars had water in the past it would probably looked like this, in fact this scenery looks out of this world!

reviews.title: THE MOST WONDERFUL BEACH IN MEXICO
reviews.text: Easy to get from La Paz to Balandra Beach, half an hour by car, taxi or bus.beach where you can walk for up to 800 meters with the water at your waist and 100% transparent full of colorful and shaped fish. Between 2 hills and a cliff is this wonderful beach where the famous mushroom-shaped rock naturally eroded by the wind is found.a beach worth visiting because it is the only one in the world like that, do not waste time and when you go to La Paz or Los Cabos go visit it is a 2 hour drive to Los Cabos, passing through Todos Santos town that you have to know too .Area protected by La Marina de Mexico with parking and eating areas. You can take any type of drinks, food and umbrellas for you to spend an excellent day. You can also camp as it is guarded and 100% safe.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach!
reviews.text: A bus from the local bus terminal will bring you here in 45 minutes.  It feels like you're in another world with the gorgeous scenery.  Bring food and drinks.  There are only a few small carts with snacks and water.

reviews.title: it is weird this atraction is not the number 1 in La Paz
reviews.text: this atraction should be the number 1 atraction in la paz, nothing can beat it, it is such a calm and beautiful beach with an otherworldly sense of tranquility, if you are from another country you will definitely love this experience

reviews.title: Stunning bay
reviews.text: Go early in the morning to avoid crowds. We were the only ones there at 8 am in a weekday. If you are fit, walk up to hill above the bay to take in the vista. The view is breathtaking. I wish we’d had time to rent a kayak.

reviews.title: Outstanding Playa!
reviews.text: I cannot think of a beach lagoon with water that looks so sparkling and clear. Our day trip out and back by bus was the highlight of our five days in La Paz. Go during the week to avoid crowds and snag yourself a free palapa. Absolute heaven!

reviews.title: Morning Kayak
reviews.text: Nice beach with a few amenities. We rented a kayak and spent a couple hours paddling around. Nice place to spend some time. Go early because the parking lot fills up.

reviews.title: Fabulous place, surprised at hectic scene
reviews.text: It wasn't so much the crowds, but the food concession and beach peddlers that disappointed me.  I went there expecting a pristine UNESCO protected beach, with no food or bathroom facilities.  We arrived complete with a cooler, towels and our own bathroom supplies. It was wall to wall people, with a much-appreciated entrepreneur renting out umbrella tables and chairs for 400 pesos as there is no shade, and 2 porta potties manned by a couple who dispensed 4 sheets of tissue for a donation, but they wiped down and sprayed after each use which was nice.  In all, the beach was an absolutely stunning experience and I am very glad I got to see it first-hand.  The rock formations there and on the highway were really cool too.

reviews.title: Balandra and tecelotes
reviews.text: Beautiful beach outside of la Paz. Head north up highway 11 and you’ll see the signs for balandra. It’s really easy to find. Follow signs towards pichilinque then to balandra. After balandra I’d you’re hungry cruise about 3-5 miles towards tecelote for food, drinks, another amazing beach with camp sites. They have about 10 beach restaurants.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Fun to enjoy the water and sun! Such a great beach for kids-- so shallow for so long. Just ok for snorkeling.

reviews.title: Used to be the most amazing natural beauty
reviews.text: There is nothing in comparison  to Balandra’s natural beauty, blue calm waters and the shallow nature of this body of water. However, over advertising it has made it crowded with visitors, bus loads full. The peaceful nature has been destroyed, but the beauty remains.

reviews.title: One of the Most Beautiful Beaches in Mexico but has Almost No Services
reviews.text: We have been all over Mexico and this is the most beautiful white sandy beach we have seen.  It is missing services and facilities which is a real problem.  Definitely worth a visit but Tecolote Beach less than a mile away is also very nice and has lots of facilities and plenty of restaurants.

reviews.title: Breathtaking beach
reviews.text: Balandra Beach is so breathtaking--you won't be disappointed! It does get crowded on weekends (we were there on Constitution Day, so like a weekend), but it emptied after 4 pm. Kayaks are available to rent, so that is very convenient.

reviews.title: A great beach but I went on a bad weather day
reviews.text: This was a cool beach , and I arrived via boat from La Paz. It’s cool to be able to walk in very shallow water for many miles with no waves BUT I will advise that my particular visit did not look as pretty as the pictures. There’s lots of pelicans. We did paddle boarding. I was cold and the ride there was bumpy. Wish I had not gone in February.

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: This is a gorgeous beach you can easily spend the day at. There are fresh fruit stands, a refreshment stand and a some people selling bread/empanadas. It’s worth a walk up on the hill for a really nice view! The water is quite shallow so you can walk around easily

reviews.title: Gorgeous and must see beach
reviews.text: This was my first time visiting this place and this nice and peaceful beach. The water is so clear, you can walk into the beach and water will just go above your ankles, and then by your knees. Nice place to go!

reviews.title: Balandra Beach - so beautiful!
reviews.text: We went to Balandra Beach at the suggestion of the owners of our hotel. We were in Todos Santos, so the route was to La Paz, then past it. Worth it!Parking was a minor issue, but we were there on a week day and I imagine it would be a lot worse on the weekend.But such a beautiful beach. Low tide meant you could walk half way across the bay! Be sure to walk all the way around the rock formations.There is a place you can hike up a short way above the beach for a spectacular view of the whole area. There are food carts at the beach. But before taking the left fork at the Balandra sign shortly before the beach, you can take the right fork which will lead you to restaurants, etc.

reviews.title: amazing place
reviews.text: playa Balandre is one of the most famous and amazing place on the earth, we were there early in the morning to enjoy the beach and the enviroment

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Wonderful fine, white sand beach. Hidden away a little and not overly busy. When the tide is down you can go out pretty far from the beach on some sand bars.

reviews.title: Paradise beach
reviews.text: We were lucky enough to get to see this beautiful beach. Not only by car, but also boat for a private lunch,on a whale sharks excursion .Where are Captain nearly caught a Mai Mai with his hands. Walk to right on Balandra Beach. Famous Mushroom Rock is on the other side of rock outcrop. Or you can walk over the hill. Gets a little crowed, and tide goes down. With no shade. Bring umbrella and pesos for fresh fruit drinks, Jewelry, Blankets and the bathroom. Road work on the way. About 20 min. from La Paz

reviews.title: Breathtaking views
reviews.text: Beautiful place to stop and take in the beautiful views! Climb up the cliff to see all around you or enjoy the beautiful shallow beach! We even saw people paddle boarding in the mangroves :)

reviews.title: Most beautiful beach in.the world
reviews.text: Balandra is just a must visit if you travel to La Paz, I personally went with the local guide Karen, she took us to an unbelievable hike and saw amazing landscapes, took us snorkeling wichh was a lot of fun, took us kayaking trough the manglar, set a camping and fed us with a delicious ceviche, a full day tour!  Her local phone: 612-1402857

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Stopped at this beach after doing some swimming with whale sharks, and it is beautiful, nice white sand, quiet cove, perfect spot for a picnic.

reviews.title: Breathtaking Bay!
reviews.text: Beautiful aqua marine water.  Safe, shallow, calm beach.  Great for famililes.  Bring your own food and drinks.

reviews.title: Day trip
reviews.text: A beautiful shallow water beach, emerald green water. The road isn’t the best but worth the trip. We drove from Cabo to La Paz 2 1/2 hr drive

reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.text: Beautiful place,. Two couples travelling together. The men hiked to the top and took pictures of the amazing views. Ordered lunch on the beach from Ceasar. Loved the 2hole experience

reviews.title: Warning its beautiful but full of stingrays!
reviews.text: The only reason I am giving this a low rating is so you may be warned that there are stingrays actually several smaller ones that blend in with the sand and they have the tiniest warning signs at the entrance of the beach so that they don’t scare tourists off but don’t get me wrong most beautiful beach Ive seen but even doing the shuffle in the sand you can still get stung by stingrays as I was and it was a terrible experience that has taken me almost a year to recover fully from the area of injury infact with the incident happen many tourists were unaware of the stingrays also please watch your kids its not worth the risk several locals informed us that happens more frequently then youd think even to the locals so if you go use a kayak and don’t risk walking because sting rays don’t always see you you shuffle because they hide under the sand.

reviews.title: Great beach if it's within a close distance
reviews.text: We drove 2 hours each way to get to Balandra Beach and although it was a beautiful beach, I don't think I'd take my whole day to do this trip again.  But if you are close, definitely visit.  Make sure that when you park, you realize that around the corner of the rocks, is a whole other section of beach which isn't visible until you continue walking.  The water was very shallow where we were but walked out to a sandbar and deeper water.  We snorkeled in open water and didn't see much.  Had we gone over closer to rocks (which didn't seem safe) there may have been more to see.

reviews.title: Fun place
reviews.text: This was a very interesting beach!  The water was very shallow, even at high tide, so you could walk around the point to get to the next point with the mushroom rock.  However, we chose to hike over the ridge - not difficult, and on to the next ridge.  We were rewarded with beautiful views, lots of flowers and cacti, and even a roadrunner (bird).  Back on the beach, there was an impromtu band playing (pretty poorly, but a LOT of fun) and vendors selling enormous donuts, empanadas, fresh fruit, and beverages.

reviews.title: Nice Beach Near La Paz, Baja Sur, Mexico
reviews.text: Take your own food and drink and enjoy this lovely beach about about 5  miles from La Paz.   It seems further.   Sadly  you need a vehicle to get there.    There are a few vendors and interesting group of beachgoers.    Nice sand, pretty water pretty clean considering that it's near the ferry terminal and port.

reviews.title: Balandra beach
reviews.text: Was a total let down. If this is a must see in LA Paz, don't waste your time the pictures did not look like the real thing. My wife had to use the bathroom, it was discussing, there was human feces all over the seat.  2 lady's where charging for toilet paper ane hand sanitizer

reviews.title: Beach Crowded, Location Gorgeous
reviews.text: When you go to Playa Balandra, be ready (at least on weekends) for a crush of people and challenging parking. The beach is crowded. Tha said, the beaches are also splendidly beautiful and are of soft sand. There are some steep, but not-too-difficult hikes up the headland that offer gorgeous views, if you want to be away from beach people and noise. Plus- with my natural history interest, I found walking around the edge of the mangroves delightful and peaceful

reviews.title: Daytrips to Balandra and Tecolote
reviews.text: What a beautiful place and thankfully fully protected from the development sharks to keep it a national treasure for Mexicans and travellers alike.Absolutely beautiful.

reviews.title: best beach
reviews.text: beautiful !  worth the visit, best not on weekends as it can get a bit crowded stunning water color , easy to get to

reviews.title: The most beautiful beach I have ever seen
reviews.text: This beach is definitely out of the way, but it felt like discovering a lovely hidden secret. It felt like an authentic, non touristy Mexico experience. White sand, dramatic bluffs, desert landscapes, the clear shallow blue water of the bay on the Sea of Cortez, families enjoying the day, street food vendors, and an absence of annoying drunk spring break types. I would definitely go back, again and again and again!.

reviews.title: Balandra Beach
reviews.text: Balandra Beach is a must visit for all.  Clear shallow water suitable for all.  Clean sandy beach a great place to spend a few hours or the entire day.

reviews.title: VIP tours
reviews.text: I went to Balendra on a whale shark/ sea lion combo tour with La Paz VIP tours. The beach itself is a wonder, where desert meets sea. Its right around the corner from San Rafaelino, a sea lion colony of about 70 animals that VIP uses as an alternative in January when the seas around Espiritu Santo get a bit gnarly. Crystal clear water and you can wade out pretty far and still be only waist deep on a six foot tall person like myself. If you have an AKASO, Go Pro, or other actiob camera bring it with you as you might be walking close to some very beautiful and interesting fish. Nice to see a beach littered with shells (among other things; I also found a triggerfish) instead of plastic. Not to be missed.

reviews.title: Awesome beach to relax
reviews.text: Amazing views.   Go early to find park g and a spot on the beach as it gets busy as the morning goes on.  You can wade in the shallow waters for ever!

reviews.title: Prettiest beach in Mexico I’ve been too
reviews.text: This is the prettiest beach in Mexico I’ve been too.  The only other part of Mexico that might have beaches that would beat this beach is in the Riviera Maya (where places like Cancun and Cozumel are located).

reviews.title: Spectacular beach!
reviews.text: One of the loveliest beaches I’ve seen!  Clean sand and Shallow clear, warm water for half a mile out. Fab vistas. You can rent umbrellas or a palapa and picnic all day. Calm waters- great kayaking or even swimming if you get to deeper water. Fruit/juice/ snack shacks and portable toilets. Parking lot gets full early but there’s a bus from town.

reviews.title: Excellent beach
reviews.text: Visited this beach twice whilst in La Paz. Such a lovely place to sit around for a few hours - take your own food/ drink as there’s not really much choice there. We hired a kayak and paddled over to one of the beaches on the other side of the bay. Lovely to have our own private beach for a while!

reviews.title: Crystal Clear Water
reviews.text: This is one of our favorite beaches in the La Paz area. The addition of washrooms at the beach is a huge improvement.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: One if the most beautiful beaches I've been to in Mexico. Lots of locals go to Balandra so there are families, couples and friends. Make sure and walk around to the right of the beach. There is more beach and not as crowded. You can walk in the water because its shallow for a long way. There were a few vendors there the day we went but don't count on it. Bring food and drink with you. The parking lot is small so get there early or park along the road. You won't be disappointed. Don't have a car. You can ride the Playa Bus from La Paz.

reviews.title: Must see and family friendly
reviews.text: One giant sandbar that allows you to walk to beaches where you will be the only one. Warm water that is perfect for wading and sitting and relaxing. You can venture out to where you can snorkel. Little to no waves so this beach is perfect for small children or elderly. No restaurants, but a food truck that served fresh fruit was there. The beach was not overrun with sellers peddling their wares, but I did see a few. No restrooms— just beautiful white sand and protection from the stronger winds. Thatched Permanente umbrellas available for shade. Picturesque and so worth a visit.

reviews.title: Incredible
reviews.text: The most incredible blue-green water I have ever seen. We stopped there on a whale shark tour with On Board Baja. Worth a visit!!!

reviews.title: Getting crowded
reviews.text: It was very sad to see that this magical place is starting to get crowded. The colors of the sea are unique and amazing. You can walk for many meters at the same hight.

reviews.title: Blue water, white sand, and You!
reviews.text: We were here mid October 2018.If you're looking for a non-overcrowded beach with blue water and white sand, then this is the place for you.We took the 40-minute city bus to, and and from Balandra.No restaurant.  No café.  There is a tienda(camper kiosk) that sells munchies and beverages.Bring a parasol and cooler for beverages & lunches/munchies.From this beach you can actually walk (via trail or shoreline) to the infamous Mushroom Rock.Enjoy your visit to Playa Balandra!

reviews.title: Stunning beach
reviews.text: the whitest sand and bluest sea the best place to while away a few hoursnothing there so you need to take everything

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Best if you visit by boat there are breathtaking places you can’t get by car!! We had a sailboat and the experience is just amazing you can swim with rays if you get near the shore.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: Beautiful beach! At the time of writing (January 2020) you can take the bus from the tourist bus station at the Malecon for about 150 pesos return. The bus leaves the Malecon every hour on the hour and departs the beach every hour on the :20. Beautiful spot and well worth a day. There are some small vendors selling fruit, water, etc.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: Such a beautiful beach to play on and have a lunch on.  Sand was absolutely amazing. At low tide you can walk across the bay.

reviews.title: the best beach ever!!!
reviews.text: this is the most incredible beach I´ve ever seen in my life, at this place you can´t miss the mushroom, dont go on weekends it is crowded, you can go on the rest of the week and early in the morning, you will have the beach just for you, the best season is at the begining of november the water and the weather is warm :)there are no restaurants it is a virgin beach.at this place I had My ring!!!!! finally :)

reviews.title: Beautiful scenery
reviews.text: Took a day trip from La Paz and came across Ballandra Beach. The gentle hike to the view spot was gorgeous. The beach is so pretty- although it was busy with a cruise ship group. Wear water shoes though!

reviews.title: Fun beach to explore
reviews.text: Even after reading about how beautiful it was, it was better than I expected. We took a 20 min Uber ride from La Paz that cost less than 200 MXN and arrived just before noon. It was a Saturday and it was fairly busy but still plenty of space to relax. There was hardly any cell phone service at the beach and no Ubers available nearby even when we did get a signal. There were taxis in the parking lot, but we managed to catch the  Playabus (which goes to/from the tourist bus terminal on the malecón) on the way home. It does come all the way into the parking lot for both drop off and pick up. 50 MXN one way. Don't forget to bring sneakers to climb up the hill and get a wonderful view. The prettier, less crowded side is over the hill or you can walk around the big rock cliff to the right end of the main beach. There were a couple vendors selling empanadas, chips, and coconuts and fruit. There were a couple port-a-potty style bathrooms in the back corner of the parking lot.

reviews.title: Be warned
reviews.text: The beach is picturesque and idealistic. Clear waters and cool breezes. However the sand hides a lot of sand fleas. Don’t lay your towels on the sand better to use the beach umbrella and seats you can rent. If you do get bites, please get some anti itch cream. Better to get it treated before it becomes an issue later. When you get home put all you clothes in dryer and run on high for 30 minutes.

reviews.title: Great sunsets
reviews.text: We are and wandered the shallows with our babe in arms.  Warm water and very safe.  Worth the short, pleasant drive out of town.  Check the tide chart before you go.

reviews.title: Beautiful but if you’ve been to Caribbean -pass
reviews.text: I couldn’t wait to go to this place because of all the rave reviews.  It was beautiful, but certainly not jaw dropping like some beaches in the Caribbean. I guess if we didn’t have to drive 2 hours from Cabo to get there it would be worth the trip.  I wouldn’t bother unless you plan to spend the full day.

reviews.title: Nice out of the wind but cold wa
reviews.text: This is a nice place not windy like Tecolote . Water cold, you can buy a coconut , there are kayaking there is a

reviews.title: beautiful beach not to be missed
reviews.text: The travel was long from Cabo San Lucas but all worth it.  Be careful with cows crossing as we almost got into an accident.  They have signs and believe those signs.

reviews.title: Once Upon a Time Gem. Now more like a flea market
reviews.text: the unfortunate downside of being beautiful and promoted = huge hordes of people.  Balandra is hardly enjoyable these days. And soon they will be building condos nearby.

reviews.title: Beautiful little piece of heaven!
reviews.text: This is a quiet and secluded beach. We felt relaxed and peaceful here.  This was part of a tour we took and we only stayed for about an hour and ate lunch.  But the water is calm and clear.  We thoroughly enjoyed this little piece of heaven.

reviews.title: Great expanse of shallow estuary with abundant bird and fish life if you paddle far.Great sunsets then Mosquitoes!
reviews.text: 14/12We three British middle aged guys were touring in BC in the first half of December. We had heard about this famous beach  and along with a Spanish friend took an Uber from our Apartment (200) all the way, taking about half an hour (some road renovations slowed us down for a bit but expect a fast road in the future (for better or worse).Arriving at about 2:30 we found quite a busy beach with stalls selling drinks and food next to the big car park. Lots of boats were anchored offshore too. There was plenty of space though and it was easy to find cool shade under the cliffs. After sorting our own drinks we took to walking across the estuary which proved very shallow at the time we were there.My Spanish friend found a puffer fish that 'blew up' when he approached it. I saw a 10 inch wide black and white skate zip past. The birds were the more interesting and visible wildlife though. Obviously there were the pelicans and herons but paddling right across to the other side of the bay I saw a couple of oystercatchers. The beaches there were completely empty next to the (set back) mangrove.On returning to my friends I went round the rocky coast looking for the sacred mushroom rock, expecting it to be a large part of the landscape. I found nothing. I must not have gone round far enough.A word of caution as the rocks are quite rough and even paddling you can scrape yourself if you tread on a rock. I am still suffering four days later with a cut little toe. Take care. The water is clear enough to navigate the rocks.The beach was remarkably clean compared to some I have visited in BC. The water was clear and free from polystyrene balls or plastic. It seems the locals and tourists do respect the area. Large bins are available in the car park, although no discernible recycling in place.Oh wandering round the rock cliffs to the right side I noticed people were still walking down the track over the hill to the adjacent bay and some had set up loud music systems which was a little annoying as it disturbed the peace and romance. The music stopped later after sunset although it was still sounding as the people left the beach.Towards dusk my Spanish friend wanted to quickly pop over to Tecolite beach the other side of the peninsula. As the sun set we found ourselves surrounded by thousands of mosquitoes! Blood was pouring out of bites and we quickly ran back as the passing bus driver laughed! It did not stop my collecting a couple of handfuls of litter strewn by the road though which I put in the big white bins in the car park before returning to my friends. It seems that the littering is a problem still where it is not enforced.On returning the sun had already set and the bay was dotted with ghostly figures in the golden and orange colours of the sky. It was all very romantic.Eventually we just had to go and rather than summoning an Uber from town half an hour away we jumped on the waiting bus, paid 50 each, at 18:15 and off it went, to Tecolote beach, the lights being turned off completely on the way so it was pitch black inside, picked up a couple of people and returned back to Balandra (lights going off again obviously to stop attracting Mosquitoes)! It then left at 18:30 promptly to get back to the Chinese Hotel Pekin by 19:30.On arriving back and looking up Dengue Fever it actually does occur in BC but in talking with locals it does not! We shall find out in a week when I am back in London!I also looked up the TA page today to see that the mushroom is not actually very big at all! I did not miss much.All in all this was a magical place and worth the excursion. We had gone relatively off peak and the car park was quite full. If it is peak time I expect it will be so busy!

reviews.title: Shallow bay with sandbanks, feeding pelicans and other seabirds
reviews.text: Shallow waters make this pretty bay safe and family friendly. Its a very large bay with multiple sandbanks so you can wade out for 100m at waist height, whilst watching feeding pelicans and other seabirds and gazing at fish and crabs in clear water.  The famous mushroom rock (hongo) needs a 15 minute wade out at high tide.  The sun sets over the bay is beautiful but be prepared to run afterwards due to heavy mosquito attack.... the nature reserve has a mangrove swamp. Buses run all day till dusk for 50 pesos each way, or Uber it for 200- 250 each way.

reviews.title: Shallow bay
reviews.text: Playa Balandra is a small bay 2 minutes from Playa el Tecolote.The beach is quite busy with tourists. Beautiful turquoise waters.It is very shallow so you can walk around in water up to you knees. Not many swimming opportunities though.

reviews.title: Balandra beach
reviews.text: Great beach.  Nice fine sand and very shallow water that goes forever.  Very  popular however and can be busy. Definitely worth the trip though.

reviews.title: Stunning clear water, beautiful color, and some protection from the N wind
reviews.text: The locals nearly all got off at this beach which was more protected than the beach Tecotote? At the end of the road.  There were bathrooms an dmore options to eat at Tecotote, but the locals much prefer the longer crescent shaped Balandra.

reviews.title: Totally in love
reviews.text: The most stunning beach I have ever been- the shallow Cristal clear water and soft white sand - go early because parking is limited we had to park on the road, no bars or restaurants so bring your own food and drink- still worth it. We have put our towels under the rock but you can pay for umbrellas if you want - my pictures were not edited so what you see is what you get !!! There is a disabled access but I have no idea where does it leads to - lack of Matt on the sand, toilets are portable type and lacking disabled ones

reviews.title: As beautiful a beach as I've ever seen
reviews.text: Great day trip from LaPaz. There is plenty to do here. Kayak rentals and food trucks make this a great place to spend the day.

reviews.title: Not too far from La Paz
reviews.text: This interesting beach would be great for anyone who is a non-swimmer!We even saw a woman walking her dog in here :)

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Really awesome spot. Took an Uber up there for a few hours. The bay is really pretty, and we brought our snorkel masks and saw lots of fish on the far end of the bay. Warm waters

reviews.title: Fantastically beautiful lagoon just minutes from downtown La Paz.
reviews.text: The largest sandy lagoon I have ever seen, this beach remains in my memory as a paradisical spot.  It's important to go at high tide - even then the water is very shallow and you can walk almost across the bay!  You can bring a picnic but there are some refreshments available on site, and some ambulant vendors on the beach.  The straw huts are free - amazing! - and the parasols are paying. Enjoy!

reviews.title: Our wedding anniversary trip
reviews.text: Balandra, amazing beach, speechless must visit if you are in Los Cabos San Lucas must take the photo with the mushroom rock it is just beautiful. clean clear ocean waters. from San Jose del Cabo it takes approximately 2.5 hours by driving your own car. bring your drinks and food. MUST bring water shoes since the entire beach is full of rocks. leave your  personal belongings in the bus, car or bring a waterproof pouch for you phone, money, keys. you must climb the rocky mountain and enjoy the spectacular view, it is out of this world.

reviews.title: Awesome Beach, but needs reliable restroom facilities
reviews.text: Balandra Beach in La Paz is an awesome beach and nobody should miss a stop here when they are visiting the Los Cabos area.  Even the drive to the beach is very scenic and enjoyable.  Parking space is limited at the beach, so go early.  Once at the beach, one should not miss the short hike up the hill to get a full view of the crescent shaped beach.  Actually, three such beaches are visible from the hill, though they are separated from each other.  Also, one can get a view of the iconic Mushroom Rock from the top of the hill, or one can get closer to the rock by hiking down to the second beach.  The water is pretty shallow and the waves are pretty calm making this is a perfect beach for families.  There several palapas, but again better to come early.  Kayaks are available for renting.  There were vendors selling some snacks, fruits and coconuts in the parking lot.  Restrooms are unreliable, if they are open at all.  This is the only drawback.  This awesome beach needs reliable restroom facilities.Balandra Beach is must-visit destination in the Los Cabos area.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach, worth the visit.
reviews.text: Stopped here for a short visit as part of an excursion. The beach is nice and the water is very shallow and warm. A must see if you are in the area, it was a nice treat when we couldnt swim in the waters at our resort. It was quite busy with lots of people but big enough to have your own space. Parking lot was busy. There was food trucks, but did not eat anything. Would definately return for a full day, the roads seem well marked to find this area also if you are driving.

reviews.title: The worlds biggest swimming pool!
reviews.text: What a really unique and cool Beach area. Balandra actually is several beaches in a Bay. The water is shallow enough to walk from one side of the bay to the other. So finding a quiet place to lay out isn't hard. There are Hills to climb to get a full view of both sides of the Bay and also serves as an amazing place to sit and watch the Sun come down. All the parking is free and public, so don't let the guys at the opening try to con you into paying for parking. I would submit pictures but apparently all my pictures are too big file sizes. Sorry!

reviews.title: Very busy, get there early
reviews.text: Arrived on a Thursday at about 1145 and the beach was already extremely busy and the parking lot full requiring you to park along the side of the road. Free palapas if you arrive early, otherwise, 400 pesos for a table, 4 chairs and Palapa. Only one food truck available, so best to bring your own cooler and snacks. There is also porta potties located at the end of the parking lot. Very calm water that allows you to walk out for some time and only be waist in. Nice beach to spend 1/2 day there.

reviews.title: We took the boat and the dog.
reviews.text: If you come to LP, this is a must see. Either Balandra or Tecalote. You won't be disappointed, and the food is amazing!!!

reviews.title: Nice beach, but...
reviews.text: The beach is very unique because it is shallow, the sand is very soft. We were there on a windy day, so the water was not the best. The "mushroom" rock has been repair and you can see metal rods in the base of the rock and some concrete patching it is not worth seeing. Also, there is nothing around this area so bring a cooler. There are some vendors in the parking lot selling fresh coconut and other stuff. The parking lot is very small so you may have to park on the side of the road.

reviews.title: Breath taking beach!
reviews.text: The place it's just absolutely beautiful wonder of nature. I recommend to bring your own food and drinks if you think to stay for the complete day although bring a bag to get all the garbage with you! The only thing I would like to say to people is that respect for the beach it's very important I saw some graffiti on the rock and a lot of people leaving garbage after they left. This is unacceptable.

reviews.title: Nice family beach
reviews.text: Nice beach. Very calm water. Several palapas. Great way to spend a day or few hours. Can take a bus from La Paz or drive and park there. Gets crowded but still was comfortable. Nice sunsets here as well.

reviews.title: The good and bad (there’s no ugly)
reviews.text: This is a popular beach especially with locals. Go early or late if you really want a palapa, otherwise bring your own shade, because there are no trees or buildings for shade. The waves are nonexistent as the water is completely still and you can walk out 1/2 mile and still touch the bottom. There is a vendor selling cold drinks out of his truck in the parking lot if you forgot yours. It’s about a half hour drive from LaPaz to get to the beach but the road is good. Also watch for stingrays. We were told by a friend in Cabo that on average whe he was there, at least 1 person gets stung. I brought my goggles as swam around for 30 minutes and sure enough, I found one. He was only about 6” across but I touched his back with a shell and he swam a couple feet away and re-hid himself! I didn’t see any other fish than that. Anyway it’s a nice spot, there’s my thoughts, Enjoy!

reviews.title: This is an unbelievable beach and water experience as you witness the tide charges the bay completely changes
reviews.text: Arrive early to get use of one of the free Palapa’s and then enjoy the beautiful water and bay are.  When the tide goes out you can walk completely across the bay in water just above your ankles at most, or walk towards the sea and see lots of fish around you without needing snorkeling gear.  Careful though if there is no breeze as the tiny black bugs carry a mean vicious bite that lasts for 3 to 4 days.  Make sure to spray.

reviews.title: Worth the long drive from Los Cabos
reviews.text: So glad we booked a day trip to La Paz from Los Cabos that included a two-hour stop at Balandra Beach. Beautiful, secluded beach with smooth sand and clear water. In fact, the water was so clear we could see fish swimming by the rocks without having to use snorkeling gear. Free palapas for those who get there early, or rent an umbrella if needed. Memorable excursion and the highlight of our trip to Baja California Sur.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: A beautiful beach, white sand and warm turquoise water, lovely little concessions offering goodies. A must see

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: This place is a hidden gem. The water is warm and clear. They have tabels and chairs avaiable for rent. There is food trucks avaiable - no beer sold here, bring your own

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: La Paz VIP Tours brought us here after our whale shark tour, and it was GORGEOUS! Totally secluded and so stunning.  Crystal clear water.  Hidden gem.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach, Lots of bugs
reviews.text: The beach is very pretty. It's Protected, no surf, so great for kids. It's shallow, so you can Wade out for a LONG time. We were there only tourists here on a week day. We've read it gets really busy on the weekends. Out of a week in Mexico this was the only place I got bit by bugs.There are porta potties and one little truck to buy some snacks at. Other than that, there are no amenities. Bring your own everything.Just down the road is another beautiful beach (I think prettier) with lots of trucks, bars, etc. But it's not as protected, so there are waves that roll in (small ones while we were there). We were told to watch out for sting rays while at both beaches. We found one at Balandra, buried in the sand.

reviews.title: Playa Bus
reviews.text: There is a turistica bus station on the malecon where you can buy round trip tickets to balandra. Taxis will charge tourists double and uber signal doesn’t pick up that far from the city. The playa bus will take you to the parking lot (at least it did for me) but will pick you up, up the road where dudes are selling fruit and coconut water. No one told me that so I waited for the bus 3 times before I realized they weren’t coming back to the parking lot. I got bit by a red ant or some bug in the sand. I left my clothes sitting on the sand and whatever it was bit me in the back when I put my shirt back on. We sat under the shady cliff rocks so not sure if the red ants are still by the palapas or not. By 3 pm there were 2 Palapas available but by noon when I got there they were all taken. It’s $13 for the hour to rent a kayak or sup board. We got one and paddled to the mushroom rock. Be sure to hike to the top to get a good panorama. The rock trail is behind the parking lot.

reviews.title: Must see, make the effort, great place for kids
reviews.text: Lovely clear water, safe place, shallow for kids for kids to play.Bring your towels, umbrella and cooler.  They do have portable toilettes and a few vendors with fruit or snacks for sale.

reviews.title: Pretty Beach slightly off the beaten path
reviews.text: This beach is very clean, in spite of the crowds.  You need to "tip" in order to get an umbrella and table, which is highly recommended.  Shallow and easy to swim in so great for families--the waves are almost non existent, and you can swim or walk in pristine waters.  There are two remote beaches right across the way that you can swim to if you are reasonable fit.Once you get done here, drive further north about a mile and you will see four or five "bar huts" right on another beach.  You can enjoy cold beer and have a decent lunch here before you head back to town.

reviews.title: Make the effort, and visit this place!
reviews.text: We were staying in CSL, but had a car, so we drove the newer highway up to La Paz, and then around it to Balandra Beach (Google maps is worthless when you try to find it, they try to point you into the center of the city for some reason.  Search for "Playa Balandra" to get the correct map).We went there on a Monday, and it was surprisingly busy, but not terrible.  They have a good parking lot, and there are Port-A-Johns on the back end of the lot (but either bring your own TP, or pay the ladies at the table next to them.  Also, they seem to lock them up around 6, so if you gotta go, you better go before dinner!)The good snorkeling was around the "mushroom" and the rocky areas in that vicinity.  Lots of fish there.  Bring a camera!

reviews.title: Hidden gem! Take your own towels, cooler, snacks.
reviews.text: We loved loved this beach!  Reminds us of Isla Mujeres crystal clear water.  Super shallow all around so very safe for kids.  We stayed in Cabo, but so worth the drive.  We only stayed about 3 hours, I wish we would have been better prepared to stay longer.  This beach was voted best beach in Mexico by my favorite YouTuber (Alan x el Mundo).  So I was delighted when we ran across one of the food vendors from his video.  Will upload pic—you gotta try her ratoncitos!  Bring lots of small change pesos for the food vendors.  My son got stung by a bee— maybe pack some bug repellent and Benadryl.  We also drive after into the town of La Paz— it was so charming!  But the beach here was heaven on Earth!  Go!!

reviews.title: Absolutely beautiful beach!
reviews.text: This was a beautiful beach. It’s all very shallow, so at some points you can almost walk the entirety of the cover and get to the other adjacent beaches. There was even an ice cream cart that was making rounds in the water. I took an Uber there and back from the Malecon, just bear in mind you may have to keep an eye out, because Ubers are only available if the driver is less than 15mins away at another beach or at Balandra dropping someone off. There is also a Playa Bus that does the rounds around the beaches and comes approximately every 30mins.
