You can rent an Umbrella for the day, and there are some built in Umbrellas for free, but come in early, or else you will be without one. It is not recommended to be under the sun without an Umbrella — it is VERY hot. There are vendors that offer food service. Bring cash with you and please tip them!! They are offering a service in weather unfit to work in, for your pleasure, so don’t be cheap. Pesos to USD or Euros are more than substantial. Would definitely recommend. Great for kids. For sure bring plenty of water and sunscreen.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: We drove the 2+ hours from Cabo San Lucas to visit the Balandra beach and had a great time.  It is like a huge swimming pool.

reviews.title: Worth going
reviews.text: So convenient to grab a bus to this pretty unique place.  I went early so was lucky enough to snag a little palapa.  It got very crowded later, even on a weekday.  If you go solo remember to take a waterproof pouch for your valuables since you can spend a long time walking across the bay.  Water shoes are nice to take also.  I will go back when in La Paz.

reviews.title: Must visit
reviews.text: If you love the beach and clear turquoise water, this is the place to go. A popular spot for locals to take their families on days off. It feels like a hidden gem of peaceful tranquility. You can walk for hours in chest deep water. If you desire an umbrella, be early for the permanent palapas or rent one. There are washrooms, donation for paper required, so take your own if you don’t want to pay. Look for food vendors on the beach wearing black aprons. They will take your order, call it in and have it delivered directly to you.

reviews.title: Calming
reviews.text: Nice beach.  Water is very calm with nice color.  You could walk out very far and still only chest high.  It was not terribly busy but I think cause of the time of the year.  There are vendors there but they were not a bother like resort beach areas.  You can see alot of marine life up around the rock areas.

reviews.title: Warm water even in th dead of winter
reviews.text: This playa has more than just cozy water the landscape is beautiful and you can walk through the water to almost every corner of the bay.  A pod of orcas visited just last May.  Sometimes there is a snack van but play it safe and BYO

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: The place is really amazing. If you are a person who is into panoramic  views this is a most in your list. It is perfect for all kind of people, kids friendly and since the water level is to low it's  great also for people who doesn't  know how  to swim. The prosBeach is very chill place.Low level water and warm.There's  2 more beaches infront if you need some more privacy or a less crowded beach and one on the side which has  the iconic mushroom looking rock in La Paz.  You can get there by kayak, boat, swimming or paddle board. There's  also a walking trail if you want to go hiking around and see the beaches from top where you can get cool views day and night.You can rent a shadow with table and seats. You can also rent kayak and paddle board. Theres also free shadows if you get there in time. The Cons: No toilets nearby.Gets too crowded so best times is to go pretty early and stay there until all people starts to arrive. Sometimes water tide is too low. Parking can be hard. Not many bins around. It is a nice place to be for a few hours and then maybe spend some  time in other beaches around.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach 🏝
reviews.text: Beautiful beach. Lots of locals. Rent a car and drive yourself. There is a snack van and plenty of parking. The drive is easy and uneventful.

reviews.title: Day trip
reviews.text: Pros: Amazing beach. Calm, turquoise water. Water level is up to your waistline for over a mile. Sugar fine sand. Con: Limited parking so be there early in the morning. Prepare to pay 10 MXN pesos to use the restroom. No restaurant close by so don't look for one. Bring your own food and drinks as you can't rely the quality of the food that's being sold in the area.

reviews.title: Scenic
reviews.text: Nice place to spend the day while in La Paz. It's like a giant kidding pool. Check current reports on water cleanliness if you are concerned.

reviews.title: No words, surrounded by mountains, calm!
reviews.text: My recommendation, go early, in the middle of the week and you’ll enjoy it more! Remember to take some food and drinks with you, there is a small parking lot, have some tennis shoes and or water shoes either to climb the small rock and reach the iconic ”Mushroom” or to go walking in the water to also reach this landmark.Have a good camera, enjoy the sunset if you stay long enough...

reviews.title: Visit Balandra Beach
reviews.text: One of the best beaches ever seen, must visit. Balandra and Tecolote are virgins beaches, beautifulUna de las mejores playas jamás vistas, debes visitarla. Balandra y tecolote son playas vírgenes. Hermosas

reviews.title: Very nice peaceful beach
reviews.text: We had a great time. We loved the fact that our kids could play in the beach like if it were a giant (long) pool most was less than 3 feet deep. Snacks available to buy and if you forgot supplies, sunscreen, inflatables, sandals, swimwear, snacks etc there was a mobile truck that would sell supplies. I saw a waiter offering services couldn't figure out were they had the restaurant.  There is shades and chairs but many people took their own and their ice chest with food. Kayaking for rent was fun, bummed that they ask for an ID and my husband forgot to get it back and now had to get a new driver's licence.

reviews.title: Totally Unique
reviews.text: A truly unique beach with splendid views of the surrounding bare hillsides serves as a majestic backdrop of waters of sapphire.must be on your bucket list. for more beautiful travel destinations follow me on Instagram:@baughbrian

reviews.title: Absolutely Amazing
reviews.text: This was amazingly beautiful, pictures can't do it justice. The water was clear and refreshing, the beach was incredibly clean. As an American I find it horrible how little respect we give to each other and natural beauty. The day we visited, the bulk of the beachgoer's were locals. Everyone picked up their waste, taking it home with them. I saw no garbage cans, especially overflowing ones like I see here at parks and Galveston. Everything was stunningly clean. Visitors were polite, considerate to others and we'll behaved. Dogs are allowed and owners apparently quickly clean up behind them.Kayaks are available for rental. Some thatched umbrellas are available to those arriving early. Many brought their own beach umbrellas as it became crowded. I advised planning to arrive between 10:30 and 11 to ensure parking at the free paved lot. We left around 2 and cars were parked along the road at least a 1/4 mile from the beach. As we loaded our car newcomers stood by to claim the parking spot by walking into it as we backed out.

reviews.title: Nice beach but crowded
reviews.text: Very crystal clear water but it was very crowded.  We went last Thursday mid day.  No place to park if we had a car.  We took an Uber there with no issue but coming back was hard. We had to find a taxi and squish several people into the cab. Overall it was a good experience.

reviews.title: Best beach close to La Paz
reviews.text: Best beach close to La Paz!  That’s what most anyone will tell you, and it’s true. There is a lot to do here, but don’t expect a ton of stores and restaurants, because you won’t find them here. The area is well protected, but there are walking sales people, and food and drinks can be purchased at one of the trailers. Kayak rentals are also available. Essentially, this beach is a super clear shallow bay That is about a mile and a half long by a mile across. It almost never goes over your waist line. The water is warm, the sand is white, and it is absolutely beautiful.

reviews.title: Try the "ratones de queso"!
reviews.text: Such a beautiful beach! Try the local treats like the ratones de queso (like a mini cheese cake) at the beach. Warning, do not get very deep on the water because you may get 'bited' by tiny parts of the agua malas, stay on the shore... such a nice place

reviews.title: Balandra is crowded!
reviews.text: Haven’t been here for almost 10 years when we used to have the beach to ourselves. It was crowded, but still very beautiful and clean!

reviews.title: Beautiful but busy
reviews.text: We went to watch the sunset on a Monday evening. It’s was still very busy. Beautiful views and blue waters. Just a shame some visitors left litter and played loud music

reviews.title: One of the most amazing and beautiful beaches in Mexico
reviews.text: Walk across a lagoon beach in the aqua waters for 30 minutes to reach the other side. It a bit a a drive yet... well worth the trip to an amazing secret location. Locals know of this special place and now we do to. Pictures don’t do it justice. Pack a lunch, and water proof bags for the phone so you can walk in waist deep water for hours.Make sure you get your pictures in front of the mushroom shaped rock.The sunset is incredible if you choose to stay.

reviews.title: One of the best!
reviews.text: Turquoise waters, swimmable beach, clear and clean.I’ve got no negative remarks. Absolutely beautiful!!

reviews.title: Glistening Beach
reviews.text: Balandra's natural features made this beach one of my favorite stops while in La Paz. The water was crystal clear. I didn't need snorkeling gear to see various small sea creatures swim past my legs. The water's temperature and depth were perfect, Lastly, it was clean and not crowded.

reviews.title: AWESOME
reviews.text: AWESOME PLACE DEFINITELY COMING BACK HERE NEXT TIME IN LA PAZ!  So much to explore here, need a full day here at least in order to see everything.

reviews.title: A must see
reviews.text: go early in the day so you can use one of the palapas for shade.  Beautiful, crystalline waters!!  inflatable kayaks are usually available to rent from the beach.  Take your own water and food.

reviews.title: nice beach but crowded
reviews.text: It was a great beach to visit but there were other beaches that were also as beautiful but were less crowded.

reviews.title: Amazing!!!
reviews.text: Went to this beach with some friends that live in Cabo. Amazing place the water is beautiful and you can walk very far out in the water. Many families enjoy the day there. One Great place I have ever visited. Worth the trip from Cabo, good highway to drive to get there, will definitely return.Hongo De Balandra is a great place for pictures and you walk through the water to see it. Amazing

reviews.title: Still a Wonderful, Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: I first visited Balandra Beach about 20 years ago and it certainly has changed, but then what hasn’t in that time. The water is amazing and most of the changes were for the better. Get there early and get a palapa or a shady spot near the rock overhangs. Wish we could have spent the day like we did 20 years ago. Don’t miss this place!

reviews.title: Beautiful beach - please keep it clean
reviews.text: This is an amazing place to visit. If you go, try to pickup at least 5 pieces of trash. The sea, the animals and our planet will be thankful that some visitors mitigate the harm made by other who came before.

reviews.title: saw the mexican movie called camino a marte its just like the movie
reviews.text: this place is beautiful almost as if you were in a different planet more specifically mars, if you saw the mexican movie camino a marte you will rapidly recogniza this beautiful place

reviews.title: so beautiful
reviews.text: another beautiful beach from baja but this is  a very special one, there no waves just you and the desert

reviews.title: Water you can walk in safely
reviews.text: It is amazing to see a beach where you can walk for about a mile in most directions without needing to swim.  The water is beautiful and picturesque.  If you hike the surrounding cliff, you'll get a beautiful overlook of the waters leading to the ocean.  The waters look like a malachite stone in color.

reviews.title: Best beach in Mexico
reviews.text: Amazing beach for kids,  beautiful sightseeing. No bathrooms or services, still you can rent some tables and chairs..  there are some palapas to be used by free, but those get busy early.

reviews.title: Amazing Place! Most Go.
reviews.text: Beautiful and unique please, must arrive early on weekend if you want a 'palapa' (sunshade). The restrooms are not fancy, just basic. This place is well maintained.

reviews.title: Unique crystal clear water
reviews.text: We arrived in the morning and were able to park in the lot.  It gets quite busy later and you have to park on the narrow road in.  Great opportunities to hike around the hills with beautiful views of the bay.  Also, you can walk around the whole bay along the beach.  The water is quite shallow so you can walk out as far as you'd like.  There are restrooms and a stand to buy some food, but no other facilities

reviews.title: Amazing and Beautiful!!!!!
reviews.text: It’s now one of the best beaches I’ve ever been to! U have to see it! We stayed in Cabo and booked a city tour to La Paz which included a two hour stop at Balandra beach! Definitely one of the best choices we made. It’s a 2hr drive to and from but tour guide fills it with great stops at towns and markets, with lunch included! Of course Balandra our highlight!

reviews.title: Amazing Beach!
reviews.text: This was seriously one of the most beautiful beaches I've had the pleasure to visit. It doesn't look like much from the distance but it's really quite lovely. The water is Crystal clear with a beautiful blue hue. The water is not too deep making it great for those who want to enjoy the water but can't swim. You can actually see where you're walking because the water is so clear. The beach had nice soft sand and some nice rocky areas that are quite scenic. The parking area fills up quick so you may want to go early or take a bus if possible. There are bathrooms but they are like outhouses so prepare for that.

reviews.title: Balandra Beach
reviews.text: Great beach for kids. Shallow water to almost no water at low tide. This beach use to be one if the best in the world. It had now been overrun with visitors and tour busses. Parking can be a real challenge.

reviews.title: As Advertised.  GO! plus the beaches along the way are amazing.
reviews.text: Go here as well and you might as well stop at the beaches along the way.  SO amazing.  We went on a sunday and it was busy.  I bet a week day you could have it to yourself.  The next beach over has bars and jet ski rentals etc.

reviews.title: A hidden jewel ..!
reviews.text: One of the top 10 most beautiful beaches in the world. Clean, safe, quiet and some reefs to do some snorkelling..!

reviews.title: Amazing place, the color of the water is unique
reviews.text: The beach is really nice, plus the view from the surrounding hills is really worth the short climb (<5mn). The beach is small and the number of free umbrellas is limited, so you should get there early (before 9am).

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Balandra beach really is beautiful, u like anything I had ever seen. The color of the water against the rock formations and mountains are so beautiful. The only downside would have to be the stingrays. There are a lot her please be careful! My son got stung by one and we had to leave In a hurry to get him to a doctor. Those stings are no fun, and extremely painful. Seeing all those children in there made me so worried sick. Drag your feet make noise that should help to get them out of your way, we learned that too late.

reviews.title: Balandra Beach is one of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico.
reviews.text: Balandra Beach is one of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico.It is very shallow so it is very safe.

reviews.title: Most unusual, amazing and picturesque beach
reviews.text: About 20mins NE of La Paz, Baja Sur you will find a piece of heaven.  This white sand beach in an incredibly shallow triple bay has warm water, gentle currents and enables you to wade 100's of yard out and along the bay.  The very gentle swells cause little undulations in the water depth resulting in alternating hues of blue.  Take a walk up the stony path to the top of the hill next to the beach for amazing views of the triple bay , the Sea of Cortez, and the mountains beyond.  Make sure you look behind you for a view of the lagoon in green march among the desert. Quite a contrast.  No facilities but usually a food truck on site.

reviews.title: Paradise for little ones
reviews.text: What a beautiful beach!!! Little ones will love the shallow waters and the soft white sand. Unfortunately there are no services at this beach, so no toilets. However there is a small van selling food and other essentials. Parking is free, but limited.

reviews.title: One of the best beaches in the world
reviews.text: Incredible view, sand and water! Go early and try to stay to the far left. And climb the mountain to see on the the best views you can find!

reviews.title: Beautiful beach, very shallow
reviews.text: We enjoyed sitting beneath permanent mushroom umbrellas (get there early if you want one), walking the beach and wading in the water.  Not many fish for snorkeling, but a good place to practice for young kids.

reviews.title: Amazing beach
reviews.text: This is the most beautiful beach in La Paz and Mexico, here is a place so quiet, with white sand beaches and turquoise transparent waters, it is surrounded by the exotic desert providing this an expectacular view.

reviews.title: Balandra Incredible
reviews.text: Is a quiet place, beautiful clear water and amazing views, if you are planning to go book with Baja Desconocida, wonderful service and profesionalism.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Nice sandy beach, gradual water depth from shore, nice swimming.  Beautiful scenery and the color of the water is that turquoise you just won't ever forget.

reviews.title: Nice place to chill
reviews.text: Peaceful and relaxing. Take a short hike up to get a better view. It is breathtaking plus a UNESCO site. There is some sun shade provided or you can purchase. We went to another side of the beach and just hung out for a bit. Note: stingrays in the area so make sure you shuffle your feet in the sand and you will be fine.

reviews.title: Great hike, snorkeling and beaches
reviews.text: Enjoyed the 3 mile hike around the beaches with incredible views, and the miles of white sand beaches, good snorkeling around the reefs. We stayed away from the main beach other than at the start and end of each day here. Shallow waters for miles.

reviews.title: WOW!!!!
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful, unique and unspoiled beaches I have ever visited. So happy it has been untouched by many of the mega resorts that have ruined many other beaches in Mexico. It is worth a trip to La Paz just to see this beach.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviews.text: Not to be missed. Check the tide table and go when it's falling so you can wade out to the mouth of the bay. Worth the drive up there.

reviews.title: WOW! Don't tell anyone about this place!
reviews.text: We were told by several that the drive from Cabo to Playa Balandra was 1 1/2 hours.  We found even without much traffic it was 2 1/2 hours one way.  We rented a car and stopped at Todos Santos to see Hotel California and at La Paz to see the local festival setting up and to get some delicious sandwiches from a cute little coffee shop to take to the beach.  This is definitely a whole day trip.  Was is the highlight of our trip? Absolutely, without a doubt!  The water is more clear than at any beach I've ever been to.  The day we were there you could walk all the way across to the other side and the water would barely be over waist high.  There were quite a few cars there, but not crowded at all.  It almost seemed like we had the whole place to ourselves.

reviews.title: Amazing beach with liw water level to walk
reviews.text: This is a especial beach where you can walk in low water crisraline turqouise waters.When you arrive tgere is a beach beside the parking lot but you keep walking around by the mountain and you can find a lot of spots to stop and use the montain side to give you shade. Taje water shoes to walk on rhat greats waters up to your waist more or less and sone food and drinks to nake a pucnic ir buy some fruits over ther and rent a chairs and un umbrella for your day. ENJOY IT

reviews.title: Shallow beach
reviews.text: You can't really swim here, or snorkel.  Thigh high water.  But beautiful, and peaceful before the tour buses show up (9am).  Good place to get sun, or kyack.

reviews.title: a nice family or couple day destination
reviews.text: This beach has low tide at bout 4:30 in the winter. Its great walk nice and shallow during low tide you can walk right up to the rock. wonderful destination; vendors always on beach renting sun shades, artisian crafts and coconuts. Get a coco preparado...yummmy.This place is picturesque, Its where I have seen people fly drones, pretend they are models posing for photos, and the cutest toddlers having a great time (on the very large sand spit at low tide). we usually spend the day taking snacks etc.At high tide you need to swim to the valadra. the beach is a big "c" shape. as soon as the sun is ready to set get your but outta there the mosquitos ravishly attack! They are not out before sunset so you can enjoy your day.Everyone is better at respecting the beaches so please respect the environment and take your stuff with you. only downfall is busy so parking lot is large, just take your time...after all your already there!

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviews.text: This is maybe one of the most beautiful beaches I've ever been to. It was windy and a bit chilly in La Paz so we assumed we wouldn't want to spend long at the beach but we got there and it was gorgeous. Hot, sunny, no wind - the perfect beach day!

reviews.title: Rated the best beach in Mexico
reviews.text: This beach lived up to the hype. Definitely a beautiful beach especially when traveling with little ones. This beach is truly breathtaking and is a must when traveling to La Paz. Calm water, knee high depth, and warm.

reviews.title: Wow, just wow!  Must see.
reviews.text: Amazing place.  We went at low tide and were able to walk across the bay to the beaches on the other side.  Water was clear turquoise, warm and shallow.  Sand was creamy white.We spent 5 hours there.  Had a spot in the shade next to the cliffs and walked around those whole bay.There are toilets in the parking lot area.Bring your own food and water.You can catch a bus here from the bus terminal on the Malecon in La Paz (Eco Baja Tours).  Costs $100 Pesos and takes 40 minutes.  One bus goes back and forth all day, with the last one being at sunset.An Uber from the centre of La Paz to here quoted $200 Pesos, so $400 Pesos return.  Drive takes 20 minutes.Also saw cyclists along the road.

reviews.title: Sand and more sand
reviews.text: Was a beautiful beach, you can walk for a long ways before it’s deep. There are some public palapa’s to use. Beware the lady just sitting under the public palapa, she will charge you to use one of her umbrellas.

reviews.title: Fun in yhe sun
reviews.text: Spent an afternoon. Very enjoyable with food available in the parking lot and walk to see mushroom rock.  Very unique.

reviews.title: Nice beach
reviews.text: This is one of the nicest beaches, I totally recomend it. It a little far to get to the Pic. But it is totally worth it.

reviews.title: Worth a morning or afternoon
reviews.text: Beautiful beach. If you're adventurous, wear hiking shoes and climb over hill to private beach (looking at beach from ocean , youre headed left.) If not, throw down towel & enjoy beach, sand and ocean views.

reviews.title: Gorgeous!!!
reviews.text: Incredible beach to bring young kids very safe no waves.  Definitely bring your own snacks and water and clean up after yourself. The water is very shallow and a beautiful light aqua there are two parts to the beach which you can explore walking on the water.  We went in February and it was warm enough for swimming and lounging. Please bring Biodegradable sun screen.  Protect these beautiful natural areas, be a traveler not a tourist.

reviews.title: Excellent beach
reviews.text: Went here with the hubby on a Monday afternoon. There were trinkets, snacks, and drinks for sale (non-alcoholic). We walked across the small bay to our own private beach were the hubs snorkeled around some rocks with excellent results. I walked around in the shallows and saw several types of fish. If you want food drive the extra kilometer to Tecolote Beach and have delish lunch right on the beach under an umbrella.

reviews.title: Must see!
reviews.text: This is an amazing beach away from tour areas of La Paz.  We took an Uber to the beach and arranged a pickup time later in the day.  We hiked, walked the lagoon, and relaxed in the sun.  It was perfect.  The water was too cold to swim (visited in February) but perfect to cool off if you got too warm in the sun.  Just walking in the lagoon you can see fish, starfish, shells, and beautiful birds.  This should be a 'must do' if you are in the area.  There is a parking lot, restrooms and food trucks so even though it is remote, there are amenities.  There are also palapas but I recommend bringing your own umbrella so you can be more selective where you want to relax on the beach.

reviews.title: A small piece of Paradise on Earth
reviews.text: If you are in la Paz and you did not visit this beach you did not go to la Paz!!!Balandra is a clean, isolated from the city (only 25 min or less), gorgeous beach that has clear waters and a beautiful natural sea made mushroom shaped rock that has been there for 100 years or more (a picture spot definitely).The water depth is so nice that you can walk for miles and miles and water will still be at your hip or knee level (depending on your height).Take a cooler down there with your beers and gatorades, one umbrella, and you should be set to enjoy an excellent day at a gorgeous beach!!

reviews.title: Hard to park but beautiful
reviews.text: We went on a Sunday which seems to be a big day for Mexican families. Very hard to park so be careful and don't go all the way up if you see a bunch of cars. The road is very narrow. But the beach was beautiful, the water was nice, and it was better than expected. I should also say that the bathrooms were very reasonable and clean

reviews.title: A nice place to spend the day if you have a car.
reviews.text: This is beach is very clean and there are palapas at no charge.  Vendors are very polite and there are not many of them.  Great place for kids as the whole bay is no more than mid thigh deep.  Mostly ankle deep.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: We loved Balandra. We took an Uber there from our hotel in La Paz and spent the day there. There is a shuttle you can take but we wanted to get there early in the morning (before the shuttle started running for the day). There are basic toilets. There was a couple keeping them clean between each use so make sure you bring money to tip them. The snorkelling was great as was the hiking. The water was pretty chilly when we were there so you may want to pack a rash guard shirt to help keep you warm.

reviews.title: Want to be there now!
reviews.text: Visited on our lunch stop on our whale shark excursion.  Pulled in, anchored the boat and enjoyed lunch, sitting on the sand.Simply Breath-taking, shallow, no one but the 8 of us there . . .the water and sand were like coves in the Caribbean.You can drive about 1/2 an hour north of the CostaBaja resort area, park in and walk, as well. It's a beach frequented by locals, so it can get crowded on holidays and weekends, we were told.

reviews.title: Best beach in La Paz!
reviews.text: We went out to Balandra Beach after swimming with the whale sharks and sea lions, the beach is majestic! Super soft white sandy beaches and plenty of fish to see while snorkeling. It is perfect for paddleboarding too!

reviews.title: Wonderful.
reviews.text: Even though we visited on the weekend, there was plenty of room on the beach. The sea was out so as there is only a gentle gradient paddling was the order of the day. Apart from someone flying a drone and a couple of others swilling beer and listening to AC/DC it was free of most annoyances.Sand is soft and the beach is free from litter.

reviews.title: Beautiful beaches!
reviews.text: Head to Balandra bay for a breathtaking day on the sea of Cortez! It’s a family friendly beach with the most beautiful clear waters and sandy shores! Away from the hustle and bustle of the resorts, you’ll find serenity while you take in some sun! If you’re looking for a bit more activity....Kayaking, whale and sea tours are available too!

reviews.title: Walk for miles
reviews.text: Very nice sand and clear water. The waves are very small. The water depth is perfect for children or people that walk to walk into the water and not worry about a drop off. The beach area is very big ....no food or thing like that when we visted but there was someone renting paddle boats . I also undersatnd you can take a bus to the beach for 70 pesco return but i did not use it ...so check it out ..

reviews.title: Pristine beauty
reviews.text: We arrived at Balandra beach by kayak and were able to enjoy an almost private beach away from parking area. Fine white sand, clear turquoise water to gaze at while eating lunch. It is possible to walk across bay at low tide.

reviews.title: Photo op!
reviews.text: Absolutely beautiful setting. Walk across the bay for privacy on the other side! When the tide is out, you can get “walk on water” pics!

reviews.title: Breath Taking Beach
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful beaches on the planet. Almost no amenities, but worth it. Just to stare and wonder at the beauty of Baja. The last time we were there, some vendors were there and we had to pay for a shaded spot. But this is a must see.

reviews.title: Very Nice but Crowded
reviews.text: We went on a weekend and the place was packed. There are palapas to rent but most people brought their own shade. Crowds aren't our thing so we wandered in the shallow waters (the tide was out) for a half hour before leaving. Very picturesque and I'd be happy to spend more time here when there are fewer people.

reviews.title: The most beautiful beach near La Paz.
reviews.text: This beach is magical. When the tide is out you can walk a long way out  to the mushroom rocks. The water is a spectacular shade of aqua. It’s a must see sea!

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: This beach was perfect! We were able to walk a little ways from the the parking lot and it felt like we had the place to our selves. The water is shallow a long ways out so it was great for strolling in water up to your hips and louging around in the ocean

reviews.title: This is one of the most beautiful beachs in the baja!
reviews.text: If you have the chance, this place is a must! Balandra beach is amazing! From cabo san lucas it is about a 2 hour drive, you can even spend the night at a hotel in town. The water is very calm and cristal clear! Perfect for kids to swim or learn on there own.

reviews.title: Girls trip to La Paz- beach day
reviews.text: We came here on a Sunday and although there were quite a few people it wasn’t overcrowded and we were able to find a peaceful spot. We got some fresh coconuts before heading to our spot. You’re able to walk out through the water across the majority of the bay as it’s only 2-3 feet deep which makes for some great photo opportunities. The weather was great only downside was the abundance of flies that liked to harass us. Would definitely go back.

reviews.title: Wade among the locals
reviews.text: A lovely temperature, you can wade up to your knees across the whole area, lounge on a beach, hike up the hill to a lookout, and walk along the beach to see the "Balandra Mushroom" Replica (original was knocked over by some rude tourists)

reviews.title: Nice beach but at low tide it is gone!
reviews.text: Balandra beach is a really nice beach. you arrive early to get a Palapa but beware that at low tide the beach disappears.  That can be good if you want to walk around the rocks to see the sites on the other side but if you want to swim! We were told there is no food there, so we brought a lunch and a few beers however there was a small restaurant.

reviews.title: Absolutely gorgeous
reviews.text: Rented a car for the day and drove up to Balandra, commute was roughly a half hour. Parked right in the very front of the parking lot closest to the beach. Grabbed a spot under one of the palapas. Wandered over the rocks and around to the other beach and walked to the mushroom rock which was a bit of work during high tide, recommended water shoes if possible but we made it with no trouble. Went back over to our spot under the palapa and sun bathed for an hour or so. Around 11am or so it started to finally get busy. I decided to rent a kayak and we ended up buying 2 cups of fresh fruit from one of the vendors and kayaked over to the other beach directly to the south. It was great, we had our own private beach enjoyed our fruit and sunbathed some more. Ended up walking up and down both ends of our beach looking for shells and marine life. Found some beautiful fish, crabs, pelicans and even a anemone. Ended up staying a total of five hours or so. If you wanna avoid the crowds highly recommend driving up early and seeing everything you’d like to. Besides the kayaks they do have umbrellas and chairs available for rent and even paddle boards. We were there early enough that we experienced both high and low tide. During the low tide there were dozens of sand bars and I even walked out about 150 yards or so and water was barely up to my shins. Water is some of the clearest I’ve ever seen. Absolutely a must visit if you’re ever in La Paz. Will definitely be coming back.

reviews.title: Beautiful natural pool
reviews.text: It's a unique beach. Awesome colors, nice sand. Be careful with the jellyfish and rocks but only in specific areas. Perfect for children and families.

reviews.title: Part of a tour
reviews.text: Went to beautiful Balandra Beach with MeXplore Tours.  Great time.  Started the tour with the whale sharks and had lunch on the beach.  A place to go see.

reviews.title: Hidden paradise
reviews.text: This beach is just amazing. We arrived in the morning after a quick visit to El Tecolote, it was about 9:30 so finding a place to park wasn’t an issue. We started to walk along the beach and just jumped into the water and we were amazed with the amount of sea life around the rocks! We walked around the rocks for quite a long time just amazed and grateful with the small things Mother Earth provides us. You can lay in the beach, you can walk on the bay from one beach to the other and see sea life or you can even hike the mountains and take some great photos of this amazing place. There’s kayaks and SUP boards to rent and some people selling refreshments and some snacks. Definitely a place not to be missed if you are in La Paz.

reviews.title: gorgeous
reviews.text: shallow, clear water, soft sand. great place for kids to play and swim. we had a picnic and the kids found lots of fish skeletons and cool things!

reviews.title: Wow.... 360 degree beach!
reviews.text: This beach ranks one of the top ten that I've ever been to.  There is something unique about being surrounded in this large 'cove', 'bay', or whatever we should call it.  The tide comes in/out and it can be like being in a swimming pool.  White sand, totally clear, turquoise water, wow.  My kids were in heaven because it was shallow, safe and they were always looking for interesting critters or shells on the white sand - easy to spot something that stood out.  Family even saw an octopus - but I missed it.  Cannot recommend this spot highly enough.  No facilities so beware and treat it respectfully.

reviews.title: Low tide
reviews.text: I guess we were there at low tide.  VERY shallow.  Was told by a tour guide that you can snorkel there.  Must only happen at high tide so be sure to check before you go.  Lovely location,  food truck and the usual vendors.

reviews.title: Beauitiful but Popular
reviews.text: An amazing natural land and seascape. I'd recommend coming ready to hike a little and perhaps wade a bit and you can get away from the crowds and maybe have a couple hundred yards of pristine beach to yourself. Hike up to get the birds eye view from the top of the central hill above the parking lots. Bathrooms were not open when I was there so that can be an disgusting issue in the desert where the landscape is so delicate and toilet paper doesn't decay anywhere as fast as in other wetter places. Pack it out people!! A kayak guide told me that years ago when he was a kid in La Paz there used to be many sea turtles in Balandra Bay but now they hardly ever appear there because of all the people. Leave them alone if you see them and maybe one day they'll come back in abundance. Look at the tide charts and time your visit to include a high tide. Our visit was almost all low and outgoing tide so we didn't get the full aqua blue water effect but still beautiful and very wade-able.

reviews.title: Awesome !
reviews.text: We loved this huge ‘pool’ . You can walk around with water ranging from your knees to your chest for the most part . If you do walk straight across the beach there’s a spot that’s deep enough that you have to swim thru it .

reviews.title: Get there Early
reviews.text: It is a very unique place.  The last 10 minutes of drive is very beautiful.  We got there early and grabbed shade under a palapa.  It did not take long for the crowds to come.  It was a week before Christmas so we expected it to be busy.Very sad to see people using the sand/beach near the rocks as a toilet.  I was totally grossed out by this and will not go back.  There are now toilettes in the parking lot, but I'm afraid some people still decide to take a crap wherever they want.  So if you want to stay away from seeing this maybe go in the water, and back to your beach towel.  Do not hike around the corner to the other beach, you might see a surprise.There are also a couple of less busy beaches on the way out there that may be worth a visit.  Obviously not as nice, but there is food and drink there.

reviews.title: Not worth a trip from Cabo
reviews.text: We were in search of diversity and authentic, less commercialized beaches and that’s exactly what we got, and didn’t like it.It’s crowded, garbage everywhere on the beach, but the water itself is fun for walking, shallow and unspoiled.Not worth a 2+ hour trip from Cabo, sorry.

reviews.title: awesome but crowded
reviews.text: Pichlingee Beach much better and has two oceanside bars......!!! Families welcome ! great drinks and service. Awesome sunset!!

reviews.title: love it
reviews.text: top 10 beaches in the world!!! u must come n visit !!!! u can rent umbrellas n chairs there if u wish , bring your own water !

reviews.title: Overcrowded Mess
reviews.text: Sad to say Ballandra has turned into an overcrowded mess. I started coming to this area more than 25 years ago, and I know things cannot stay the same, but this beach has become overrun with the tourist bus crowd as well as individual visitors. Get there early? Maybe a bit better but hideously overrun.

reviews.title: Peaceful wade in clear waters!
reviews.text: Balandra beach (really it is three coves of gorgeous white sand beaches) is a wonderful way to spend the afternoon. It is about a 30 minute drive outside of La Paz with good roads. The beaches have no amenities (such as washrooms). There is one vendor with kayak rentals and a t-shirt vendor. Many Mexican families come to spend the day and bring their picnics, chairs and blankets. The water is very shallow and one can easily walk into each of the coves. Pretty fish to see. I recommend wearing water shoes in case you come across a ray in the sand. Come prepared with your water, snacks, sunscreen and towels to spend a glorious day. No entrance fee.

reviews.title: Balandra
reviews.text: Beautiful beachVery good point of viewIdeal for child because not dangerous at allNot easy to park car because many people

reviews.title: Its probably the best spot in Baja
reviews.text: Honestly, beach is simply awesome. Water is warm, quiet and so pure. The cool visit could be in week days (early in the morning) because is very popular. Parking for free. Eco-friendly bathroom. No showers but is fine. Palapas (eco-umbrellas) are for free: first come, first serve. Also you can ask for some lunch in restaurantes near there. Is a perfect spot to spend a day and even a Night of camping (for free). So, paradise exist. Is here.

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: Love it. The best vista is the south part of the beach with a view of the mountains and the beach. Get a coco for 60 pesos, enjoy the white sand. Climb to the top of the hill for the best view.

reviews.title: Great beach even with holiday crowds
reviews.text: Family oriented beach with minimal services available. Take the bus from the malecon for a few dollars or rent a car. Parking was limited on the Christmas holiday we visited. Had a great experience with the bus. There were vendors offering service from a restaurant 1 km away but may only happen on busy days. Clear beautiful water with a family oriented vibe.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Please arrive early so you can enjoy the beach without the crowd. Take goggles and a snorkel because fish are beautiful in there, and prepare to spend hours of il dolce far niente. Amazing place with cristaline water, no waves, nd you can walk a mile with the cold water up to your waist line. Few beaches this beautiful.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: A beautiful beach surrounded by rock and cactus. Our hotel ran a shuttle to the beach which was about 30 min away. There are shaded palapas however they were all taken when we got there. Henry was renting umbrellas, table and chairs if you want. A couple of stalls selling cold drinks and juices. No food. Few people selling tourist items to purchase. There were a couple of portable washrooms.  The tide changes dramatically and reveals many sandbars. You can walk and walk and walk and walk and still be maybe your knees.  Lots of people had small dogs that were loving it. We stayed for a couple of hours and then walked over to the tolocote beach about 30-40 min walk away with restaurants on the beach.  A great place to spend the day. Be sure to bring sunscreen in case you can’t get an umbrella

reviews.title: Amazing beach
reviews.text: This is a great beach, especially if you have little kids (which we don't). Its really shallow and has "3 lagoons". You can actually walk across to the other side to several other beaches as well, its nice and shallow. But if you want to go for a swim you can definitely wade out into deeper waters too. We did some stand up paddle boarding too. There are kayaks and paddle boards for rent there. We went there 3 times/days. Overall a great beach and very photogenic one too.

reviews.title: The most incredible beach I’ve ever visited
reviews.text: Beautiful shallow beach where you can wade for hundreds of yards in any direction! Clear, clean water that feels great. If you’re in La Paz, you HAVE to come here.I do have some suggestions on how to make sure you get the best experience. Think of this beach as more of a park than a tourist attraction—there aren’t many amenities. So, you should:•Bring a cooler with plenty of beverages. If you bring alcohol, you might also pack some drinks high in electrolytes like gatorade to stay hydrated.•Use a bathroom before.•Pack your basic beach needs: sunscreen, sunglasses, towels, etc.•Buy some cheap lawn/beach chairs to sit in. If you rented a car to tour the area, these can come in handy at other beaches as well! You can give them away before you go back home.

reviews.title: Stunningly beautiful
reviews.text: This is a must see when visiting la Paz. The water is crystal clear and warm.  You can wade comfortably for several hundred yards.  Recommend hiking the trails above.

reviews.title: Beautiful Bay!
reviews.text: Gorgeous turquoise bay facing the Sea of Cortes.  The water is shallow with sandy bottom so you can literally walk across to the other side.  I walked across bare foot but there are some stinging sting rays under sand,  so would use Aqua Socks next time. Take the Aguila bus from La Paz for $100pp/round trip.

reviews.title: Lovely all day
reviews.text: The beach was picture perfect and super warm. Even with a few people there it did not seem crowded. A great way to spend two or three hours.

reviews.title: Day at beach
reviews.text: Wonderful beach. Great hike around to the mushroom rock formation around the corner. The tides are interesting as well as it almost empties out at low tide.

reviews.title: its a magnificent white beach.
reviews.text: Dont stay on the first beach, there are three! Summon up a little effort and walk/swim around to the third bay and you might have your very own paradise!

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Wow ! So pretty here just go see it! Everywhere you look here it’s gorgeous! We loved it so much we went back the next day!

reviews.title: Gorgeous- just wish there were more services
reviews.text: Beautiful here, but you need to be prepared for no bathroom and no bar or restaurant.  The water is calm as a bathtub. Lots of interesting birds to see.

reviews.title: Nice beach, mediocre snorkeling
reviews.text: This place is the busiest beach we visited while in Baja Sur. The main beach was a little crowded, so we waded around the rock point to the second beach and had a great time sunning and swimming. The only good snorkeling we found was on the rocks near the mushroom rock. There's lots of sandy and shallow water, which is fun to pay in though, and our kids enjoyed that. And frankly, since this is such a draw for people, it meant other beaches (with better snorkeling) were relatively empty.

reviews.title: Favorite beache
reviews.text: This places is so beautiful, it’s my favorite beach of baja! I love spending all day at this beach and the color of the water is beautiful

reviews.title: Tour stop
reviews.text: Our tour group spent an hour here. The water is amazing...super calm and you can walk to the other side since the water was so shallow.  There are people here selling snacks and renting out equipment and chairs and umbrellas. Would have rated this beach a 5 except the outhouse style bathrooms were locked up with padlocks ☹️.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: We were lucky enough to make it out here several times during out visit to La Paz and is always worth the trip!  It is a beautiful spot!

reviews.title: Beautiful waters
reviews.text: Extremely beautifully clear water . Great place to spend the day.. We packed a cooler and spent the entire day

reviews.title: AMAZING
reviews.text: We rented a car and drove to balandra , very easy and fast from La Paz. No need to tell you how, just follow signs . Amazing scenery , you’ll see mangroves .... cactus forest and amazing beaches on the way there.  There is a truck that sells a bit of everything , so if you are one of those who doesn’t like to carry anything around , you’ll be able to buy at least something to drink and a floating device (lol). They have restrooms on site. Before you get to the parking you’ll see a trail going up to the top of the hill that seats right Above balandra.  You’ll get amazing views of the entire bay ( recommended ). Go earlier in the day , ties change during the day.

reviews.title: Love this beach!
reviews.text: I was here at low tide and was able to walk out to the mushroom rock but take water shoes or sandals incase the water is higher. What an amazing sight!

reviews.title: Beautiful shallow bays with white sand beaches - a must see if in the area!
reviews.text: The public beach has parking and porta potties, incredible views, warm shallow waters, white sand and was very clean when we were there on a Saturday. Plenty of space to spread out too. Other beaches in the area can be reached only by boat and are also spectacular. Take a photo with Mushroom Rock!.

reviews.title: Clearest water I've ever seen.
reviews.text: This beach is pretty amazing totally chill, guys selling hats and food kids playing nobody acting stupid the clearest calmest water I've ever seen white sand, slight drive to get to but no big deal. I'd give it  5 stars but at the end of the day it still just a beach.

reviews.title: Beach that paints itself!
reviews.text: This is a must while visiting La Paz. The bays are full of colors and life. The parking lot leads to one of the bays that most of the people go to. I would recommend going over the small hill and go to the other bay. Bring snorkel gear, umbrella and environmentally safe sunscreen. They have a small snack shop and a guy with coconuts for sale. You can rent a umbrella on the beach for 200 pesos for the day. This bay has a lot of people were you can rent kayaks or walk 500 plus feet in waste high water depending on the tide. If you want a view from above to see both bays, you can go up a small hill that will lead you to a path that leads you to the point. You can see this path from the parking lot. Enjoy!!!

reviews.title: Nice Beach
reviews.text: Great beach for kids, a few vendors with umbrellas, etc. Make sure your trip does not coincide with a ferry departure - took us more than 1hr from La Paz due to ferry traffic. Our toddler loved the water, but I have never seen so many wasps in one place.

reviews.title: Looks like small lake
reviews.text: Driving from las Cabos to la Paz is scenic and interesting drive on mostly well-paved divided Hwy. The malecon walk and drive thru the centro area are the main attractions of the town. The Balandra Beach is not worth spending time to drive. Contrary to our expectation that the beach would be right on the ocean, rather it s enclosed on three sides with little mountains and an inlet for sea water from the fourth side. Nothing extraordinary of its being with shallow water and smooth off-white sands. A couple of food trucks are there to sell snacks, cold drinks and fresh coconuts slit open for sweet water. For a day trip to la Paz it is not worth going to Balandra, rather enjoy the town and plenty of restaurants on the Malecon.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I have ever seen. A true gem with clear and calm waters and beautiful hikes

reviews.title: Lots of people and lot of moise
reviews.text: The beach is beautiful but full of algae. There is a lot of people and a lot of noise and music. The parking is just next to the beach which is very ugly. You can climb the mountains and walk all the beach across.

reviews.title: Ranked as one of the top beaches in the world
reviews.text: The water is crystal clear and you can walk around the cove as the water is chest high at the deepest point. There are 2 coves to explore. Kayak & SUP boards available to rent. I would bring a float, sunscreen, a small cooler, and sun umbrella. Uber is available and very reasonable may cost you only $8-$10 one way from La paz. Do not miss this beach! It is a very memorable lifetime experience of breathtaking beauty & fun.

reviews.title: Nice way to spend the day
reviews.text: If you are visiting, you can rent an umbrella, chair and get food and drink at the beach. Of course, you can always bring your own. Not much for snorkeling, but it is a relaxing spot to soak up some sand. There is a public bathroom there as well.

reviews.title: Perfect spot for lunch on the sand
reviews.text: As part of our tour with VIP tours, Captain Eddy and guide Katrin prepared a great lunch on the beach.  We'l come back on our own as it is an easy drive from La Paz.

reviews.title: We arrived late so it was not as busy
reviews.text: We decided to head to Balandra after visiting La Ventana and the area (actually we did a big loop from El Triunfo, up to La Ventana and then to Balandra Beach which was a nice way to spend a day). There were still a lot of people at the beach and in the water which looked as if it was quite shallow for quite a ways out. We arrived for the sunset so that was about 630pm. What I didn't get to see because I arrived so late, was the beautiful blue of the water. It looks incredible. Lots of parking at this time and the sunset was pretty. I think I'd come back again during the day to experience it more.

reviews.title: Fun
reviews.text: This is a wonderful beach about 20 mins drive from La Paz. We got there around 10 am and found it to be quite and easy to park. Contrary to other reviews the is a refreshment truck selling drinks and snacks, and also toilet facilities ( just think of a massive litter box for people, and you’ll get the idea. Go in, do your business, and cover it with the sand provided!!!!😬😬😬). During the coarse of the morning, the proverbial beach vendors arrive in droves to sell their wares, rather annoying, unless you’re in dia need of a flotation devise or beach attire.  SUP and kayaks can be rented for about $18 an hour. We found this particularly useful as it was high tide , and access to the mushroom would have been impossible without it.The beach itself is fairly clean, although it’s obvious that there are some people that camp there , and maybe don’t pick up after themselves as much as they could.Another issue is that there were many dogs there with their owners........ they are not able to use the human litter box, rather they just go in the sand. Not so nice if your digging in it, and come across a big dog turd!!On the whole, this is a must if you’re in the area.  Check for tidal updates........

reviews.title: Quite and beautiful!!
reviews.text: As we were driving....we came across this beautiful beach! When we arrived, there was only 2 other couples there. Later in the day it got busier. We came in the mid morning and then stopped to have lunch down the road to another great find!

reviews.title: The best beach in La Paz
reviews.text: We (2 adults and an 11 year old) spent an afternoon at this beach. This one is in my opinion the best 'family' beach. Warm clean waters, shallow beach, and white soft sand.  What more can you ask for!And if that isn't enough at low tide you can walk along the shoreline to the famous El Hongo 'mushroom' rock, or hike to it (over a hill).Bring food & beverages and a parasol as it can get really hot early to late afternoon.Take the bus there, it's only a 25-30 minute ride and relatively inexpensive.Cheers :o)

reviews.title: Stunning beach!!
reviews.text: Definitely preferred this beach hands down over Tecolote beach! Palapas are free to the public. Get there early and stay all day! Bring lunch, water, snacks in a cooler because no restaurants around. Beach is super clean, water is pristine and you can walk out prettty far and still be touching the ground and the water is refreshing. You can also rent kayaks and paddle boards there if you want.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: A must while in La paz or cabo.A 2:30 hour drive from cabo this is truly one of the most beautiful beaches on earth.Peaceful and clean.Highly recommend to BOB since there is no restaurants or stores.

reviews.title: Beautiful area
reviews.text: I really liked Balandra Beach its really nice and the water is very warm. Please help keep this area clean when going. Note: this location does not have restrooms or changing area, since its a protected area by the government.

reviews.title: Balandra Beach
reviews.text: Amazing bay! The water is crystal clear, cactuses all around the hills. If you rent a car you should take a visit even if your hotel is in San Jose Del Cabo like ours.

reviews.title: Paradise!!! Exists
reviews.text: A must when visiting La Paz or Los Cabos.Nice, beautiful, clean.A real jewel.Take care of our planet and be conscious.Keep it clean.Nice people and attention.A must...

reviews.title: Very Nice
reviews.text: This is a beautifull little cove just north of La Paz if you want to kick back on the beach and relax, It could do with a little resturant or a bar or even a shack that served food and drinks but worth a visit if you're in the vicinity.

reviews.title: The most beautiful beach at La Paz
reviews.text: This was our favorite beach. Very nice and peaceful. The level of the water would barely go over your knees. Depending on the day, there could be almost no waves which makes it perfect for kids or people who are afraid of waves. Important to know: there are a few free Palapas, that are nice and can offer you the shade you need to survive the sun. However you need to arrive early if you want to get one of these!

reviews.title: Paradise
reviews.text: The perfect beach at the perfect location. We went during the week and it was not packed. I can see on the weekends the place being full but we were lucky to get one of the palapas and enjoyed a lovely day in this piece of paradise. A must when visiting La Paz

reviews.title: Good beach near La Paz
reviews.text: Although it’s a little bit overrated, as you need to walk more than 100 meters to get the water pass your knees, is a nice and safe beach to go with little ones.

reviews.title: Peaceful relaxation!
reviews.text: This quiet beach is absolutely gorgeous!  Shallow turquoise water await to refresh and soothe you.  The contrast against the white sand and arid backdrop is stunning!  Not much in terms of activity... which is part of the charm!  You CAN rent some kayaks and there is one snack-bar (no tables) at the entrance but Balandra is best enjoyed with your own cooler.  No need to taxi if staying in La Paz:  bus terminal has regular buses for 100 pesos per person (return - 45 min drive along the coast). We went on the 1:30pm bus to miss the hottest part of the day.

reviews.title: Overhyped
reviews.text: We made the trip from Cabo to Balandra with much anticipation. Positives? Great coconut stand and soft sand. If you have kids it allows for wading without too much worry. Negatives? We found the beach a little smelly with dark weeds on parts of the sandy shoreline which was not attractive at all! Compared to beaches in the Virgin and Cayman Islands and Jamaica, Balandra leaves a lot to be desired.

reviews.title: Beautiful blue water !!!
reviews.text: Beautiful place with a nice blue water,  but when we went,  the tour man told us it was the first time in his life that the place was crazy crowded, so we didn’t enjoy the please . It was impossible to get to the “ mushroom spot” because it was too many people , but when we went to the the Espíritu  Santo island , we passed by on the boat and I took some pictures .

reviews.title: stroll in the beach
reviews.text: Balandra was spectacular, its the first I strolled in the beach..water was so clean & clear and you can walk from the shore and across walking..although the the end acroos is a deep cavity that you can’t see the bottom so be careful...water was warm & perfect for non swimmers...so family oriented..there are no abnoxious vendors to harrass you..they are regulated and they stay where there suppose to... you can rent umbrella beach for 180 mexican pesos

reviews.title: Great beach and area
reviews.text: Easy to find, good parking area, very clean, shallow water, great to take children and pet. No restaurants in the area, BYO food and drinks or go to Tecolote next to it for lunch

reviews.title: Best Beach ever !!!’
reviews.text: I’ve been to most of the best beaches all over the world and Balandra Beach is right there in the top.It is the most beautiful place,many different coves that all face different directions.Each one more amazing than the last.Kayaks are available for rent and you can paddle around the whole area which is huge or you can walk through the thigh deep water to some.The water is crystal clear with white sand beaches. I never wanted to leave ever,but you know how that goes.I was in La Paz for the whole month of July and spent much time at Balandra. If you love beaches like I do then this is a can’t miss!!!

reviews.title: Amazing Beach and Clean Water
reviews.text: Balandra is amazing!You can swim in clean waters, I recommend you to use snorkel equipment.If you arrive on morning you have the beach only for you. You can also do Kyak and aquatic sports in this beach.Greetings from Portugal

reviews.title: Beautiful beach with warm tranquil waters!
reviews.text: Balandra Beach is a beautiful retreat about 2 hours from Los Cabos.  It is worth a day trip!  The water is crystal clear and very warm.  It is a lagoon so there are no waves or rip currents.There are some local vendors with fresh fruit, beverages, shaved ice and souvenirs.  You can rent chairs, sun umbrellas and kayaks.

reviews.title: Spectacular and safe swimming beach
reviews.text: Great place for kids, very shallow waters. A must see attraction if you can't surf, but want to relax in the water. You can wade hundreds of meters out to sea, and a few vendors had delicious mangos on a stick.

reviews.title: Great but avoid the Sunday
reviews.text: White sands, turquoise water, good palapa and also a place to rent umbrellas and buy something Everything you need to enjoy a great beach

reviews.title: Top 5 beach in Mex
reviews.text: Not to miss when visiting La Paz. 30 minutes by car. Sandy White beaches, great for snorkeling. Suggestion take an umbrella and chairs and cooler with food and drinks. Don't miss this place

reviews.title: Beautiful (and crowded)
reviews.text: The beach is gorgeous, but if you happen to be there during the weekend be ready to share the beauty with many many other people. We got there a little before noon and the beach was already pretty packed, but more people kept arriving steadily all afternoon. If you're not carrying to many things can always go for a swim or climb to cross the rock barrier that separates the crowded beach from it's private secluded twin (but the walk or swim can be a little tricky). We ended up paying for a parasol and a couple of chairs and finding a nice little spot on the right side of the beach next to the rocks).

reviews.title: Great for kids bur crowded
reviews.text: Certainly not what it used to be, does not live up to the hype anymore. Still a very nice beach in the early hours before it becomes super crowded. Perfect spot for kids, safe shallow crystal clear waters. No restroom or other services. Get there early and grab a free family shade or get in late and rent a tiny umbrella shade for 300-400mxn pesos. Bring your drinks and food and lots of sun protection.

reviews.title: Vacayion
reviews.text: My cousins and I came to Playa Balandra from Cabo San Lucas. Unfortunately, we came on a Sunday and it was packed, no area to put our stuff, visitors with loud DJ speakers. We decided to go to Playa Tecolote.

reviews.title: nice small beach
reviews.text: we went here as part of the boat tour with the cortez club so they dropped us here while the divers went out.  it's a pretty little spot with crystal clear water and a nice beach.they have a mushroom rock to look at and you can snorkel there as well.it was empty in the morning but when we came back in the afternoon it had filled up.

reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text: Not as cool as it used to be. Bit dirty nowadays. Super crowded. I rather visit other beaches. Small parking lot.

reviews.title: Crowed in July
reviews.text: I read all the wonderful reviews and was so hyped to take my teen son there. Got there on a Tuesday about 1PM and was so disappointed. Car lot was full and people were parked along both sides of a one lane unpaved road leading up to entrance so our van guide couldn't drive in. I was determined to at lease take my son to see it, so we left the rest of the family in the van to walk down there. My dad couldn't make the walk. We got to the beach and it was so crowded. Families had staked out every possible area to lay a towel. There were a handful of vendors with mangos, drinks etc. My son and I walked into the water, noticed a couple of small fish, the mushroom rock and left. Our driver took us to Tecolote Beach. A much better beach. I'll do my review for this one too!

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach!!
reviews.text: Loved this beach, it was very busy when we went. Bring lots of water and snacks, and an umbrella for shade.

reviews.title: Great Beach and Vibe
reviews.text: We have spent several days at Balandra so far this trip, and it is our favorite hangout in La Paz. Heartily recommended.We have been riding the public bus from the terminal on the Malecon (just across from the two story waterfront pavillion) near the whale museum. Ecobaja counter sells tickets...100 pesos roundtrip.The trip follows the coast through desert north of town and takes about 40 minutes, depending on locals getting on and off at various stops. First bus (the one you want to catch to avoid the crowds) is at 10 AM. Returns roughly every two hours, with last one early evening.The early bus drops you at the public parking area by the beach, but because the road fills up, it picks you up several hundred meters up the road. Make sure you clarify with driver where pickup is!There are two beach areas. The main beach where 90% of the people go has vendors and blue portable rental umbrellas (200 pesos per day-ish). About 99% of visitors we have run into are locals or from other parts of Mexico.  That may just be the season...not sure.The best beach, though, is "around the corner" to the right when facing water, and requires either walking in shallow water around a point to see the cove, or a climb up and over the rocks to reachit. This beach is gorgeous and calm, and has only a fraction of the visitor load of the main beach area. This is also the area with the "mushroom rock". We have only gone to the more secluded beach, and avoided the booming crowd that seems to gather each day at the main beach.Note: There are no bathrooms at either beach. Also, please, please, PLEASE pack out your trash.  We take an extra bag to carry out any trash we find...which hasn't been much, but is heartbreaking to see.Despite temperatures of over 100 F each day we have been there, the water has been siper clear, cool and refreshing, and there have been very few (if any) biting insects. Wear reef walkers and/or shuffle your feet in water to avoid stingrays. Lots of small fish, some larger ones cruising through, all sand bottom and very shallow lagoon. The whole bay / cove has truly incredible colors of different aquamarine shades with the water right up to sand dunes with a desert backdrop and red / brown cliffs.Really, Balandra is one of our very favorite beaches ever, right up with any we have visited in the Agean islands in Greece,  Crete, Thailand, Bali, other parts of Mexico and the Caribbean. It is a special, lovely spot.

reviews.title: Balandra Beach Spectacular
reviews.text: Came here on the city bus from la Paz. Earliest bus is at 10am 100 pesos rt then it runs every 2 hours coming back.  Beautiful and quiet when you get there early. There are palapas on the beach for shade. If they are all taken people don’t mind sharing. You spend most of your time in the water anyways. Bring a snorkel and mask and you can see some fish by the rocks.  Don’t forget your sunscreen and waterproof bag for your camera.  Water shoes are needed if you want to go on the rocks to take pics of the mushroom rock.  Enjoy the unspoiled area.

reviews.title: It is a fascinating place - very shallow water for the whole bay, sand bottom
reviews.text: This is an extraordinary place unprecedented in my experience.  The whole huge bay it set in the midst of desert hills about a half-hour drive from La Paz. There are no bathrooms or restaurants at the beach, just a few food trucks. Its a locals family beach. The whole bay is less than chest deep, no kidding, and you can walk hundreds of yards off the beach and still be mostly dry. It's beautiful, but it is a hang out, no waves, place.

reviews.title: Warning about theft from this beach
reviews.text: Stopped at this beach for a quick swim. Left a camera and some cash in the trunk of the rental car. Returned a short time later and the car was still locked and seemingly undisturbed. Discovered cash missing when i got my wallet - no credit cards were taken. They went through my wife's purse and very carefully took some small amounts of cash, went through all our bags and took a couple of other small items (Kindle) then looked uip and took off. Granted we're an easy mark and made the mistake of leaving stuff in the car but it was a just a quick dipso didn't fuss with the usual security. This is clearly a very organized theft so just use this as a reminder.Otherwise, an okay beach but nice water - like a giant ocean swimming pool.

reviews.title: Breathtaking! A must visit
reviews.text: Highlight of our trip to la Paz. Water has great visibility and super shallow. We could see the little fish swim around and could walk half way across the beach with the water until our waist. Most beautiful sunset of our lives!

reviews.title: This is a great preserve
reviews.text: This location is well worth a stop. It is a part of the natural preserve. It is very pretty and a clean area. On the day we visited, it was a bit cloudy and we got a break from the heat of the sun. This area has no staff members to help with questions and answers.  There were several boats anchored in the area.  Most of them had smaller boats to get to the beaches.

reviews.title: Remote beach worth the drive!
reviews.text: Beautiful beach with pure white sand and shallow water. There are no facilities so pack a cooler, sunscreen, beach umbrella and snacks for a fun day. Bring your favorite floats to soak up the sun or snorkel. Approximately 3 hour drive each way from Cabo San Lucas.

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach
reviews.text: This one is clean and looks like a pool. My favorite from the area. Make sure you were swimming shoes.

reviews.title: Visitor
reviews.text: All a good experience. The favorite locals beach they say. We were given chairs to sit on the beach. Good place for children.

reviews.title: Lovely beach
reviews.text: Our friends and we like to leave our "stuff" on the beach and walk out a little into the water and plant our umbrellas and chairs. It's fun sitting in the water. If you go out further, you need to shuffle your feet so the little rays know you're coming their way so they have time to get out of the way. Not difficult and its a great view.

reviews.title: Best Beach period.
reviews.text: I can honestly say this is the nicest beach I have ever been to, the sand is so nice and soft, the water is so clear It feels like a big pool, awesome place to visit!

reviews.title: must see
reviews.text: if you're in la paz you have to explore this beach. bring some ceviche, water, beer and you're good to go :)

reviews.title: Beautiful scenery
reviews.text: A great place to relax, but a bit crowded sometimes. You can easily walk across the bay if the crowds get too much. Not much snorkeling. Great views from the hill overlooking the bay.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: Wow! I thought it was so beautiful here. Shallow, warm water that is perfectly still. I could have swam around all day. It was part of a tour so only had an hour. If you like swimming and the beach it is a must go while in La Paz.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Balandra is  an amazing beach young children and adults love this beach. About 2 miles of walking inside the warm water which never reach above our shoulders. Crystal clear water. Just beautiful. We adore this place.

reviews.title: A hidden gem
reviews.text: About 2 hours drive from Cabo. It’s a hidden gem. We have visited so many beaches around the world, and this one is on the top of the list. Nature at its best. You can rent an umbrella and relax. Make sure you stop by la Paz for seafood on your way back

reviews.title: Fun in the Sun
reviews.text: Nice outing with a visiting amigo.      When you go bring your own umbrella or get there early to score one of the many pomfon shaded areas on the shore

reviews.title: Breathtaking!!!
reviews.text: This beach is absolutely gorgeous. Traveling with small children we have to be mindful of the waves and the water was absolutely perfect for our toddler here. It was something out of a postcard! We tried going the first time but didn’t arrive until 11 and the palapa were all taken so next time we arrived at 10 am and snagged one. Only thing to note: SAND FLEAS! Bring bug spray. I was eaten alive!

reviews.title: AMAZING!
reviews.text: We thoroughly enjoyed this beach, only a short trip from La Paz.  Kayaked in the mangroves and walked through the crystal clear, warm waters.  You don’t need a mask and snorkle to see an array of sea life.  Next time we’d take a cooler with cerveza and maybe a few snacks since the beach hasn’t been commercialized at all.  Totally unique beach experience.

reviews.title: Day excursion
reviews.text: We rented a car from Cabo to head this way, it was well worth the drive. The beaches are white, warm waters and crystal clear you can walk for miles in waste high water. Bring you own food and drinks as the cart is very expensive since it’s unpopulated. You can rent paddles boards or kayaks. This is the sea of Cortez side which is very different than the pacific. The drive was safe and fairly easy directions wise. A must adventure and you can stop at other places along the way.

reviews.title: Aqua Agua: Wade in Clear Shallow Water Among the Schools
reviews.text: This beautiful beach was full of surprises. Maybe because I didn't do my homework, went on a whim and had no idea what to expect. Many wouldn't drive 2 hours out of Cabo San Lucas (the tourist area) and come to a beach they only heard from a local "was beautiful and you can wade out as far as you can imagine and see fish and stingrays!" Well, that was enough for me to visit this amazing aqua reserve and I was pleasantly surprised. Perhaps I was a bit nervous on the ride up as we rented a car to get there and braved the foreign roads on our own. Certain things to note that you don't see in the US are military vehicles with large guns and men in military garb commonly driving by on the roads. They are common in the area, however, and most likely looking out for the safety of tourists.We drove through a few "deserted" desert areas, some random desert homes, and eventually ended up in La Paz. (It is pretty much a straight shot on the freeway so you will not get lost.) La Paz was built up and rather quaint. It was the traditional beach town, complete with statues, a harbor, restaurants, markets, and most helpful was an information booth, which provided free brochures. (Balandra is about 45 minutes outside of La Paz.) We took the brochure and were off.This Sea of Cortez treasure was like nothing I had ever experienced. I have been in some amazing locations and a few beaches stick out such as a tiny beach on the Caribbean Island of Carriacou which also had some shallow beaches, but they were not tucked away and protected such as this. They also were not shallow nearly as far out as Balandra Beach.It was an extreme delight to not even need snorkeling gear. The water was so clear you can see schools of assorted fish left and right (obviously be careful not to get too close to the stingray.)

reviews.title: Amazing Place
reviews.text: If you visit La Paz, Balandra beach is a must.  Its a very safe beach, and you can walk inside the sea more that 100 yards. The scenario is amazing combining the dessert and the sea.

reviews.title: Beautiful place!!
reviews.text: Go as early as possible! One time we went by car around sunrise and it was so magical. There was no one there, climbed up the little mountain for a perfect view and enjoyed it so much. If you go early you are sure you have a beach umbrella to project yourself against the sun. Another time we took the bus from Malecon (100 peson return), it was way more crowded on the beach but still wonderful!

reviews.title: Hidden Gem!
reviews.text: Balandra is one of my favorite beaches to visit in La Paz BCS. It is located about 25min drive from La Paz. The beach offers turquoise blue clear waters that are amazing to walk and swim into.  You can walk hundreds of feet into the ocean and will not sink in, 3-4ft deep. It's a Giant Natural swimming pool, perfect for Kids! I was a little skeptical to get in the water due to we were warned by locals to watch for stingrays, I recommend shuffle your feet in the sand.  But really no Stingrays to be seen. There are vendors that rent kayaks and paddle boards. We had an amazing day enjoying the beach, waters, and taking all the vitamin D from the sun. My recommendation is to stop by an Oxxo and buy a cooler and drinks to go, you may also take snacks. Lots of sunscreen needed or get there early to get a Palapa, about 15 of them available for public use at no charge. Parking is also available at no charge. If by the time you leave and feel hungry, just drive about 7minutes to El Tecolote Beach and they have variety of beach front restaurants. Balandra is a must visit!

reviews.title: Balandra Beach is Unadulterated Beauty
reviews.text: Unadulterated beauty is necessary in this world. Why, one might ask, is it necessary? I say it is because of the potential for a sort of epiphany one might experience in the magnificence of the natural world that is not possible through any other medium of human expression; whether it be art, music, or literature. Balandra Beach is an epiphany waiting to happen for you. Go there.

reviews.title: beautiful
reviews.text: Came here and it was amazing, crystal clear waters and light blue colors. there was just some garbage around which was disappointing.

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: The most gorgeous beach ever!!! You can walk and walk and the cristal clear water doesn't go higher than you're waist. It has beautiful white sandy beaches and it's an adventure to get to the famous rock!! Worth the climb through the rocks!!!One of my favorite places to go!!!

reviews.title: One of the best beaches in Mexico
reviews.text: 2nd time in this beach and it is just very amazing. Last time there was no people, but this time, although it was crowded, we enjoyed very much.Worth going there even if you are in Cabo.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Balandra is an absolutely amazing place. It is so peaceful and serene. It is the absolutely perfect place to spend a day. It's great for small children to play and enjoy the water safely. My 16 month old was able to wade in the water without fear of waves or rip tides. It was a little less than knee deep when we went, but I hear it can get as deep as waist high. It is a bit of a drive and in the middle of nowhere, but that just adds to its appeal. It is the perfect place for kayaking, canoeing, or paddleboarding. The day we were there it was 104 degrees outside, but there was a nice breeze and it only felt to be in the 80s (I was incredibly surprised when I saw the actual temperture). It has parking and a decent amount of palapas for shade, but there are no other amenties; no food or bathrooms.
