There was a truck vendor selling miscellaneous items, but you should take any food or water you want to consume. We went midweek and there were a decent amount of people there. I would expect it to be very busy on the weekend as it is such a great place.

reviews.title: Very nice, quiet and scenic beach
reviews.text: It is one of the beaches I never saw before due to the good quality of water and the scenic landscaping.

reviews.title: Paradise
reviews.text: Absolutely beautiful location just 30 minutes from La Paz. In May the water is still a little chilly, but warm enough to snorkel or play... floating in the rafts was too cold.  If you take snorkeling equipment, walk around the point towards the right, walk across that new beach to the next point. This is where the mushroom rock is. Get in the water there then keep heading that direction down the coast. You’ll see a good variety of fish, including puffers if you are paying attention. Also some anemones, soft corals, urchins, etc.  it was impressing for shore based snorkeling

reviews.title: Mire than what you can exepct !!!
reviews.text: Don ‘t loose this place ! It is unforgettable. No doubt that is one of the best spot in Baja California

reviews.title: Breathtaking Balandra Beach
reviews.text: During our 7-day trip to Cabo, we opted to be courageous and drive to see the famous Balandra Beach in La Paz, Mexico. The approximately 2-5 to 3 hour drive was fun. Parking was a breeze and it wasn't packed since most folks were either in school or at work. The water was at least knee height throughout the entire day just as we were told it would be. Area is very safe and there are no issues in the parking lot or in the actual bathing area. We would definitely come back with friends and family as well as a bit better prepared with gear. Balandra Beach was very clean as well. Great place for couples as well as family and friends.

reviews.title: One of my favourite Beach!
reviews.text: Balandra is by far one of my favourite beach in Mexico! It can be crowded but you can always find a spot to be on your own. It's just like paradise!!

reviews.title: Heaven on Earth
reviews.text: My friend and I spent a couple days in Baja California Sur México and got a chance to take a road trip from Cabo San Lucas to La Paz BCS is around 2hrs away, we had been told about Balandra Beach, saw a couple of pictures online and decided to go, OMG!! What a beautiful place, so if you're in BCS México tristemente me it's worth the trip!

reviews.title: Time at the beach
reviews.text: Everyone should take the time to visit this beach.Beautiful stunning color and very shallow to walk in.Nice short drive from Hyatt Place where we stayed 20 minutes.There are no washrooms at this beach which was the only negative. Plenty of parking and there was a good amount of visitors which made the beach feel more safe.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: We were able to rent SUP and cruise around the whole area. It was beautiful beach with clear blue water.

reviews.title: Nice beach, nice scenery but not for swimming
reviews.text: Balandra Beach is a lovely beach about 30min out of La Paz.The sand is nice and there are shelters around the beach but get there early if you want one.The water is warm and reasonablely clear but you can walk out a couple of hundred metres and still only be knee deep, so not for swimming.Around the point is Mushroom Rock which is a nice 10min walk either along the sand and across the rocks at the point or in the water a lower tide.There's a vendor there that sells mangoes but not much else so bring drinks and any food you want for your stay.To get there Ecobajatours, at the Malecon terminal, have regular buses that cost 100 Pesos for the return trip.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: I have never seen a beach like this. The water is crystal clear and you can walk out so far and the water wont go past your waist. Get there early if you want an umbrella/palapas. There are about 20 of them and they get taken fast. Other than that there is no shade. We encountered some rude people who would not share there palapa even though there were just 2 of them and were in the water the whole time. But besides that bring a ton of sunscreen and have fun. There is no restrooms so your on your own. They do have a little vendor and they come around and you can order ceviche or fresh fruit which is really nice. Definitely worth the visit.

reviews.title: Wow
reviews.text: Breath taking beach, get there early to get a shade umbrella, we arrived around 10:30 on a tuesday.  Remember bug spray as the sand flies bite a lot in the shade.

reviews.title: Relaxing and secluded
reviews.text: We spent two days here just relaxing. A few quiet, quaint, accessible beach used by tourists and locals alike.  It's not much for swimming or waves - excellent for wading, SUP/sea kayak and just enjoying the beautiful, peaceful setting. No services.. you can go to the next beach (about a 5 minute drive) if you need food and restrooms.

reviews.title: Not to miss but arrive early
reviews.text: This beach is not to miss if you are in La Paz. It’s not far and really great. But it gets crowded quite quickly, which can change the experience. Arrive early. And don’t forget to climb on the top of the small mountain next to the beach you will be rewarded by a breath taking view.

reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.text: There are several bays and you can walk in the sea from one beach to the other. Shallow and transparent water. Lots of fishes. No services on the beach, but still it is wonderful. Must see place! You can rent a car, go by taxi or by bus from Malecon. Buses just pass every 1.5 hour.

reviews.title: Beauty beyond belief
reviews.text: Balandra beach was my favorite beach we visited! We drove 2.5 hours from Los Cabos to go there thanks to the locals we spoke with at our resort. They all recommended Balandra for its beauty and the shallow, beautiful waters. Balandra has beautiful white sand (in complete contrast to Los Cabos’ pebbly sand beaches). The sand was like sugar. Very fine and soft. The water was placid and very shallow for several hundred feet. We could let the kids roam and explore without fear of waves or drop offs in the water. We rented a paddle board for $16/hour and tried that out. Was the PERFECT place to learn / self- teach paddle boarding! The water, due to the depth, was warm and inviting unlike the other areas of the Sea of Cortez which were still quite cold!! As other posts have mentioned, there is little shade at Balandra. There are now approximately 10-12 palapas to escape the sun under. There are also overhangs from the cliffs where we found shade along with the very friendly locals. There are now a few vendors who sell food out of the back of their truck. A man was asking the locals if they wanted ceviche (he seemed like a delivery guy) but he didn’t ask us. If my Spanish were better, we would have enjoyed ceviche on the beach.... We did however, enjoy empanadas on the beach from Doce Cuarenta, a hip coffee and sandwich shop in La Paz.

reviews.title: Calm, serene and beautiful!
reviews.text: This beach was lovely. The water was crystal clear and still as can be. We went to the section that you can only reach by boat, and it was very secluded which made for an incredibly peaceful experience. I recommend checking it out!

reviews.title: Beautiful Bay
reviews.text: Crowded when we visited over Easter weekend.  This is a beautiful beach!!  I wish it hadn’t been so busy when we visited but this is a place to hang out for the day.  Water is clear with lots of marine life.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: This is a very beautiful beach just outside of La Paz. Totally worth the drive. Pack your own snacks...no services.

reviews.title: Picture Perfect!
reviews.text: Spent several hours here with 6 adults and 6 children (ages 8-5 months). We brought our inflatable paddle boards and spent the day on our own private spot. Fun in the sun, snorkeling, and loving life.

reviews.title: Best beach on the continent
reviews.text: Love Balandra Beach.  My brothers and I frequent La Paz and always spend a day or two swimming around Balandra.  If you can handle the trek, keep walking to the last beach in the bay.  The water is clearer, and the fish are more plentiful.  For a real good swim, go from Balandra to Tecolote.  The swim between the two has even better snorkeling and larger fish.

reviews.title: A must see, clearest water ever!!
reviews.text: Go early in the day as it can get quite busy. Take a beach umbrella with you, there are some shade palapas but you might not get one.

reviews.title: Hideaway beach
reviews.text: Really cool semi-hidden beach.  The water is pretty shallow, especially when the tide is out, so you can walk pretty far out in the water.

reviews.title: Bad timing on our part
reviews.text: Samana Santa is a huge celebration here in the Baja sur.  Everyone goes to the beach with family.  Not just this beach, all beaches were packed.  We got all the way there from San Jose del Cabo (2hr+ drive) and couldn’t even get to the beach it was so busy.  Definitely bad timing for us.

reviews.title: Beautiful treasure
reviews.text: This place is beautiful. We were luck enough to visit when it wasn’t too crowded . The second time we went there was not parking so we left and stopped by a beach closer to La Paz but no were near as nice.

reviews.title: Too Hot
reviews.text: We visited Balandra Beach in the middle of the day. It is just as pictured - shallow water, nice beach, beautiful. BUT be forwarned: there are no toilets, no wind, no waves, no shells for beachcombers, & if you aren't lucky enough to snag a spot under an umbrella, it is just too hot. So we relocated to Telecote Beach: food, toilets, wind, waves & plenty of shells. Balandra would be fun for families with toddlers, but not for us.

reviews.title: It's all true
reviews.text: Previous posters have summed it up quite well... Playa Balandra is a beautiful place.  The various hues of blue water against a backdrop of desert mountains is stunning.

reviews.title: Balandra beach
reviews.text: Amazing beach ideal for families. You can walk forever and before the water level reaches your waist. Calm water, beautiful  beach!

reviews.title: One of the best beaches ever!
reviews.text: Such an incredible beach!  Get there early to snag one of the palapas on the shore.  Also pay attention to tide charts because at low tide there is almost no water in the Bay, a perfect place to go at high tide.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: This beach is gorgeous. The water is so clear and shallow. We went in few feet and the water won’t go above our waste. Just make sure you bring your own food/drinks/snacks since they don’t sell anything there. Great place to relax and enjoy the view.

reviews.title: Get there early!
reviews.text: What a gorgeous beach. I am sure by previous posts it has already been said. We got there by 9:30 and was one of three cars. We left at 1:00 and it was packed. Several vendors for a Thurs. We rented SUP for an hour. 250 pesos an hour. Go. Enjoy. Relax!

reviews.title: Pristine and lovely
reviews.text: Probably the nicest beach in La Paz! Go early as the crowds are minimal and the basin is filled with water. At low tide the basin practically empties out and you're left with wet sand. Located a 30 minute drive from the La Paz Malecon it can be challenging to get to but taxi cabs take will you out there for approximately 300 Pesos ($15) which isn't bad considering the distance. However, there are public buses (at Obregon and Cinco de Mayo) that run approximately every hour for less than 100 Pesos. There are no public services at the beach such as changing rooms or restrooms so put your suit on ahead of time and bring your own TP if you think you'll need it. Bring lots of sunscreen and a hat if you have one!

reviews.title: Swimmable, beautiful beach!
reviews.text: My husband and I travel to Cabo at least once a year, and Balandra iso ne of our favorite spots. We rent a car and drive up from our hotel. It is a swimmable beach, which if you've been to the Cab area you know that is rare.  The water is beautiful, warm and calm.  IT gets busy, so get there early if you want to claim some shade. There are always a few vendors there for snacks, drinks and necessities.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: The Beach is beautiful, the major problem that I found is the lack of available parking lot and that there’s no restrooms available; so you should guess your options available when you gotta go... hope the authorities solve this issue because this is a great place to visit in La Paz.

reviews.title: Just beautifuk
reviews.text: Great beach.  Get there early for shade.  Walk to the mushroom walk and enjoy a serene beach.  Shallow, but sparkling blue.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: Watch out for the bus timetable - they do their own thing. We had to hitch back. No cafe/bar - take everything you need - it’s a must see.

reviews.title: Just unique
reviews.text: It’s really like two crescent shaped bays connected to each other. You have to walk or wade to the right side to get to the iconic, mushroom shaped rock formation. At high tide we could walk across the bay at about waist depth, at very low tide it was about to knee depth.  Out past the iconic rock where it gets deeper you can actually swim. If you wade or swim around the outcropping of rocks beyond the iconic rock there is another, even nicer beach. We took the local bus from La Paz, which was very easy and took about 40 minutes but was a scenic ride for 100 pesos round trip. The bus also goes to Técoloté about 5 minutes away (the bus stops at Balandra coming and going).Note that there is a parking lot next to the beach (behind the row of palapa) and garbage cans, but no other facilities, i.e., no restrooms and no vendors.

reviews.title: Completely worth the drive
reviews.text: I was completely blown away.  Our trip to Cabo is complete with our day excursion at LaPaz.  Balandra Beach is simply amazing.  We can't wait to come back.

reviews.title: Really amazing beach!
reviews.text: This is such a pretty spot.  You can easily get away from the "crowds",  we went on a Sunday, the busiest day of the week and it was still very peaceful.  Safe, gorgeous, unspoiled, clean.  You can take a short hike up a hill to get an amazing view.  You can wade (it is very shallow) across the bay to a private beach. There is decent free parking (no restroom though)

reviews.title: Unexpected beauty
reviews.text: This was the first stop and we only stayed 45 minutes.  If I were to go again I would take an umbrella and snorkel gear.  A lunch and ice chest are recommended.  This is a spectacular bay and not to be missed.   Warning no facilities available.

reviews.title: Balandra Beach
reviews.text: A peaceful place to spend time walking between the different beaches across from each other and next to each other. There’s a total of 7 white sand beaches. No one bothers you. You need to take your own picnic

reviews.title: It was worth the travel
reviews.text: We red the reviews from Trip Advisor and decided to drive out there.  It was worth the drive.  It was not your regular beach.  One side was black rocky mountains and other side was super fine sand.  Water was really shallow and light blue.  You have to walk for a while to actually get to deeper area to be able to swim.  There was free parking very close to the beach.  Many palapas for people to use.  We went even further and found a secluded are to sit.  Mountain looked like it was an inactive volcano.  There were caves at the bottom where people were sitting  there to hide from the sun.  We were there till 4 pm.  We returned thinking water may be returning soon.  We didn't want to get trapped in the area we were in.  THERE ARE NO BATHROOMS.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: This is a beautiful beach only 15 to 20 min drive from la Paz baja, also very shallow waters.only minor problem there aren't public bathrooms but you can drive 5 mim arond the corner to coyote beach and there is a seafood restaurant bar.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach but no beach bar or restaurant facilities
reviews.text: A lovely beach but Tecolote is the better beach a few minutes away. Good for kayaking and snorkelling but it was cool in February when we visited. Water was warm but ambient temp was off-putting.  Just one man’s opinion.

reviews.title: The most beautiful beach you’ve never heard of
reviews.text: If you surf, there are no waves. Beautiful white sand shallow cove. Mangroves at the top of the cove. Natural tunnels in the rock structure. Palapas open to the public.

reviews.title: Unique. Awesome.
reviews.text: Rustic and no facilities. But so fantastic. Sheltered from wind. Shallow crystal clear water. Shells for kids. Snorkel for adults. Palapa for shade. A view I will not soon forget!

reviews.title: Beautiful, but crowded
reviews.text: Balandra Beach is beautiful and remote, but it was very crowded on a Saturday afternoon. There is a fairly big expanse of sand along very shallow water, so it would be great for families with small children. There are several palapa-style umbrellas, but I imagine they are claimed fairly early in the day. There are many sandbars, so it is fun to walk way out in the water and only be up to your ankles. You may want to wear water shoes so you can explore the rock formations and tide pools at low tide. No bathrooms or other facilities. There were a couple of pick-up trucks in the parking area selling fresh fruit, but no other food or beverages. It is in a very quiet cove, so you are facing rocks not the open sea. Worth a visit, but I didn't think it was quite worth the hype.

reviews.title: Natural pool exciting view
reviews.text: Do no miss it ! It is the only beach to check out in the area. 25 min north from La Paz doen town, you can park your car on a small public parking and access the beach, take your shoes off here you are in. Just connect mother nature and enjoy the feeling, and the panoramic view

reviews.title: Shallow tidal lagoon
reviews.text: Awesome place to visit. Went at low tide, when you can walk for at least 300-400 feet and the water is just waist deep. Great place to take kids and specially those who love to see crabs and fish. The sunset from the hilltop is breathtaking. Besides some nice shades there are no other facilities here.

reviews.title: Beautiful!,,
reviews.text: You need a car or take a tour, but this place is gorgeous. There are no services - bring your own water and snacks. Good place to let the kids go in the water because it is so shallow

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: A must, jus be careful to take all your beach gear and food/water if you are planning to stay the day. It is a virgin beach area.

reviews.title: Amazing stretch of beach with enormous area of shallow water to enjoy
reviews.text: Good, clean beach that stretches for ever surrounding a huge lagoon-like area of shallow sea.  Excellent for relaxing or paddle-boarding

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: A large perfect beach in a protected cove. About 20 palapas lined up on the beach (no charge). Very shallow water but we were able to use a kayak. OK snorkeling around the rocks on the other side of the cove. A bit cool in February but still swimable. It's about a 25 minute drive from downtown La  Paz. There's also a city bus.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Nice virgin beach. It's like a giant pool, not deep at all.Calm water.I think it could have some ecofriendly infrastructure, it´s the only thing missing to have an excellente place

reviews.title: Pretty place
reviews.text: Very pretty little bay, fairly clean too! Easy place to wade in the water. Had some fun helping a little fish build his house!

reviews.title: Most amazing beach I've ever visited
reviews.text: I am not a beach person. I feel the need to preface this review with that statement, because I did not want to leave Balandra Beach the day we visited. It is truly one of the most beautiful places I have ever been.The enormous bay is only waist deep for hundreds of meters, and the pristine waters and sand just enhance every aspect of the place. I would return in a heartbeat.The beach isn't overrun with vendors like many other popular beaches in Mexico, and the distance from La Paz seems to keep crowds down. We were there on a Saturday in February, and while finding shade was tough, the place was not so crowded that it was overwhelming.

reviews.title: Relaxing
reviews.text: Beautiful beach, not crowded and much cleaner than the private resort beach! Easy short drive from town

reviews.title: Cool Place, Better on a Sunny Day
reviews.text: La Paz is a very industrial port city but some of the beaches are interesting because the water is clear, very shallow and walkable.  It was fun to take a hike in this area that has sand dunes and some great places for pictures.

reviews.title: Beatiful beach
reviews.text: We had a great time there, this beach has a lot of people on weekends, it is beautiful ant there is the famous stone fungus, a symbol of la Paz

reviews.title: Belongings Stolen
reviews.text: Beautiful area however we went out for one hour and our camera and phone were stolen. It was super busy and we hid them in our car... I know i know... I'm in Mexico... don't leave stuff in the car but I can't exactly take everything with me out... Saddest part is all the memories /photos gone. Lesson learned. So beautiful and a must see but go looking poor and leave NOTHING behind. That way you will enjoy and not have the bad experience we had.Adios

reviews.title: Great Day Trip
reviews.text: While driving the Baja we stopped in to check out this beach. It was nice and sheltered as this was a windy day. Great for a little kayak adventure.

reviews.title: Amazing!!!
reviews.text: I love this place! Incredible views and great place to spend a great day! Bring your own umbrella also water and things to eat because there no place to buy things!

reviews.title: beach trip
reviews.text: best beach in bajashallow warm un busywould def recommend to visitabout 45 mins by buslots of other great beachs near by

reviews.title: Absolutely beautiful!!
reviews.text: This beach was absolutely beautiful and different from any beach I’ve ever seen. We stopped by to have some lunch after our day or snorkeling with whale sharks and sea lions. Watch out for things that may have washed ashore, my boyfriend stepped on a dead porcupine fish and the spikes punctured his foot. We were lucky enough to spot a shark very close to the beach. We had just climbed back into the boat and started to take off when I saw something, the captain even got his phone out to record because he said sharks never come into the beach there.

reviews.title: Easy access to an amazing beach!
reviews.text: We have visited this beach a few times and love it for its tranquil blue waters and white sand. Great for relaxing, bird watching, snorkeling and swimming. Its just a short drive from La Paz.

reviews.title: Relaxing day at the beach
reviews.text: Very beautiful public beach where you can enjoy the water and views (climbing up the rocks).Kayaking is also nice - although the water in winter is still quite cold.Unfortunately day tours pass by the beach so it has become quite touristic.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Beautiful beach for walking if too cold to swim. There were a few areas that provided shade, so nice spot for a picnic.

reviews.title: Beautiful and easy fun
reviews.text: Bring a picnic and shade. No bathrooms. It was nice to not have any vendors hovering around. We did not encounter stingrays. We got to experience a relaxing and more secluded time near the rock formation in the first half of our day. When we returned to the beach closer to parking, we enjoyed the party crowd with live music even! It felt like two different places but in good way.

reviews.title: The Largest Swimming Pool in the Wrold
reviews.text: We recently revisted Balandra Bay after a twenty year absence.  Its beauty continues to take your breath away.  Its depth is only mid-calf, extending for probably a half-mile plus from shore.  We were informed it is now a protected area, and we noticed how visitors were careful to pick up their garbage.  There is a parking area with adequate spaces during mid-week, but you might have to park on side of road during a weekend.  There are no facilities, bathrooms or restaurants.  It is peaceful, tranquil, a gem.

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: Must see!  Climb the hill for the view.  Shallow, safe, no amenities. Easy drive from La Paz.  Good parking.

reviews.title: Amazing!!
reviews.text: I truly believe after going up and down the Baja, that by far this is the most amazing beach in all of Mexico. The sand is icing sugar white and soft, the water is clear clean warm and completely beyond words amazing

reviews.title: Worth the visit!
reviews.text: Beautiful and very clean beach! Worth the visit!! to walk on the sea its great, water is without waves.. very peaceful and beautiful place.

reviews.title: A bay like no other!
reviews.text: We spent 2 days here, SUPing and swimming and wading. Breathtaking scenery and clear, beautiful water.

reviews.title: Beach day
reviews.text: We drove from Cabo to La Paz for the day; it was a beautiful drive. The crystal clear waters of the bay were amazing. It was not as secluded as we thought but the beach is huge and everyone is spread out so it was fine. We had a palapa (free) which was great. Fun for swimming, exploring, and relaxing.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach, go early!
reviews.text: We were cancelled for our diving trip and decide to head to Balandra Bach to know the place. Once we get there, the beautiful of the place catch us and desire to stay the day there. Was really fortunate for us just to arrive early, we could choose a nice Palapa to have shadow from the sun and spend all morning there.

reviews.title: Incredibly beautiful and peaceful
reviews.text: Incredibly beautiful and peaceful, even during a norte! The ports were closed, but it was beautiful in this protected cove.

reviews.title: Beautiful sunset with Mushroom Rock in pictures
reviews.text: The beach was not difficult to get to, about 25 minutes from the tourist area of La Paz.  Once parked, you walk about 15 minutes to the rock.  Beach was quite clean and I am glad people respect the environment and did not throw much trash around, unlike some places in Asia or elsewhere.  Go late in the afternoon, like 4 pm or after to catch sunset and there will be less tourists clamoring over the rock then.  You can take pictures without others around.

reviews.title: It is paradise!
reviews.text: You must visit this beach , water is super clear and crystal , nature so amazing that you can walk across the bay from one side to another, the sea only reaches knee height.  When the tide starts to reside in the afternoon, the bay is even shallower and small sand islands start to appear.  It’s beautiful!  Locals said that there are mosquitoes or kind of bees after 4pm, so be careful , I believe perfect timing to visit this beach from 11-4pm.  Has some palapas, no food around , you will see some caves and rocks around , beautiful!

reviews.title: Low tide experience
reviews.text: This is a cool tide pool, sea life walk around beach expereince- tons of sealife all around- daughter did get a small Jellyfish sting wading in water- not without dangers but worth the great memories

reviews.title: Bello pero peligroso
reviews.text: Una playa muy bonita con aguas muy claras. Pero tengas cuidado con las medusas. Yo fui y me pico una. No hay servicios de sanitario y/o un lugar para comer. Hay mejores playas sin duda. Beautiful beach with crystal clear waters. But be careful with the jellyfish!! I went a few days ago, and I was stung by one. There are no bathrooms and a place to eat. I think there are better beaches.

reviews.title: Beautiful but watch out for bees
reviews.text: We drove to Balandra on one of the days staying there in La Paz. It was beautiful and the fact that you can walk out so far on low tide is fun. You can also rent kayaks and take it around. The only part that I didn't like was that from the moment you drive in, you start seeing bees flying around. I'm nervous around so many so that was a major distraction. To my luck, I got STUNG by one however it was my fault for laying back on my towel, and not looking first. That's how many bees there were! I still have the bruise today a week later. Would I go back? Maybe but I'd be distracted....

reviews.title: Beautiful spot
reviews.text: We were there on an overcast day but it was still absolutely beautiful. Lots of tide pool critters to see and the beach was totally wadable during low tide.

reviews.title: Worth the taxi ride!
reviews.text: Balandra was probably the highlight of our trip. Absolutely gorgeous beach, pretty secluded, if youre willing to venture along the coastline you can easily find private areas where very few people are out there. Highly recommend, only complaint is we didnt bring beer!

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Shallow beach so you can walk out a long way. The water is no deeper than waist deep.It was easy to find and get too.

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach at high tide.
reviews.text: at high tide, it is one of the most beautiful beaches we have ever been to. But at low tide, its not as good.  Also, depending on the time of year, it can get packed with lots of locals.   Be sure to climb up to the top of the overlook very carefully.  Lots of loose rocks, but its well worth it. The views are amazing and the sunset is one of a kind.

reviews.title: Gorgeous Rocky Beach!
reviews.text: This place was truly amazing. The water was crystal clear with white sugar sand. The backdrop looks like a chunk of the Grand Canyon with wild cacti growing on the mounds.

reviews.title: Drove there on a cloudy day.
reviews.text: Beautiful spot! The four stars are only because of the weather, which was out of our control. Highly recommended as cloudy days are extremely rare.

reviews.title: Amazing...just amazing.
reviews.text: Just no words describe the beauty of this place. The Palapas have just been redone. Beach is very kid friendly. There are however no public restrooms and the trash cans seem to fill up quick.

reviews.title: Paradise no more, it's been discovered
reviews.text: We went on a Saturday. Parking lot full, palapas taken (last time I visited there were no palapas..)Still a pretty spot, but not what it was ten years ago.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach 🏖👍🏻☀️
reviews.text: One of the best beaches we visited when in Cabo. Was worth the drive of 2 hrs with screaming/hungry kids in the car.You can walk all the way across and the water would reach a little over your waist. Water is a little chilly but once you get in and with the scorching nice sun you later feel the water get a little warm. Also water was a bit salty unlike any other beach .Don’t recommend taking any sodas since there’s quite a few bees 🐝 . Also make sure to use the restroom before you get there (maybe an OXXO) since no restrooms or showers at all, especially if your traveling like us with 9 kids. There’s a couple of umbrella’s but have to get there early to get your own, since later in the afternoon more people come. There’s also a guy renting Kayaks for an hour for 2 or 3 people in a single kayak , 2 people was $250 pesos for an hour which is not bad. Highly recommend you wearing water shoes since there’s quite a few unusual things in water eg. some type of slugs and some small fishes.Overall would definitely visit again.

reviews.title: spectacular
reviews.text: ok, everyone wants to find that special beach with white sand and crystal clear water.  Well this is it.  the netire bay is no more than 5 ft deep at any point and lots of fish to snorkle with as well.take food and drink as No restaurants or bars there. but 5 min away at Tecolote Beach

reviews.title: Hidden gem near La Paz
reviews.text: This beach is excellent for those who can't swim well since the crystal clear water is pretty shallow. And the best part, at least for those who'd rather travel by foot than with a rental car, is that there IS a bus that goes here from La Paz's Bus Terminal (Aguilar). From November to December, the bus for that route runs every 2 or so hours, and the last bus back to La Paz is at 5:45PM. For a round-trip ride, the cost is 100 pesos (5 USD), and the travel time is about an hour each way. I highly suggest taking an earlier bus to get the full glimpse of the beach in all its colorful splendor. Unfortunately for me, I only had enough time to take the 3:30PM bus, and I didn't get there until around 4ish. The beach was still beautiful but it didn't have the alluring blue color that I was hoping to see. It's quite a sight to behold with the shallow beach stretching in every direction being wrapped in a mountainous embrace by hills that are adorned with green, spiny cacti. When planning a trip to La Paz, make sure you allot enough time for this beach as well as the Tecolote beach, which is a bit farther away. I only got to see Balandra but it's still worth it.

reviews.title: Great White Sand Beach
reviews.text: This was a clean beach with free plapas if you get there early. You can walk around the rocks to the Flower Rock when the tide is low.

reviews.title: Pretty but crowded
reviews.text: This beach is beautiful, but the day we went there were WAY too many people.  The water is calm, clear and shallow.  Perfect for famililes with small children and conveniently close to town.  Fortunately we found other beaches nearby that weren't as congested.

reviews.title: Cabo whale shark tour
reviews.text: Incredible sunset visit to balandra water very warm. One of the most spectacular beaches in Mexico great for snorkeling and enjoying the beach and views

reviews.title: Beautiful beach and bay!
reviews.text: Just a short 30 minute drive from La Paz, definitely the nicest beach in the area.  The road is not marked very well but if you hit the ferry port you are on the right track.  Nice clean shallow water, great for kids.  There are many palapas on the beach but are taken by 10:30 so get there a bit early if you want shade.  We shared ours with an older Mexican couple who had come out later in the day.

reviews.title: Water is stunning !!
reviews.text: Decide to drive here from San Jose del Cabo.. maybe 3 hours (one way).  Would of loved to have stayed near by for a night instead of driving back right away, lots of places I would of loved to stop at ..but we were leaving for home the next morning:(I read where people mention something about a food truck.. but not while we were there. Come prepared with extra bottled water, food, blanket to sit on and a floating device (this would if been the bomb for me). No restrooms.A handful of palapas lined the beach.  We hunkered down by the rocks to get a break from the sun.I did see a vendor renting out kayaks and such.  If we would have gotten here earlier in the day, would have defiantly done that. Great inlet, could of went over to the other side to visit.. but you really could of walked to the other side, water was waist deep if that ....so beautiful and relaxing.Couple dogs were out running in the water ..looked like they were enjoying this as much as we were.Lot of great rock formation.  As of right now,  this place it pretty much untouched..but give it time and their will be building all over this area :( which will be just another tourist trap.Would defiantly take this drive again..

reviews.title: An absolute must "go to" when in La Paz!
reviews.text: Take everything you need, because they don't sell a thing here, but pack the cooler, some shade and spend the day swimming in this natural pool!

reviews.title: Good Beach- Be Prepared
reviews.text: Hello-Good day at the beach.   We are staying in Cabo so it's a drive!  The waiter at the Cape recommended we go since we had a car.  Be prepared - there are no close facilities/food/stores so think ahead.  We only stayed about 1.5 hours because I didn't want to drive back in the dark.  It was lovely and it's truly a locals only spot.

reviews.title: Beach paradise
reviews.text: Perfect turquoise warm waters and white, fine sand. This is one of the most picturesque beaches we've seen and incredibly quiet. If you're in La Paz, Balandra is a must visit!

reviews.title: Most beautiful beach ever!
reviews.text: Wonderful beach a 30-minute busied from the Malecon in La Paz. There are very few services, so bring everything you need!

reviews.title: A must see in La Paz but you don't have to spend all day
reviews.text: This beach is definitely a must see.  We spent about 3 hours here and it was very enjoyable.  The water is from waist to chest high for what seems like miles.  The water was a great temperature and we never did get chilled nor did we need a wetsuit.  There weren't a lot of fish in the first 500 feet of beach but, once you get to the rocks you will want your snorkel gear because the snorkeling was great.  From where you park your vehicle as you look out over the Palapas the rocks are off to the right.  As you go around those rocks you will see another beach which you can't see from the parking lot.  At the end of that beach is the balancing rock that everybody photographs.  Once you get to the balancing rock, this is the place for some good snorkeling and fish viewing.  We did not end up with a Palapa and I probably wouldn't again unless I had young ones.  Kakaks were available and I think it was $250 pesos per hour.  If you are in a hurry I would grab a kayak.

reviews.title: Gorgeous!
reviews.text: Beautiful beach! Water is blue and clear. Great for snorkeling and walking along the rocks. Bring food-drinks

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Worth the drive, very clean beach.  Great for taking in the view of the Beautiful Sea of Cortez.  It can be very busy.

reviews.title: Paradise!
reviews.text: One of my favorite beaches, great for families with young kids, friends and couples, the colors of this place makes you believe in paradise!

reviews.title: Pretty beach if a little remote!
reviews.text: A lovely beach some 30 minutes south of La Paz. There are palapas for shade along the beach and kayaks for hire too. Worth a visit.

reviews.title: Most amazing beach area.
reviews.text: No stingrays and we walked for hours barefoot in the water. Highly recommend the kayak. No bathrooms, no beverages or food for sale. There are like 12 palapas

reviews.title: Desert vs Ocean = Contrast
reviews.text: Based on reviews, I had high expectations on this beach. When we visited Balandra it was low tide and 90ish F weather and had just visited Coyote beach. The contrast was magnificent as you sea the dry desert, but yet you have a beautiful crystal clear ocean and when you look further you can see a deeper blue ocean with sea boat passing by. People were taking advantage of the low tide and were walking to the other side of the mountains or kayaking. We admired the views, took some photos and ran to our car with ac. They don't have any vendors on the beach so you must bring your own beverages, but they had free palapas. I would recommend Coyote beach as the waters were calmed and you can swim and there were vendors. By all means, visit Balandra and admire the contrasts.

reviews.title: Beautiful locals beach and cove
reviews.text: We were so excited to have found this spot! It was relatively uncrowded, had plenty of parking, and public palapas available for use (some in the water and others on the beach). All palapas were being used when we arrived so luckily we brought our own beach umbrellas, which were great for the crazy hot sun, but it was so windy they kept getting blown away (not sure how often it's windy since we only came once). The water itself was surprisingly cool since most of the bay is no more than waist deep. Snorkeling wasn't great although you could see several school of fish swimming around. There are no facilities or food/drinks for purchase anywhere on this beach. There also were no vendors anywhere on the beach, which was a great relief from Cabo! I recommend getting there early (before 2 pm) to get a public palapa!

reviews.title: Most beautiful beach in Mexico
reviews.text: Amazing beach, protected from the waves which makes it very easy to swim. As it is quite big and far from the city, not a lot of people go there. One of the most beautiful beaches in Mexico.

reviews.title: Beautiful bay
reviews.text: Don’t miss this stunningly beautiful beach. No sign of any jellyfish when we went - just amazing. Not very crowded either.

reviews.title: Very beautiful public beach
reviews.text: This is my first time in Mexico. It is very beautiful beach. You have to visit the mushroom, icon of la paz. Good thing to realize that this is a public beach. My friend told me that peoples of la paz refused hotel investment in order to make this beach publicly accessible and to protect environment. It's like people's wins over capital. No fee to enjoys this beach

reviews.title: Great Snorkling
reviews.text: It is October my family and I spent the day here.  The water is higher than when we visit in the winter months.  Went snorkling around the rocks near the upside down rock (on the right side of the beach) and it was great.  I continued snorkling quite far and came to another white-sandy beach.    It is true, there are agua malas (microscopic jelly fish) and they do sting.  I applied a thick coat of vasoline jelly as a barrier between my skin and the agua malas and it worked.  I didn't get stung once but other people did.  Suggestion is to pack a cooler with water and food.  It gets very hot out there so bring shade with you i.e. cabana or tarp with poles.

reviews.title: Beware the “Agua Mala”!
reviews.text: Balandra Bay is very pretty, but please be aware that in the warmer months (like now, October) swimmers can get badly stung by tiny invisible creatures. The locals call it “agua mala” — “bad water”. I call it “a bunch of tiny microscopic bendejos”! I went there for a snorkel at about 9:30am on a lovely clear October morning. The place was deserted, the water was warm and clear, and I set out with my snorkel gear and thankfully a long-sleeved swim shirt. That shirt saved me from having a horrible itchy rash over my whole body... I hit an area where these little buggers congregate, and got badly stung. It feels like stinging nettles being rubbed all over your skin. I have been stung by jellyfish before in Mexico, but there was nothing to see in the water. The rash didn’t,t appear until that night, and an awful, bumpy, itchy rash it is. Thank goodness I had that swim shirt on... most jellyfish &o their nasties can’t sting through even a thin layer of fabric. Even nylons offer protection -next trip I am bringing several pair.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: We spent Christmas Eve on this beach in 2016 and it was lovely.  We were able to walk all the way across the bay to the other side.  The beach was clean and uncrowded.  There is a small snack stand there where you can buy limited things, but it's good to bring your own

reviews.title: Great Beach
reviews.text: Well but much to say other than it's a nice Beach, one of the best in town, this Beach has great sunsets too!

reviews.title: Quite disappointing
reviews.text: We came to this beach with very high expectations because everybody told us that it was amazing. Arriving there and walking around for a while, we could not understand at all the hype about this beach. Shallow and brackish water, not really clean beach. Definitely no place to swim or even pass the day in our opinion. Even Playa el Tecolote 2 minutes drive from there was nicer for a swim. Both of them still nothing in comparison to the beaches around Todos Santos.

reviews.title: best beach in La Paz
reviews.text: this is a must on your trip... far but totally worth it!!beautiful beach, beautiful views, free, nature, calm & short water, ideal for kayak!don't miss it

reviews.title: one of my favorite spots
reviews.text: I never want this place to be crowded so I should keep everyone away but really it's amazing!  Not easy to get to. We rented a car and drove from San Jose Del Cabo.  Long drive but went by fast and we would do it again.

reviews.title: Nice surprise
reviews.text: We heard about this beach from another guest at the hotel. We recommend it. It's a state beach and they take good care of it. Go early to get a palapa, they are free to the public.

reviews.title: No sign of impact from hurricane Lidia
reviews.text: We explored all the famed Cabo swimmable beaches after hurricane Lidia and will not feel comfortable sending our kids into the water except this one. Beautiful and don't forget your snorkeling gear - no vendor here for equipment rental

reviews.title: Great Sunset !
reviews.text: It is a really nice and quaint beach with a stunning outlook for a sunset. I climbed the hill to get a better look and was totally worth the hike.

reviews.title: Hermoso paisaje
reviews.text: Una de las playas más bonitas que he visistado en Mexico. One of the most beautiful beaches in mexico, You might wanna go after raining season so the water level goes up.

reviews.title: Beautiful spot
reviews.text: Balandra beach has a huge expanse of sandy beach with lots of shallow water to play in. The snorkelling out around the rocks was quite good too.

reviews.title: Touring La Paz
reviews.text: Calm water,  clean and everyone was friendly.. also not too deep for those that don't swim.  We didn't realize to bring swimming outfits. Also you can see fish swimming

reviews.title: The natural paradise endless pool
reviews.text: The beach of your dreams. A natural pool with no end.You should come and walk to the stone, little far but worth it!

reviews.title: Relaxing beach, great for small kids.
reviews.text: Picturesque beach on the northern outskirts of La Paz offer calm shallow water which is great for little kids.Recommend getting there early to get a Palapa.

reviews.title: Beautiful Place
reviews.text: We went kayaking in Bay with Cortez Club and was well worth our time.  Really a beautiful area with a number of beach, crystal clear water and easy to kayak across all of it.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach but not worth the drive.
reviews.text: Don't get me wrong, it is a beautiful beach but it was super packed. There was no parking and it was a Tuesday afternoon.It was just okay.

reviews.title: Great beach. Shallow and warm forever. Rent a kayak and head to the right along the shore. Turquoise and gorgeous wayers
reviews.text: Private beach with about a dozen shade shelters. A few vendors - food and trinkets - and you can rent kayaks (which I recommend). Very accessible via bus from the malecon in La Paz. I would be there now if I could be.

reviews.title: Interesting Place
reviews.text: It's a beautiful and interesting place. Not sure if it's worth a drive from cabo san lucas. We rented a car and drove to the beach from Cabo via todos santos and a stop at Hotel California and it took about 2.5 hours. The beach parking lot was small and filled to the brim but we managed to find a place to park. The bay was beautiful however, the water was warm and had an unpleasant smell near the beach and there was lots of sea scum floating in the water which was pretty pretty gross. You could walk out into the bay forever and the water was only waist deep, pretty cool as far as that goes. And if you had a kayak it would be all the more interesting as it is such a big area to explore.

reviews.title: Hands down the best beach in BCS
reviews.text: Pull out the checklist:1. Crystal clear water-check2. Swimmable-check3. Plenty of aquatic life--check4.  Desolate-check5. Minimal tourists--check 6. White sand-check7. Pure nature- checkThis list can go on and on, but you get the picture.

reviews.title: Beautiful calm waters perfect for children, 1st time paddle boarding & view
reviews.text: Make the trek to Balandra Beach to enjoy the calm shallow waters of this amazing beach.  You can swim, snorkel and just kick back.  There are a few vendors that rent stand up paddle boards and kayaks.  If you get there early, grab a palapa for the shade.  There are chairs and tables set up on the beach that you can use.  Personnel on the beach do sell snacks, water and 1 vendor appeared to be selling fish.  The best vendor is the ice cream cart that is in the water..:)

reviews.title: Magical Beach in Baja
reviews.text: Loved this beach, a lovely expansive shallow lagoon with clear water surrounded by gently rolling, desert hills. Nice beach with palapas, parking and restrooms. A great place to spend the day, very relaxing.

reviews.title: Gorgeous!
reviews.text: Shallow waters all around, you can walk to the other side and have your own private beach. However recommend you bring some of your own shade if you come on a busy day

reviews.title: One of the most beautiful beaches
reviews.text: Balandra is one of the most beautiful beaches in the world!! A hidden gem, but make sure you take your gear there when you go visit! Take a towel and an umbrella if not you would have to rent one, it is insanely hot but the water is amazing!!! Water reaches about 5ft high, its like a giant swimming pool!!

reviews.title: One of the most beautiful places on earth
reviews.text: It is a paradise!Its better to get there by boat. We went with Cora Tours they really know the place, so they tell you exactly where the best scuba diving spots are.it is great for kids because its very shallow.Dont miss it if you ever go to La Paz

reviews.title: so we decided to visit the mushroom shape rock
reviews.text: after being some days in cabo we decided to visit the famous mushroom shape rock in balandra breach, it was a very very quite beach there were no waves so we could easly walk a lot of meters in this beach, it is very relaxing and admiring the mushroom rock was worth the visit

reviews.title: Most Beatiful Beach
reviews.text: This is the most beautiful beach you will ever see. The water is crystal clear, the beach is gorgeous and a must see.

reviews.title: One of The Most Beautiful Beaches in Baja California Sur
reviews.text: The first time I laid eyes on Balandra Beach, I was stunned. Having traveled the Baja Peninsula extensively, I thought that I had seen the most beautiful of what the beaches had to offer. This place is magnificent.

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach
reviews.text: Went there twice in our short 3 days getaway in la paz....... Gorgeous.. The water is nice..... The activity is affordable.

reviews.title: BEAUTIFUL AND CALM
reviews.text: This beach is very calm. I recommend it for smaller kids. Most beautiful beach I have visited in La Paz

reviews.title: Most beautiful beach!
reviews.text: If you are in La Paz make sure you check out Balandra. One of the most beautiful beaches in the world. Completely isolated and protected beach means nothing but absolute serenity.

reviews.title: Warm and clear water with wonderful views
reviews.text: I went there after going to Isla Espiritu Santo with On board Baja travel agency, they took us to a part of the beach that is not accessible by car or walking, so it was a more private part of the Beach. This is a very big place and the depth of the water varies a lot depending on where you are, what doesnt really change is that it is amazingly beautiful wherever you look at. It has a little for all tastes, there is a part  of the beach (where the famous stone is) which is crowded and if you are more into privacy, you can walk a little bit more of do SUP until you get to a more quiet place.

reviews.title: Bring everything!!
reviews.text: It's a nice, calm and pretty beach at La Paz! We brought our full face snorkel mask and we expend the entire day in water. Bring a wetsuit coz the water is a little chill. Food and drinks are a must coz there is just a small kiosk and nothing else.

reviews.title: paradise beach
reviews.text: It is a jewel of nature, I had never seen such a beautiful bay and could walk safely and admire the surroundings ... worth spending some time there and just make the trip to meet her

reviews.title: Beautful Beach!!!
reviews.text: Balandra beach is absolutely the most beautiful beach in Baja Mexico!  The water is stunning and the color changes depending on the angle of the suns rays. Incredibly breath taking. Its not deep and you can walk out forever.  Definitely a must see if you visit La Paz!

reviews.title: It's a Drive, But Worth It!
reviews.text: Beautiful!  If you want a relaxing, photo op beach....this is it.  It was an all day trip for us.  We drove from San José Del Cabo and it took about 2 to 3 hours to get there.  (We stopped on the way and had lunch.) There are two ways to get there from San José Del Cabo. On the way there, we went the Hwy 1 route.  It's mostly a two lane highway that goes through the mountains.  It was nice, but the steep turns/curves to get through the mountains became relentless.  If (when) you get stuck behind a slow truck or car, it's really hard to get around it because there are very few long enough stretches to see if a car is coming from the other direction (and I'm not a timid driver).  On the way back, we decided not to re-live Hwy 1, so we took the route that is mainly Hwy 19 with a partial toll in Cabo (about 35-50 pesos).  It was less hectic and we even managed to get to our dinner reservations on time--which we thought wasn't gonna happen.  We used our iphone 7 to take a panoramic pic of the view and it was beautiful to send to friends and family at home or on social media.  (Ok, my 15 yr old daughter did it, but I used it. ;) )  The really nice thing about the water there is the fact that it's about waist high deep.  You can walk out very far (maybe even to the opposite beach, I'm not sure) throughout the cove.  My daughter and her friend went paddle boarding and said it was super easy to rent the boards and loved it.  There are snacks and drinks you can buy as well as umbrellas, tables, and chairs to rent.  (We rented an umbrella, one table, and four chairs for 250 pesos.)  I think we got the last umbrella, so be aware that it isn't an endless supply.  (You will definitely need some sort of umbrella if the weather is nice, don't think you won't.)  The beach had a lot of people on it, but not too many at all (at least the day we went on a Thursday).  We had plenty of room around us.It's considered one of the best beaches in the world. So, if you are near or even if it's a bit of a drive to get there....go experience this beach.  You won't regret it.

reviews.title: Awesome!!!
reviews.text: This is one of the beaches in Cabo for children. I have a 7 year old that was able to swim almost through the whole place in the ocean. He also did some kayaking there and visited the mushroom rock. Water was clear!!! Great place for children.

reviews.title: Very busy beach
reviews.text: We arrived around 10 am. Already, the parking lot was getting full. We found a corner for the car (Toyota Prius) but could not pull forward entirely because the spot had a huge rock. The parking was free.Already all the public umbrellas were taken. A vender offered to rent some chairs, table and umbrella. This came up to 250 pesos. People keep on arriving. It was a Monday, and I just cannot imagine this place on a weekend. I searched for some food. Not a lot of options there. Someone had a stand and sold candy and lots of unhealthy food, and some cold sodas. Someone else had mango. It would have been a great idea to be better prepared with some sandwiches. Dogs were permitted on the beach, but not in the water. When we were ready to go, we could not proceed. Someone with a huge Toyota Hilux had packed right behind the Prius. I saw someone else wanting to leave, but there was also a car parked right behind him. This is when I witnessed the Mexican collaboration system. A group of men lifted the badly parked car and moved it just enough to allow the other guy to leave. Eventually we found the Hilux owner and he left with his big truck. Lots of other eager drivers wanted the spot and I had to stand in the way to prevent them from taking the spot until the Prius was out. That parking lot was a madhouse. The beach itself was the best one. The water was very shallow and clear.

reviews.title: Just amazing!
reviews.text: Balandra Beach is unlike any other spot I have seen, and I've been to many of the best beaches in the world. Totally unexpected as the Pacific side of Mexico is not usually as clear and blue as the Cancun side. This place is an exception. It's like mother nature coughed up tons of pure white sand and filled the whole bay. Then flooded it with clean clear water that never goes past waste or chest level. You can wade all over the bay, look at fish, cool rock formations, hills of sand piled high and deep on the shores, and just float around in warm clear blue water. Warm water and warm beaches make this place a one of mother natures masterpiece's. Go there!!

reviews.title: Relaxing day at beach
reviews.text: We took a cab out to the beach, walked along the waters edge to the beach around the point and had the beach to ourselves all day. We hiked up the hill and over the top to the little rental building where the cab dropped us off  I do not recommend that hike,  to many rattle snakes. Stay by the beach. Take lots to drink.

reviews.title: Lovely beach
reviews.text: We went there after swimming with sea lions, and it was really lovely. It's nice and calm and so pretty. Chrystal clear water

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviews.text: One of the Best Beaches I have ever seen in my life! A must visit place! La Paz! 30 minutes from Downtown and Malecon La Paz! Please arrived at least 8:30am to save your palapa but must bring your own food and drinks! Loved it!! Will come back!

reviews.title: Just AMAZING!!!
reviews.text: This is the place to take your young kids if they are into snorkeling or just playing at the beach.  It's not that crowded when I came here and nearly walked across to the other side of the bay.  Bring your picnic snacks and make sure you potty ahead of time.  Else fine a bush because there is not bathroom.

reviews.title: Loved it!
reviews.text: I loved being at this beach with the locals. We walked across the walked to the other side.It was awesome!

reviews.title: Perfect spot to relax
reviews.text: This beach is beautiful. The water is very shallow and calm so it is perfect to visit with children or people who can't swim. We took por paddleboards and explored other nearby beaches. Definitely one of our favorite spots in La Paz.

reviews.title: World Class Beach so far unspoiled by Commercialization *Heads Up no Washrooms* Dog Friendly :)
reviews.text: Stunning Beach, warm clean water. We went 4 times during our 10 day stay we loved it so much! We were staying at the Hyatt Place La Paz and therefore were only a quick 15 minute drive from this glorious beach. Small parking lot, that did overflow on the weekend. We were there at the end of May beginning of June and the water was perfect. Apparently it gets quite cold in the winter months. You can rent paddle boards etc there. there are free palace's that fill up first and then you can rent umbrellas and chairs for approximately $5-$10 depending how busy the beach is.... worth it! There was a food truck and souvenir sales there as well. No washrooms so plan ahead before leaving town or prepare to go in the desert!

reviews.title: Beatiful and unrefined...
reviews.text: Balandra Beach is a beautiful location. We took the time to follow the beach and walked to Mushroom Rock. This place is magical. I suggest that you follow the shore toward Mushroom Rock to more secluded beaches. Be aware to NOT climb the sand dunes, there are snakes on them. The Baja is a magical place and this beach is part of that magic.

reviews.title: Balandra Beach!
reviews.text: Just amazing and a great place to visit!! You definitely need to kayak and go see the famous rock of Balandra!

reviews.title: Worth the Drive....
reviews.text: We drove all the way from Cabo San Lucas which took about two hours. Getting through Cabo with the road construction and navigating through the unknown streets of La Paz took some time. Allow yourself extra time if this is your first trip.We stopped for lunch along the Malecon in La Paz which afforded us a much needed break. The drive up to Balandra (Spanish for sloop) took about 30 minutes.The waters are crystal clear and you can virtually walk across the bay. The depth is mostly 3 ft and at the deepest maybe 5 feet. There are kayaks, chairs and umbrellas for rent. Local venders have water, and other cold drinks. There are no restrooms.If you have kids of any age, this is the pace to take them. No currents and the consistent clear shallow water will put anyone at ease.We were there during the week in early June and the parking lot was full. I am not sure what it's like on weekends as this beach is popular with the locals.As we have a place in Cabo we will plan on spending the night in La Paz to allow us more time for all the other activities there.

reviews.title: WHAT A BEACH...!!
reviews.text: This is one of the most photographed and popular beaches in La Paz, and for the Baja as well. About a 30 minute drive out the bay from the city, you wouldn't know it was there until you made the final curve. White-sand beaches, and desert-like cliffs add to the experience. A must-see for anyone visiting the area.

reviews.title: Ranked one of the best beaches in the world
reviews.text: At low tide you can walk all the way across the bay. The water is warm and the sand is fine. Also the location of El Hongo (the mushroom rock).

reviews.title: Beach till you drop
reviews.text: walk forever is crystal clear warm water, see fish and wildlife, soft sand, amazing colours and landscape, best beach ever.

reviews.title: Stunning beach close to La Paz - worth the drive!
reviews.text: We headed out to Balandra mid morning and the place was already busy!  Rented chairs, table and umbrella on the beach and enjoyed the fabulous view.  Also rented a SUP and took turns paddling in the cove.  The water is so warm and shallow you'd think you were in a bath!  Busy, but everyone was so friendly and social it made for a very fun day.  No bathrooms is the only real downside. Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Very nice beach
reviews.text: Beautiful beach in the middle of the desert, perfect for kayaks. There are no bathrooms there, so you can go to the town next to Balandra, no more than 4 minutos away, the name of this beach is Tecolote.

reviews.title: Fanstatic Beach
reviews.text: This is one of the best beaches I have experienced in Mexico.  The water is calm and clear. The water level is low enough to walk across to the other side of the beach.  This seems to be a favorite spot for the local - so it gets crowded with families and large groups.  However, still a great place to spend the day or few hours.  There is only one vendor that has a few snack items for sale; umbrellas and chairs for rental - so, it is best to bring your own stuff.

reviews.title: Giant swimming pool!!
reviews.text: The water is so calm and blue! It was also a pretty nice temperature when we were there as well. It's also very shallow. You have to walk out really far to even get waist deep! I recommend bringing plenty of snacks, drinks, etc in a cooler so you can stay for several hours. There are people selling food, drinks, water, hats etc. in the event that you forget something, but the selection may be limited. This is a great place to go for fun in the sun!

reviews.title: Top beach
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I have ever been. Feels like being in Greece. Unfortunately some people visiting are loud, noisy, irrespectful and lack in education and sensitivity to admire this paradise.

reviews.title: Extremely crowded
reviews.text: Water level waaay too low and very crowded no umbrella rentals available. People selling mangos tried to rip me off bought 2 mangos and gave them a $20 USD and try to give me back 60 pesos.

reviews.title: A day of sun and sea
reviews.text: Beautiful beach with colors that reflect a true acquarium. A bus service from downtown La Paz make it easy to reach from town without the need of a car, snacks and drinks can be bought on place and kajak rental is available as well. It's advisable to arrive in the early morning to have the chance to enjoy a free umbrella.

reviews.title: Wedding Anniversary
reviews.text: Gorgeous place hidden in La Pax, you definitely have to visit this paradise...You will not regreat it, tour Lobito with Edgar is who to book with.

reviews.title: Perfection
reviews.text: Wow, clean warm and perfect.  We visited for a  few hours in our Panga with Baja Expeditions and could have spent a day "earthing" in this pristine spot.

reviews.title: one of the most stunning place i have visited
reviews.text: It is imposible to be in Baja California Sur and not pay a visit to this place! So easy to get to. Spend the day, it is never overly busy.

reviews.title: Marvelous spot
reviews.text: just a lovely, peaceful beach, about 30 minutes from the Malecon ... WELL worth the trip.  Only downside, no food available for sale... so take a picnic

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: We went mid week in late April. It was pretty quiet and a beautiful beach with a shallow, warm, clean, bright blue bag that is ideal for paddle boarding or families. Well worth the drive.

reviews.title: Everyone loves this beach
reviews.text: It is a beautiful white sand beach, absolutely packed with families camping out for the day.  Not my cup of tea, the beach in front of our hotel was just as calm and much quieter.

reviews.title: Great Place For Family
reviews.text: The bay is amazing.  It is mostly shallow and you can walk out into the middle of the bay.  Just make sure you shuffle your feet to avoid being stung by any sting rays.  Also, make sure you walk up to the mirador from the road leading to the parking lot for some amazing views and photo opportunities.  There are hardly any fish in the bay and so not much to see underwater.  They rent kayaks as well which we did as a family.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: It is a beautiful beach.  Make sure to rent one of the umbrellas...it gets really hot and the sun is very intense.  We were there on a Saturday and the crowds started showing up in the later afternoon.  We took the Eco Baja Tours bus from the Malecon.  It was a good price, but the buses are a little unpredictable...sometimes they pick you up and drop you off at different spots so it is easy to miss the bus.  There is limited food and water here, so pack something.  There are manta rays here, so be careful.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Beautiful beach.....too crowded for me. Beautiful water but all of the tourists go here too packed for my likings

reviews.title: Don't miss this beach!
reviews.text: Absolutely beautiful!!!! Gorgeous soft sandy beach and clear water. Take a cooler. Although no food/drink place at this beach definitely the most beautiful of this stretch of beaches

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: Although the water was really Cold, its scenary its very beautiful. In the Beach you can find snacks, drinks (sodas and water) and you May rent umbrellas and chairs.

reviews.title: Crystal water
reviews.text: If you're planning to go to balandra, be there early.There is not a lot parking slots, and the umbrella renting is limited.Beautiful beach with crystal water and you can have a nice walk to go on the other side of the watch an emblematic rock like a mushroom.If you have aqua shoes bring them, a lot of rocks on the way and some at the bottom of the sea.

reviews.title: Super beach
reviews.text: Clean and relax beach natural space with great view . You can see and stay for a long  time enjoying the water you can walk to the balandra stone to take pictures and enjoy the natural  blue water

reviews.title: Pristine beach better accessed by boat
reviews.text: even though we were here at the highest possible time (Easter), it still felt quite private and extremely enjoyable. Great quality sand and very clear water.

reviews.title: Amazing beach
reviews.text: Get there early or late to avoid the crowds but spectacular beach.  Make sure and bring most of what you need as there isn't much to buy there which is part of the beauty.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Quiet and lovely. Recommend going early in the morning. We have rented a car to get there and it was good decision.

reviews.title: Not to be missed!
reviews.text: Balandra is one the most beautiful beaches I've ever been to. You can walk forever out in the water! Make a point of going up there when you are in LaPaz!

reviews.title: Heaven on earth
reviews.text: Paradise -perfect beach to relax at or kayak or paddle bots! Not much food , so eat lunch in La Paz before !

reviews.title: Balandra Beach Beauty
reviews.text: Approximately 2 and 15 min away from Cabo by car was a wonderful find in La Paz. Highly recommended if you are staying in Cabo for some time. Beach is not crowded at all during the week Water is warm tranquil so inviting to jump in. Bring your cooler with drinks as there really is nothing there as far as resorts. Young kids love it. You can Rent a kayak or stand up board along with chairs and umbrellas at that beach. No beer sales only snacks sold there. Safe drive

reviews.title: Beautiful if you come into it by water; just OK otherwise
reviews.text: This beach is a quick drive (less than 30 minutes) from La Paz.  Now that it has become more popular, like anything, it's lost some of its awesomeness.   Aside from the long sandbar and a view of the icon of La Paz, a mushroom stone carved away by water (think of it like Lovers Arch in Cabo), another beach up the way is just as beautiful (Tecolote)   But you probably would not feel this way if you hadn't seen it previously.   The truly breathtaking way to see it is to come into the cove by boat.  From that perspective there are several beautiful and secluded sand bars to lounge on.  Perfect for paddle boarding because the water is so calm.  There's also a mangrove area which is OK to paddle through, but it is a bit stiffeling with no air moving around much.

reviews.title: Most beautiful beach!
reviews.text: We love coming to this beach when we visit La Paz. It is so beautiful. We rented a kayak to paddle around the coves, but it really was too windy for this. Be aware of the wind before you rent. It's easy to wade around the shallow water even if it's cool like it is in January. Pick a sunny day during this month. There are a few permanent thatch umbrellas that you can use or bring your own. Fun place to take kids. There is a little vendor truck where you can rent paddle boards and kayaks. They also have snacks, drinks and sunscreen. There was a souvenir vendor the day we went also. We travelled here January 2016.

reviews.title: A favorite daysail from La Paz - Picnic, swim, and be back before sundown
reviews.text: Balandra is about a two hour sail from La Paz.  In the daytime, we anchor off the famous "Mushroom Rock".  We swim and snorkel in crystal clear water about two fathoms deep.  As always, the colorful reef fish favor the rocky areas.  This is a superb area to learn standup paddle boarding in the calm inner coves.  Novice kayakers have much to explore along this coast.  Larger sailboats and motor yachts anchor far out near the entrance to the bay.  Other visitors have warned about the stingrays that lie in the shallow waters, so shuffle your feet when you walk and they will move out of your way.  They are not aggressive, only defensive.  Summer is not the best season to visit as the bobos and other flying insects may pester you.  We haven't been bothered by jellyfish, but they may be a periodic issue.  It's always a good idea to ask the locals and observe carefully before entering the water anywhere.

reviews.title: Crystalline
reviews.text: Beautiful, quiet beach. No motor boats allowed. Several palapas to sit under. Shallow , clear water with many sand bars. Must walk out a bit to swim. Perfect for little ones!

reviews.title: Beautiful place
reviews.text: This is truly a most wonderful place.  The beach is wide, white and usually not overly crowded but we were there on a week day so not sure about weekends. Bring your own umbrella or there are some rentals.  Not much shade.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: This beach is about a 30 minute car ride from La Paz. The road is being worked on so there could be some delays. Also, there is a port near there so there are lots of big trucks speeding on the two lane road. One you pass the port, then the road is less crazy. There is a parking lot, small place to buy some drink and rent gear. The water is calm and the tide takes the water out quite a ways. You can walk out far with the water still at the knees. Be aware that there are small stingrays resting in the sand under the water. It is safer to scoot your feet while in the water instead of picking them up. Apparently, people get stung quite frequently and it is very unpleasant. There are some umbrellas on the beach. You can easily swim or walk around the rocks and there is a really nice deserted beach on the other side of this one. I felt the water a bit too cold to swim but that is my personal taste. I like warm water. Probably better to rent a car so you can come and go as you please.

reviews.title: What a beautiful landscape, great place to relax!!
reviews.text: Balandra beach is not mentioned in most of the travel guides we've used to plan our trip. Talking to a local person, he suggested it to us, and what a great surprise!!This beach offers calm water, with different colors due to sand benches and a beautiful rock formation that completes the visual. It is easy to go up on the mountains that surround the beach and take incredible pictures... and the sunset is simply terrific!!We took the day to relax there, in the main beach part you can find shadow and some infrastructure, but in the next one, where you can find the hongo, you must be prepared for the sun, nothing there.We had a car, so we went to another beach, with waves, Tecolote, to have lunch, and I got the best pulpo ceviche of the trip!! Unfortunately I won't remember the name of the restaurant, but it has a sign with pictures of the food... so fresh, awesome.We came back to Balandra to see the sunset, a bonus to close the day!!

reviews.title: Balandra one of the top ten beaches in Mexico according to the US Today
reviews.text: Beautiful beach and one of the top 10 beaches in Mexico rated by the US Today as I found this article by google it and I can say that for sure it is like to have a private paradise!! Balandra is a public beach with nothing in it but the beautiful sea of Cortes and the incredible almost white sand that everybody can enjoy for free. So if you go to La Paz visit Balandra is a must!!! It is amaizing the beautiful landscape you can apreciatte whe you are there!!

reviews.title: For a day at the beach...perfect!
reviews.text: Balandra beach is a popular local/family beach. The water is shallow and warm for a LONG distance so kids can play in a large area. If you want more quiet and you're mobile, just walk to the next beach around the corner but bring an umbrella if you want shade. If you want even more peace and quiet, just walk around the next corner and it's even better...very few people and a rock overhang that give shade until around 4 pm. Note: no bathroom facilities at all so you need to go au natural. There are some vendors at the first beach but bring what you want just to be safe. The walk to the second beach is fairly easy, but to the third is over coarse volcanic rock and you need to be nibble-footed and in shape to make it there. The first beach you cand drive straight there or take a local bus. Either way, go earlier as most people start showing up at around 11 and the shade huts at the first beach get taken up quickly.

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: Beautiful, peaceful beach. Few amenities. You can walk a long ways in the warm, very shallow water. If you love beaches you should not miss the one.

reviews.title: The best beach I've ever been to.
reviews.text: This place was increditable. Soft white sands, clear water. Great for kids. Get there early to get a good spot.

reviews.title: Heaven in beach form!
reviews.text: Had heard of Balandra the same time I heard of La Paz....had very high expectations for the beach and it did NOT disappoint. Plus, it was far less touristy than I would've thought! Easy to get to either by $5 bus round trip or your own car. Beautiful, breathtaking, calm, relaxing- water is crisp and cool. Would pack your own drinks and food! Definitely a place you think you'll hang out for a few hours but end up wanting to be there from dawn to dusk

reviews.title: Breathtaking
reviews.text: White sand, azure blue water surrounded by rocky mountains creates a beach experience that will be memorable.  My husband and I arrived at the beach beach after swimming with whale sharks and seals.  Lunch on the beach..a lovely day.  You can reach the beach by car.  If you are in La Paz take a ride to this beautiful beach and enjoy.

reviews.title: Balandra Beach
reviews.text: Do not miss a visit to this exquisite beach. Gentle shallow water.Get there early for the best light for photography.

reviews.title: Mother Nature's giant turquoise wading pool!
reviews.text: This place is amazing. The water is so clear and shallow throughout the whole bay. Reco buy a cheap floaty on Amazon. Also b/c they have no services I reco bringing an ice chest with some beers and snacks. We hired a van to take us there and paid approx $7/hr for him to wait for us.

reviews.title: Protected and isolated
reviews.text: This beach is a few miles out of La Paz, and is in a protected bay so the water is very calm. There is a decent sized beach and a concession stand for snacks. If you drive a few hundred meters from the beach, you can pull over to the side of the road, climb a very steep hill, and see toward La Paz and out to the Sea of Cortez - a beautiful view.

reviews.title: Most Beautiful Beach in the World
reviews.text: All I can say is just plan a full day at this beach. If you can, get there at high tide and watch it go out and back in again. Walk all over, take pictures all over,take in the blues, browns, greens and crystals. If you are lucky, grab a palapa. Bus ride from town if $5 round trip.

reviews.title: A giant pool!!!
reviews.text: We did Balandra on day two of our trip and definitely want to go back. The beach was large with plenty of room to find your own personal oasis. Water was clear and very cool. There's a little stand where you can rent tiki hunts, kayaks, SUP, and buy small snacks The scenery just leaves you in awe. One of the best beaches I've ever been to

reviews.title: Not for low tide
reviews.text: Great beach at high tide, but not that pretty at low tide.  Bring whatever you need because there's not much available there.

reviews.title: Named one of the best beaches in Mexico
reviews.text: Balandra is a site to behold. This is the place that my husband and I got married 8 years ago. There is a very large beach with many palapas to rent.
