When the tide is out, the water goes forever and only to your ankles while in the bay. Then as you round a bend, there the water gets a little deeper - your knees - and there is another beach that will take you to the infamous Mushroom Rock.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach, great for windy day
reviews.text: After fighting the winds at El Tecolote, I headed to Balandra and had a completely different experience.  Sheltered, shallow, non-commercial...several little beaches tucked in amongst the cliffs.  Wonderful, peaceful place to relax, at least on a weekday in March...can't speak to busier weekends or holidays.

reviews.title: It's like a 3D postcard of paradise.
reviews.text: We got here early (10:30AM) so that we could score on of the free palapas - and then lounged and bathed for hours. The water is so clear and you can walk (for quite a ways) and have the water not even hit your waist. Water was cool but refreshing in March but we loved this place so much that we came back twice! Rented a double kayak for an hour from a local guy (had to give our ID which I wasn't thrilled about but we got it back afterwards). Even offered to share our palapa with a local family that showed up later when all the palapas were gone - safe, fun and enjoyable. Had no problem leaving my stuff under the palapa while my husband and I swam. I saw some people came as part of a tour - so if you don't have a rental car, you can do that. Plenty of parking and the usual people selling local wares. No one was pushy - a simple "no gracias" had them moving on.  The one guy you shouldn't say "no gracias" to is the burrito guy. He came by the first time and I didn't take him up on his offer of a burrito - but there isn't any food out there so on the second visit I decided to give it a try.  $30 pesos for 2 - not your traditional American style burritos but smaller almost like a "roll up". Get the meat one - the bean one doesn't stay warm and isn't good. He delivers to your palapa but on the way out, I stopped by his car where his family was working to grab another ... and he had hot sauces! A definite treat!

reviews.title: Beautiful but no bathroom
reviews.text: This beach was absolutely breathtaking!!! Unfortunately we had to cut the day short, as there was no public washroom that we could find. 😬Remember to shuffle your feet to stir up any sting rays so you don't step on them.

reviews.title: Beauitiful
reviews.text: This beache´s colors are out of this world, come take a photo with you at your personal in-the-open office ;)

reviews.title: Great beach for everyone
reviews.text: The bay is very shallow so the water is safe for young children.  There are water toys for rent.  A good pic site but check on the tide before you go.  Make certain you navigate the shore to the mushroom rock.

reviews.title: Bandera Beach
reviews.text: Beautiful. Easy to get to from La Paz. Shallow, clear, popular beach with stunning rock backdrop. Some hawkers at beach. A few concessions. Good place for swimming, kayaking, sunning?

reviews.title: Gorgeous but the Whale Sharks Had Just Blown My Mind
reviews.text: We did this as a blend of two tours (I was the only one booked to go to Balandra so they merged this and the Whale Shark Tour) - and I went with the Museum of the Whale (you get a free tour of the museum too).It is one of the most beautiful beaches in the world, but after the tour we were cold and being put on the beach felt more like a punishment, I just wanted to wrap up and get in a hot shower.  But it is stunning.

reviews.title: Born to be wild
reviews.text: Probably the wildest though accessible beach of BajaThere is a parking lot and a small food and beverages shop just beside. The water is really shallow so great for young kids and elder peopleI don't concur with the "best beach of BCS or even Mexico" but it's definitely the best of this area.

reviews.title: Unbelivably beautiful beach.
reviews.text: Spent a wonderful day here with our kids (7 and 10). The beach is stunningly beautiful and the water is so shallow that you can just walk out for hundreds of metres. Would be a great place for those with young children. I can't do justice to it with words so go and see for yourselves!

reviews.title: Heaven!!
reviews.text: What can we say??  I have been all over the world and this was by far been the most gorgeous beaches we are ever at. So beautiful and amazing crystal-clear water blue blue. Don't miss it.

reviews.title: Beautiful spot, can be a bit crowded.
reviews.text: Go during the week if you can, it gets a bit crowded on the weekend.  Lovely spot for wading, and if you climb around the corner (through a spot that unfortunately is often used as a bathroom) then you're on another beach, and on the way to the rebuilt balancing rock (La Honga I believe).  Past that you can keep going, wading and walking, and get to another beautiful beach which you're likely to have to yourself.  Go when the sun is out and the water is beautiful blue (it loses a bit of color as the sun goes down).

reviews.title: One of the highlights of our trip.
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful beaches we've ever visited. The water is so clear and pristine. So glad we had the opportunity to vist this most spectacular setting. A word to the wise...check the tide charts before you go. The second time we went the entire bay was almost empty of water! We still had a good time but not as enjoyable as we had to walk so far to get to the water. Did manage to get to the Mushroom that trip though and it was worth the walk. I would definately recommend this beach.

reviews.title: Beautiful scenery!
reviews.text: You have to hit this beach just for the stunning photo opportunities!  Make sure you go right around the corner to the right, walk the beach on the other side until you get to the Hongo.  But beware little stinging jellyfish in the water, and we are pretty convinced we saw a shark on the far side of the Hongo.  Another couple said it was a dolphin and some kids told us it was a Marlin... we will never know for sure, but best to be prudent.

reviews.title: My favorite beach near La Paz - beautiful water and scenery!
reviews.text: We spent several hours at this beach - the beach is really beautiful and it is fun to hike up the rocky parts for beautiful views of the beach. The water was very clear and shallow for a long stretch - we enjoyed walking in to the beach in the clear waters. Highly recommend this beach if you are in La Paz. Also, it is very easy to get to from La Paz - you can take the Aguila bus from the Malecon bus station and it runs quite often during the day. They have a schedule at the bus stop and it was only 70 pesos for the bus ride from Malecon to Balandra beach.

reviews.title: Clear, warm waters. Great view!
reviews.text: This is a short drive out of La Paz but well worth it. When we arrived it was a bit busy but the beach and the water was very, very clear. The hills surrounding the area were very dry and brown which provided an excellent contrast to the aqua colored water. There are a few beaches around this bay, two that are easily accessible from the parking lot, two that had people on them but I don't know how they got there. There are chair and kayak rentals on the beach. Unless you really have the urge to kayak, I'd recommend skipping it. You can almost walk the entire bay area.

reviews.title: A hidden gem
reviews.text: We visited Balandra Beach while vacationing in Cabo San Lucas.  The 4 hour round trip was well worth it. The Beach was beautiful and clean.  We made some great memories there.

reviews.title: Best beach ever!
reviews.text: Beautiful, remote, awe- inspiring. Water is crystal clear. Great for snorkeling. Shallow water for kids.

reviews.title: When tide is out, there is a lot less beach
reviews.text: Best part of Balandra is the short hike up the rocky hills for beautiful views of the sand and water expanse.  The bay area that Balandra is in is very shallow, so the tide level (in or out) make a huge difference in the look of the beach area.

reviews.title: the most beautyful beach in La Paz
reviews.text: turcoise water, long beach, nice to walk or swim,repaired from the wind, the sand is so thin!! You have to go there, and take wonderful pictures!!

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: The sand is soft, the bay is shallow and walkable, and palapas line the beach. Claim your spot and enjoy warm sun and cool breezes in Baja while your friends shiver up north!  When the tide is coming in wading birds fish along the rocks...white ibis, egrets, herons...all having dinner while people walk around them. A great place to spend the day and see the mushroom rock - one of the La Paz landmarks. Just remember it's a natural area. Pack your food and drinks in and your trash out. There is no restaurant or bathroom at this beach but nearby beaches have both - El Tesoro, Pichilingue and Tecolote. Just buy a drink or food at the restaurant and you can use their facilities.

reviews.title: A place to catch your breath
reviews.text: Don't let the popularity of the place fool you, it's relatively unpopulated. Keep walking around the "mushroom" and find a spot to perch during low tide and you will likely be the only person in sight-the rocks keep most people on the sand. Take along a snorkel and mask to catch sight of flute fish and minnows. I waited several hours until the tide came up and swam back to the beach. What a serene experience!

reviews.title: The most beautiful beach in mex
reviews.text: We were there only for a couple of hours unfortunately we didn't had more time, but the time we spend there was awesome, the views, the beaches are so clean and well preserved, they are so virgin no one is there selling you a thing, you can find peace and very amazing sight seen the views are just out of this planet, I would recommend to be there around noon (12:00pm) the color of the sea changes with the sea level

reviews.title: Cool beach, beautiful views, lots of people
reviews.text: We were here on a weekend so lots of people but as we arrived around 3, we still were able to get a spot under a palapa. I think it would be cool to get their early and rent a kayak to go across to one of the isolated beaches across the way. It's very shallow so you can walk quite a distance so perfect for kids. Want more peace and quiet, go further down or across to a quiet beach

reviews.title: Beautiful beach !
reviews.text: A short 15 minute drive from La Paz. Get there early to grab a public umbrella. Rent a kayak. There is a path on the road leading up to a hill from you have a fantastic view of the beaches.

reviews.title: Calm lovely beach !
reviews.text: One of the best beaches I ever saw. Perfect to go with family and even younger kids. You can walk far into the sea water is clear and beautiful . There are no restaurants or so hence real calm . During the day less Mexicans or tourists in the evening a bit more when it is cooler. It is about 30 minutes drive from la Paz . But a must go .

reviews.title: Beutiful beach north of town
reviews.text: Took a 30 minute cab ride out here.  Spent a couple hours out here walking around in the shallow water.  Took lots of photos of birds and the mushroom rock.  Several of us got stung a few times in the legs while in the water.  Did not see anything in the water but felt like mosquito bite and luckily it did not leave a mark or welt.  Not much shade or shelter from the sun so take sunscreen and wear water shoes.  There are no services here.

reviews.title: Tiny cove open on wonderful beaches when tide is low
reviews.text: Close to Tecolote beaches, very different but as attractive, tenants of shops offer canoe and other nice activities in a safe context

reviews.title: paradise!
reviews.text: one of the most beautiful beaches i've ever laid eyes one. scored a 4/5 because i found it to be a tad too windy. if you plan on spending the day, bring a lunch. there is nothing out there.

reviews.title: Among Best Beaches We Have Visited
reviews.text: We are not great surf beach people.  But we do admire a great beach, and this is one.  Although I have pictures, there are already enough here.  We stopped for lunch.  No facilities that we could find here, so be on notice.  There was a truck selling drinks.  And free thatch umbrellas, although in late January it was so beautiful not needed.  The inlet that the beach is on is all of 3-4 feet deep so you can walk across.  Great kayaking and they are for rent.  You need to be aware of a few jellyfish and some rays asleep in the middle of the channel, but hey, this is Mexico.  A great and beautiful place to stop.

reviews.title: clear water and amazing views
reviews.text: i was there with Friends, the water was very clear and great temperatura. we could see lots of fish, great for scuba diving

reviews.title: Must see beach
reviews.text: beautiful water and white sand, secluded beach.  if I could give more stars, I would!  walk along waters edge and see crabs scurrying along the rocks

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: This is the most beautiful beach ever. It's a little out of the way. You have to drive outside of LaPaz past the port but it so worth. There are summer palapas, chairs and kayaks available to rent. There are also a few local vendors to see. The real draw to the beach is after you walk or past the rock face to the right. Breath taking. We live in Cabo and make the two hour drive at least once a month to relax in the peacefulness.

reviews.title: Gorgeous scenery.
reviews.text: The stark contrast of color within the scenery here alone is worth a visit. Time your arrival at high tide for best scene and swimming. Weekends are busy with local day trippers. There are numerous palapa shade structures available free of charge. We opted for a umbrella and two lounges-$22 US- from the kayak rental/snack truck guys. The water is crystal clear and quite shallow for a great distance.

reviews.title: Tranquilty
reviews.text: Amazing tranquility and warm waters. Nice to be able to wade out as far as you can to find that you are waist high in water.

reviews.title: Nice
reviews.text: This is a very nice beach. It is shallow so would be good for kids & good for kayaking. We walk from one side of the bay to the other & water only got our waist. Worth the drive out from La Paz only about 20 min - 30 min.

reviews.title: Beautiful sandy blue water beach
reviews.text: I absolutely loved this beach. You can wade out quite a long way and walk into the water. There are grass huts for shade or you can rent chairs but you just need to throw a blanket down under one and enjoy the sun.

reviews.title: A nice slice Baja Mexico
reviews.text: Stayed in La Paz for a week and it was a blast!! it is a samll fishing town with enough activites to keep you busy for a week, slow pace good food and firendly folks

reviews.title: One of the most beautiful beaches I've been to.
reviews.text: This place is breathtaking. Water is turquoise - emerald. Beach is super clean with free palapas. Super easy access from the road. Must see when in La Paz!

reviews.title: Disappointing Balandra!
reviews.text: No idea why Balandra is the best rated beach - especially when Playa Tecolote is 2 minutes down the road!! Balandra is crowded, with little parking. Because the beach is so shallow for such a long way out (really bad when the tide goes out), sting rays  come and nestle under the sand, to warm themselves. Really important to wear beach shoes in the water, and to shuffle your feet when you walk - you need to disturb the sting rays or risk being stung.

reviews.title: Beautiful - like something from Jurassic Park!
reviews.text: Rather than the typical "beach" from a postcard this is more of an inlet creating shallow water right across the bay. Its about 25 min drive from the centre of La Paz or $300 ish in a taxi. We didn't have a car so relied on the taxis but they were very good about retuning at the end of the day to collect us again.Take supplies as there is only one little stand selling drinks.A great place to spend the day taking in the scenery and paddling from one cove to the next.

reviews.title: Beautiful scenery and beach but not much good for swimming
reviews.text: We arrived quite early (9.30) in the morning and for the first half an hour there were quite a few sand flies because of the absence of wind; we were told they come from the mangroves at the back of the beach. So remember to bring some spray just in case (luckily we had some). The beach is lovely (but not one of the best I have seen) and the water is crystal clear but very shallow (and the tide was going out so it got even shallower), so forget about swimming. On the plus side you can walk around the point to the next beach and see the rock called Hongo (much smaller than we had thought). Balandra beach is equipped with some umbrellas so you can get some shade, which is good as the vegetation at the back of the beach is very low.We  went for a short hike following a path up a hill and came upon many different species of cactae and once reached the top we had a stunning view of all the bays and beaches and the beautiful turquoise water. It really is worth the hike.

reviews.title: Our Favorite Beach!
reviews.text: This bay is just fabulous, nothing quite like it.  Can easily walk for a mile through the shallow water.  We wore reef walkers so as not to step on anything.

reviews.title: One of the best beaches I have been
reviews.text: Balandra is a protected beach with no restaurants and vendors It is extremely tranquil with no waves and it is not deep so you can walk a lot inside the small bay and water will hardly go above your knee level. Ideal for small children There is a small hill that you can hike to get outstanding views.

reviews.title: One of the most beautiful beaches anywhere and so peaceful
reviews.text: We enjoyed a wonderful afternoon at balandra.   Such a Wonderful beach.  So quiet, so clean, clear water. Wow!  Note the city bus comes here.

reviews.title: Beautiful setting, large crowds!
reviews.text: Balandra bay is a beautiful natural setting, within easy reach from La Paz. It is ideal for kids as the shallows extend forever and make for an inviting playground. The area is now very developed and hugely popular. The days of sitting there on the beach quietly by yourselves are definitely over. Many more palapas have been erected along the beach, sometimes occupied by people with boom boxes, and garbage and cigarette buds are omnipresent. Sad for such a natural gem. Nevertheless, a trip to that beach is a worthwhile outing. While walking in the shallow water be aware of small stingrays, which deliver a very painful, yes sting! Shuffle the sand to make them aware of your presence.

reviews.title: High Tide & Low Tide
reviews.text: We visited La Paz specifically to see Balandra Beach "The most beautiful beach in Mexico" we were not disappointed. We had the opportunity to return during high tide & go kayaking. It was amazing! During low tide we were able to walk to the mushroom rock & take great photos. It's definitely a place you have to see for yourself. We didn't venture very far in the kayak but our friends did and they were able to be on a beach all to themselves. We hiked up a trail to get a higher view of the entire beach. It was well worth the hike. Pleasant place to spend the day. Arrive early for high tide and stay for the low tide and walk to mushroom rock. Fantastic experience for the family.

reviews.title: Nice, but crowded
reviews.text: Very nice beach, but it is more for families or picnics. you cannot really swim. You can just relax. There are beaches around which are more spectacular.

reviews.title: Stunningly beautiful beach
reviews.text: Loved this beach and can't wait to go back. Clear, calm water that you can walk through or paddleboard on and gorgeous views. White sand and sand dunes to climb. Just a great place to spend the day.

reviews.title: Over rated beach
reviews.text: First there is no water , never mind swimming.Be very careful with the guy renting the chairs keep you eyes open he plays the money trick ,i did not pay attention and he change my 100 pesos  to a 50 Pesos ,stay away from him or make sure to give him the correct change and keep you eyes on the money

reviews.title: Spectacular Beach
reviews.text: This beach was absolutely stunning. Gorgeous water, impressive geology making for amazing views, and beautiful white sand. Very peaceful spot and a great place to spend the afternoon unwinding and getting some color.

reviews.title: Prettiest beach I've ever seen
reviews.text: This beach is gorgeous. Took us a bit to figure out how to rent paddle boards, but once we did we were all set! We went earlier on our second visit to get a palapa. This beach is an amazing place, services are limited, so bring your own food etc.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Beautiful sandy beach. Very shallow. Can walk almost anywhere especially at low tide. Not well maintained. Cigarette butts and garbage left on beach. Some mildly annoying peddlers. One creepy guy staring at women. No washrooms. Great kayaking at high tide.

reviews.title: Very unique beach, popular amongst locals but no facilites around.
reviews.text: This is a beautiful beach with very unique formations. Nice to walk and perhaps snorkel (did not do). Can get crowded. Do not bring valuables as there is no security, there are no buildings or anything so you will have what you need with you from towels to swimming gear.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: We caught the eco baja shuttle out to this beautiful beach.  We spent the afternoon snorkelling and wading in the water 💦 and walking the beaches.  Its a popular beach, if you have an umbrella, bring it.  There is a small kiosk with cold pop and a few snacks. There did seem to be umbrellas to rent too.

reviews.title: Pristine beautiful beach
reviews.text: This beach is absolutely beautiful and serene and pristine.  We spent Christmas Eve there.  Just a word for those wanting some libations on the beach - they only sell sodas.

reviews.title: Balandra Beach Beautiful
reviews.text: We drove 2.5 hours from San Jose del Cabo to this gem.  It is worth the day trip.  Coming Highway 19 from the south, take the 11 bypass around southeast La Paz to save yourself from going through downtown.  On a nice day, plan on getting there early just to get parking.  The beach of course is beautiful and the water is crystal clear.  Get a stand up paddle board ($8 per hour) or kayak and go away from the main beach and visit one of the several other private beaches just to get away from the crowd.  Don't get me wrong, although there were quite a few people here, there is enough space for you to relax.  The water is shallow out to 75 meters or beyond and at low tide you can walk nearly half way across the bay.  Bring food and snacks because there isn't much there.  No bathrooms.  Stop at Pichilingue beach on your way out for a nice lunch.

reviews.title: Quiet beach
reviews.text: Quiet cove for snorkeling. They rent kayaks and SUP boards on the beach. As well as table, chairs, umbrellas and lounge chairs. Water and tamales for sale. No toilet facilities. Bring your own lunch and beer

reviews.title: Spent the day lounging by the sea
reviews.text: The water at this beautiful location is clearer than many Caribbean islands we have visited.  The snorkeling was excellent. You can climb the sand dunes.  Bring a cooler of food and drink and spend the day soaking up god's beauty!!  We went by car to Balandra but the boat ride on the 2nd trip was way better.  Stopped to watch Sea Lions and a Stripped Marlin playing in the lagoon.  This area is something out of National Geographic!!!!

reviews.title: Simply Wonderful
reviews.text: I visited in December so did not have to deal with the crowds. Most all of the visitors were locals on vacation. The back drop to this shallow, warm bay are the desert mountains. Palapas line the wide, expansive beach area with soft white sand. Perfect for SUP, kayak, and wading. When it is low tide, you can easily reach the north side of the bay on foot. For those up for a hike, there is an easy climb for a fantastic view of the Sea of Cortez.

reviews.title: Scenic Beach
reviews.text: Very beautiful scenery, lots of people, but you can always walk a little further to get away from the crowds.  Rented a SUP for a bit to get to the mushroom rock, some swam but got stung by little plankton if you got further out in the water.  Very shallow and calm water, beautiful place.

reviews.title: A must visit beach
reviews.text: A crowded place but wonderful. The shallow water goes on forever and you can find yourself a secluded place all to yourselves. No facilities but a small trailer that sells some items

reviews.title: Awesome beach for snorkeling and swimming
reviews.text: We rented a double kayak and paddled almost straight across the bay to our own beach and snorkeled along the rocky cliffs. Great snorkeling continues towards the mouth of the bay and around into the next cove. There is where the best fish viewing occurred. Romantic and secluded was our impression. Just perfect, day after day. Well worth the low price to rent the kayak. Easy to paddle here as the water is warm, shallow and mostly protected from the wind.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Beautiful beach. We were told that there were no facilities there. There were palapas (umbrellas) and one stand selling snacks. They don't sell much, so you should bring your own snacks.

reviews.title: Its the place to go for 'the rock'
reviews.text: Nice scenery you can walk out in the water for ever, we were told to shuffle your feet because of the small sting rays

reviews.title: Most beautiful beach in the world.
reviews.text: Excellent for swimming, sunbathing, and snorkeling, but beware of thieves scouting the area and hitting your car while they notice you are off in the water swimming.  Other than that, this is a small piece of heaven.  Located a good 10-15 miles out of La Paz proper but so worth the drive.  Crowded on weekends but almost deserted at times during the week.

reviews.title: Gorgeous
reviews.text: If it wasn't windy it would have been perfect. Beach was very clean and water was beautiful. We hiked around the rocks and nestled up on the beach away from many people.

reviews.title: Great Kayaking
reviews.text: We kayak here during the winter months.   Its one of our favourite places  within a short distance to La Paz.

reviews.title: Shallow!
reviews.text: The water is very shallow all the way across the bay.  You can only snorkel when you swim around the corner past "the mushroom" rock.  It is the best protected beach from wind and is lovely.

reviews.title: amazing!
reviews.text: almost virgin beach with a service of kayak rent, beautiful landscape, very peaceful (we were there in December and was not high season)

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: We took the day and walked the beaches. Tide went very low. Good beach for walking around and sunbathing, not so much swimming as the water is not deep. Very serene.

reviews.title: Popular but so beautiful, so well preserved, so clean and so virgin.
reviews.text: This is one of my most favorite beaches in the whole world.  The difference between Balandra from Mexican Caribbean beaches or Thai beaches in Thailand (where I am from) is the local people protect it.  There are no restaurants, no hotels, no development, even though it is very easy to to get to.  The water is so clear and shallow and the sand is white.  If you keep walking to the right, you will find your private beaches.  I moved to La Paz from Chiapas for a year because of these virgin beaches!  Take your picnic lunch when you go there.  It coud be so hot because in Baja there is almost no shade and no trees!  So beware of that.  I have never camped there as I heard that there are a lot of mosquitos at night.  In winter, the water is too cold for me.  Best months are from March to October.

reviews.title: Best beach ever
reviews.text: This is the most beautiful beach I have ever seen. Water like a warm pool. The sand is beautifully soft and white. They have palapas, some caves for shade and multiple beaches ! Great fir kids and kayaks

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviews.text: The first of a few local beaches our friends took us to. We have a car with us but if you don't, there is a bus service from the Malecon downtown to both Balandra and Tecolote beaches. Balandra has over 20 free palapas for your use, a food stand, but no washrooms. Stunning vistas and warm shallow teal water to wade through. Nice white sandy beach. What's not to love???

reviews.title: Divine!
reviews.text: If you are a beach person and a water person then you should not miss a day at this beach. It is so safe and shallow with warm water and no current. There are palapas and you can rent chairs. It is a well populated beach on weekends without feeling too crowded. You can walk away from the more populated area to get a spot by yourself away from it all. There are paddle boards and kayaks for rent as well.

reviews.title: One of Mexico's Best Beaches
reviews.text: This beach made our 2 hour drive from Cabo worth it. The last 10 miles of the drive were scenic enough to make it worth it, and then you arrive, seemingly at the end of the world, and there are a bunch of locals on this beach surrounded by mountains. The water is shallow enough to wade out for hundreds of yards, and if you're adventurous enough, you can snorkel out past the "mushroom" rock formation and check out a great variety of marine life, which we recommend. Pictures don't do this beach justice. Just go.

reviews.title: One of the prettiest beaches ive ever stepped foot on!
reviews.text: You must go to believe. You can walk about a 1/4-1/2 mile out and still be in water less than waist deep. If you dont mind walking the views are other worldly from the small peak above the beach. Rent a paddle board or kayak right on the water to enjoy the calm waters and stunning vistas. This is an absolute must if you are in La Paz and on the way back to la paz, stop in to anyone of the tiny little spots to eat as they are all good!

reviews.title: Loud, though maybe we caught a special (bad) day?
reviews.text: Looked like a beautiful beach, but we couldn't walk far enough to get away from the awful blaring music from the loud speakers,.... so we left and went to Tecolote beach instead.

reviews.title: One of the most beautiful beaches
reviews.text: Simply stunning.  So scenic and chilled out. The only minor negative was a bit of broken glass on the main beach.

reviews.title: Good for kids
reviews.text: We rented a car for the day and drove down to Tecolote and Balances beach for the afternoon. We didn't get a chance to stay too long in Balances since it was near 5pm (sunset). But from what I can see, this is a perfect place for kids. Miles of pristine, shallow water will guarantee your kids to have a great time for the afternoon.

reviews.title: Anchored out at balandra
reviews.text: A beautiful picturesque spot. We anchored there on our way to la Paz and just can't wait to go back.

reviews.title: Like the Maldives!
reviews.text: Like the Maldives!Shallow water and multiple small cove beaches set to a mountain background and beautiful natural rick formations.  Authentic, quiet,  clean and seemingly undiscovered. One if my favorite beaches in the world so far!

reviews.title: Beautiful with great snorkeling
reviews.text: Calm water and beautiful white sand beaches are nice, but go around the corner past the mushroom rock and the snorkeling is great! Lots of animals to see and just over 30 minute drive from La Paz. Tide pools are great on low tides, too.

reviews.title: A small hidden paradise
reviews.text: Just about 30 minute drive from La Paz this place is quiet, calm and so naturally beautiful. This is still a virgin beach location so nothing but water and sand. There are no restaurants or hotels at the location but is a short drive from La Paz with great sights on the way. Great for a romantic intimate get away.

reviews.title: A swimming pool in the ocean
reviews.text: Is a beach you have to visit if you are in La Paz, is a enormous swimming pool in the ocean, you can walk for miles and see a wonderful fishes under the surface!!

reviews.title: Beautiful !!!
reviews.text: Beautiful beach....take the kayak and go to the beaches in  front!! Great beach for small children , no waves

reviews.title: Perfect for small kids in November
reviews.text: The tide was low the whole day so the kids could search the tide pools for treasures with no problems

reviews.title: Have you ever seen a Martian Landscape by the Beach?
reviews.text: This is one of the most unique and beautiful beaches I have ever seen!Enjoy the clear and tranquil waters, the beautiful white sand and a perfect setting.Balandra is one of La Paz' icons.Love to go there and enjoy a day at the beach!

reviews.title: Must see!
reviews.text: Very popular beach but never crowded at all. Must see in la Paz! I'd recommend cruising around the corner to the mushroom rock!

reviews.title: Perfect for kuds
reviews.text: Balandra is the safest beach in the world, especially for kids. I love taking my toddler here and letting him run and explore.

reviews.title: Sun and relaxation
reviews.text: Very good place if you want to chill and also if you have small children.  Protected from wind and big waves... always a mellow place  to visit.

reviews.title: Visit
reviews.text: A very nice beach and water.  The cove is protected.  Not too far from town. We will be going back at a warmer time of year.   You could walk a long ways

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: Amazing beach white sand crystal clear water shallow can cross the entire width of that bay walking fun place for family couples a real hit with locals

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: It's a long drive to this beach, which seems to be very popular with locals.  The water is very shallow. The calm water and sandy beaches make this a good family spot.

reviews.title: Breathtaking!!!  As nice as any beach in the Caribbean!
reviews.text: I started coming to La Paz about 5 years ago and every trip to Cabo ends with a visit to La Paz.  this beach is beautiful and pictures don't do it justice.  the water is a color that is indescribable.  Make sure to walk out to Mushroom Rock.  It is a very important symbol to the people of La Paz.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Beautiful beach with basic services. Very shallow and sandy so not great for my snorkeling interest but nice for families  with small children.

reviews.title: great place for day trip. taxi or rental car access
reviews.text: If you cant make it to Espiritu santo this is a great option. location of famous mushroom rock. bring a lunch

reviews.title: Excelent and beautiful
reviews.text: This beach is the most beautiful place to swimming, has a great view, cold water and you con see a lot of small sea animals.You need to go with your weather, beers or sodas and a lunch.If you walk around 10-15 minutes you can see the "balandra" mushroom

reviews.title: Beautiful beach winding road to reach
reviews.text: The drive out of La Paz was a fun winding road, beware because no guardrails. As usual in Mexico, the speed limit is more of a suggestion! We slowed and pulled over a few times to allow people in a hurry to pass.The beach itself far more beautiful than the camera could ever capture. We arrived after 3pm and near low tide. We found no stingrays but the beach was still filled with many local people. You could walk seemingly forever in 30cm of water. Kind of fun to sit down and have tiny fish investigating the invading humans!Take your time and enjoy the sun and make the adventure your own.The vendors were there but not pushy. All in all it is a place to be remembered fondly and a return visit is in order.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: This is a very pretty spot to go hang out for a few hours.  Before you go, ask when high tide is, if you go on low tide, you'll be "swimming" in 8 inches of water.  The place is very pretty and because it's a pretty closed in bay, the water is very calm and totally clear.  WORTH THE VISIT.

reviews.title: Absolutely stunning
reviews.text: Six of us went on a day trip. Our host was Sammy Alcocer. The water crystal clear and warm. Just breathtakingly beautiful.

reviews.title: Balandra
reviews.text: This beach is amazing. Secluded, quiet, clean, beautiful white sand and crystal clear water with no annoying vendors.Tips: 1. If you are driving from Cabo leave early to get a palapa. They have 23 of them at the beach. There is one vendor that rents umbrellas once the palapas are gone. If you do get there late, everyone was nice and sharing palapas.2. Bring a waterproof camera/phone and a gopro if possible. 3. Stop at an OXXO store to get a cooler full of drinks and food. 4. Waterproof sunscreen and a hat are a must5. Bring a change of clothes dor the ride home and dinner6. Bring a water and wash rag to clean the dried salt off your skin. 7. Leave around 4 or 5pm to stop at Todos Santos on the way home to check out the Hotel California and eat dinner.

reviews.title: Balandra Balandra,Balaandraa!!!
reviews.text: The iconic beach of La Paz, were yo can see the "mushroom rock" or Balandra, cristal clear waters, wake free, surf free...then again.. facilities free, it is a shame how such a gorgeous place can be ruined by trash from visitors,  it is a must when in La Paz, no doubt.Good snoerkeling beach, you can walk for half a mile at low tide across the bay  and walk back, take yoru kayak and go in the the mangrove, don forget your camera, great location for sunset shots and bird watching.Bring your food and drinks, take your trash, only a dozen palapas available so take your own shade and be carefull with the tide, unless you are prepare to do a bit of rock climbing and trial walking you could end swimming back to the parking area..  recently voted the most beautiful beach in Mexico.

reviews.title: A day in Balandra !
reviews.text: It was our first time visiting this Beach in La Paz. Our concierge in our hotel mentioned that Balandra was a Beautiful Almost Virgin Beach since it's very isolated, so we decided to rent a car for the day and drive to this amazing beach. Be prepared to bring some water, snacks, or food in a cooler since there's no shops around. However there's a few people selling beer & snacks & they also rent chairs if you need any. We took towels from the hotel so that's all we needed. Don't forget your sunblock, sunglasses, or a Hat, The sun is pretty strong and there's not that much shade. Also No Restroom near by, we used one in a restaurant we stopped by on our way back to our room.

reviews.title: Beautiful pristine spot.
reviews.text: This is a breathtakingly gorgeous place. Sacred if I want to view it that way. I was warned about the Sting rays but did not encounter any in a negative way. We did see some swimming so you much be aware that they are there.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviews.text: Balandra a is 40 minute drive from La Paz via México 11.  The beautiful white sand beaches seem too perfect to be real, and the sea is the most stunning shade of blue you will ever see. The water is very shallow and warm, and perfect for wading and swimming! You can rent SUP or sea kayaks and export around the bay or some of the more secluded beaches along the shore. Be sure to bring an umbrella, or get there early to get a palapa. You will also want to pack food and water as there are only small vendors which are not always open. While at Balandra wonder over to check out El Hongo, a mushroom shaped rock one cove over. Do beware of STINGRAYS, and make sure to do the stingray shuffle while walking in the shallow water. About 5-10 minutes from Balandra is Tecelote. Here they have more rentals, and a restaurant and bar. The margaritas and chocolate clams here are a must after a day at Balandra.

reviews.title: Gorgeous Beach
reviews.text: Gorgeous Beach, just remember to bring insect repellant! The beach is very secluded and quiet, you can rent paddleboards and also kayaks and a small both has refreshments!

reviews.title: Beautiful!
reviews.text: When I first went to Mexico, I went thinking I was going to only Cabos San Lucas. When my husband I got there, we started to tour around. We look at the map and wanted to take a road trip. To be Honest the best way to do this vacation is to rent a car and drive and venture out. I did my research and found Balandra, after seeing the pictures I just knew we had to go. the pictures doesn't do it justice. Balandra was amazing. I didn't want to leave. I suggest you to go to this place. However it happens, make it happen!

reviews.title: Beautiful calm water and friendly people
reviews.text: Beautiful calm water and friendly people!  Get there early for one of the palapas (it is crowded most days...you will definitely want to arrive before noon) and bring a cooler with some snacks or cold drinks.  There is a small concession selling some snacks but no restrooms.  You can rent kayaks and paddleboards - the water is so calm (and shallow) that it is great for beginners.

reviews.title: Nice, but...
reviews.text: A beautiful bay, but the water depth is only about a foot or so for many hundreds of feet out.   Not a great swimming experience, more like a nice bathtub - with stingrays!

reviews.title: Beautiful beach - one of the best
reviews.text: As soon as you arrive at this location you appreciate the silky white sand, warn sun and happy smiling faces, mostly from the locals. This is a beach where you can barely arrive at before you have to go for a swim, the water is amazing and the shallow areas are the best. If you wade out (and you can go very far waist high) you will discover a second beach off to the right - thats the bonus.A small kiosk with chips and drinks are on site, but bring food if you plan to stay for a while. No alcohols is sold on-site and parking is easy.Kayak rentals and sun shades are available in addition to the fixed umbrellas already on-site.

reviews.title: Definite hit
reviews.text: It's really pretty with public palapas. Affordable kayak rentals. If you go early, you'll have the place to yourself.

reviews.title: Amazing beach!
reviews.text: Very recommended visit. Good for a whole day activity. Kayak renting is possible to explore the beautiful area.

reviews.title: Simplemente Increíble
reviews.text: Increíble. Easy to get to in any type of vehicle. About a 15 minute scenic drive from La Paz. No real amenities on site. However, the scenery is breathtaking.

reviews.title: breathtaking
reviews.text: A must see! it really is what dreams are made of. hike up a beautiful white sand doon for an epic view!!

reviews.title: Absolute paradise
reviews.text: We got the bus from La Paz and could not believe how beautiful this beach was! Go there - you will not regret it! There was a man selling drinks from a cool box but I'd recommend going with lots of supplies (and your own cool box if possible!). You can rent kayaks for 200 pesos per hour which was an incredible experience. The clearest calmest water you can imagine with a stunning backdrop of desert and mountains.

reviews.title: Incredible beach!
reviews.text: Definitely make the drive out to Playa Balandra.  One of the best beaches I have visited.  The water is bathwater warm and like a large crystal clear teal blue pool.  Worth the visit for sure.

reviews.title: this beach on a must visit list
reviews.text: A bit out of the way, another 15-20 north of La Paz in the middle of desert but located in a secluded bay off sea of cortez.  Literally walked/swam to the other side, to a very secluded beach maybe 300-400 meters across; fairly shallow. Beware of tide and also tiny jellyfish? got stung a bit but not too bad.  Beach has thatch huts you can rent from a little shack set up that also rents kayaks and SUPs.  Bring your own food,  and be prepared, the porta potties are nasty.  But the white sand beach is beautiful and worth the trip up from Cabo San Lucas where we were staying for the week. About a 2.5 hour drive.  Sun is strong and warm but felt good.  Was mid week but beach was hopping with people which was so unexpected.  As the drive from La Paz to get to beach was somewhat desolate then you come up on this beach and BAM! parking lot full of cars and beach full of people (lots of locals) everyone friendly.  Enjoy just lounging around, not much to do except swim, layout, and find serenity. Peace,  RandyCP

reviews.title: Balandra beach
reviews.text: To me it was ok not awesome just ok. The water made my eyes burn really bad for a few minutes.  There were a lot of flies Everywhere.  To me the water didn't feel fresh just yucky.

reviews.title: Great beach
reviews.text: This has to be the best bay in all of Baja California. Lots of palapasfor rent but being your own food and drinks.

reviews.title: A must do!
reviews.text: Let's be honest, this entire coast is bountiful when it comes to stunning beaches. Balandra beach is just a touch more special. You'll have to visit to see why. For starters, it's very accessible by car, just a short drive out of La Paz town. When we arrived, there was a sea turtle laying eggs on the beach. If that isn't a special, magical welcome then I don't quite know what is!If you're lucky and arrive at low tide, you can walk/wade in the water over to the other bays. If it's high tide, you'll have to hike over the desert hills or rent a kayak. It's not difficult to hike but the hot sun is definitely an element to deal with. We managed to hike over the hills to four other bays. We had these pristine ocean front areas all to ourselves! It did take us four hours but we didn't really notice as we were too busy exploring. We encountered numerous butterflies, sea birds, and picturesque photo ops with desert cactus against the blue sea of Cortez. Many people access Balandra by boat. If you don't have the money, you can enjoy it by foot. You will just have to work harder for it but the reward is great.

reviews.title: An Infinity Pool with Sand
reviews.text: Balandra is breathtaking!  Depending on the tide, you can walk  straight across to the other side, usually in the morning. Crystal clear water, but be very careful, manta rays camouflage under the sand and the sting is very painful. Balandra Rock is a landmark and may be seen by walking along the beach.  A must see and only a short  drive from La Paz.

reviews.title: Best Sandy beach - cannot find words to describe this.
reviews.text: We are so glad someone told us about this beach as it was pure paradise and as Jaques costeau says it is a natural  aquarium. The colors of aquamarine green, copper sulphate blue and dark blue come together where the depth of the waters ares shallow for miles and miles.  You can literally walk for hours on this water at it is shallow. Though cash rent kayaks and tables, umbrellas ans chairs for the day. Ranges from 150 to 240 pesos. The kayak can get you close to a mushroom shaped rock nearby. We spent so many hours here. People sell food and some gift items in their cars so our is not commercial.   This is  surrounded by mountains. We were sing by some thing like a needle pick whixh could have been the tiny jelly fish after the hurricane.  However this is not the poisonous like the box jelly and you don't feel it once you are out. This beach is ideal across generations as young kids and grandparents can enjoy this. Food options added 5 to 10 mins drive away.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Has the best time here the beach was beautiful we rented a canopy and a paddle board. People are selling food at the beach but take drinks in a little ice chest. Will definitely go again

reviews.title: Careful with the mini jelly fish
reviews.text: The beach is very beautiful, shallow, perfect for kids.. The down side is: lots of jelly fish that you can't see. Take Windex with you. Will save some burns!

reviews.title: Beautiful but beware
reviews.text: So, kept hearing about this beach from locals in Cabo San Luca.  They said if you go to La Paz, you have to go to Balandra Beach. It is beautiful, but it's not touristy at all.  It's off the beaten path - which we like!  But, it's not very clean at all.  Lots of beer bottle tops and other small debris in the sand.  Porta potty for restrooms and they were NASTY!   There were only a handful of people there when we arrived (it's a Wednesday, so makes sense).  However it did pick up a bit.  Water is beautiful and you can wade out for several hundred yards.  Unfortunately, something in the water (maybe a mite or something) decided that I was their snack.  My legs got very itchy and a rash broke out.    It only affected 3 of the 4 of our group.  The local guy there said it was something in water and rubbed sand on it to help.  Not sure what happened, so will research it.  It took a few hours before it was painful.  This may be a seasonal thing since it's  summer and water is warm. So - come if you want peace and an amazing view.  Just be prepared.

reviews.title: Pure white sand, shallow water and snorkeling
reviews.text: This is a beautiful beach with very white sand, shallow water, and some nice snorkeling around the rocky edges of the south side of the bay.  You can drive to the beach, but that part is somewhat crowded, so a better way to do is arrive by boat and drop and anchor in the sand. The water is very clear and warm this time of year. (August ...)

reviews.title: Amazing Balandra
reviews.text: Excellent beach spot close to La Paz. Dont miss it when you are there. One of the beaches nearby the city. And one of the beautiful.

reviews.title: One of the most beautiful beaches in the world.
reviews.text: We have visited this beach many times, and have enjoyed the warmth, the spacious nature, and terrific vistas, this area provides.  Matches the beaches of Rio, without the pollution, and shoreside development.

reviews.title: Good but watch out
reviews.text: With no chances to swim, relax yourself in this charming bay: peaceful romantic atmosphere, almost no waves, transparent water but seriously watch out from rays living camoiflaged in the sand

reviews.title: Awesome beach
reviews.text: It is a nice beach in a bay secluded from the ocean, with great mangroves which can be visited easily by swimming or kayak. Therefore, there are hardly any waves which makes it easy to do activities like snorkeling, kayaking and SUP-boarding. The water is very shallow (about 50 centimeters) which can be preferable (child proof) but also annoying if you want to swim more quickly. There are parasols, kayaks, etc. for rent from local people. Also, you can take a 30-minute shuttle from La Paz bus station (Malecón station) for 100 MXN round trip p.p.

reviews.title: Top beach ever
reviews.text: This beach was a pleasant suprise. Love that it is secluded and is some of the clearest water I've ever been in.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: When you get there you can not believe we still have these kind of beaches in our beautiful Mexico. There is literally nothing but calm, gorgeous blue sea. Great place to go with kids but you need to consider shelter (it's really hot on summertime), lots of sunblock, water and if you want, some food.

reviews.title: A must
reviews.text: This has to be one of the most beautiful bays I have seen in El Mar de Cortez. If you are in La Paz, this is an awsome day trip and you could include the broken rock as well in the excursion.

reviews.title: Most amazing beach- EVER!
reviews.text: Absolutely fantastic. Beautiful beach and gorgeous water that you can walk around. Visiting on the weekend will bring a large crowd, but still a fantastic experience. Plenty activities as well as locals selling delicious treats.

reviews.title: Walk across the bay
reviews.text: Shallow warm water, beautiful clear and inviting. The three of us enjoyed several hours of aquamarine seas and warm surf. We walked out to the iconic "symbol" of La Paz. Bring sun screen, sunglasses, and a hat. Several of us wore shoes for the rocky parts, but you can go bare foot - just avoid "lug" worm castles. Parasol rentals are available; if you have a boogie or surf board, you can wander the whole bay, including the mangrove forests. Finish the day with a picnic, or head on out to Tecolote Beach, at land's end, only a half mile further down the road.

reviews.title: Best Beach for kids
reviews.text: My favorite beach, it's like a very big pool, the best for family retreats, kids don't need to know how to swim it's so low, no rocks just sand. Lovely to visit.

reviews.title: A Must See
reviews.text: This was a very relaxing and peaceful beach. The water is not deep at all. Food trucks available for snacks. Bring your own food and drinks. Lots of pelicans, at first this was nice, up close with nature. Then I got a little tired of the large birds.

reviews.title: Gorgeous beyond belief
reviews.text: We visited this beach at the end of July. It is absolutely worth the drive outside La Paz, just gorgous. It's safe to swim for adults and kids, and the water is shallow very far out. Bring a snorkel and a mask if you want to explore underwater, there's lots of little schools of fish everywhere and it's great for the kids to see.

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.text: A fantastic beach, pretty "personal" and not crowdy at all, the tours to Espiritu Santo island are quite unique.

reviews.title: Best beach in La Paz
reviews.text: Great beach. Clear green water. Definitely picture- worthy. Very shallow out about 800 yards. It's about 3 - 4 feet, sometimes almost 5. It becomes more and more crowded as the day goes on, so get there before 10am to enjoy the beach to yourself. In the afternoon, many families have staked their areas in the shade of the giant rock to the right, but the further you walk to the left, the more isolated you will be. Bring a towel and a cooler and enjoy the day here. There aren't any restrooms or restaurants here, although a vendor sold snacks and sodas out of his truck. You can catch the colectivo van over to the next beach, Tecolote, where there are restaurants and restrooms. It's a 7 minute drive away. Transportation info:All La Paz buses arrive to/leave from the Terminal Turistico across the street from the malecón. Ask anyone and they'll direct you. - This is where you can catch a combi bus (van) to Balandra or Tecolote Beach. Buy a round trip ticket for 98 pesos. There are about 5 vans a day and they leave around 1.5hr apart. The bus station can tell you the route times, although the return van was 45 min late, so it's not an exact science. Tip: Board the van as soon as it pulls into the station/parking lot. They do not count the tickets sold, so it's first come, first serve. Grab your seat ASAP. Hope that helps! Enjoy La Paz!

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Open beach for locals and tourist alike, has very minimum shade, you can rent a palapa if you get there early. I saw a lady renting beach umbrellas if you want to make your own shade. There are no restrooms or shower to clean yourself after a day on the beach. I would highly recommend it if you have small children, water is warm and no waves at all, it's like a big waist deep lagoon. Food truck selling a few selections of snacks and fruits, check it out !!!

reviews.title: Stunning!
reviews.text: This beach offers beautiful views and opportunity to walk long distances in very shallow water. Although it's a popular destination it doesn't feel crowded.

reviews.title: Fantastic!!
reviews.text: I spent a few hours in this beach. Great for swimming.  Bring a canopy, no shades. It is not possible to hike inland but the views in the beach are great. A good place to relax.

reviews.title: This is a great beach!
reviews.text: This beach is beautiful. My family enjoyed it because it is so shallow. Even though it was crowded it was still easy to enjoy since the water is so shallow for such a huge area. The sand is so soft and easy to walk on. The rocks were fun for the kids to play on, too. It looks like if you get there early enough you might be able to snag a covered tent but we weren't there early enough for that. We definitely liked it and it was beautiful!

reviews.title: Unique layout
reviews.text: It was more crowded than we expected, but the gin-clear water, 2-3 feet deep nearly all the way across the bay, was nice.  Lots of fish, and it was fun for us to hang out in a different sort of beach.  Bring your snorkel and fins--plenty to see.  Bring your own food/drink; nothing available there (fruit vendor, though).

reviews.title: perfect beach for families
reviews.text: Crystal water with no waves. Perfect for children, kayaking and relaxing.The perfect hour to visit it is in the morning or before 4 pm due the sun and the hot weather.

reviews.title: One of the best beaches I've been to!
reviews.text: Very Beautiful! Great for individuals, couples or families! Amazing! Bring your water proof camera, you'll want to take it with as you explore the entire area and surroundings.

reviews.title: Awesome spot only a short boat ride away.
reviews.text: Great spot for families and young kids, the bay is very shallow and has a cool little snorkeling spot. Make sure you go by boat, it's much better for snorkeling.

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach with diverse crowd and great atmosphere
reviews.text: A lovely place, well preserved without commercial facilities other than helpful rentals.  Interesting crowd of all types from families to hippies, all enjoying the location and providing a very positive vibe.  Really beautiful beach and bay.  Strongly recommend your own car to get there.

reviews.title: beatiful beach!!
reviews.text: ive been in so many beaches: Bahamas, cancun, florida , Rio de Janeiro, Ilha Grande (brazil) Costa Rica, Nicaragua, La Jolla (san diego), cabo san lucas, Waikiki,  culebra (Puerto Rico) St Thomas,  so far this is my second favorite after flamenco (culebra) ... is an amazing beach....clear turquoise waters...

reviews.title: Getting popular
reviews.text: This was always our secret 'wow' spot with visitors.  A great place to feel like s cast away.  But lately, even on weekdays, there are lots of people.  Harrumph- too good to last I guess.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviews.text: This is one of my favorite beaches, its crystal clear water, no waves, warm temperature, it is just perfect to relax and chill with a nice cold drink.

reviews.title: Relaxing Sunday
reviews.text: CLEAN YOUR TRASH!!!! Amazing beach, weather and view. Too bad for all the trash left behind. There's overpriced chips and some street food. Ceviche and other options available but you save a buck or two by bringing your own food.

reviews.title: very scenic beach
reviews.text: We stopped by Balandra beach which is one of the favorite beaches for the locals.  Long shallow waters make it a great place for kids.  Get there early for a spot under the palapas provided.Very scenic.

reviews.title: Most beautiful beach I've been to
reviews.text: This is the nicest and most beautiful beach that I have been too. It's basically perfect. I have no complaints not anything that was lacking.

reviews.title: The most beautiful beach ever
reviews.text: Don't have the words to explain how much i loved this place. For sure i have to go back sometime. Everything is perfect! The only thing is that you don't have any place to eat or to drink a beer nearby. You have to go somewhere else.

reviews.title: A beautiful bay to visit
reviews.text: It is true that Ballandra Bay is one of the most picturesque bays near La Paz. To really take advantage of the Bay you need to be there early and if possible avoiding the weekend crowds. The best beaches are a walk and a swim across the far side of the bay away from the car park beach but be sure to do the stingray shuffle if you are walking across. There are sit on kayaks to be rented on the beach and that can be an excellent way of exploring the area and getting away from the crowds at weekends. There are few facilities there other than  a few sun shades, a mobile taco shop and the Kayak rental. The area is within a easy twenty minute drive from the city through some spectacular countryside and I would suggest that if you want to make a day of it either take your own picnic or go to Pichilingue where you will find two very good restaurants that specialise in seafood. Tecolote is further north with several more possibilities for eating but Tecolote is probably the most popular beach with the local population and it can get very crowded at week ends and summer evenings.

reviews.title: Beautiful shallow water bay outside La Paz
reviews.text: A stunning bay and beach. Deep blues, and pelicans diving for fish. Get there early before the day trippers arrive in the coaches.

reviews.title: Beautiful, swim across
reviews.text: A must see/do in La Paz! Walk across to the other beaches away from the main beach. The sand is perfect and it's an amazing view. Bring some water and snacks. Go to the bathroom before you head to the beach. There are no bathrooms here. One of the most amazing beaches to experience!!

reviews.title: Beautiful, but come early
reviews.text: Balandra beach was tipped as one of the most beautiful beaches near La Paz. We rented a car and visited the beach early, which was good because we where the only ones. Enough time to enjoy the fresh, clear water and the stunning surroundings. Recommended!

reviews.title: Relaxing beach
reviews.text: Relaxing, beautiful beach, calm water, you can rent a kayak for 15DLS, take with you some beers before you arrive to the beach.

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach for lying in the sand and walking the beach!
reviews.text: The beach is lovely, there is a big sand parking lot and lots of palapas to lie under to get out of the sun. There is just one 'service' truck for food, and they don't have much of a selection, but we had brought our own. We had to walk WAY out in the water before it got deep, and it was kind of gooey on the bottom, so we went back to the car and got water shoes. Cool hiking trails around the area!

reviews.title: Calmed & very nice beach, with a rare stone.
reviews.text: The reasons why this beach is special for those in La Paz: the beach is like a big pool, camping is really nice paying the corresponding fees, there is a rock that faced erosion with water & air that now has the form of a enormous mushroom. It was untouched for several years till a nuthead recently climbed it and broke it. Authorities did everything to restore it, so you´ll be able to see this curios wonder.

reviews.title: One of the nicest and most beautiful beaches anywhere.
reviews.text: Pluses: crustal clear turquoise water and white sand. The water is mostly knee-deep. There are some reefs with good snorkeling. Minuses: there is no surf whatsoever. The water is like a lake. That could be a good thing, depending on your point of view.

reviews.title: magical beach
reviews.text: Extremely gorgeous, I went midweek so i had it pretty much all to myself and the people I went with, but i have heard that it can get full, and that the people that go don´t pick up their trash. you can walk and walk till your hearts desire.

reviews.title: Secluded paradise
reviews.text: My husband and i stayed in la paz for a week and ventured here one day.  Absolutely breath taking!  We rented a kayak for 100 pesos per hour from a local guy.  It was a fantastic experience and there were maybe 20 other people there on a Wednesday.  Only a 20 minutes drive from the Malecon in la paz.

reviews.title: The most beautiful beach in Baja!
reviews.text: Crystal clear waters that unlike any other in Baja!  Be sure to bring an umbrella as there is no shade, but plan to spend the day!

reviews.title: Kids or adults a bit of something for all beach lovers
reviews.text: This beach location is gorgeous with its aqua water and brillian white sand.  It's shallow most of the time, and on a low tide one can walk all the way to the other side - it's about waist deep.  Near the center is a 'blue hole' that is quite deep, so if you're not a swimmer, best to stay away from this.  Because it's so shallow it's great for kids. and it's usually a nice tempurature even in late summer.Kayaks and palapas can be rented.  Bring a cooler with drinks and snacks, floaties and sand toys and enjoy the day.  But remember your sunscreen and hats!

reviews.title: Blue waters exquisite beach
reviews.text: Arrived by boat on a early weekday morning and spent a good amount of time just walking the beach enjoying the blue waters and white sand beach. Very serene and peaceful. Encountered a group of researchers doing a study of the sand, measuring distances between crab holes and the tide line. Water was warm and very clear. Just a delightful place to chill.

reviews.title: Doesn't Get Better
reviews.text: This is a beautiful white sand-azure water beach, The little cove is very shallow and thus kid-friendly, but one must watch out for sting rays, especially in the hotter months. The concessionaire at the beach has snacks, beer and soft drinks, and rents kayaks and paddle boards. The mangrove-lined lagoon in back of the beach (accessible by kayak) is a treat for bird watchers.

reviews.title: Piece of heaven
reviews.text: This huge swimming pool is an unbelievable place, so virgin you wont even find restrooms, so take your precautions.It´s a very enjoyable area and is so spacious that is almost impossible to feel is crowded.

reviews.title: Great place to spend a day
reviews.text: The sea is so shallow that you can walk across the bay at low tide. The water is clear and warm and it quite easy to get to from La Paz.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach and great if you have kids or non swimmers
reviews.text: While staying in Cabo we took a day trip down to La Paz and then spent several hours in the afternoon at this beachThe water is amazingly clear and because of the white sand the blue colors will rival any Caribbean beach.  The stark contrast of  blue and turquoise water with the white sand dunes and several interesting rock formations make this beach a great photo opportunity as well,If you have kids or people in your party that don't know how to swim this is the perfect place for them as the water is only knee deep and therefore warm in almost the whole little bay.  VENDORS - There are vendors on the beach which will rent chaises and table with chairs -(we paid $215 pesos for two chaises, a chair, and an umbrella) - or if you arrive early in the morning you can lay claim to one of several palapas that are on the beach. Also the chair vendors do have kayaks which are $200 pesos per hour to rent.  We saw one person walking the beach selling tshirts and hats.  FOOD - We went on a Monday so did not see any food vendors  however just a little way down the road is Tecolote beach which had several restaurants - so either  way bring food or plan to check out Tecolote beach and enjoy lunch there.RESTROOMS - There are no bathroom facilities on this beach so be aware of this.SNORKELING - A few fish in the water but no real snorkel opportunities here

reviews.title: Heaven on Earth
reviews.text: This is one of my top 3 beaches (along with X'cacel in Quintana Roo, and Carrizalillo in Oaxaca).You have this caribe-like colors, you can walk hundreds of meters with the water level not rising much (kee-deep and chest-deep most of the way), you are surrounded by amazing mountains (and that is a very special feeling that most people fail to note when telling you about beaches in La Paz).Bring your own food and beverages. Stay all day long. Please be considerate of others and DON'T bring music with you.

reviews.title: Picture Perfect Beach
reviews.text: Only had an opportunity to stay here around 45 minutes because we were on our way to snorkel in the nearby islands but wow this beach looks amazing. Around 15 - 20 minutes away from La Paz, just bring all your items, no service here of any kind but it's well worth the drive or bus ride (about 90 pesos) to just be here.

reviews.title: Stunning!!!!
reviews.text: This beach is like living a piece of paradise on earth for the time you spend there. Crystal clear water from your ankles to waist with baby powder sand under your feet stretching for hundreds of yards. Oh yeah, surrounded by mountains. Are you kidding me? 30 minutes out of La Paz, piece of cake. We drove the 2 hours from Cabo and it was totally worth it. Maybe it was the time of the year but we encountered NO stingrays or jellyfish. A dozen or so extremely friendly locals and a couple other travelers scattered about completes the scene. Leave the resorts folks, explore, you'll be glad you did.

reviews.title: Most amazing beach
reviews.text: This beach is a bit out of the way, but let me tell you, it is worth it!!  You feel like you are in the Caribbean, crystal clear, aqua water!!  The water is only about waste deep, you can walk to other beaches, in the water!!  Stunning beach, mountains all around you, well worth the trip.  You can rent kayaks, chairs & umbrella.  Or there are about six umbrellas on the public side that are free.  No food for sale, bring cooler if you plan on being there a while.

reviews.title: Gota the most beutifull beeaches that i have seréis gin mi life ,
reviews.text: Ok these beach it amaizing Tito like a Lagoon , you can walking at least 200 meter in the ocian , the color of the water is cristal , and i mean cristal you can see , everything , the color aré out of these word , there aré 3 bays , one is the beach on the parking área , the main beach , if you walki tours the mashroom , its a famosos Stone, you will fine the second beach , and you keep walking north troug the Roks you will fine the 3 beach , its the most beutifull and quait and beutifull , off all, balandra is a protected área ,so brindg all you Needs, water food , toilet papaer everything becouse you wont fine anything there , taking for personal experiencia on My first da y , on main beach you can rent a kajack , recomiendes , i m love with these place , i cant wait to come beack , dont forget the cámaras ,

reviews.title: Beautiful blue water, shallow
reviews.text: Lovely beach to look at because of the shallow blue water.Stingrays in water - shuffle your feet to get them to move.  No restaurants, bring your own food and drink.

reviews.title: Nice for inexpensive kayaking
reviews.text: The water was clear. No fish but birds galore. Chairs and umbrellas available. Snack available. Some locals said you you have to shuffle your feet to scare the stingrays away. The kayaks were 200 pesos for double kayak.

reviews.title: Gorgeous but shallow beach.  Great for hanging out with friends, family and kids!
reviews.text: Gorgeous? Yes, a 100x over.  Fine white sand and varying shades of turquoise, can't go wrong here. The water is warm and at best when the tide is high, probably waist deep in most areas, and i'm 5'.  There are areas that are deeper though, crossing to the different beaches.  It's really perfect for kids because they can play in the water and since the water is shallow in most places and the bay is protected from big waves, it's generally safe for kids.You can walk around to the different beaches, some more isolated than others if you want privacy.  The scenery is just stunning.  For a view of the whole area, you can hike to the top of a hill.  There are kayaks for rent at the main entrance and small huts for shade.  Other than that, there is little shade and the sun can get pretty strong.  There are also some vendors selling souvenirs.  Bring your own snacks and beverage as there is no food or little food sold in the area.  It can get pretty crowded with tourists and locals, it was when we were there.  The good thing was, we came towards the end of the day when a little of people  were leaving and we caught the sunset.  We experienced the place when it was crowded and when there were barely any people left.  When it was quiet, it was serenely beautiful.My one MAJOR complaint was there were trash in some areas.  We walked the shoreline going towards the mushroom rock, the scene was beautiful with the sun setting, and you turn towards the rocks by the shore and you see soda cans and food wrappers jammed into little crevices.  So sad.

reviews.title: Other than the friends I stayed with, this Beach made my trip.
reviews.text: One heck of a changing of the tide and really something to see specially coming from a land locked Canadian. It's wading pool deep so perfect for children to play.  The view is spectacular.  I promise you won't be disappointed.

reviews.title: Wow Wow Wow
reviews.text: This is my new favourite beach of all time.   The combination of subtle desert hues and brilliant turquoise water is simply stunning. I love that there is no development, only a guy renting beach umbrellas and paddle boards (bring food and drink). It's also super clean in contrast to nearby Tecolote beach. Balandra is actually a collection of several beaches set in a sheltered bay with very shallow water...if the first beach by the parking lot is too busy, which it wasn't on the 2 days we were there, it is easy to wade along the shore to the next beach. We rented a car to get there but noticed that EcoBaja has many daily departures leaving from the bus terminal at the La Paz malecon. Do not miss Balandra!!!

reviews.title: solo
reviews.text: Walking out o your shoulders and it is only knee deep. The water is a tourquoise,  the scenery out of this world. I came on a calm day. It was stunning. The mushroom rock.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: This beach is a must to visit. Crystal clear ,clean blue water. You can walk for ever and be only up to your knees. This is a super beach for kids.

reviews.title: Beyond beautiful
reviews.text: Well worth the drive from Cabo.  Beyond a vendor selling potato chips there was no food available, so pack a picnic and enjoy the day at once of the finest beaches Mexico has to offer.

reviews.title: Well worth the trip
reviews.text: This is the most beautiful beach in the La Paz area and certainly in the top ten beaches in all of Baja Sur.  We drive up from Cabo San Lucas simply to spend a few hours here away from the crowds.  The beach is remote (about 30 minutes past La Paz), the sand is clean, the water is clear and the inlet so shallow you can almost walk across it.  Just a wonderful place to relax and enjoy the sun and water.

reviews.title: Most beautiful beach in La Paz
reviews.text: It's the most beautiful beach in La Paz, The water is so clear and you can rent a kayak and paddle around the lagoon.

reviews.title: Road trip to La Paz
reviews.text: Most beautiful beach  ever! Definitely worth driving to. It's a quiet beach mainly visited by locals. About 25 minutes from La Paz.

reviews.title: Beautiful but lots of jellyfish and stingrays
reviews.text: This beach is every bit as beautiful as everyone says. But if you love being in the water prepare to stung by a jellyfish a time or two.

reviews.title: Last night on KharmaSeas
reviews.text: The most beautiful beach in the world, I spent my last night aboard my sailboat anchored for two days. Umbrellas for rent. Kayaks also! Has road access to drive in. If you get to La Paz and you don't visit Balandra you will miss the best beach you can ever see!

reviews.title: Unbelievable beauty
reviews.text: Took a drive and drove till the road ended and lo an behold we were in paradise. Beautiful clear water and white pristine sandy beach. There were palapas to shade you and kayaks for the adventurous. Loved it...would recommend the drive!

reviews.title: Gorgeous and only little used
reviews.text: Possibly because there are no facilities for bathroom or food, this beach seemed to me to be an undiscovered gem.  Parking for a few dozen cars.  A few free umbrellas and more that are rentable.

reviews.title: Beautiful place to spend a morning
reviews.text: Lovely water and peaceful surf the day we visited. The lush tropical plants that grow in the area can lull you into thinking this is a real paradise.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: This is a really lovely, peaceful beach.  The distance is a little far out from town so you need to either get a taxi, tour or rent a car.

reviews.title: Beautiful setting
reviews.text: Great place to go and hang out for the day. We took a taxi from our hotel, but there are buses that can take you there. Bring your own towels and water. There are fruit snacks and ice treats available on location  during weekends and  busy week days but are limited. You can walk from one beach to the next which is just amazing.

reviews.title: Shades of blue
reviews.text: My husband and I had been to Balandra a few years back and enjoyed the warm, shallow waters. To can walk across to more secluded beaches or stay at them aim beach and rent paddle boards and kayaks. If you are coming to snorkel you will be disappointed as there are little to no fish (no reef or rocks). Truly a lovely place if you are a beach goer!!!

reviews.title: Best beach for couples, family, and seniors
reviews.text: This is by far the must beautiful safest beach I've ever been to. You can walk a mile in and just be waste deep. Super clear water. Few things to note, there are no bathrooms or restaurants so take your own food and use the bathroom prior to getting there.

reviews.title: Natural Wonderland!
reviews.text: We drove to Balandra Beach as a day trip from Cabo. The two and a half hour drive was well worth it! The white sand was so soft and the shallow waters allowed you to wade around the area. Be sure to bring good shoes or sandals in order to hike up and around Mushroom Rock. You cannot possibly miss that view! Kayaks and paddle boards are available for rent, but beware that as the tide goes out, it exposes lots of sand bars which can make kayaking tricky. Also, bug spray at Balandra Beach is a must.....we didn't have ours and left with many bites from tiny knats on the beach.

reviews.title: Sunset visit at BAlandra beach
reviews.text: Expensive cab ride but worth the 550 pesos. Beautiful shallow water you can walk and it only goes up to your belly. We went at Sunset and it was very quiet.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: We took a taxi from downtown to this beach and it was absolutely amazing! Clear waters, quiet place and a beautiful beach. If you have the chance to go, do not miss it!

reviews.title: Thus is a local secret there's a reason
reviews.text: This was the most beautiful beach I have seen in years, you can walk for miles before the water reaches your chest. And the atmosphere is amazing.

reviews.title: beautiful beach!
reviews.text: Amazing shallow beach , you can walk in the sea for around 100 meters or more and water is still beneath your knees! Kayaking is a nice adventure across the bay to the beaches. You can see volcanic formations and dunes, paradisiac! Keep the good job by keeping it clean locals!

reviews.title: Beautiful but water still cold
reviews.text: Water not yet warm enough for this guapa however I loved lounging and sunning in such a gorgeous location... Def check this place out!

reviews.title: Not to be missed!
reviews.text: Take a packed lunch and enjoy this amazing beach of calm water and beautiful views. There are no restaurants which makes this beach even more beautiful.

reviews.title: Stunning setting near La Paz.
