reviews.text: We spent the day at this beach, and enjoyed it's shallow water and clean, soft sand. What a perfect place for kids! We arrived early (about 10am), and got one of the free palapas, which was a welcome shelter from the sun. It seems very family oriented, and the tide was out, so the sand bars went clear to the other side of the bay almost! We would've loved to have seen it at high tide, as the water was a gorgeous shade of Caribbean blue towards the mouth of the bays. Bring your picnic and enjoy!

reviews.title: Very Nice Beach Near La Paz
reviews.text: I have visited this beach several times over the past 15 years or so, most recently during the Holy Week before Easter this year.  The beach is nice and fairly clean, and the water in the shallow bay is a beautiful turquoise.  In past visits, there were few people on the beach and few boats in the deeper outer edge of the bay, and it was fun snorkeling around the rocky edges of the bay.  A good way to spend a few hours while visiting La Paz, from which it is a 20-30 minute drive.  During the the recent visit, though, the beach and attached parking lot were full, and the tide was out, so the bay was really too shallow to swim and snorkel in, and the experience wasn't as good as it had been at other seasons/times of day.  My recommendation is to check the tide tables and avoid national holidays.  A must-do is to walk up to the top of the hill next to the beach for a panoramic view of this scenic area.

reviews.title: The best beach in Mexico
reviews.text: Not kidding, Balandra just won the bes beach in Mexico, better than any one in the mexican caribbean, it is AMAZING, clear turquoise water, white sand, dessert surrounding it, it´s a paradise, do not miss this beach if going to La Paz you won´t regret it.

reviews.title: Beautiful and peaceful beach with amazing water colors
reviews.text: The beach is surrounded by mountains so the view is spectacular. The water is very clear in colors turquoise and light blue. It is very shallow so you can cross walking from one side to the other on the beach. It is a great place to spend the day relaxing and having fun. There are small spots to rent a kayak or beach umbrellas for the day.

reviews.title: Most amazing beach
reviews.text: I almost didn't want to write a review because I dont want this beach to become popular. Then I read an article about the beach being protected for not to became a comercial-touristy place.If we are talking about just the beach and the clear waters,this is the most beautiful beach I've ever been to. Also, for me, what makes it beautiful, its the lack of the human trail(no hotels,no restrooms,no restaurants..no nothing except sand and sea). This could be inadequate for some,but for us it was perfect.

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach
reviews.text: Get to this beach early because it become very full and popular later on in the day. Gorgeous beach no shops near just very expensive ice creams, water and fruit so I would recommend stocking up before you get there. You can walk via the water around to the right to experience a quieter beach (past the mushroom rock). Not a lot of shade so I would recommend taking or renting a umbrella. Definitely worth visiting I loved it!

reviews.title: What a relaxing time in front of an incredible view.
reviews.text: My brother in law lives in La Paz and he promised us to take us to the best beach for my 4 & 6 year old kids. He was right, Balandra is  definitely iconic!  Love to go back soon.

reviews.title: Lovely beach and calm waters if you want to rent a boat.
reviews.text: It was a windy day so there was no one at the beach. It is a lovely spot, often used by Mexican families for picnics and some beach fun

reviews.title: Safe swimming in lovely sheltered bay.
reviews.text: A favourite beach near la Paz by car, just above Pichilingue. Unusual scenery, soft sand, palapas, rental tables and chairs, and kayaks. The addition of toilets would be a definite plus.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: This is a really pretty beach- you have to go out and around to get the best view. There is no alcohol served/sold here so bring your own if you want it.

reviews.title: Balandra beach
reviews.text: Amazing. Recommended visiting early (9 am) as later on many people come. To see the Balandra rock one has to go on the right from the parking

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful beaches in my travels. It is in a large cove with clear shallow water you can wade through. Mushroom Rock is around the corner and easy to get to. Many boats spend the night in the cove as it is protected from the wind. It is a wonderful beach for small children and families.

reviews.title: Gigantic white sand kiddie pool
reviews.text: I can't imagine a more perfect beach for a family with multiple young children. We arrived in the AM when most of the beach was about 1.5 feet deep in crystal clear, still water. After about two hours, it had become a giant sandbox and the close in water was ankle deep. Lovely palapas, easy to park, don't forget the sand toys! If you are hoping for jumping in waves or swimming, go elsewhere.

reviews.title: Garbage everwhere near this beach
reviews.text: We stopped by when we were in La Paz.  The shallow warm water was cool, but there was garbage everywhere.  There are nicer beaches nearby.

reviews.title: crowded but nice
reviews.text: we went there adn turned around and went to another beach we passed on the way.Same water less people

reviews.title: Great beach for children (and adults ;-))
reviews.text: Very nice and lovely beach/bay! As the water is very low it is ideal for little children. You can walk for several minutes before the water starts to get deeper. And the bay itself is amazing.

reviews.title: Sailed into the anchorage
reviews.text: Beautiful white sand beaches, shallow water for paddling and deep enough for swimmers, lots of kayaking and beach walking. Home of the world famous mushroom rock.

reviews.title: Beautiful Beach
reviews.text: A very quiet, beautiful beach enjoyed by the locals. Some wonderful shade palapas. Lots of families enjoying themselves.

reviews.title: Too popular for my taste. Beautiful but lots of people.
reviews.text: If you don't mind enjoying the beach among the crowds this is beautiful. Otherwise, go elsewhere. There is food available. Merchants walking along the beach.

reviews.title: Paradise!
reviews.text: an absolutely gorgeous beach. clear, blue water, ideal for families,a great spot to visit! you can walk out about a quarter mile and it's still up to your knees

reviews.title: Watch for sting rays but wow what a place
reviews.text: This beach is one of a kind and if you are in La Paz you should see it.  The water is warm and not very deep making it a comfortable experience

reviews.title: Amazing Beach with Azure Waters and Soft White Sand
reviews.text: This is a picturesque beach with warm blue water and soft white sand. Very shallow for family fun. SUP boards and kayaks are available to rent or bring your own. There is no food or drinks served so bring your own and enjoy a day in the sun !

reviews.title: special beach
reviews.text: It s a magic place, the location has outstanding views. It is not much indicated how to get there, but once you are there, you can just sit and relax watching the sunset over Balandra beach.

reviews.title: Stunning
reviews.text: We could not have had better conditions, and this beach took our breath away. Arrived in the morning on a Tuesday and it was not crowded. We snagged a palapa, relaxed for a while, then did a long walk around in the warm shallow water. I think it is nicer in the morning than the afternoon, as by 1, the people had doubled and the tide gong out impacted the incredible aesthetics of the blue-green water.

reviews.title: Beautiful quiet beach
reviews.text: Nice sandy beach that you can walk out in. water is warm, good for families,easy to see your kids as it isn't busy at all. Water colours are also nice. A bit of a drive from La Paz but easy to find- watch out for large trucks and don't be in a rush to get there, would not drive on the road at night.

reviews.title: So beautiful and pristine...I almost don't want to share it with you.
reviews.text: A rare protected and totally undeveloped beach with beautiful shallow water. perfect for beginner snorkelers, sun bathers and anyone searching for peace and quiet.

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: We visited Balandra beach twice during our seven day stay in La Paz.  It was so beautiful.  It was absolutely the perfect beach to take our five year old to have his first beach experience.  Be sure to walk to mushroom rock if the tide is out and check out the tide pools.  We enjoyed checking out all the various sea creatures and fish in the pools.

reviews.title: Unspoilt Paradise
reviews.text: Peaceful place, clean clear water, You can walk for long distance in the see and the water is still in your ankle.Beautiful place a must if you are visiting La Paz.

reviews.title: Words fail me
reviews.text: I did a ton of research online trying to decide where I wanted to spend my 50th birthday.  My choices were pretty much anywhere American or Southwest flew.  We chose this beach, and it did not disappoint.  Pack light and walk a bit, as the crowds are all close to the parking lot.  (But even on a Sunday, it was not crowded.)  The beach is astounding in its beauty.  And the HUGE rocks offer tons and tons of shade, like shallow caves.  Not much infrastructure so if you want restaurants and bathrooms, go to one of the other beaches on either side of this spectacular bay.

reviews.title: What's not to like!
reviews.text: Balandra Bay is gorgeous....we arrived by private tour boat and brought kayaks with us to explore the Bay.  The water was crystal clear in most parts.  We stopped at a couple of the beaches to hang out. We had the beaches we went to to ourselves.  Very peaceful and relaxing.  There were a couple of boats moored in the Bay and a group of paddleboarders.  So glad this area is preserved.  Definitely worth a visit - it is a must do if you are near La Paz.

reviews.title: Gorgeous cove !!!
reviews.text: We came to this beautiful beach in the early morning. We were all alone for over an hour and someone camping in the rocks played the guitar. It was magical !!!  What a great way to start the day !!!  I will return to Balandra Beach !!!

reviews.title: Best Beach in Mexico--Balandra Beach in La Paz
reviews.text: Someone told us about La Paz and Balandra Beach so we had to see it. We rented a car from Cabo San Jose from National for a day about $60 dollars. It took us 2 1/2 hours driving 70 mph through the mountains on a paved highway. This beach is hidden behind the mountains before La Paz Centro. Make sure you use google maps so you won't get lost. The drive was worth it !! Bahamas beach in Mexico!!!

reviews.title: Beautiful beach!
reviews.text: We took a little drive up from La Paz and checked out the beaches along the way. Very pretty area, nice to just sit and look or walk around. A little cold for swimming with the breeze when we went otherwise would have stayed longer :)

reviews.title: Great place to spend the day
reviews.text: Beautiful white sand beach, warm clear water.  Safe for young children as it doesn't get deep for a very long ways, and sheltered by a sand bar from strong pulling waves.

reviews.title: Awesome secluded beach
reviews.text: A great little secluded beach at the end of the road in La Paz. A great place to walk around and see an amazing sunset and just relax. you can pretty much walk on top of the water, because its so shallow.

reviews.title: Loved it
reviews.text: Amazing beach!! You can walk and see clearly into the water the she time. Down side since my husband and I went alone someone walked off with my sandals -_- besides that amazing bringing my fam next time.

reviews.title: best beach in la paz area
reviews.text: This review includes the beaches adjacent to Balandra. The main beach is tucked away in a cove. The water is never very deep, and at low tide it is barely up to your knees. Note that there aren't really waves here.If you walk to the right around the rocks you get to another beach, and if you go to the end of that one and walk around those rocks you get to another. There are fewer people the farther you go. Those 2 beaches are a little more "classic beach" than Balandra, as they aren't really in a cove.You can also hike up the hills bordering the beach, which provides some pretty good views.There is a snack truck in the main parking lot where you can get some water, soda, chips and stuff, but there are no full-service restaurants. You can also rent kayaks.

reviews.title: Beautiful Balandra!
reviews.text: Stunning beach with crystal clear water.  When the tide goes out (around 1:00 pm in February), you can walk a LONG way and the water is up to your knees.  Nice shallow beach for the kids!

reviews.title: Nice spot to kill an hour or two
reviews.text: So the draw here is that the tide goes out and leaves sand bars that you can walk across the bay to other beaches on.It's very pretty and because the water is so shallow it can be pretty warmThere are no services here so bring your own food/water.  If you go looking for a private spot to pee you'll likely find that others have done the same and some spots are packed full of poop coated toilet paper and used tampons.  It can be a bit nasty but then people can be kinda nasty sometimes.They rent table, 4 chairs and umbrella here but they charge it for a full day even if you only stay an hour and they charge $20.Make sure to walk around the point on the right side.  There's a LOT more over there than you might think.

reviews.title: Photo Perfection
reviews.text: Lovely setting - sand that goes for miles! Easy to access and fun for small children to play.  Opportunities for various water activities and varied interests.

reviews.title: BEAUTIFUL BALANDRA BEACH
reviews.text: My daughter and I went scuba diving off of La Paz. The dive company which is excellent (Dive in La Paz) took us to this beach for a lunch they had prepared. Sitting on this beautiful white beach looking at the scenery and eating  fresh cervechi was so calm and peaceful. The sand is powdery and doesn't even stick to you. Definitely a unique experience. Since we were the only ones there, this is not at all what happens when you go to a CA beach.

reviews.title: A tropical paradise of blue water and white sand
reviews.text: An incredibly beautiful place and on the day we went there was hardly anyone else there, great for a swim and to see the mushroom rock

reviews.title: Shallow, private, beautiful waters and beach
reviews.text: We took a road trip from San Jose del Cabo to La Paz and came to Balandra Beach and were very glad we did, the beach is a very cool experience with water only about up to your knees as far out as one could walk, perhaps a 1/4 mile or more. The shallow water would make a perfect setting for families with young children and we even saw a dog on a paddleboard! They have palapas for you to sit under if you want shade, but there are no other facilities except a vendor selling snacks and trinkets.  If you wanted, you could walk across the inlet through the water with your things and set up in one of the many completely private beach areas, which we will definitely do next time.

reviews.title: Stunning beach, secluded, untouched, a must see
reviews.text: This beach has 3 parts, 1 part you can drive to, and the other two you need to take a boat to get there. Go to the boat only portions, as there are fewer people, and it really feels like you are on a secluded beach, with beautiful shades of blue waters, and fine white sand. Bring a nice lunch and relax in the Sea of Cortez.

reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.text: don't forget your camera, is spectacular! flat water and white sand! Bring also food and drinks, as there is nowhere to buy

reviews.title: Walk Forever when the Tide goes out
reviews.text: Went two times to Balandra beach. The second time the tide was going out, stayed for the afternoon. By the time we left around 4 o'clock The Bay was nearly empty of water. So if you hadn't seen it prior and arrived late in the afternoon you might be disappointed.As you couldn't really kayak and it looked desolated. But all the other reviewers are correct it really is beautiful! The different birds are really something to watch and photograph. There are Palapas to hook your belongings onto the poles. The day we went it was also windy, so probably a good choice to be protected from the wind.

reviews.title: Beautiful, Must See
reviews.text: We went to Balandra beach this last Saturday for about 4 hours in the afternoon. There were some tourists and many locals at the beach but it was not overcrowded. The beach is clear and the water was moderately warm. The water is about knee high for several hundred yards out and there are several smaller beaches in the bay you can walk to through the water. We took a taxi for 550 pesos (about $33 with the current exchange of 18 pesos=$1) from the Costa Baja resort. Taxi drivers can drop you and return at a specified time. There was one vendor open on Saturday who was renting umbrellas and chairs for 200-300 pesos. There are some fixed umbrellas on the beach, so if you are there during the week you can likely snag one of those. There are no bathrooms and only some drinks and light packaged snacks for purchase. I am unsure how often the stand is open on weekdays when the beach is likely far less busy.

reviews.title: A "must go" in La Paz
reviews.text: This beach is just beautiful, quiet and has a magnificent view! If you plan to be there for a long time is best to bring some food and drinks because there is not much around.

reviews.title: Fantastice public beach
reviews.text: Just the most beautiful beach near La Paz!!  Easy to find and super safe for children.  Lovely rock formations too.

reviews.title: You can wade for a mile
reviews.text: It seems that way, anyway.  The water is warm and cerulean, the sand is white, the rocks are volcanic, the children are laughing, it's like a dream.

reviews.title: My favorite 5 star beach in the world.
reviews.text: So many people come to La Paz and don't get out to this excellent swimming, snorkeling beach in rural setting. Only 20 minutes out of town and well worth the drive. Child safe as you can walk out aprox half a kilometer in pristine clear turquoise water. No wind as its sheltered in a quiet cove. No services but ample parking. Often a food trailer has snacks drinks and souvenirs.

reviews.title: Rent Kayak to truly enjoy the Balandra Beach
reviews.text: Most beautiful beach I have ever seen. Went  twice just to enjoy the beauty. Rent a kayak and cruise the bay. You see lots of fish while kayaking.

reviews.title: Very nice beach
reviews.text: Very nice beach not too far from La Paz.  Waded around in shallow water and checked out the mushroom rock.  Didn't really find a good place to snorkel.  A little bit of trash from some ignorant beach goers, but unfortunately that happens.  Much cleaner than Tecolote which we visited afterword.

reviews.title: Must See Beach in Baja
reviews.text: The is possibly the best beach for kids I've ever been too. It is a lagoon/bay that fills in to waist height at high-tide and has no waves. At low tide, the lagoon nearly empties and you can walk out and explore the inter-tidal marine life for hundreds of meters. I've probably been 10 times in 5 years, and it hasn't changed a bit. It is great for SUPing, kayaking, relaxing on the shore or wading out for as far as you want. It is a spiritually significant beach to the indigenous people of Baja and is protected from further development, so should stay pristine indefinitely. There is one small kiosk in the parking lot where you can get snacks, rent a kayak or a SUP, but they don't serve beer - everyone brings their own.

reviews.title: Beautiful, get there early its popular!
reviews.text: Amazing bay, sooo. shallow. We wore our reef shoes and shuffled our feet as told, we didn't see any sing rays. Walked all the way round to the famous rock and snorkelled in water only 4 foot deep, very clear and chilly. No toilets here. We sat on the beach near some locals cooking up lunch for the entire family. Car park is small. So we headed over to Tecolote for lunch.

reviews.title: Gorgeous beach
reviews.text: If anything a bit too crowded because easily accessible. Lovely at end of day or early in the morning.

reviews.title: I have never seen such a beach!
reviews.text: I wanted to go to this beach for about 6 years, ever since I first saw a picture.  Be sure to wade out and explore around as many corners as possible.

reviews.title: Good as the pictures
reviews.text: Spent a half day there and it was a beautiful as the pictures we had seen in the magazine.  It was sunny all day so that helped the color of the water which was turquoise and clear.  We were warned about stingrays but walked all the way across to the deserted beaches, back and then across to the mushroom rock and never saw one.  There were four of us so don't be deterred by that.  Yes, there were wasps here and there but nobody ever got stung.  If you are in the area, it is a must see.

reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.text: We sailed into this gorgeous bay and anchored in crystal clear water. The rock formations around the bay are very cool and there are 4 or 5 seperate white sand beaches to laze around on. This beach is a popular picnic beach just a short drive or panga trip from La Paz so its popular with the locals. The craggy mountains to the south are Coyote hills I believe. It is a special place.

reviews.title: Wow. Just Wow.
reviews.text: This beach is surreal. Miles and miles of knee-deep, crystal clear water and white soft sand. Lots of fish and birds - off-the-beach snorkeling near the rocks is amazing. A perfect place to take a day off, find a sheltered cove, read a book, take a dip, hike a hill and do whatever you like. One of the most beautiful places I have ever been to. Magical.

reviews.title: It is the best beach for kids
reviews.text: Water there is so shallow and calm,  you can walk long way in and still in shallow water. It's parking lot is so crowded and most people are locals. No restaurant. Only good beach. Bo one told us this beach and found it by ourself. Highly recommend it.

reviews.title: Possibly nicest beach in La Paz
reviews.text: This is a beautiful shallow bay with very safe swimming for children.  Unfortunately if you want to swim in deep water you will have to go very far out.  However the beach is very clean (not always the case in Mexico) with little garbage.  On the weekends and holidays it can get very crowded with locals. There is a SUB rental kiosk but no food or drink for sale.  You can see that means it is not really used by tourists, possibly because you need a car to get there

reviews.title: Beautiful beach, lots of people
reviews.text: This beach was beautiful! The water is very shallow for much of it, but we had a very lovely time. Great views, lots of birds!

reviews.title: Paraiso
reviews.text: The beach you dream about at your desk on Monday morning! An amazing little "hidden" gem with white sand beach, palapas for shade and a wide, shallow, warm-watered bay for splashing around in. Minimal  services (NO restrooms) include a truck selling cold sodas and packaged snacks and a kayak and umbrella rental. Though small, the bay is deep and rocky so even if there are many people here, they are spread out along the beach allowing for privacy even on busy days.

reviews.title: Our favorite beach near La Paz
reviews.text: We think Balandra is the prettiest beach near La Paz.  Plenty of room to spread out.  Good wading and snorkeling in the shallow bay (but shuffle your feet if you're wading to avoid the stingrays).  There is a snack bar that has drinks and rents umbrellas, chaises and kayaks.  Kids love it.

reviews.title: very touristy
reviews.text: There were a lot of vendors looking for you to spend your money. It was interesting to see the marina present as they had a first aid station set up. Not as nice as tecolote

reviews.title: Restful and scenic
reviews.text: Amazing. Beautiful turquoise waters crashing steadily on soft white Sandy shores. Incredible conglomerate walls of volcanic rock. Private beach with a few locals and some tourists. There are peddlers.

reviews.title: Great experience
reviews.text: If you love to exploring inside to cortez of sea, this is a great place for snorkeling. We went with friends at this beach in La Paz and is like little lost paradise in La Baja that you must to exploring !! I recommend this place if you visit la paz one day

reviews.title: Too beautiful for words
reviews.text: Perfect turquoise beach. White sand, wading pool depth, and pretty as a picture. Be sure to shuffle walk when baby manta rays are present!

reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text: Beautiful place. The water is very warm and shallow. Would be a great place to take kids to swim. We rented snorkeling equipment, and found beautiful tropical fish here.

reviews.title: QUIET TRANQUIL WATERS
reviews.text: Playa Balandra is 24 kms. from La Paz where you will find the calm tranquil waters perfect for families and travellers to escape from everything.  The lagoon comprises 7 private beaches of which 5 are only accessible by kayak, paddle board (for rent at the main beach) and swimming.  At low tide, guests can almost walk across to the other beaches.On windy days, the beaches are well protected. Although Balandra is absolutely beautiful, there are no food or drink services, but Palya El Tecolote is only 1 km. from Balandra where you will find bars, restaurants and palapas to enjoy.Palapa Azul, a bar restaurant, serves the best Margarita in all of Baja, along with a full menu of delectable seafood dishes.I live on the mountain overlooking these beaches and has been my home for 7 years.Don't forget to see the "mushroom rock" which Balandra is famous for!

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text: Beautiful beach on a bay, not a ocean beach with waves. Bring food and drinks. Very relaxing. Kayaking and paddle surfing available for a small fee.

reviews.title: Unique Beach
reviews.text: We took the advise of other reviewers and ventured out to this place - not too easy to find if you don't have a GPS since the road signs were non-existent.  Fortunately the local police on the road directed us.  The area is still not developed yet.  All we saw were few cars and a vendor truck and that's how we guessed we arrived.  It took us 3 hours drive from Los Cabos.  It was a very windy day as we could feel the sand pelting on our face.  However, the water was still calm.  The water is shallow and you can walk in for quite a distance before the water reaches your waist.  We could see that this would be a great family beach with future resorts build around it.  If we didn't have to drive for such a long time to get back to Cabos and if we had beach chairs and umbrella, we would have stayed longer!

reviews.title: beautiful and quiet
reviews.text: perfect for couples looking for nice secluded beach (on weekdays) and for families with children as there are no waves and it is shallow for a long distance. I visited on a cloudy and windy day and still worth seeing it. Visit with your car or hire a cab for a day (80$) and visit all the beaches in la paz but you can spend most of your time here.

reviews.title: A beautifully hidden gem near La Paz!
reviews.text: Quite the hidden gem. Loved it. If you can get a shuttle or taxi or take a rental car here, do it.  It's a quiet and beautiful beach with clear blue water. Not a lot of wind since it's in a protected bay.  Not a ton of people. Some Locals and Tourist. Like any beach, bring your towels, coolers, sun umbrella and your own food. I saw one group pitch a tent. There is a small truck that rents out paddle boards, kayaks, some tables, umbrellas, and very limited snack like chips and soda. There are some permanent Palapa style umbrellas but that's on a  first come basis. Again, not a ton of people here so the chances of getting one early in the day is good.You can hike up the rock mountain or walk around the beach to see the mushroom rock. Great views from the top of the rock mountain but make sure to wear the proper shoes. Lots of loose rocks and as you make your way to the Mushroom rock, you will encounter sand and water depending on the tide.There is parking lot. I saw a porta potty.This is a great little adventure nearby. The kids will love it. You will love it too.

reviews.title: Big hype for the mushroom, better seen by boat
reviews.text: This beach gets really croweded on the overhype of seeing the famous mushroom rock. You can see it better coming from the ocean in a boat.

reviews.title: AMAZING!
reviews.text: This is a must while in LaPaz. I was in heaven for the day. Turquoise water and white sandy beach. Hardly onyone on the beach. Bring a cooler and food with you. Really nothing there at all. A hut to rent paddle boards and a vendor at the beginning of the beach. Take a walk around the rocks to the right. You will end up inside a beautiful bay. It is shallow crystal clear bay.It was windy everywhere else on the coast. This beach is protected. We will be going back for sure!

reviews.title: Speechless
reviews.text: Pictures are not good enough to show how nice is this place. Calm ocean, blue transparent water and clean sand

reviews.title: A five star hike and snorkel.
reviews.text: Our guide, Manuel Rodriguez from RED Travel Mexico, headed us out of LaPaz,month to the Bay. He filled in the details of how this important area was saved from development. The views were breath-taking.

reviews.title: One of the best beaches in La Paz
reviews.text: Lovely beach, very clean and the water is amazing. A must when visiting La Paz. Take a cooler, a shade and some food with you, there is very little services so be prepare. There are some rental umbrellas and a soda truck near by but that's about it.

reviews.title: Great beach for windy day
reviews.text: In la Paz if the wind is high, this is one of the few protected beaches. The sand is nice beach clean and water warm but very shallow.  The surrounding cliffs make a picturesque view from the water. There was a food truck with some paddle boards.  Visited by locals and tourists.

reviews.title: calm spectacular beach
reviews.text: fairly large beach, shaped like 2/3 of a circle with lots of little coves going around.  the mushroom rock is pretty cool to check out but being able to walk couple hundred feet from shore tells you how calm and shallow a lot of the water is here.  naturally its nice and warm as a result.  southern end has some ok snorkeling but this is more of beach to just relax and melt away.
